tools.name: Kickserv
tools.tagline: QuickBooks-friendly field service software for small service businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Seat-capped plans: Start $60/mo (5 users), Run $119/mo (10 users), Scale $199/mo (20 users); annual subscription saves 20%. QuickBooks Online integration from Start; QuickBooks Desktop integration is a $50/mo add-on from Run. 30-day free trial. Verified against kickserv.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Small service businesses (1-15 employees) that run their books in QuickBooks and want affordable, simple scheduling and invoicing
tools.weaknesses: Reporting is basic; QuickBooks Desktop sync is a paid add-on from the Run plan; no built-in phone system; thin inventory and automation
tools.long_description:
Kickserv is field service software for small service businesses. Founder Todd Eccles, who came from a family of plumbing and HVAC businesses, launched it as ServiceSidekick in 2006 and renamed it Kickserv in 2011; EverCommerce acquired it in August 2023. It targets solo operators and small shops that want straightforward scheduling, estimating and invoicing tied to QuickBooks, without the price or learning curve of enterprise platforms.

The product's strength is simplicity: a drag-and-drop calendar, contact management and a short job-to-invoice flow, with a mobile app for scheduling, time tracking, signatures and payments. Plans map to headcount rather than features: Start ($60/mo, 5 users), Run ($119/mo, 10 users) and Scale ($199/mo, 20 users), with 20% off for annual billing and a 30-day free trial. QuickBooks Online integration comes with every plan; QuickBooks Desktop integration is a $50/month add-on from the Run plan.

The trade-offs: reporting is basic next to Jobber or ServiceTitan, there's no built-in phone system, and inventory and automation are thin. Kickserv suits a small QuickBooks shop that wants to get organized and get paid, not a growing operation that needs depth.

pros_detail.title: Genuinely easy to learn
pros_detail.explanation: The drag-and-drop scheduling calendar and one-screen job-to-invoice flow are simple enough that non-technical owners and crews adopt it without much training. For a shop coming off paper or spreadsheets, that low learning curve is the whole point.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online integration is included from the $60 Start plan; QuickBooks Desktop users can add the Desktop integration for $50/month from the Run plan.

pros_detail.title: Affordable, seat-based pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Start is $60/mo for up to 5 users, cheap for a full FSM with QuickBooks sync. Because tiers scale by seats (5/10/20) rather than locking core features behind upgrades, small shops aren't forced to pay enterprise prices for basic capability.

pros_detail.title: Transparent public pricing
pros_detail.explanation: All three plans and their user caps are published, so you can evaluate without a mandatory sales call.

pros_detail.title: Mobile app for iOS and Android
pros_detail.explanation: Field techs can schedule, track time, capture digital signatures, and take payments from the app on every plan. It covers the day-to-day field workflow that a small shop needs.

pros_detail.title: 30-day free trial
pros_detail.explanation: Long enough to run a full month of jobs and confirm the QuickBooks flow with your own data.

cons_detail.title: Basic reporting
cons_detail.explanation: Reporting covers the basics but lacks the customizable reporting of Jobber's higher plans or ServiceTitan. Shops that want deep job-profitability or technician-performance analysis will hit the ceiling.

cons_detail.title: Test the mobile app with your crew
cons_detail.explanation: The app is the field team's main tool, so trial it with your actual techs and devices before rolling it out.

cons_detail.title: Test the QuickBooks sync with your data
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks is the main reason most shops pick Kickserv, so confirm customers, invoices and payments flow the way you need during the trial; Desktop users should price the $50/month add-on.

cons_detail.title: No built-in phone system
cons_detail.explanation: There's no native VoIP, call recording, or dispatcher call routing. Shops that rely on inbound phone volume (the Workiz use case) will need a separate phone tool, adding cost and setup.

cons_detail.title: Thin advanced features
cons_detail.explanation: Inventory is light, there's no membership/service-agreement management, and automation is basic. Kickserv is built for simple small shops; businesses that scale past ~15 techs or want recurring-membership programs will outgrow it.

tools.implementation_notes: Kickserv is built for self-service setup. Import customers (CSV or QuickBooks), set up services and price items, and connect payments. Because QuickBooks is the main reason most shops choose it, configure and test that integration first, and decide whether you need the Desktop add-on. Then run in parallel with your old system for a couple of weeks before cutting over. Field training is light, but trial the mobile app with your actual crew. There are no required setup fees, and the 30-day trial is long enough to validate the QuickBooks workflow end to end.

tool_faqs.q: Is Kickserv a good fit if I use QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, that's its core use. QuickBooks Online integration is included on every plan, including the $60 Start plan; QuickBooks Desktop integration is a $50/month add-on from the Run plan. Test the flow with your own data during the 30-day trial before you commit.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Kickserv cost?
tool_faqs.a: Three seat-capped plans: Start at $60/mo (up to 5 users), Run at $119/mo (up to 10 users) and Scale at $199/mo (up to 20 users), with 20% off for annual billing and a 30-day free trial. QuickBooks Desktop integration is a $50/month add-on.

tool_faqs.q: Kickserv vs Jobber: which should I pick?
tool_faqs.a: Jobber has deeper features and more room to grow. Kickserv wins on low cost, seat-capped plans and QuickBooks-first simplicity. A QuickBooks-centric small shop on a tight budget leans Kickserv; a shop that wants more features and room to scale leans Jobber. Both publish pricing, so trial each before deciding.

tool_faqs.q: What size business is Kickserv best for?
tool_faqs.a: Solo operators up to about 20 users, the Scale plan's cap: small shops getting off paper and spreadsheets that want simple scheduling, estimating and invoicing tied to QuickBooks. Operations that need deep reporting, memberships or inventory will outgrow it.

tool_faqs.q: Does Kickserv have a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The iOS and Android apps let field techs schedule, track time, capture signatures and take payments. Trial it with your actual techs before rolling it out shop-wide.

tools.name: SingleOps
tools.tagline: Tree care and plant health care business software, now sold by Granum

pricing.pricing_note: Per-company plans with a monthly charge for each extra office or sales user; crew users are free. Essential $200 a month billed annually ($220 monthly), extra office or sales users $55 a month each. Plus $350 a month billed annually ($385 monthly), extra users $115 each. Premier $500 a month billed annually ($550 monthly), extra users $150 each; timesheets and GPS tracking are listed as an add-on. Every plan includes a dedicated implementation specialist and one-on-one training. No free trial is published. Verified against granum.com/singleops/pricing/ 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Tree care and plant health care companies, from single-crew outfits to multi-crew operations, that want estimating, tree inventory, scheduling, crew work orders and invoicing in one system
tools.weaknesses: Costs more than entry-level field service apps: Essential starts at $200 a month billed annually and each extra office or sales user is $55-$150 a month depending on plan; route optimization and reporting are Premier features; timesheets and GPS tracking are an add-on; no published free trial
tools.long_description:
SingleOps is business management software for tree care and plant health care (PHC) companies. It is now sold as SingleOps by Granum. In November 2024 SingleOps merged with Landscape Management Network (LMN), alongside a growth investment from existing investor FTV Capital with participation from Five Elms Capital. In October 2025 the combined company launched Granum as the parent brand for LMN, SingleOps and the Greenius crew-training product. SingleOps says it has served arborists since 2013, and its 2025 press materials give Atlanta, Georgia as its headquarters. Granum is led by CEO Mark Sedgley, who ran SingleOps before the merger.

The product covers the path from lead to payment: a CRM, estimating with digital proposals and upsell options, and a Tree Inventory that records species, condition, risk and work history on a map of each client's property. It adds time-based scheduling and routing, digital crew work orders with notes, photos and checklists, automated proposal follow-ups and renewals, and invoicing with online payment by credit card, ACH or debit. Payments run through SingleOps Payments, which is powered by ProPay, part of Global Payments. SingleOps has a two-way sync with QuickBooks Online and connects to QuickBooks Desktop through the Web Connector. A client portal lets customers request service.

Prices are published per company, with a monthly charge for each extra office or sales user; SingleOps says crew users are free. Essential is $200 a month billed annually ($220 monthly), with extra office or sales users at $55 a month each. Plus is $350 a month billed annually ($385 monthly), with extra office users at $115, and adds options-based proposals, job site measurements and mapping, map-based scheduling, a one-way Google Calendar sync and automations for proposals and invoice due dates. Premier is $500 a month billed annually ($550 monthly), with extra office users at $150, and adds route optimization, more automations and follow-ups, and business insights and reporting. Timesheets and GPS vehicle tracking are listed as an add-on. Every plan includes a dedicated implementation specialist and one-on-one training.

Before the Granum launch, SingleOps described itself as software for the wider green industry, including lawn care, full-service landscaping, sod farms and landscape supply. Granum now presents SingleOps as its tree care product and LMN as its landscaping product.

The trade-off: SingleOps costs more than entry-level field service apps, extra office seats add up on the higher plans, and route optimization and reporting sit on the top plan. No free trial is published, so evaluation is through a demo.

pros_detail.title: Built around tree work
pros_detail.explanation: Tree Inventory maps each client's trees with species, condition, risk and work history, and that record feeds proposals and work orders. Generalist field service apps do not model individual trees this way.

pros_detail.title: Lead to payment in one system
pros_detail.explanation: CRM, estimating, scheduling, crew work orders, invoicing and online payments (card, ACH or debit) run in one platform, with automated follow-ups on proposals and renewals.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks sync
pros_detail.explanation: SingleOps has a two-way sync with QuickBooks Online and connects to QuickBooks Desktop through the Web Connector, so clients and invoices do not need double entry.

pros_detail.title: Free crew users
pros_detail.explanation: Only office and sales users add cost. SingleOps says crew users are free, which helps companies with large field teams.

pros_detail.title: Guided onboarding on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Each plan includes a dedicated implementation specialist and one-on-one training, and support is available by phone, email or chat.

cons_detail.title: Higher starting price
cons_detail.explanation: Essential starts at $200 a month billed annually ($220 monthly), and each extra office or sales user adds $55 a month. That is a lot for a one-person tree service.

cons_detail.title: Seat fees rise with the plan
cons_detail.explanation: Extra office or sales users cost $115 a month on Plus and $150 a month on Premier, so a growing office team raises the bill quickly.

cons_detail.title: Key tools on the top plan
cons_detail.explanation: Route optimization and business reporting are Premier features ($500 a month billed annually), and timesheets with GPS tracking are an add-on whose price is not published.

cons_detail.title: Tree care focus
cons_detail.explanation: Granum now sells SingleOps as its tree care and PHC product and LMN as its landscaping product. It is not built for HVAC, plumbing or electrical work.

cons_detail.title: No published trial
cons_detail.explanation: SingleOps offers demos rather than a self-serve free trial, so you cannot test it on your own before talking to sales.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with a demo, since SingleOps publishes no free trial. Every plan includes a dedicated implementation specialist and one-on-one training. Before kickoff, gather your client and property list, your service catalog and prices, and any tree records you want in Tree Inventory. Connect QuickBooks early: QuickBooks Online connects from account settings, while QuickBooks Desktop needs the Web Connector. If you want card and ACH payments, set up SingleOps Payments (processed by ProPay) and decide whether to pass processing fees to clients, which the payment settings allow. Count your office and sales users before choosing a plan, because crew users are free but each extra office seat is billed monthly.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns SingleOps?
tool_faqs.a: Granum. SingleOps merged with LMN in November 2024, with a growth investment from FTV Capital and participation from Five Elms Capital, and the combined company launched the Granum brand in October 2025. The product is now sold as SingleOps by Granum.

tool_faqs.q: How much does SingleOps cost?
tool_faqs.a: Essential is $200 a month billed annually ($220 monthly), Plus $350 ($385 monthly) and Premier $500 ($550 monthly). Extra office or sales users cost $55, $115 or $150 a month depending on plan, and crew users are free. Timesheets and GPS tracking are an add-on.

tool_faqs.q: Does SingleOps integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. It has a two-way sync with QuickBooks Online and connects to QuickBooks Desktop through the Web Connector. Plus and Premier also include a one-way Google Calendar sync.

tool_faqs.q: Is SingleOps for landscapers or tree care companies?
tool_faqs.a: Granum now markets SingleOps to tree care and plant health care companies and LMN to landscaping companies. SingleOps used to describe itself as serving the wider green industry, including lawn care and landscaping.

tool_faqs.q: How does SingleOps handle payments?
tool_faqs.a: Through SingleOps Payments, powered by ProPay (part of Global Payments). Clients can pay by credit card or ACH, you can save cards for autopay, and you can choose to add a processing fee to invoices.

tool_faqs.q: SingleOps or Arborgold for a tree service?
tool_faqs.a: Both are built for tree work. SingleOps (from $200 a month billed annually) includes Tree Inventory on every plan and charges per extra office user. Arborgold starts at $129 a month on annual payment with a twelve-month commitment, and puts tree inventory mapping on its $499 Enterprise plan. Demo both with your own jobs.

tools.name: Arborgold
tools.tagline: Business software for tree care, lawn care and landscaping companies

pricing.pricing_note: Per-company plans: Starter $129, Professional $299 and Enterprise $499 a month with annual payment, or $149, $343 and $573 a month with monthly payment. Every plan requires an annual contract (twelve-month minimum commitment), and customers must give at least 60 days' notice to cancel. Additional mobile-only licenses are sold separately (price on request), and some integrations may require third-party apps at extra cost. No free trial is published. Verified against arborgold.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Tree care, plant health care, lawn care and landscaping companies that want CRM, proposals, scheduling, crew time tracking and invoicing in one system, with chemical tracking and tree inventory mapping available on the higher plans
tools.weaknesses: Every plan requires a twelve-month minimum commitment and at least 60 days' notice to cancel; chemical tracking needs Professional and tree inventory mapping needs Enterprise; extra mobile-only licenses are priced on request; some integrations may need third-party apps at extra cost
tools.long_description:
Arborgold is business management software for tree care, plant health care, lawn care and landscaping companies, and it also markets to pest control and snow removal businesses. Its about page says it was established in 1994 by Jon and Donna Garner, who came to software from the tree and landscape business. It is run by Tree Management Systems, LLC (doing business as Arborgold) from South Jordan, Utah. Arborgold says thousands of tree, lawn and landscape businesses use it.

The Starter plan covers CRM, estimating, unlimited land measurements, drag-and-drop scheduling, route optimization, job management, messaging, invoicing and e-payments, reporting and crew time tracking. Professional adds job costing, automated renewals, material inventory management, chemical tracking and an autoprice calculator. Enterprise adds plant and tree inventory mapping, sales automation, custom templates, expense tracking, equipment maintenance tracking and project scheduling. For plant health care work, Arborgold says crews can record weather conditions and chemical usage at the job site so state regulatory reports can be printed. The MobileCrew app for iPhone and Android lets crews punch in and out by job and records each punch on a map, and there are mobile apps for sales estimators and a customer portal.

Arborgold lists integrations with QuickBooks Online and Desktop, Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Twilio (text and voice), SendGrid (email marketing), SiteOne (materials and purchase orders) and LandscapeHub. Its pricing page notes that an integration may require third-party applications at additional cost. Arborgold Payments has no monthly fee; Arborgold lists 2.9% plus $0.20 per authorization for Visa, Mastercard and Discover, 3.5% plus $0.30 for American Express, and 1% for ACH capped at $15 per transaction.

Prices are published per company: Starter is $129, Professional $299 and Enterprise $499 a month with annual payment, or $149, $343 and $573 a month with monthly payment. Every plan carries a twelve-month minimum commitment, and customers must give at least 60 days' notice to cancel. Extra mobile-only licenses for estimators and crew leads are sold separately, with pricing on request. Onboarding includes instructor-led virtual training, done-for-you data migration and help syncing integrations.

The trade-off: the annual commitment and 60-day notice make Arborgold harder to leave than month-to-month tools, and the features that set it apart for tree and plant health care work (chemical tracking and tree inventory mapping) sit on the $299 and $499 plans.

pros_detail.title: Plant health care tools
pros_detail.explanation: Chemical tracking (Professional and up) lets crews log weather and chemical usage on site for printable state reports, and Enterprise adds plant and tree inventory mapping with photos on interactive maps.

pros_detail.title: Routing and time tracking from the first plan
pros_detail.explanation: Starter already includes route optimization, drag-and-drop scheduling and crew time tracking. The MobileCrew app records each punch in and out on a map.

pros_detail.title: Wide integration list
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online and Desktop, Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Twilio, SendGrid, SiteOne and LandscapeHub are all listed on Arborgold's integrations page.

pros_detail.title: Published per-company prices
pros_detail.explanation: Plan prices are on the website ($129, $299 and $499 a month with annual payment), so you can budget before a sales call.

pros_detail.title: Published payment rates
pros_detail.explanation: Arborgold Payments has no monthly fee and lists its card and ACH rates, including a $15 cap on ACH fees.

pros_detail.title: Long track record
pros_detail.explanation: Arborgold says it was established in 1994 by founders who ran tree and landscape businesses.

cons_detail.title: Twelve-month commitment
cons_detail.explanation: Every plan requires a twelve-month minimum commitment, even when you pay monthly, and cancelling needs at least 60 days' notice.

cons_detail.title: Signature features on higher plans
cons_detail.explanation: Chemical tracking and job costing start at Professional ($299 a month with annual payment), and plant and tree inventory mapping needs Enterprise ($499).

cons_detail.title: Some costs not published
cons_detail.explanation: Extra mobile-only licenses are priced on request, and Arborgold warns that some integrations may need third-party apps at extra cost.

cons_detail.title: Green industry only
cons_detail.explanation: Arborgold is built for tree, lawn and landscape work (plus pest control and snow removal). It is not a fit for HVAC, plumbing or electrical shops.

cons_detail.title: No self-serve trial
cons_detail.explanation: Arborgold offers product tours and demos rather than a published free trial.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo or product tour first, since Arborgold publishes no free trial, and choose your plan carefully because every plan carries a twelve-month minimum commitment. Arborgold's onboarding offers instructor-led virtual training, done-for-you data migration and done-with-you integration setup, so gather your customer list, service items, prices and any tree or chemical records beforehand. Connect QuickBooks (Online or Desktop) early, and ask whether any integration you need requires a third-party app at extra cost. Then roll out the MobileCrew app so crews punch in and out on each job, which records time by person, job and service.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Arborgold?
tool_faqs.a: Arborgold is operated by Tree Management Systems, LLC (doing business as Arborgold) in South Jordan, Utah. Its about page says Jon and Donna Garner established it in 1994. Its website and terms do not name a parent company.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Arborgold cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starter is $129, Professional $299 and Enterprise $499 a month with annual payment, or $149, $343 and $573 a month paid monthly. Every plan has a twelve-month minimum commitment, and extra mobile-only licenses are priced on request.

tool_faqs.q: Can I cancel Arborgold at any time?
tool_faqs.a: No. Every plan carries a twelve-month minimum commitment, and Arborgold requires at least 60 days' notice to cancel.

tool_faqs.q: Does Arborgold track chemical applications?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, on the Professional and Enterprise plans. Arborgold says crews can record weather and chemical usage at the job site so state regulatory reports can be printed.

tool_faqs.q: Does Arborgold integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with both QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop. It also lists Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Twilio, SendGrid, SiteOne and LandscapeHub.

tool_faqs.q: Arborgold or SingleOps for tree care?
tool_faqs.a: Both are built for tree work. Arborgold starts lower ($129 a month with annual payment) but requires a twelve-month commitment and puts tree inventory mapping on its $499 Enterprise plan. SingleOps starts at $200 a month billed annually, includes Tree Inventory on every plan and charges for each extra office user. Demo both with your own jobs.

tools.name: Contractor+
tools.tagline: Free all-in-one estimating, invoicing, and job app for contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Free Freedom plan (up to 250 leads/clients and 5 estimates or invoices per month); Pro $29/mo for 1 user; Pro Team $58/mo with the first 2 users included, +$20/mo per additional user; Max $500/mo with unlimited users. Prices shown are monthly-plan rates; annual billing saves up to 40%. Its FAQ also offers 14-day trials of most premium features (such as the job schedule and the team chat). Verified against contractorplus.app/pricing 2026-10-03.

tools.best_for: Solo contractors and small trades teams that want a genuinely free, all-in-one estimating, invoicing, and job-management app on mobile
tools.weaknesses: Lighter than mature FSM platforms on advanced dispatch and membership management; QuickBooks, Zapier, API and job costing sit on higher plans; little public company history; teams scaling past about 10 people will likely outgrow it
tools.long_description:
Contractor+ is a mobile-first, freemium app for solo contractors and small trades teams. It bundles estimates, invoices, scheduling, client management and payments into one app for iOS and Android, and its standout is a free Freedom plan (basic CRM, up to 250 leads and clients, and 5 estimates or invoices a month) with no time limit.

Paid plans stay inexpensive: Pro at $29 a month for one user removes the caps, Pro Team at $58 a month includes two users and adds QuickBooks Online, Zapier and a developer API, and Max covers unlimited users; annual billing saves up to 40%. Every plan takes card and ACH payments, and homeowners can apply for Wisetack financing from invoices. The integration list is broad for a tool this size: QuickBooks, CompanyCam, Hover and EagleView, Angi and Thumbtack, and supplier connections including Lowe's, Menards, ABC Supply and QXO.

The trade-off is depth and maturity. Contractor+ is lighter than Jobber or Housecall Pro on advanced dispatching and membership management, and the company publishes little about its history. For a solo or very small operation focused on estimating, invoicing and getting paid, that's an acceptable trade; for a growing shop that needs deep scheduling and reporting, look at a more mature platform.

pros_detail.title: Genuinely free entry tier
pros_detail.explanation: The Freedom plan provides real, usable functionality at no cost, not a crippled trial. For a contractor unsure about committing to a monthly subscription, that removes the biggest barrier to getting off paper.

pros_detail.title: Inexpensive paid plans
pros_detail.explanation: Pro is $29/mo for one user and Pro Team $58/mo with two users included, well below most mature FSM platforms.

pros_detail.title: Broad integrations for its size
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online, Zapier and an API, CompanyCam, Hover, EagleView, Angi, Thumbtack, and supplier connections such as Lowe's, Menards, ABC Supply and QXO.

pros_detail.title: Fast estimate-to-invoice on mobile
pros_detail.explanation: Built mobile-first, Contractor+ makes it quick to produce a line-item estimate with photos and convert it to an invoice from the field, which is exactly the workflow a solo contractor needs most.

pros_detail.title: Payments and financing built in
pros_detail.explanation: Card and ACH payments come on every plan, and Wisetack financing lets homeowners apply from an invoice on jobs of $500 to $25,000.

pros_detail.title: Broad fit for solo and small trades
pros_detail.explanation: From handyman to small GC to single-truck HVAC/plumbing/electrical, the core estimate-invoice-schedule-collect loop applies across trades, making it easy to recommend to a wide range of small operators.

cons_detail.title: Lighter depth than mature FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Contractor+ covers the core workflow well but lacks the advanced dispatching, membership management, and deep reporting of platforms like Jobber, Housecall Pro, or ServiceTitan. Growing shops will feel the gaps.

cons_detail.title: Key features sit on higher plans
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online, Zapier and the developer API arrive on Pro Team, and job costing and the client portal on higher tiers, so check which plan you actually need.

cons_detail.title: Little public company history
cons_detail.explanation: Contractor+ publishes little about its ownership and history. For operators who weigh vendor longevity heavily, ask about it before committing years of records.

cons_detail.title: You can outgrow it
cons_detail.explanation: The simplicity that makes Contractor+ great for a solo operator becomes limiting as you add crews and need real dispatch and reporting. Plan to reevaluate once you push past roughly 10 people.

tools.implementation_notes: Contractor+ is built for self-service setup: it is mobile-first and aimed at solo and small operators. Start on the free Freedom plan to test the core workflow (an estimate with photos, converted to an invoice, paid by card or ACH) before deciding whether Pro or Pro Team is worth it for your volume. Coming off paper or spreadsheets there is little to migrate: enter your services and price items and go. The main thing to test is whether the scheduling and reporting are enough for how you run jobs, since that is where Contractor+ is lighter than mature platforms.

tool_faqs.q: Is Contractor+ really free?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, the Freedom plan is a genuinely free tier rather than a time-limited trial, capped at 250 leads/clients and 5 estimates or invoices per month. Paid tiers (Pro at $29/mo, Pro Team at $58/mo with 2 users included, and Max at $500/mo with unlimited users) add capacity and features; the free plan suits contractors sending only a handful of estimates or invoices a month. Annual billing saves up to 40% on paid tiers.

tool_faqs.q: Who is Contractor+ best for?
tool_faqs.a: Solo contractors and small trades teams (roughly 1-10 people), such as handymen, small general contractors, and single-truck HVAC/plumbing/electrical operators, who want an affordable, all-in-one app for estimates, invoices, scheduling, and payments. Larger shops that need deep dispatch and reporting will likely outgrow it.

tool_faqs.q: Contractor+ vs Jobber: which should I choose?
tool_faqs.a: Contractor+ wins on price (free entry tier, cheap paid plans) and simplicity for solo and very small operators. Jobber is more mature, with deeper scheduling and reporting and a longer public track record, which makes it better as you add crews and need to scale. Budget-conscious solos lean Contractor+; growing shops that want room to scale lean Jobber.

tool_faqs.q: Does Contractor+ handle payments?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Every plan includes card and ACH payments from invoices, and the Max plan advertises its lowest card rates (from 2.59%) with ACH capped at $5. Customers can also apply for Wisetack financing from invoices on jobs of $500 to $25,000. Confirm current rates in the app, since payment terms can change.

tool_faqs.q: What are the limits of Contractor+?
tool_faqs.a: It's lighter than mature FSM platforms on advanced dispatching and membership management, several features (QuickBooks Online, Zapier and the API, job costing, the client portal) sit on higher plans, and the company publishes little about its history. For a solo or small team focused on estimating, invoicing and getting paid, that's an acceptable trade; for a growing multi-crew shop, a more mature platform is usually the better fit.

tools.name: Aurora Solar
tools.tagline: Solar design, proposal and permit plan set software with published per-user plans

pricing.pricing_note: Per-user plans. Basic is $135 per user per month billed annually ($1,620 a year) or $159 month to month; Premium is $220 per user per month billed annually ($2,640 a year) or $259 month to month. Each Basic or Premium license covers 1 user and 50 projects a month. Annual plans carry a one-year commitment; monthly plans have no minimum and cancellations take effect at the end of the billing period. Enterprise is custom-priced per project with unlimited users and adds AI-assisted site models, APIs, advanced permissions and dealer configurations. Paid add-ons include on-demand site models (from $9.99), expedited site models, plan sets, engineering stamps, premium support, training, technical consultation and a design API. No free trial is listed. Verified against aurorasolar.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential and commercial solar installers and sales teams that want 3D design, proposals, financing and permit plan sets in one platform and are fine paying per user
tools.weaknesses: Per-user pricing ($135-$220 per user per month billed annually, $159-$259 monthly) with 50 projects a month per Basic or Premium license; AI-assisted site models are listed under Enterprise; plan sets, engineering stamps and on-demand site models cost extra; no free trial is listed
tools.long_description:
Aurora Solar is solar design and sales software for residential and commercial solar installers. It was founded in 2013 by Christopher Hopper and Samuel Adeyemo and is based in San Francisco. Aurora says its platform has been used to design more than 20 million solar projects and that more than 7,000 organizations use it. It has bought two other solar software companies: Folsom Labs, maker of the HelioScope commercial design tool, and Lyra, a plan set company, in 2024.

The core workflow runs from a roof model to a proposal. Design Mode builds a 3D model of the site from satellite imagery and LIDAR data, and Aurora says its AI can produce a 3D roof model in under 15 seconds. The software then estimates production and shading, sizes batteries, and feeds Sales Mode, where reps present a tablet-friendly proposal with savings and financing options. Aurora has built-in financing links to GoodLeap, Mosaic, Dividend, Sungage Financial, EnFin and LightReach, and lets you add other lenders as custom financiers. In September 2026 it added quoting for HVAC, EV chargers and batteries for US installers and launched the full platform in the UK.

Aurora also covers the step after the sale. Its Plan Sets Service delivers permit-ready plan sets, including single-line or three-line diagrams with conductor sizes, and engineering stamps can be added. Aurora says Plan Sets Service has a 95% first-time approval rate with permitting offices. Expert Design Services, Contract Manager and drone mapping are sold alongside the software.

Pricing is published and per user. Basic is $135 per user per month billed annually ($159 month to month) and Premium is $220 ($259 month to month); each license covers 1 user and 50 projects a month. Premium adds LIDAR-assisted modeling, bankable shade reports and more battery modeling. Enterprise is custom-priced per project, with unlimited users, AI-assisted site models, APIs and dealer configurations.

The trade-off: Aurora is priced per seat with a project cap on each license, and several useful pieces (on-demand site models, plan sets, engineering stamps, premium support) cost extra. A small team can get started on Basic, but model the add-ons you expect to use before comparing it with free tools such as OpenSolar.

pros_detail.title: Fast 3D site modeling
pros_detail.explanation: Aurora builds 3D roof models from satellite imagery and LIDAR data, and says its AI can produce a roof model in under 15 seconds. That speeds up the step reps find slowest when they model roofs by hand.

pros_detail.title: Design to proposal in one flow
pros_detail.explanation: The roof model, production and shade estimates, battery sizing and a tablet-friendly homeowner proposal live in one workflow, so a rep can go from address to priced proposal in one sitting.

pros_detail.title: Permit plan sets from the same app
pros_detail.explanation: Aurora's Plan Sets Service delivers permit-ready plan sets with single-line or three-line diagrams and conductor sizes, and engineering stamps can be added. You can order them from the project you already designed.

pros_detail.title: Built-in lender links
pros_detail.explanation: GoodLeap, Mosaic, Dividend, Sungage Financial, EnFin and LightReach are integrated, and other lenders can be added as custom financiers, so monthly-payment options show up in the proposal.

pros_detail.title: Published, self-serve pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Basic and Premium prices are on the website with a monthly option and no minimum commitment, so a small team can sign up without a sales call.

pros_detail.title: Commercial design too
pros_detail.explanation: Aurora owns HelioScope, a commercial and industrial design tool, and added storage modeling to it in 2026, so a company that does both residential and commercial work can stay with one vendor.

cons_detail.title: Per-seat cost with a project cap
cons_detail.explanation: Each Basic or Premium license is $135-$220 per user per month billed annually ($159-$259 monthly) and covers 1 user and 50 projects a month. A multi-rep team pays for every seat.

cons_detail.title: Add-ons raise the real cost
cons_detail.explanation: On-demand site models (from $9.99), expedited models, plan sets, engineering stamps, premium support and training are paid add-ons. Price the add-ons you expect to use, not only the license.

cons_detail.title: AI-assisted modeling sits in Enterprise
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page lists AI-assisted site models under the custom-priced Enterprise plan. Basic and Premium users can buy on-demand site models instead, so confirm which modeling option your plan includes.

cons_detail.title: No listed free trial
cons_detail.explanation: Aurora does not list a free trial. Monthly billing with no minimum is the lower-risk way to test it.

cons_detail.title: Not an operations platform
cons_detail.explanation: Aurora covers design, sales, contracts and plan sets. Install tracking and project operations usually run in a separate tool, such as Enerflo, which integrates with Aurora.

tools.implementation_notes: Sign up for Basic or Premium on Aurora's website, or talk to sales for Enterprise. Set up your equipment catalog, pricing, adders and proposal templates first, then connect the lenders you sell with (GoodLeap, Mosaic, Dividend, Sungage Financial, EnFin or LightReach) or add others as custom financiers. Train reps on Design Mode and Sales Mode together, since the proposal is only as good as the roof model behind it. Decide early how you will handle permitting: order plan sets and stamps from Aurora, or keep an in-house or outside engineering process. If you run a CRM, use Aurora's API and webhooks (the help center has walkthroughs for HubSpot and Zoho CRM) so projects are created and updated without retyping customer data. Start on monthly billing if you want to test before committing to a year.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Aurora Solar cost?
tool_faqs.a: Basic is $135 per user per month billed annually ($1,620 a year) or $159 month to month. Premium is $220 per user per month billed annually ($2,640 a year) or $259 month to month. Each license covers 1 user and 50 projects a month. Enterprise is custom-priced per project with unlimited users. Site models, plan sets, engineering stamps and premium support are paid add-ons. Prices verified on aurorasolar.com/pricing on 2026-09-29.

tool_faqs.q: Does Aurora handle permits and electrical design?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, as a paid service. Aurora's Plan Sets Service delivers permit-ready plan sets with single-line or three-line diagrams and conductor sizes, and engineering stamps can be added. The software also has a single-line diagram editor. Aurora bought Lyra, a plan set company, in 2024 to build out this part of the product.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Aurora does not list a free trial. You can sign up for Basic or Premium on monthly billing with no minimum commitment and cancel at the end of the billing period.

tool_faqs.q: Aurora Solar vs OpenSolar: which should I use?
tool_faqs.a: Aurora charges per user and includes paid services such as plan sets and stamps. OpenSolar is free to use and makes its money from hardware and finance partners. Teams that want Aurora's modeling, plan set service and lender links often pay for it; cost-conscious or newer installers often start with OpenSolar. Trying both on a few real jobs is the fairest test.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Aurora Solar?
tool_faqs.a: Aurora Solar is a privately held, venture-backed company founded in 2013 by Christopher Hopper and Samuel Adeyemo and based in San Francisco. It has not been acquired; it has bought Folsom Labs (HelioScope) and Lyra.

tools.name: OpenSolar
tools.tagline: Free solar design, proposal and project management software funded by partners

pricing.pricing_note: The design, sales and project management platform is free to use, with no licensing fee; OpenSolar is paid by its hardware, finance and service partners. Since 16 April 2026, connecting OpenSolar to outside systems costs extra: API Access is a per-project fee charged when a project is created (30-day free trial), and OpenSolar-built connectors such as Xero and QuickBooks are a flat monthly subscription per organization with regional pricing. Premium imagery (Nearmap, MetroMap, 3D Plus, depending on country) is bought per image; free imagery is included. Paid items are charged through a prepaid OpenSolar Wallet. Fee amounts are shown in the app, not on the public site. Verified against opensolar.com/api and opensolar.com/post/free-platform-data-export-pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Solar installers of any size, in the US, UK, Australia and many other countries, that want free design, proposal and project software and accept partner-funded placement
tools.weaknesses: Partners pay for placement, so in-app lenders and products are not neutral; API Access (per project), connectors (monthly) and premium imagery cost extra and prices are shown only in the app; some features depend on your country
tools.long_description:
OpenSolar is free solar design, sales and project management software. It was founded in 2017 by Adam Pryor and Andrew Birch and is headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with a remote team around the world. OpenSolar says more than 28,000 solar professionals in over 185 countries use it. It raised US$20 million in equity in October 2025 from investors including Titanium Ventures and Google.

Installers do not pay a licence fee. Instead, OpenSolar says its partners (equipment makers, distributors, lenders, permitting providers and training companies) pay to be part of the platform. In return, their products and loans are offered inside the software: the Shop and bill of materials, Integrated Finance, and other marketplace features.

The software covers the job from lead to invoice. Auto Design and the Mounting Designer produce 3D designs on free or premium imagery, with year-round shading analysis and a performance engine based on the System Advisor Model (SAM), and the Single Line Diagrams tool builds editable diagrams from templates for Australia, the US, the UK, Germany, Italy and Spain. Sales Machine proposals include financing from lenders such as GoodLeap, Sungage, Dividend Finance and LightReach in the US, and local lenders in the UK, Australia and Germany, plus e-signature. A built-in CRM handles projects, and CashFlow handles invoices and customer payments in the US, UK and Australia. OS 3.0, released in September 2025, added Ada, an AI assistant that can take voice or chat instructions to create projects and start designs.

Some items cost money. Since April 2026, API Access is charged per project and OpenSolar-built connectors (such as Xero and QuickBooks) are a monthly subscription, and premium imagery from Nearmap, MetroMap or 3D Plus is bought per image. These are paid from a prepaid OpenSolar Wallet, and the amounts are shown in the app rather than on the website.

The trade-off: the software is free because partners pay for placement, so the lenders and products you see first are OpenSolar's commercial partners. Teams that connect OpenSolar to other systems through the API or connectors pay usage fees, and some features (SLD templates, payments, imagery providers, connectors) depend on your country.

pros_detail.title: No licence fee
pros_detail.explanation: Design, proposals, e-signature, CRM and project management are free to use. OpenSolar says partners fund the platform and that it remains committed to keeping it free for installers.

pros_detail.title: Wide reach
pros_detail.explanation: OpenSolar says more than 28,000 solar professionals in over 185 countries use it, and it has lender and imagery partners in the US, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and parts of Europe.

pros_detail.title: Financing inside the proposal
pros_detail.explanation: Integrated Finance includes US lenders such as GoodLeap, Sungage, Dividend Finance, EnFin and LightReach, plus local lenders in the UK, Australia and Germany, so homeowners can see payment options in the proposal.

pros_detail.title: Single-line diagrams built in
pros_detail.explanation: The SLD tool generates editable diagrams from your design, with templates for Australia, the US, the UK, Germany, Italy and Spain.

pros_detail.title: AI assistant (Ada)
pros_detail.explanation: OS 3.0, released in September 2025, added Ada, which takes chat or voice instructions to create projects and start auto designs.

pros_detail.title: Invoicing and payments
pros_detail.explanation: CashFlow lets you invoice and collect customer payments inside OpenSolar in the US, UK and Australia.

cons_detail.title: Integrations now cost money
cons_detail.explanation: Since April 2026, API Access is a per-project fee and OpenSolar-built connectors such as Xero and QuickBooks are a monthly subscription. Amounts are shown in the app, not on the public site.

cons_detail.title: Partner placement is not neutral
cons_detail.explanation: OpenSolar is paid by the lenders, distributors and manufacturers on the platform. Check that the defaults match the products and loans you actually want to sell.

cons_detail.title: Wallet dependency for API users
cons_detail.explanation: Paid items come out of a prepaid OpenSolar Wallet. OpenSolar's help center says that with API Access on, new projects are not created if the Wallet is not set up or is short of funds.

cons_detail.title: Country-dependent features
cons_detail.explanation: SLD templates cover six countries, CashFlow runs in the US, UK and Australia, and imagery providers and connectors vary by region. Confirm what is live in your market.

cons_detail.title: No advertised stamp service
cons_detail.explanation: OpenSolar's SLD page does not mention wire sizing or engineering stamps, so plan how you will get stamped permit packages if your jurisdictions require them.

tools.implementation_notes: Create a free account and set up your company profile, equipment and pricing first, since proposals pull from them. Turn on the lenders you actually offer in Integrated Finance, and review the partner products shown in the Shop so the defaults match what you install. Build a few test designs on free imagery and buy premium imagery only for the jobs that need it. If you need to connect OpenSolar to a CRM, accounting or reporting tool, check the in-app price for API Access or connectors in your region, set up and fund the OpenSolar Wallet, and use the 30-day API trial to test the connection before billing starts. Check that your country has SLD templates and CashFlow before relying on them.

tool_faqs.q: Is OpenSolar really free?
tool_faqs.a: The core design, sales and project management platform is free to use, with no licence fee. OpenSolar is paid by its hardware, finance and service partners. Since 16 April 2026, API Access (per project) and OpenSolar-built connectors (monthly) cost extra, and premium imagery is bought per image.

tool_faqs.q: What is the catch?
tool_faqs.a: Partners pay to be on the platform, so the lenders and products surfaced in the software are OpenSolar's paying partners. If you connect OpenSolar to other systems, expect usage fees paid from a prepaid Wallet.

tool_faqs.q: Where is OpenSolar based and who owns it?
tool_faqs.a: OpenSolar was founded in 2017 by Adam Pryor and Andrew Birch and is headquartered in Sydney, Australia. It is privately held and raised US$20 million in equity in October 2025.

tool_faqs.q: Can OpenSolar make single-line diagrams?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Its Single Line Diagrams tool generates editable diagrams from your design, with templates for Australia, the US, the UK, Germany, Italy and Spain. The SLD page does not mention wire sizing or engineering stamps.

tool_faqs.q: Does OpenSolar connect to QuickBooks or Xero?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, through OpenSolar-built accounting connectors billed as a monthly subscription per organization. OpenSolar says they may be available only in certain regions, so check availability and price in the app.

tools.name: Enerflo
tools.tagline: Residential solar operations software linking sales, design, financing, contracts and install tracking

pricing.pricing_note: No public prices. Enerflo charges a flat-rate monthly subscription based on your average monthly volume, with no per-seat, per-design, per-proposal, per-contract or per-job fees, and offers tiered pricing and volume discounts for high-volume companies. A one-time implementation fee applies, and new partners sign a 12-month minimum contract. Monthly fees include onboarding, training and dedicated account support; core integrations are included, while custom API development and some advanced features may cost extra. Book a discovery call for a quote. Verified against enerflo.com/about/faq 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: US residential solar dealers, installers, EPCs and vertically integrated companies that want one workflow from lead to installation on flat, volume-based pricing
tools.weaknesses: No public prices (discovery call required); 12-month minimum contract plus a one-time implementation fee; US residential and light commercial solar only; value depends on how well your design, lending and CRM tools are connected
tools.long_description:
Enerflo is operations software for residential solar companies. It calls itself 'The Operating System For Residential Solar' and connects sales, design, financing, contracts and installation tracking in one workflow. It was founded in 2019 by a solar salesperson and a software developer, works as a distributed company with an office address in Huntington Beach, California, and sells to US-based residential solar companies in all 50 states. Enerflo says more than $16 billion in solar transactions have run through the platform.

It is built for the way residential solar is sold: sales dealers, installers, EPCs, hybrid companies and vertically integrated providers. Sales Core runs the sales process, Virtual Sales Rep captures and qualifies leads from your website, Docflo handles solar contract signing, and Lendflo connects deals to lenders. After the sale, the Install Tracker follows each project through installation (or you keep your existing CRM), a white-labeled customer portal shows homeowners their project status, and reporting is powered by Domo.

Enerflo does not force you to replace your other tools. It lists more than 150 integrations, including Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive and Zoho for CRM; Aurora, OpenSolar, Aerialytic, Scanifly, Solargraf and Solo for design; and GoodLeap, Sungage Financial, Sunlight, Dividend, EnFin and LightReach for financing. Design can run through its deep Aerialytic integration or the design tool you already use.

Pricing is a flat monthly subscription based on your average monthly volume, not per seat, design, proposal, contract or job. There is a one-time implementation fee, a 12-month minimum contract for new partners, and volume discounts at high volume. Prices are not published; you book a discovery call. Support runs Monday to Saturday, 6am to 7pm Pacific time.

The trade-off: Enerflo sits on top of your other software, so the value depends on how well your design, lending and CRM tools are connected and configured. It serves residential and light commercial solar in the US only, and the 12-month minimum and implementation fee make it a bigger commitment than a self-serve proposal tool.

pros_detail.title: One workflow from lead to install
pros_detail.explanation: Sales Core, Docflo contracts, Lendflo financing, the Install Tracker and a customer portal share the same deal record, so fewer details get retyped between sales and operations.

pros_detail.title: No per-seat fees
pros_detail.explanation: Enerflo prices on your average monthly volume, with no per-seat, per-design, per-proposal, per-contract or per-job fees, so adding reps does not add seat costs.

pros_detail.title: Keeps your existing tools
pros_detail.explanation: Enerflo lists more than 150 integrations, including Salesforce, HubSpot, Aurora, OpenSolar, Scanifly and major solar lenders, and core integrations are included in the subscription.

pros_detail.title: Built for dealer and EPC setups
pros_detail.explanation: Enerflo is aimed at sales dealers, installers, EPCs, hybrid and vertically integrated companies, so dealer and installer handoffs are part of the design rather than an add-on.

pros_detail.title: Onboarding and support included
pros_detail.explanation: Monthly fees include onboarding, training and dedicated account support, and the support team works Monday to Saturday, 6am to 7pm Pacific time.

cons_detail.title: Pricing not public
cons_detail.explanation: You need a discovery call to get a price, so you cannot compare cost up front.

cons_detail.title: Contract and setup commitment
cons_detail.explanation: New partners sign a 12-month minimum contract and pay a one-time implementation fee. Custom API work and some advanced features can cost extra.

cons_detail.title: US residential solar only
cons_detail.explanation: Enerflo serves US residential and light commercial solar companies. Commercial-only solar firms and other trades are outside its scope.

cons_detail.title: Depends on your tool stack
cons_detail.explanation: Because Enerflo connects other tools rather than replacing all of them, a poorly connected design, lending or CRM setup limits what you get from it.

cons_detail.title: More than a small shop needs
cons_detail.explanation: A one or two rep installer may get what it needs from a proposal tool such as OpenSolar or Solo and add an operations platform later.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with a discovery call and get the quote's volume assumptions, implementation fee and included integrations in writing, since new partners sign a 12-month minimum. Map your real process from lead to installation before setup, including dealer and sub-dealer structures. Enerflo configures your instance during implementation; your team connects the design tool (Enerflo's Aerialytic integration or your current Aurora, OpenSolar, Scanifly, Solargraf or Solo account), your lenders and your CRM, then sets up Sales Core, Docflo contract templates and Install Tracker stages. Train sales reps and operations staff separately, since they use different parts of the platform, and use the included onboarding and account support. Enerflo's developer documentation is at docs.enerflo.io if you need custom integrations.

tool_faqs.q: What is Enerflo?
tool_faqs.a: Enerflo is operations software for US residential solar companies. It connects sales (Sales Core and Virtual Sales Rep), design integrations, financing (Lendflo), contracts (Docflo), installation tracking and a customer portal in one workflow.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Enerflo cost?
tool_faqs.a: Enerflo does not publish prices. It charges a flat monthly subscription based on your average monthly volume, with no per-seat, per-design, per-proposal, per-contract or per-job fees. A one-time implementation fee applies, new partners sign a 12-month minimum contract, and volume discounts are offered at high volume. Book a discovery call for a quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does Enerflo replace my design tool and CRM?
tool_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Enerflo integrates with design tools such as Aurora, OpenSolar, Scanifly, Solargraf and Solo (or uses its Aerialytic integration) and with CRMs such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive and Zoho. You can use its Install Tracker or keep your existing CRM for project management.

tool_faqs.q: Enerflo vs Aurora Solar: are they competitors?
tool_faqs.a: Mostly they work together. Aurora is design and proposal software; Enerflo is an operations layer that can pull in Aurora designs and run financing, contracts and installation tracking around them. Enerflo lists Aurora as a design integration.

tool_faqs.q: Who can use Enerflo?
tool_faqs.a: US-based residential solar companies in all 50 states: sales dealers, installers, EPCs, hybrid and vertically integrated providers. Enerflo says it serves residential and light commercial solar, and commercial-only companies are outside its scope.

tools.name: Solo
tools.tagline: In-home sales and proposal software for solar, roofing, HVAC and generator installers

pricing.pricing_note: No public prices. Solo's pricing page offers flexible plans based on usage, support level and scale, and every plan includes unlimited users, a concierge onboarding program and support. Solo describes its model as one price depending on what you use; concierge design is pay for what you use. Book a demo for a quote. Verified against gosolo.io/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential solar sales teams, and roofing, HVAC and generator installers selling in the home, that want fast proposals with built-in financing and the option to have Solo's team do the design
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (demo required) and cost tied to usage; its pages do not advertise permit plan sets or engineering stamps; Roofing Studio only launched in July 2026
tools.long_description:
Solo is in-home sales and proposal software for home improvement companies, starting with residential solar. It is run by Speed of Light Ops, LLC, doing business as Solo, and is based in Lehi, Utah. Solo says more than 6 million proposals have been built on the platform and more than 1 million installations have come from them. It now sells separate Studios for solar, roofing (launched July 2026), HVAC and generators.

For solar, reps can design and present in the same sitting. Solo Studio detects rooflines and obstructions with AI, adds setbacks, models shading and performance, suggests panel layouts, and checks the design against lender and code requirements. Solar Studio turns that into a branded, interactive proposal with multiple lender options built in. If you do not want to design in-house, Solo Concierge has Solo's team build the design and proposal; Solo says a complete, install-ready proposal arrives in minutes.

Solo leans on production accuracy. It says its production estimates carry '99.9% certified accuracy verified across 1,400+ homes', publishes a DNV report comparing its engine with the real output of installed systems, and says its internal design check typically cuts change orders by 15%. Solo lists more than 70 integrations, including Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, JobNimbus, Enerflo and DocuSign, and lenders such as GoodLeap, Mosaic, Sungage, Dividend, Sunlight Financial and LightReach.

Prices are not published. Solo's pricing page offers plans based on usage, support level and scale; every plan includes unlimited users, concierge onboarding and support, and you book a demo for a quote. Support runs Monday to Friday 8am to 8pm and Saturday 8am to 4pm Mountain time (Saturday for Professional Support only).

The trade-off: without published prices, you cannot compare Solo's cost until you get a quote, and usage-based pricing means cost moves with your proposal volume. Solo is built around the homeowner sale; its pages do not advertise permit plan sets or engineering stamps, so plan that work separately.

pros_detail.title: Design done for you if you want it
pros_detail.explanation: Solo Concierge has Solo's team build the design and proposal, and Solo says an install-ready proposal arrives in minutes. Teams that want control can design in Solo Studio and use Solo's design service for overflow.

pros_detail.title: Accuracy backed by a published report
pros_detail.explanation: Solo says its production estimates carry '99.9% certified accuracy verified across 1,400+ homes' and publishes a DNV report comparing its engine with the real output of installed systems.

pros_detail.title: Built for the kitchen-table sale
pros_detail.explanation: Reps can go from conversation to a ready-to-present proposal without leaving the in-home presentation, with multiple lender options and e-signature in the same flow.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Solo's pricing page says every plan includes unlimited users, concierge onboarding and support, so adding reps does not add seat costs.

pros_detail.title: Broad integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Solo lists more than 70 integrations, including Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, JobNimbus, Enerflo, DocuSign and lenders such as GoodLeap, Mosaic, Sungage and LightReach.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Solo quotes plans based on usage, support level and scale, so you cannot compare cost without booking a demo.

cons_detail.title: Usage-linked cost
cons_detail.explanation: Solo describes its pricing as one price depending on what you use, so spend rises with proposal volume. Get the quote's volume assumptions in writing so you can budget.

cons_detail.title: No advertised permit package
cons_detail.explanation: Solo focuses on the sale. Its pages do not advertise permit plan sets or engineering stamps, so you still need a way to produce permit-ready drawings.

cons_detail.title: Non-solar track record is shorter
cons_detail.explanation: Solo's proof points (proposal counts, accuracy report, installations) come from solar. Roofing Studio launched in July 2026, so non-solar buyers should ask for references in their own trade.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and get the plan terms in writing: what usage is included, the support level, and how cost changes with your proposal volume. Solo includes a concierge onboarding program on every plan. Set up your equipment, pricing, adders, lenders and proposal branding first, since every design and proposal pulls from them. Decide whether reps will design in Solo Studio, send jobs to Solo Concierge, or mix the two. Connect your CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, JobNimbus and others are supported) and, if you use it, Enerflo, so deal data flows without retyping. Train reps on presenting and editing proposals in the home, and plan permit drawings separately.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Solo cost?
tool_faqs.a: Solo does not publish prices. Its pricing page offers flexible plans based on usage, support level and scale, and every plan includes unlimited users, a concierge onboarding program and support. Book a demo for a quote and ask how the price changes with your proposal volume.

tool_faqs.q: What is Solo Concierge?
tool_faqs.a: It is Solo's done-for-you design service. Solo's team builds the design and proposal, and Solo says a complete, install-ready proposal arrives in minutes. You pay for what you use. Teams that prefer to design in-house can use Solo Studio and send overflow to Solo's design team.

tool_faqs.q: Is Solo only for solar?
tool_faqs.a: No longer. Solo started in residential solar and now also sells Roofing Studio (launched July 2026), HVAC Studio and Generator Studio for in-home sales.

tool_faqs.q: Solo vs Aurora Solar?
tool_faqs.a: Aurora publishes per-user plans and sells design software plus paid services such as permit plan sets. Solo does not publish prices, includes unlimited users, and offers a done-for-you design service. Teams that do not want to staff designers often look at Solo; teams that want to own design and need plan sets from the same vendor often look at Aurora.

tool_faqs.q: Does Solo produce permit plan sets?
tool_faqs.a: Solo's pages do not advertise permit plan sets or engineering stamps. Solo Studio checks designs against lender and code requirements, but plan how you will produce permit-ready drawings before you rely on Solo alone.

tools.name: SmartMoving
tools.affiliate_note: Referral program, not an affiliate program: WrenchStack may earn a referral reward from SmartMoving when a company referred through this link becomes a SmartMoving customer.
tools.tagline: Moving company software for sales, estimating, dispatch, crews, storage and payments

pricing.pricing_note: No public prices. SmartMoving's pricing page lists one Growth plan with no price and offers monthly, quarterly or annual terms; add-ons listed without prices include the SM-100 Managed Tariff and the Pre-Move Survey App. SmartMoving's July 2025 launch announcement priced the Smart Insights analytics add-on at $199 a month, and its Smart Scout AI sales agent page offers 30 days free. No free trial of the core platform is published. Verified against smartmoving.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Moving companies, including multi-location and franchise operators, that want sales, estimating, dispatch, crew, storage and payments in one system and are willing to go through a quote
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing, so you need a demo and a quote to learn your cost. Some tools, such as Smart Insights analytics, are paid add-ons. Built only for moving and storage companies.
tools.long_description:
SmartMoving is software built for moving companies. Tobe Thompson founded it in Dallas in 2018, and it is still based there with Thompson as CEO. In 2022 it took a $41.5 million investment from the growth equity firm Mainsail Partners, and in January 2026 it announced that it had acquired Remedy Payments, the payment processor that already handled payments for most SmartMoving customers. SmartMoving says thousands of movers use it.

The platform follows a move from first call to final invoice: sales automation with lead routing and automated follow-ups, estimates built from custom pricing periods and rate tables, dispatch and crew management, a crew app for iOS and Android that collects signatures, photos and payments on the job, storage management, payroll, accounting and payments, more than 40 pre-built reports, and online reputation tools. It handles local, intrastate and interstate moves in the US and Canada, and it supports multiple locations, brands and franchises with separate pricing, payments and documents for each.

Integrations listed in its help center include QuickBooks Online, Mailchimp, RingCentral, LiveSwitch (virtual surveys and AI inventory), Remedy Payments, Wisetack financing and an open API. Newer add-ons include Smart Insights, an analytics dashboard SmartMoving launched in July 2025 at $199 a month, and Smart Scout, an AI sales agent that SmartMoving says answers inbound calls 24/7, creates leads and gives estimates during the call.

The trade-off: SmartMoving does not publish prices. Its pricing page shows one Growth plan with no price, offered on monthly, quarterly or annual terms, so you cannot compare costs without a demo. It is also built only for moving and storage companies, so it is not an option for other trades.

MoveitPro is moving company software from Longwood, Florida. Founder and CEO Jason Bergenske took over his family's moving and storage business, could not find software that fit, and began building his own in 2011. He funded development from the moving business rather than with outside investors. The company says it has served the moving industry for more than 15 years.

The current product is MoveitPro+, which the company calls the next generation of its software, and the founder's site says it was completely rebuilt from the ground up. It manages leads, estimates, dispatch, calls, analytics and automation in one platform. MoveitPro's site also has pages for electronic bills of lading and claims management, a migration hub for companies switching from other software, and the Pro App for crews, which includes GPS tracking and offline mode.

Pricing is by quote. MoveitPro's pricing page says MoveitPro+ starts with a flat monthly per-user fee but does not publish the amount. Advanced features such as AI calling and texting use prepaid tokens, sold in packs from 5,000 to 250,000 tokens, with larger packs discounted by up to 50%. The Pro App costs $20 per crew user per month and is free for office users.

The trade-off: you cannot compare MoveitPro+ on price without a demo, and AI usage adds a variable cost on top of the per-user fee. MoveitPro+ is also a rebuild, so ask how long the new version has been in production and how your data moves over from the classic MoveitPro or another system. Like the rest of this category, it is built only for moving and storage companies.

tools.long_description:
Supermove is software for moving and storage companies, based in San Francisco. It was founded by Wonjun Jeong, who previously worked at Pinterest and Facebook, and a co-founder; the company says both are engineers who started by working with a local mover in California. Supermove is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Founders Fund. It says it serves thousands of movers across the US and Canada, and its customer testimonials range from companies with 1-3 trucks to fleets of 10-15 trucks.

The product is a set of four apps. The Office App handles leads, CRM, scheduling, dispatch and customer communication. The Crew App gives crews digital bills of lading, payment collection, GPS tracking, crew photos and a timesheet calculator. The Estimator App runs virtual surveys with automatic calculations and e-signatures, and the Storage App manages stored inventory and storage billing.

Supermove's AI tools include the AI Sales Copilot, which shows live checklists and objection-handling scripts during calls, records and transcribes calls, scores them and drafts follow-ups. Supermove also describes AI voice agents that answer inbound calls 24/7 and automated outbound calling. The Sales Copilot integrates with Twilio, Dialpad and RingCentral phone systems, and Supermove lists QuickBooks Online, CallRail and a custom API among its integrations. In its 2024 review, Supermove said it shipped more than 200 software updates that year, including a Zillow integration and an improved QuickBooks integration.

The trade-off: Supermove does not publish prices, so you need a demo and a quote before you can compare it with other moving software. It is built only for moving and storage companies. Its site cites large revenue and closing-rate gains from customer stories, so ask for references from movers your size before you rely on them.

tools.long_description:
Elromco is cloud software for moving companies, based in Canton, Massachusetts. The company says it was founded in 2015 by people from the moving industry and that more than 400 moving companies across the United States use it, from small local movers to large interstate carriers.

It covers the whole job. Sales tools include a CRM with lead scoring, a pricing engine for hourly, flat-rate and long-distance moves (with seasonal rate tiers and fuel surcharges), and embeddable online quote forms that show customers a real price on the spot. Customers can then use a branded client portal to update their inventory, sign, pay a deposit and book online. On the operations side there is a drag-and-drop dispatch board, a job tracker, electronic bills of lading, a mobile web crew portal with navigation and inventory checklists, storage management, automatic invoicing, and crew payroll with commissions and tip splitting. Elromco AI adjusts message tone, translates for customers and drafts replies, and AI Inventory builds an inventory from photos.

Elromco publishes its prices. Professional is $289 a month with 3 office users and unlimited crew members, and Enterprise is $399 a month with unlimited office users, multi-branch management, API access and a dedicated account manager; extra branches are $99 a month each. Billing is month-to-month with no setup fees, and onboarding, training, data migration and support by phone, email and live chat are included. Integrations include QuickBooks, QuickBooks Payroll, ADP, Gusto, Google Calendar and RingCentral.

The trade-off: the 3-user cap on Professional means a growing office moves to Enterprise, and multi-branch management is only on Enterprise. Support hours are not published, and the crew portal runs in the phone's browser rather than as a native app. Like every tool in this category, it is built only for moving companies.

tool_faqs.a: Small and mid-size moving companies that want published prices and one system for instant online quotes, booking, dispatch, eBOL, storage and crew payroll. Companies with several branches need the Enterprise plan.

tools.long_description:
Encircle is field documentation software for restoration contractors. Crews use its mobile app (iOS and Android) to capture photos, videos, 360-degree images, notes, moisture readings, drying logs, moisture maps and contents inventories on a loss, and Encircle organizes that into carrier-ready reports. The company was founded in 2012 in Kitchener, Ontario, where its office is still based, and it says more than 3,000 restoration businesses use it. In November 2025 it acquired The Edge, a rough order of magnitude (ROM) estimating tool, which is now sold as the Encircle Edge add-on.

Beyond documentation, Encircle sells Scope to Estimate, which uses the field data to draft an IICRC-aligned scope and a first-draft Xactimate estimate priced to your own Xactimate price list, then exports it to Xactimate. Encircle Floor Plan scans produce 2D floor plans that import into Xactimate to create the property sketch. Encircle says the app works fully offline and syncs in real time, and office tools include custom forms, e-signatures and payments processed through Stripe.

Pricing is per company, based on how many jobs you run a year, with unlimited users (including sharing) and storage on every plan. Field Documentation is $285 a month billed monthly for up to 200 jobs a year, on a 12-month term; paying annually gets one month of Field Documentation free. Scope to Estimate is added on top and lists at $350, $590 or $845 a month for the up-to-200, 201-400 and 401-600 job bands. Field Documentation prices for the 201-400 and 401-600 bands are shown in the pricing page's job selector, and above 600 jobs a year the price is a custom quote. Every plan includes onboarding, a dedicated account manager and help desk access, and the 14-day free trial needs no credit card.

Encircle's integration page lists restoration job-management systems (Albi, PSA, iRestore, Xcelerate and JobDox), Verisk and VCA under claims management, Tramex moisture meters, Ricoh and Insta360 cameras, and equipment trackers from Kahi, Phoenix and Nero. Zapier and an open API cover other systems.

The trade-off: Encircle covers the field and estimating front end of a job, not scheduling, job costing or accounting, so most restoration companies run it next to a job-management platform. Check that your job-management system is on its integration list, and model the job-volume pricing against your annual job count, since the price steps up by band.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users and storage
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes unlimited users (including sharing) and storage, so the whole crew can document jobs without per-seat fees.

pros_detail.title: Built around restoration documentation
pros_detail.explanation: Photos, video, 360-degree images, moisture readings, drying logs, moisture maps and contents inventories are organized by job and turned into carrier-ready reports.

pros_detail.title: Path to an Xactimate estimate
pros_detail.explanation: Scope to Estimate drafts a scope and a first-draft Xactimate estimate from the field data and exports it to Xactimate, and Floor Plan scans import into Xactimate as the property sketch.

pros_detail.title: Works offline
pros_detail.explanation: Encircle says the app works fully offline and syncs in real time, which helps on sites with poor signal.

pros_detail.title: Broad integration list
pros_detail.explanation: Integrations cover job-management systems (Albi, PSA, iRestore, Xcelerate, JobDox), moisture meters, 360 cameras, equipment trackers, Zapier and an open API.

pros_detail.title: Onboarding and trial included
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes onboarding, a dedicated account manager and help desk access, and the 14-day free trial needs no credit card.

cons_detail.title: Not a job-management system
cons_detail.explanation: Encircle does not run scheduling, job costing or accounting. Most restoration companies pair it with a separate job-management platform, so budget for both tools.

cons_detail.title: Price steps up with job volume
cons_detail.explanation: Pricing is by jobs per year, so a busy shop moves into a higher band. Only the up-to-200-jobs price ($285 a month) is shown outright; higher bands appear in the pricing page's job selector, and 600+ jobs a year is a custom quote.

cons_detail.title: 12-month term
cons_detail.explanation: Plans run on a 12-month term, billed monthly or annually. Plan changes are handled with your account manager before renewal.

cons_detail.title: Add-ons cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Scope to Estimate ($350 to $845 a month by band), Floor Plan, AI Item Descriptions and Encircle Edge are paid add-ons, so the full stack costs well above the base Field Documentation price.

cons_detail.title: Restoration only
cons_detail.explanation: Encircle is built for restoration and insurance claim documentation, not general field service work.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with the 14-day trial on real jobs to confirm the capture flow suits your crews. Before signing, count your jobs from the last year to pick the right band, and decide whether you need Scope to Estimate, Floor Plan or Encircle Edge. Set up custom forms and report templates to match what your carriers and program partners ask for, then train field techs on the mobile capture flow: photos, moisture readings, drying logs and contents. If you run a job-management system such as Albi or PSA, connect it early so jobs and documentation flow between the two, and enable the Xactimate integration if your estimators work in Xactimate. Because users are unlimited, add everyone who documents jobs.

tool_faqs.q: What does Encircle do?
tool_faqs.a: Encircle is field documentation software for restoration. Crews capture photos, video, 360-degree images, moisture readings, drying logs, moisture maps and contents inventories on a phone or tablet, and Encircle turns that into carrier-ready reports. It also sells Scope to Estimate for drafting Xactimate estimates. It is not a full job-management or accounting system.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Encircle cost?
tool_faqs.a: Field Documentation is $285 a month billed monthly for up to 200 jobs a year, on a 12-month term, and paying annually gets one month free. Scope to Estimate is an add-on at $350, $590 or $845 a month depending on your job band. Higher job bands cost more, and 600+ jobs a year is a custom quote. Every plan includes unlimited users and storage, onboarding and a dedicated account manager.

tool_faqs.q: Does Encircle work with Xactimate?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Encircle Floor Plan scans import into Xactimate to create the property sketch, and Scope to Estimate exports a first-draft estimate, priced to your Xactimate price list, into Xactimate.

tool_faqs.q: Do I still need job-management software if I use Encircle?
