tool_faqs.a: Usually. Encircle handles documentation and scoping, not scheduling, job costing or accounting. Its integration list includes job-management systems such as Albi, PSA, iRestore, Xcelerate and JobDox.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Encircle offers a 14-day trial on real jobs with no credit card. It includes all features, including Scope to Estimate, and 5 free Floor Plans.

tools.name: Albi
tools.tagline: Restoration job-management software with CRM, field documentation and built-in call tracking

pricing.pricing_note: Per seat per month: Base $60 (field techs) and Pro $100 (office staff). Albi has a $6,000 minimum annual subscription, which any mix of seats can meet. The Small Business package includes 4 seats (2 Base, 2 Pro), 10 automation workflows and Albi Pay, with optional personalized onboarding at $1,000 one-time. White Glove onboarding is $2,500 one-time and Enterprise onboarding $4,500. Analytics and Automations packages start at $250/mo each. Midsize and Enterprise pricing on request. No free trial or contract length published. Verified against albiware.com/albi-pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Restoration and insurance-repair contractors that want CRM, job management, field documentation, drying logs and invoicing in one platform, and can meet a $6,000 minimum annual subscription
tools.weaknesses: $6,000 minimum annual subscription; office features such as calling, invoicing and estimates need the $100 Pro seat; onboarding and the Analytics and Automations packages cost extra; younger company (founded 2020); built for restoration only
tools.long_description:
Albi, made by Albiware, is job-management software for restoration and insurance damage repair contractors. It was founded in 2020 by Alex Duta, who grew his family's Chicago-based restoration business, and software developer Shamoil Soni. Albiware went through Y Combinator (Summer 2022 batch) and raised a $2.8 million seed round in September 2022. Its privacy policy gives a mailing address in Oak Brook, Illinois.

Albi covers the office and the field in one system: CRM, job management, a mobile scheduler, photo and field documentation, moisture mapping and drying logs (Albi Drylog 2.0), equipment scanning, a time clock, e-signatures, floor plans (Albi Capture), call tracking and recording, and payments through Albi Pay. Seats come in two types. The Base seat ($60 a month) is meant for field technicians and covers projects, tasks, notes, field documentation, the time clock and the schedule. The Pro seat ($100 a month) is meant for office staff and adds professional reports, project forms, email, calling with call recording, price lists, business reports, work and purchase orders, invoicing, estimates and inventory expensing.

Albi has a $6,000 minimum annual subscription, which can be met with any mix of seat types. The Small Business package includes 4 seats (2 Base, 2 Pro), 10 automation workflows and access to Albi Pay, with optional personalized onboarding for $1,000 one-time. Larger companies can choose White Glove onboarding ($2,500 one-time, covering setup and data migration) or Enterprise onboarding ($4,500, adding two days of in-person training). The Analytics and Automations packages start at $250 a month each, and Midsize and Enterprise pricing is on request. All plans include unlimited storage and projects and a dedicated account manager.

Albi's help center lists integrations with Xactimate (Albi creates Xactimate project shells, pulls completed estimates into Albi and can push floor plans to Xactimate), XactAnalysis, QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, CompanyCam, Encircle, EagleView, Clean Claims, Kahi and Zapier. Albi says its support has a 7-minute response time and a 24-hour average resolution time.

The trade-off: the $6,000 yearly minimum works out to at least $500 a month on average, even for a shop with few seats, and office users need the $100 Pro seat. Albi is also younger than long-running restoration platforms such as DASH and PSA, so ask about term length and renewal terms before you sign.

pros_detail.title: One system for office and field
pros_detail.explanation: CRM, job management, scheduling, field documentation, moisture mapping, drying logs, equipment scanning, invoicing and payments sit in one platform, so a restoration company does not have to stitch several tools together.

pros_detail.title: Seat types matched to roles
pros_detail.explanation: Field techs can use the $60 Base seat and office staff the $100 Pro seat, so you pay the higher rate only for users who need calling, invoicing and estimates.

pros_detail.title: Built-in calling and call recording
pros_detail.explanation: Pro seats include calling with call recording, and Albi lists call tracking among its features, so the office can handle customer calls inside the same system.

pros_detail.title: Restoration integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Albi connects to Xactimate, XactAnalysis, QuickBooks Online and Desktop, CompanyCam, Encircle and EagleView, plus Zapier for other apps.

pros_detail.title: Stated support speed
pros_detail.explanation: Albi says its support has a 7-minute response time and a 24-hour average resolution time, and every plan includes a dedicated account manager.

cons_detail.title: $6,000 minimum annual subscription
cons_detail.explanation: The yearly minimum works out to at least $500 a month on average, so a very small shop pays for more than a few seats would cost on their own.

cons_detail.title: Office features need Pro seats
cons_detail.explanation: Calling, invoicing, estimates, work and purchase orders and business reports are Pro seat features at $100 a month per seat.

cons_detail.title: Onboarding and packages cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Onboarding is $1,000, $2,500 or $4,500 one-time depending on the option, and the Analytics and Automations packages start at $250 a month each.

cons_detail.title: Younger company
cons_detail.explanation: Albi was founded in 2020, so it has a shorter track record than older restoration platforms such as DASH and PSA.

cons_detail.title: Restoration only
cons_detail.explanation: Albi is built for restoration and insurance damage repair contractors and is not a fit for other trades.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and ask for a quote that shows how your seat mix meets the $6,000 annual minimum, along with term and renewal details. Decide which staff need Pro seats (anyone who calls customers, invoices or writes estimates) and which field techs can use Base seats. Choose an onboarding option: personalized onboarding ($1,000) for small businesses, White Glove ($2,500) if you want Albi to handle setup and data migration, or Enterprise ($4,500) for in-person training. Connect Xactimate, XactAnalysis and QuickBooks (Online or Desktop) early, and set whether new projects create Xactimate project shells automatically or at a chosen status. Then train field techs on the mobile app for photos, moisture mapping, drying logs and equipment scanning.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Albi cost?
tool_faqs.a: Albi charges per seat: $60 a month for a Base seat (field techs) and $100 a month for a Pro seat (office staff). There is a $6,000 minimum annual subscription, which any mix of seats can meet. Onboarding is extra ($1,000, $2,500 or $4,500 one-time), and the Analytics and Automations packages start at $250 a month each.

tool_faqs.q: Does Albi require a contract?
tool_faqs.a: Albi's pricing page sets a $6,000 minimum annual subscription. It does not publish cancellation or renewal terms, so ask about them in your quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does Albi integrate with Xactimate?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Albi can create Xactimate project shells automatically or manually and pull completed estimates into Albi, and it can push floor plans to Xactimate. It does not push estimates from Albi into Xactimate. It also integrates with XactAnalysis.

tool_faqs.q: Does Albi work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Albi's help center covers integrations with both QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Albi?
tool_faqs.a: Albiware, founded in 2020 by Alex Duta and Shamoil Soni. The company went through Y Combinator's Summer 2022 batch, raised a $2.8 million seed round in September 2022 and lists a mailing address in Oak Brook, Illinois.

tools.name: DASH
tools.tagline: Restoration job-management platform from Cotality (formerly CoreLogic), originally built by Next Gear Solutions

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing. The DASH product page on cotality.com shows no prices, and cotality.com and nextgearsolutions.com offer demo requests and a sales line only. DASH was built by Next Gear Solutions and is now a Cotality (formerly CoreLogic) product. Verified against cotality.com/products/dash and nextgearsolutions.com 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Established restoration contractors that want a configurable, workflow-driven job-management system with equipment tracking, mobile apps, XactAnalysis notes sync and QuickBooks Online sync, and are fine with quote-only pricing
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (demo and quote only); Xactimate estimate import is not described on the current DASH pages; moisture mapping is not listed on the current DASH pages; Cotality sells several related restoration products, so the scope of a quote needs checking; restoration only
tools.long_description:
DASH is job-management software for restoration contractors. It was built by Next Gear Solutions, which formed in 2008 in Oxford, Mississippi, and which later bought ClientRunner, Luxor CRM, MICA Software and Moisture Mapper. CoreLogic completed its acquisition of Next Gear in September 2021, and CoreLogic rebranded as Cotality in March 2025. DASH is still sold under the Cotality name, through cotality.com and nextgearsolutions.com.

Cotality describes DASH as a platform that runs restoration jobs from the field to the office: centralized job records with real-time tracking, a customizable workflow builder with automated tasks, reminders and approval notifications, photo and video documentation with automatic time stamps, budget tracking and compliance management. A calendar handles task scheduling, DASH Timesheets tracks work hours and labor costs, and equipment tracking is built in, with DASH Inventory in the MICA Mobile app scanning barcodes in the field. Property details can be filled in from Cotality property data, and image analytics can tag damage types in photos. DASH has iOS and Android apps and holds a SOC 2 Type II certification.

On integrations, DASH offers two-way sync with QuickBooks Online, and its release notes say historical notes from Claims Connect and XactAnalysis sync into DASH automatically. It can also link DocuSketch 3D documentation. Next Gear announced an integration linking DASH to Xactimate and XactAnalysis in 2014, but the current DASH pages do not describe an Xactimate estimate import, so confirm how estimates reach DASH during a demo.

Neither Cotality nor Next Gear publishes DASH pricing; both sites route buyers to a demo. The Next Gear site also lists related Cotality restoration products, including a CRM, MICA, Mitigate, Engage and BI Reporting, so ask which of them a quote includes.

The trade-off: DASH is a configurable, established system backed by a large property data company, which suits restoration operations with defined processes. You cannot see a price before a sales call, and some capabilities, such as moisture mapping or an Xactimate estimate import, are not described on the current DASH pages. Ask for a quote and a demo that covers your full workflow.

pros_detail.title: Configurable workflows
pros_detail.explanation: DASH includes a customizable workflow builder with automated tasks, reminders and approval notifications, so you can model your own job process.

pros_detail.title: Equipment tracking
pros_detail.explanation: Equipment tracking is built in, and DASH Inventory in the MICA Mobile app scans barcodes to manage equipment from the field.

pros_detail.title: Claims notes flow in
pros_detail.explanation: Historical notes from XactAnalysis and Claims Connect sync into DASH automatically, so job history from the carrier side sits in one place.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online sync
pros_detail.explanation: Two-way sync with QuickBooks Online connects job data to your books.

pros_detail.title: Mobile apps and property data
pros_detail.explanation: iOS and Android apps cover field work, property details can be auto-filled from Cotality data, and image analytics can tag damage types in photos.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Cotality and Next Gear publish no DASH prices. You need a demo and a quote to learn the cost.

cons_detail.title: Xactimate link not documented today
cons_detail.explanation: Next Gear announced a DASH integration with Xactimate in 2014, but the current DASH pages describe only XactAnalysis notes sync. Confirm how Xactimate estimates reach DASH before you buy.

cons_detail.title: Owned by a large data company
cons_detail.explanation: DASH has belonged to CoreLogic, now Cotality, since 2021. Roadmap and support decisions sit with Cotality, so ask about both in your evaluation.

cons_detail.title: Related tools sold separately
cons_detail.explanation: Cotality lists several restoration products (DASH, CRM, MICA, Mitigate, Engage, BI Reporting). Check which ones your quote covers.

cons_detail.title: Restoration only
cons_detail.explanation: DASH is built for restoration contractors and is not a fit for other trades.

tools.implementation_notes: Request a demo through cotality.com or nextgearsolutions.com and ask for a written quote that lists which Cotality products are included (DASH alone, or with MICA, Mitigate, Engage or BI Reporting). Map your job stages before setup so they can be built in the workflow builder with automated tasks and approvals. Connect QuickBooks Online and your XactAnalysis account early, and confirm on the demo how Xactimate estimates reach DASH. Set up equipment records and barcode labels if you plan to use DASH Inventory in the MICA Mobile app, then roll out the iOS and Android apps to field crews. If you are moving from another system, plan the data migration with the vendor.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns DASH?
tool_faqs.a: DASH was built by Next Gear Solutions, formed in 2008 in Oxford, Mississippi. CoreLogic completed its acquisition of Next Gear in September 2021, and CoreLogic rebranded as Cotality in March 2025. DASH is now sold as a Cotality product.

tool_faqs.q: How much does DASH cost?
tool_faqs.a: Cotality does not publish DASH pricing. Both cotality.com and nextgearsolutions.com route buyers to a demo, so you need a quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does DASH integrate with Xactimate?
tool_faqs.a: Next Gear announced a DASH integration with Xactimate and XactAnalysis in 2014. Today's DASH release notes confirm that historical notes from XactAnalysis and Claims Connect sync into DASH, but the current pages do not describe an Xactimate estimate import. Confirm this on a demo.

tool_faqs.q: Does DASH track restoration equipment?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Equipment tracking is part of DASH, and DASH Inventory in the MICA Mobile app lets crews scan barcodes to manage equipment from the field.

tool_faqs.q: Does DASH work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Cotality lists two-way syncing with QuickBooks Online.

tools.name: Restoration Manager
tools.tagline: Restoration job-management software from Verisk, the company behind Xactimate

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing. Verisk says Restoration Manager is licensed per company with a guided rollout and routes buyers to a demo request. Training resources and paid add-on services are offered through Restoration Manager University. Part of Verisk's Xactware business since Verisk acquired Service Software in December 2017. Verified against xactware.com/home/products/restoration-manager.html 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Restoration contractors that work carrier and program jobs in Xactimate and XactAnalysis and want work orders, scheduling, equipment tracking and job financials tied to those estimates
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (licensed per company, quote only); built around the Verisk and Xactware ecosystem, so shops that rarely use Xactimate get less from it; integration updates need care; restoration only
tools.long_description:
Restoration Manager is job-management software for property restoration contractors. It was developed by Service Software, which Verisk (Nasdaq: VRSK) acquired in December 2017 and made part of Xactware, the Verisk business behind Xactimate and XactAnalysis. Support runs through a Verisk address (rmcares@verisk.com).

Verisk pitches it as a way to keep office, field and trade partners working as one team. Dashboards show performance, job progress, profit and loss and equipment summaries. Work orders are generated from Xactimate estimates imported into the system, scheduling updates and sends notifications when a task slips, and equipment is tracked by scanning with the ManageIT Mobile app. A customer portal shares job status, documents and photos with customers and trade partners, and reports come in standard and custom formats, exported as PDF or Excel.

Its integrations page lists two-way integrations with Xactimate, XactAnalysis, QuickBooks Desktop, QuickBooks Online and Sage 100 Contractor, plus a one-way integration with Sage 300 Construction (Timberline). Verisk also pairs it with XactRestore. Restoration Manager offers data migrations from DASH, PSA, ClientRunner, Salesforce and ACT.

Verisk does not publish a price. The product page says Restoration Manager is licensed per company with a guided rollout, and buyers request a demo. Training documents, recorded webinars and paid add-on services are available through Restoration Manager University.

The trade-off: Restoration Manager is most useful when your jobs start in XactAnalysis and get estimated in Xactimate; a shop that does little insurance work gets less from those links. Pricing is quote only, so get a written license quote before comparing it with per-seat tools.

pros_detail.title: Built on Xactimate estimates
pros_detail.explanation: Work orders are generated from imported Xactimate estimates, and two-way XactAnalysis integration brings in program assignments.

pros_detail.title: Accounting integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Two-way integrations with QuickBooks Desktop, QuickBooks Online and Sage 100 Contractor, plus a one-way link to Sage 300 Construction, cover the most common contractor accounting systems.

pros_detail.title: Dashboards and equipment tracking
pros_detail.explanation: Dashboards show job progress, profit and loss and equipment summaries, and crews track equipment by scanning with the ManageIT Mobile app.

pros_detail.title: Customer and trade partner portal
pros_detail.explanation: A portal shares job status, documents and photos with customers and trade partners.

pros_detail.title: Migration paths from other systems
pros_detail.explanation: Restoration Manager lists data migrations from DASH, PSA, ClientRunner, Salesforce and ACT.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Verisk licenses it per company and publishes no prices, so you need a demo and a quote.

cons_detail.title: Tied to the Verisk ecosystem
cons_detail.explanation: Much of the value comes from the Xactimate and XactAnalysis links. Contractors doing little insurance work get less from it.

cons_detail.title: Integration updates need care
cons_detail.explanation: Restoration Manager's integrations page warns that updating an integrated product to its newest version can break the integration, and it recommends checking with support first.

cons_detail.title: Thin public product detail
cons_detail.explanation: The verisk.com product page shows little detail, and most information lives on xactware.com and the Restoration Manager University site, so plan to get specifics in a demo.

cons_detail.title: Restoration only
cons_detail.explanation: Restoration Manager is built for property restoration and is not a fit for other trades.

tools.implementation_notes: Request a demo and a per-company license quote from Verisk. Before rollout, connect your Xactimate and XactAnalysis accounts so assignments and estimates flow in, and choose your accounting link (QuickBooks Desktop, QuickBooks Online, Sage 100 Contractor or Sage 300). Check with Restoration Manager support before updating any integrated product, since its integrations page warns that a new version can break the connection. If you are leaving DASH, PSA, ClientRunner, Salesforce or ACT, ask about the matching data migration. Set up dashboards, schedules and equipment records, then roll out ManageIT Mobile to field crews and the customer portal to homeowners and trade partners. Training documents and recorded webinars are available through Restoration Manager University.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Restoration Manager?
tool_faqs.a: Verisk (Nasdaq: VRSK). Verisk acquired its developer, Service Software, in December 2017 and made it part of Xactware, the Verisk business behind Xactimate and XactAnalysis.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Restoration Manager cost?
tool_faqs.a: Verisk does not publish a price. It says Restoration Manager is licensed per company with a guided rollout, so request a demo and a quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does Restoration Manager integrate with Xactimate and QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Its integrations page lists two-way integrations with Xactimate, XactAnalysis, QuickBooks Desktop, QuickBooks Online and Sage 100 Contractor, and a one-way link to Sage 300 Construction. Work orders can be generated from imported Xactimate estimates.

tool_faqs.q: Does Restoration Manager have a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. ManageIT Mobile gives field crews job access, and equipment is tracked by scanning with the app.

tool_faqs.q: Can I move to Restoration Manager from DASH or PSA?
tool_faqs.a: Restoration Manager lists data migrations from DASH, PSA, ClientRunner, Salesforce and ACT. Ask about the one for your current system during the demo.

tools.name: PaintScout
tools.tagline: Estimating, proposal and sales software built for painting contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Billed annually: Sales $99 a month including 1 user; Sales plus the Operations add-on ($79) comes to $178 a month. Billed monthly: Sales $119 and Operations $99. Additional users $20 per user per month. Optional one-time Success Packages: Plus $999, Pro $1,499, Premium $1,999. Free onboarding included. Card and ACH processing fees apply to PaintScout Payments. 14-day free trial, no credit card required. Verified against paintscout.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Painting contractors whose main need is fast, consistent estimates and professional proposals priced from their own production rates, with the option to add CRM and scheduling
tools.weaknesses: Painting-only; scheduling, job management and pipelines need the paid Operations add-on; browser-based with no app-store app; extra users cost $20 each per month
tools.long_description:
PaintScout is sales and estimating software built for painting contractors. It was co-founded by Jon Bryant, who ran his own painting business, and software developer Bryce Tymrick; Bryant is the CEO. The company is based in Calgary, Alberta (its terms of service name the operator as Tapristocrat Inc.), and it says thousands of painting businesses across North America use PaintScout.

Estimating is built around production rates. You set your own rates for surfaces and services such as walls, ceilings, trim, doors, cabinets, decks and floors, enter room dimensions on site, and PaintScout works out labor and materials. Estimates become interactive proposals with optional upgrades the customer can pick, electronic signatures, and a Pay Now button for deposits once the customer accepts. Payments run through PaintScout Payments (credit card and ACH, or EFT in Canada) or a Stripe connection, and consumer financing is available through Wisetack. The Sales plan also includes customer chat, automated email and SMS follow-ups, and sales leaderboards.

The Sales plan is $99 a month billed annually ($119 billed monthly) and includes 1 user; additional users are $20 per user per month. The Operations add-on, announced in May 2026, adds contacts and leads, drag-and-drop pipelines, job management, scheduling with Google Calendar two-way sync, crew assignment and team tasks for $79 a month billed annually ($99 monthly). There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card required and free onboarding, plus optional one-time Success Packages from $999 to $1,999 for setup and training. Integrations include QuickBooks Online, Xero, CompanyCam, Dropbox, Wisetack and Zapier, with CRMs such as HubSpot and Pipedrive connected through Zapier.

The trade-off: PaintScout is painting-only and estimating-led. Scheduling, job management and pipelines sit in the paid Operations add-on, and it runs in a web browser (you can add a home-screen icon on a phone or tablet) rather than as an app-store app. Multi-trade contractors, or painters who mainly want a low-cost all-in-one app, may prefer a broader tool such as QuoteIQ.

pros_detail.title: Production-rate estimating
pros_detail.explanation: You price work from your own production rates for each surface and service, then enter room dimensions and let PaintScout calculate labor and materials, instead of building generic line items.

pros_detail.title: Interactive proposals
pros_detail.explanation: Proposals can include optional upgrades the customer picks, electronic signatures, and on-site acceptance, with deposits collected through a Pay Now button after the customer accepts.

pros_detail.title: Payments and financing
pros_detail.explanation: PaintScout Payments takes credit card and ACH (EFT in Canada) on estimates and invoices, Stripe can be connected instead, and Wisetack adds consumer financing.

pros_detail.title: Wide integration list
pros_detail.explanation: PaintScout connects with QuickBooks Online, Xero, CompanyCam, Dropbox, Wisetack and Zapier, and uses Zapier to reach CRMs such as HubSpot, Pipedrive and Monday.

pros_detail.title: Onboarding included
pros_detail.explanation: The 14-day free trial needs no credit card, and PaintScout says free onboarding and live chat support come with every account.

cons_detail.title: Operations costs extra
cons_detail.explanation: Scheduling, job management, pipelines and team tasks are in the Operations add-on at $79 a month billed annually ($99 monthly), on top of the Sales plan.

cons_detail.title: Extra users add up
cons_detail.explanation: The Sales plan includes 1 user. Each additional user is $20 a month, so a shop with several estimators pays noticeably more than the headline price.

cons_detail.title: Painting-only
cons_detail.explanation: PaintScout is built for painting contractors. A company doing several trades may be better served by a multi-trade tool.

cons_detail.title: No app-store app
cons_detail.explanation: PaintScout runs in a web browser on phones, tablets and computers. You can add a home-screen icon, but there is no native app to download.

cons_detail.title: Paid setup help is optional but costly
cons_detail.explanation: Free onboarding is included, but the Success Packages that build out production rates, templates and presentations cost $999 to $1,999 one time.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 14-day free trial (no credit card required) and use the included onboarding. The main setup job is entering your production rates for each surface and service, then building estimate and presentation templates with your branding and optional upgrades. Connect PaintScout Payments or Stripe for deposits, Wisetack if you offer financing, and QuickBooks Online or Xero for accounting. Add users at $20 each per month, starting with the people who write estimates. If you want scheduling, pipelines and job management, add Operations once the estimating side is set up. PaintScout runs in the browser, so add a home-screen icon on the phones and tablets your estimators carry. If you want hands-on help with rates and templates, the optional Success Packages ($999 to $1,999) cover setup and training.

tool_faqs.q: How much does PaintScout cost?
tool_faqs.a: The Sales plan is $99 a month billed annually or $119 billed monthly, with 1 user included. Additional users are $20 per user per month. The Operations add-on is $79 a month billed annually or $99 monthly. There is a 14-day free trial.

tool_faqs.q: Does PaintScout include scheduling and CRM?
tool_faqs.a: Those come with the Operations add-on, which covers contacts and leads, pipelines, job management, scheduling with Google Calendar two-way sync, crew assignment and team tasks. The Sales plan on its own covers estimating, proposals, payments and follow-ups.

tool_faqs.q: How does PaintScout estimating work?
tool_faqs.a: You set production rates for surfaces and services such as walls, ceilings, trim, doors and cabinets. On site you enter room dimensions, and PaintScout calculates labor and materials and builds a proposal the customer can view, accept and sign online.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a PaintScout mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: PaintScout is web-based and runs in your browser; its help center says there is no app store download. You can add a home-screen icon on a phone or tablet so it opens like an app.

tool_faqs.q: What does PaintScout integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Its integrations pages list QuickBooks Online, Xero, Stripe, CompanyCam, Dropbox, Wisetack, Zapier, Google Calendar, Pipeline CRM, Workglue and HeyPros, plus HubSpot, Pipedrive, Monday and Jobber through Zapier.

tool_faqs.q: PaintScout vs QuoteIQ for painters?
tool_faqs.a: PaintScout is painting-only and built around production-rate estimating and proposals, with CRM and scheduling in a paid add-on. QuoteIQ is a multi-trade all-in-one app priced per company with user caps, with a paint calculator and AI tools. Painters who want estimating depth tend to look at PaintScout; those who want a low-cost all-in-one tend to look at QuoteIQ.

tools.name: QuoteIQ
tools.tagline: All-in-one CRM for home service contractors, with painting tools and AI features

pricing.pricing_note: Flat price per company with user caps, billed monthly: Essentials $29.99 (1 user), Beginner $74.99 (2 users), Pro $149.99 (4 users), Elite $299 (10 users), Max $699 (unlimited users). Yearly billing is $299.90, $749.90, $1,499.90, $2,990 and $6,990 (about 2 months free; Essentials works out to $24.99 a month). Each plan includes monthly AI Credits (500, 1,500, 3,000, 5,000, 8,000) that reset monthly; extra credits and an AI website builder below Max are paid add-ons. Payment processing fees apply to payments. 14-day free trial on all plans. Verified against myquoteiq.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Solo operators and small home service crews, including painters, who want estimating, scheduling, invoicing and payments in one flat-priced app with a paint calculator and AI tools
tools.weaknesses: AI features draw on a monthly AI Credit allowance; client portal, job costing and QuickBooks Online start on Pro ($149.99 a month); QuickBooks Desktop not supported; multi-trade rather than painting-only
tools.long_description:
QuoteIQ is an all-in-one CRM and field service app for home service contractors. It was built by contractors Mike Vidan and Justin Rogers and is based in Savannah, Georgia. The company says it launched in October 2023, is 100% bootstrapped with no venture capital, and is used by more than 40,000 contractors across 50+ industries, including painting, pressure washing, lawn care, HVAC and roofing. It runs on iOS, Android and the web.

For painters, QuoteIQ includes a Paint Calculator on every plan that turns dimensions into gallons, room-by-room line items (a room such as a master bedroom can carry prep, primer, two coats and trim as sub-items), and four estimate formats: Standard, Quick, Options (Good/Better/Best side by side) and Package. An AI Before/After generator creates an "after" preview from a photo of the customer's property, also on every plan. MapMeasure Pro, which measures walls, roofs, decks, fences and driveways from satellite imagery, starts on the Beginner plan. Payments run through Stripe (cards, ACH, Apple Pay and Google Pay), and QuickBooks Online sync starts on Pro.

Pricing is a flat monthly fee per company with a user cap, not a per-user fee. Essentials is $29.99 a month (1 user), Beginner $74.99 (2 users), Pro $149.99 (4 users), Elite $299 (10 users) and Max $699 (unlimited users). Paying yearly gives about two months free (for example $299.90 a year for Essentials). Each plan includes a monthly allowance of AI Credits (also called IQ Credits), from 500 on Essentials to 8,000 on Max, that power the AI features. Credits reset monthly and do not roll over, and extra credits are sold separately. There is a 14-day free trial on all plans.

The trade-off: important office features are tiered. The client portal, job costing, QuickBooks Online and email and text automation start on Pro, while pipelines, route optimization, inventory and the EmployeeHub team tools start on Elite. AI use is metered by credits, so heavy AI users should check how many credits their normal week uses. QuoteIQ is a multi-trade tool, so painters who want an estimator built only around painting production rates may also want to compare PaintScout.

pros_detail.title: Flat pricing with user caps
pros_detail.explanation: Plans are priced per company, not per user: Essentials is $29.99 a month for 1 user and Max is $699 a month for unlimited users. QuoteIQ says there are no per-user fees.

pros_detail.title: Painting tools on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: The Paint Calculator, room-by-room line items and the AI Before/After image generator are included from the $29.99 Essentials plan, according to QuoteIQ's painting page.

pros_detail.title: Several estimate formats
pros_detail.explanation: Standard, Quick, Options and Package estimates let you send a detailed line-item quote, a fast simple quote, or Good/Better/Best choices side by side.

pros_detail.title: Satellite measuring from Beginner
pros_detail.explanation: MapMeasure Pro measures wall runs, roofs, decks, fences and driveways from satellite imagery and attaches screenshots to the estimate, starting on the $74.99 Beginner plan.

pros_detail.title: Payments built in
pros_detail.explanation: Stripe-powered payments take cards, ACH, Apple Pay and Google Pay. QuoteIQ says there is no monthly or setup fee to turn payments on; processing and platform fees come out of each payment.

pros_detail.title: Review requests included
pros_detail.explanation: The Review Multiplier tool for requesting customer reviews is included from the Beginner plan up.

cons_detail.title: AI use is metered
cons_detail.explanation: AI features draw on a monthly credit allowance (500 on Essentials up to 8,000 on Max). Credits reset monthly and do not roll over, and Google Calendar sync also uses credits per event.

cons_detail.title: Office features start on Pro
cons_detail.explanation: The client portal, job costing, QuickBooks Online and email and text automation start on Pro at $149.99 a month, well above the $29.99 entry price.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Online only
cons_detail.explanation: QuoteIQ's painting page says its QuickBooks connection is for QuickBooks Online only, so QuickBooks Desktop users need another route.

cons_detail.title: Multi-trade, not painting-only
cons_detail.explanation: QuoteIQ serves more than 50 industries. Its painting tools are real, but it is not built only around painting production rates the way a painting-specific estimator is.

cons_detail.title: Young company
cons_detail.explanation: QuoteIQ says it launched in October 2023 and is bootstrapped, so it has a shorter track record than older field service platforms.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 14-day free trial on the plan you expect to use, since several features are tiered. Enter your services and rates, set up the Paint Calculator and your estimate templates (including Options estimates for Good/Better/Best pricing), and connect Stripe to take card and ACH payments. If you use QuickBooks Online, you need Pro or higher to connect it. Try the AI Before/After tool and, on Beginner or higher, MapMeasure Pro on a real job, and track how many AI Credits a normal week uses before you pick a plan. QuoteIQ is a standalone system, so plan to move customer records over from any previous tool.

tool_faqs.q: How much does QuoteIQ cost?
tool_faqs.a: Billed monthly: Essentials $29.99 (1 user), Beginner $74.99 (2 users), Pro $149.99 (4 users), Elite $299 (10 users) and Max $699 (unlimited users). Yearly billing gives about two months free. Every plan has a 14-day free trial and a monthly AI Credit allowance.

tool_faqs.q: What painting features does QuoteIQ have?
tool_faqs.a: Every plan includes a Paint Calculator that turns dimensions into gallons, room-by-room line items, four estimate formats including Good/Better/Best Options, and an AI Before/After image generator. MapMeasure Pro satellite measurement starts on Beginner, and job costing starts on Pro.

tool_faqs.q: What are QuoteIQ's AI Credits?
tool_faqs.a: AI Credits (also called IQ Credits) power QuoteIQ's AI features, and each feature uses a different number of credits. Plans include 500 to 8,000 credits a month. They reset monthly, do not roll over, and extra credits can be bought.

tool_faqs.q: Does QuoteIQ work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with QuickBooks Online on the Pro plan and above. QuoteIQ says the sync covers invoices, payments, customers and expense categories. It does not list QuickBooks Desktop support.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns QuoteIQ?
tool_faqs.a: QuoteIQ was founded by contractors Mike Vidan and Justin Rogers and is based in Savannah, Georgia. The company says it is 100% bootstrapped with no venture capital.

tool_faqs.q: QuoteIQ vs PaintScout?
tool_faqs.a: QuoteIQ is a multi-trade all-in-one app priced per company with user caps, with painting tools on every plan. PaintScout is built only for painting contractors around production-rate estimating and proposals; its Sales plan is $99 a month billed annually for 1 user, with extra users and an Operations add-on costing more. Painters who mainly want estimating depth may prefer PaintScout; those who want scheduling, payments and AI tools in one low-cost app may prefer QuoteIQ.

tools.name: CorkCRM
tools.tagline: CRM built for painting companies, from leads and proposals to crew timecards and invoices

pricing.pricing_note: Flat monthly price per company with user caps: Bronze $149 (1 user), Silver $224 (3 users), Gold $299 (5 users), Enterprise $349 (unlimited users). Every plan lists the same features, including QuickBooks integration and reports; email support on all plans, scheduled phone support on Silver and up. Month to month, no contract, no annual option listed. 14-day free trial, no credit card needed. Verified against corkcrm.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Painting companies that want one painting-focused system for leads, appointments, proposals, contracts, job scheduling, crew timecards and invoices
tools.weaknesses: Painting-only; entry plan is $149 a month for 1 user; phone support starts on Silver; browser-based with no app-store app; little public information about the company
tools.long_description:
CorkCRM is a CRM built for painting companies. According to its about page, founder Michael Henry started a painting business in 2010 and founded CorkCRM in 2013; the software is sold by Cork CRM, LLC. It is aimed at the sales-to-job workflow of a painting business rather than at trades in general.

The feature list covers lead tracking with automatic follow-up, appointment booking online or by phone with Google Calendar sync, custom proposals, contracts that customers can sign electronically on the spot or later by email, a job schedule where you set start and end dates and assign a crew, crew timecards reported from a phone or computer, invoices generated automatically when a proposal is accepted and when a job is completed, credit card payments, and reports covering areas from job costing to lead generation. Listed integrations are QuickBooks Online, Google Calendar, Twilio, Mailparser (for automatic lead entry), Mandrill, MX Merchant for card payments and Zillow Zestimates. CorkCRM runs in any mobile browser with no installation.

Pricing is monthly with no contract. Bronze is $149 a month for 1 user, Silver $224 for 3 users, Gold $299 for 5 users and Enterprise $349 for unlimited users. Every plan lists the same features, including QuickBooks integration and reports; the tiers differ by user count and support, with email support on all plans and scheduled phone support on Silver, Gold and Enterprise. CorkCRM advertises a 14-day free trial and says no credit card is needed to try it.

The trade-off: CorkCRM is painting-only, and there is little public information about the company beyond its founder and CTO. The entry plan covers a single user at $149 a month, which is more than a solo painter pays for QuoteIQ's $29.99 Essentials plan, while a crew of five or more gets the full feature set at a flat price. It is browser-based rather than an app-store app, so test the mobile experience with your crews during the trial.

pros_detail.title: Built for painting companies
pros_detail.explanation: CorkCRM was founded by a painting business owner, and its workflow (appointments, proposals, contracts, job schedule, crew timecards, invoices) follows how a painting company sells and runs jobs.

pros_detail.title: Same features on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Bronze through Enterprise list the same features, including QuickBooks integration, Google Calendar sync, credit card payments and reports. You choose a plan by headcount and support level, not by feature.

pros_detail.title: Flat price for bigger crews
pros_detail.explanation: Gold covers 5 users for $299 a month and Enterprise covers unlimited users for $349, so cost does not climb with every new user.

pros_detail.title: Proposal-to-invoice automation
pros_detail.explanation: Invoices are generated automatically when a proposal is accepted and when a job is completed, and customers can e-sign contracts on the spot or later by email.

pros_detail.title: No contract
pros_detail.explanation: CorkCRM bills month to month and says you can cancel any time without penalty or move between plans.

cons_detail.title: High entry price for one user
cons_detail.explanation: Bronze is $149 a month for a single user, which is steep for a solo painter compared with lower-priced multi-trade apps.

cons_detail.title: Painting-only
cons_detail.explanation: CorkCRM is built for painting companies. A contractor spanning several trades is better served by a multi-trade tool.

cons_detail.title: Phone support from Silver
cons_detail.explanation: All customers get email support, but scheduled phone support starts on the $224 Silver plan.

cons_detail.title: Browser only
cons_detail.explanation: CorkCRM runs in a mobile browser with no installation. There is no app-store app for crews.

cons_detail.title: Little public company information
cons_detail.explanation: The website names the founder and CTO but gives no office address or customer numbers, so there is less to go on when judging the vendor.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo or start the 14-day free trial (CorkCRM says no credit card is needed). Pick a plan by headcount, since features are the same on every tier: Bronze for 1 user, Silver for 3, Gold for 5 and Enterprise for unlimited, with phone support from Silver up. Set up your proposal and contract templates, connect Google Calendar for appointments, connect QuickBooks Online for accounting and MX Merchant for card payments, and set up Mailparser if you want web leads entered automatically. Add your crews and have them report hours through timecards on their phones. Re-enter or import your open leads and customers before you switch over.

tool_faqs.q: Who is CorkCRM for?
tool_faqs.a: Painting companies. It covers leads, appointment booking, proposals, e-signed contracts, job scheduling with crew assignment, crew timecards and invoicing in one painting-focused system. It is not a multi-trade platform.

tool_faqs.q: How much does CorkCRM cost?
tool_faqs.a: Bronze is $149 a month for 1 user, Silver $224 for 3 users, Gold $299 for 5 users and Enterprise $349 for unlimited users. Billing is monthly with no contract, and there is a 14-day free trial.

tool_faqs.q: Does CorkCRM integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. QuickBooks integration is listed on every plan, and the features page names QuickBooks Online. Other listed integrations are Google Calendar, Twilio, Mailparser, Mandrill, MX Merchant and Zillow Zestimates.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a CorkCRM mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: CorkCRM is mobile responsive and runs in any mobile browser with no installation. Crews can report their hours from a smartphone, and customers can sign contracts on a phone, laptop or tablet.

tool_faqs.q: What is the difference between the plans?
tool_faqs.a: The number of users and the support level. Every plan lists the same features; Silver, Gold and Enterprise add scheduled phone support on top of the email support all customers get.

tool_faqs.q: CorkCRM vs QuoteIQ vs PaintScout?
tool_faqs.a: All three serve painters. CorkCRM is a painting-only CRM with flat plans from $149 a month. QuoteIQ is a multi-trade all-in-one app from $29.99 a month with a paint calculator and AI tools. PaintScout is a painting-only estimating and proposal tool from $99 a month billed annually for 1 user, with CRM and scheduling in an add-on.

tools.name: Estimate Rocket
tools.tagline: Estimating, CRM and project management software for service contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Monthly price per company with included users: Launch $139 (3 full users), Accelerate $259 (7 full users), Expand $359 (15 full users). Additional full users $79, $39 or $19 a month by plan; field users $10 a month on all plans. All core features, one-on-one training and onboarding on every plan; optional Advanced Setup Package listed at $995 (regular $1,595). No annual price listed. 30-day free trial; refund of 100% of payments made in the first 90 days on cancellation. Verified against estimaterocket.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Service and trade contractors, including painters, remodelers and franchise systems, that want estimating, proposals, scheduling, job costing and invoicing in one web app for a small office team plus field crews
tools.weaknesses: Web app only, with no native mobile app and no offline access yet; entry plan is $139 a month; QuickBooks Online sync may run through Zapier; multi-trade rather than painting-specific
tools.long_description:
Estimate Rocket is an estimating, CRM and project management platform for service contractors. It was founded in 2015 by Thomas Droste, who is its CTO, and lists its address in Newburyport, Massachusetts. It serves more than 50 trades, including residential painting, roofing, landscaping, HVAC, plumbing and electrical work, and it offers a franchise package that gives franchisors logins to franchisee accounts and consolidated reports.

The workflow runs from lead to payment. On the sales side it has estimate and document templates, customizable and interactive proposals with optional add-ons and electronic signatures, automated follow-up campaigns for bookings, proposals and invoices, a client portal with 24/7 access to estimates and invoices, and two-way messaging by text or email. On the job side it has crew and sales scheduling, time and expense tracking from the field, and job costing that compares budget to actuals. Invoices can be paid by credit card or ACH, and reports cover sales, lead pipeline, open receivables, profitability and closing ratios.

Pricing is monthly per company with included users. Launch is $139 a month with 3 full users, Accelerate $259 with 7 and Expand $359 with 15. Extra full users cost $79, $39 or $19 a month depending on the plan, and field users are $10 a month on every plan. All plans include all core features, one-on-one training and onboarding help; an optional Advanced Setup Package was listed at $995 (regular price $1,595). There is a 30-day free trial, and Estimate Rocket says it refunds 100% of payments made in the first 90 days if you cancel. Listed integrations are QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop (by export), Zapier, CompanyCam and YouCanBookMe.

The trade-off: Estimate Rocket is a mobile-friendly web app rather than a native iOS or Android app, and the vendor lists offline access as still in development, so crews need a signal to update jobs. The entry plan costs $139 a month, more than apps aimed at solo operators, though it includes three full users. It is a multi-trade tool, so painters who want surface-by-surface production-rate estimating may also compare PaintScout.

pros_detail.title: All core features on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Launch, Accelerate and Expand include the same core features. The plans differ by the number of full users included and the price of extra users.

pros_detail.title: Lead-to-payment workflow
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates, interactive proposals with e-signatures, follow-up campaigns, scheduling, invoicing and card or ACH payments sit in one system, with a client portal for customers.

pros_detail.title: Low-cost field seats
pros_detail.explanation: Field users cost $10 a month on every plan, so crews can see schedules and job details and log time without paying for full office seats.

pros_detail.title: Job costing from field data
pros_detail.explanation: Labor, travel and expenses logged in the field roll up to each project, so you can compare budget to actuals while the job is running.

pros_detail.title: Franchise tools
pros_detail.explanation: The franchise package gives franchisors logins to franchisee accounts, call-center lead routing to franchisee calendars and consolidated reports.

pros_detail.title: Long trial and refund window
pros_detail.explanation: There is a 30-day free trial, and Estimate Rocket says it refunds 100% of payments made in the first 90 days if you cancel.

cons_detail.title: No native app or offline mode
cons_detail.explanation: Estimate Rocket is a mobile-friendly web app with no app-store app, and the vendor lists offline access as still in development. Crews working without signal cannot update jobs.

cons_detail.title: Higher entry price for solo operators
cons_detail.explanation: The cheapest plan is $139 a month. It includes 3 full users, but a one-person business pays for seats it may not use.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks setup varies
cons_detail.explanation: The integrations page describes QuickBooks Online sync through Zapier and a direct export for QuickBooks Desktop, while feature pages describe direct QuickBooks Online sync. Confirm how it works for your books before you commit.

cons_detail.title: Multi-trade, not painting-specific
cons_detail.explanation: Estimate Rocket serves more than 50 trades. Painters who want pricing built around painting production rates by surface may find a painting-only estimator closer to how they quote.

cons_detail.title: Paid setup package
cons_detail.explanation: Training and onboarding are included, but the optional Advanced Setup Package was listed at $995 (regular price $1,595).

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 30-day free trial and book the included one-on-one training. Build your estimate and document templates first (proposals, work orders and invoices with your branding), then set up the follow-up campaigns for bookings, proposals and invoices. Decide who needs a full user and who only needs a $10 field user, since field seats cost much less. Connect accounting early: confirm with Estimate Rocket whether your QuickBooks Online sync runs directly or through Zapier, and use the export if you are on QuickBooks Desktop. Connect CompanyCam if your crews already take job photos there. Because it is a web app with no offline mode yet, have crews log in from their phone browsers and test it at a job site with weak signal.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Estimate Rocket cost?
tool_faqs.a: Launch is $139 a month with 3 full users, Accelerate $259 with 7 and Expand $359 with 15. Extra full users are $79, $39 or $19 a month by plan, and field users are $10 a month. There is a 30-day free trial.

tool_faqs.q: Does Estimate Rocket have a mobile app for crews?
tool_faqs.a: It is a mobile-friendly web app that works on phones, tablets and laptops, not a native app. Field users ($10 a month) can see schedules and job details and log time and expenses. The vendor lists offline access as still in development.

tool_faqs.q: Does Estimate Rocket integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. It lists QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop. Its integrations page says QuickBooks Online syncs through Zapier and QuickBooks Desktop uses a direct export, so confirm the setup in a demo. Zapier, CompanyCam and YouCanBookMe are also listed.

tool_faqs.q: Is Estimate Rocket painting-specific?
tool_faqs.a: No. It serves more than 50 trades, including residential painting, roofing, landscaping, HVAC and plumbing. Painters can use it, but its estimating is not built only around painting production rates.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial or refund?
tool_faqs.a: There is a 30-day free trial. Estimate Rocket also says that if you cancel within the first 90 days, it refunds 100% of the payments you made in that period.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Estimate Rocket?
tool_faqs.a: Estimate Rocket was founded in 2015 by Thomas Droste, who is its CTO. The company lists its address in Newburyport, Massachusetts.

tools.name: Contractor Foreman
tools.tagline: Affordable all-in-one construction management for small-to-mid contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Annual billing, per company with user caps: Basic $49/mo (1 user), Standard $105 (3 users), Plus $166 (8 users), Pro $221 (15 users), Unlimited $332 (unlimited users). Quarterly billing costs more ($132 / $206 / $282 / $415, no Basic). More users means moving up a plan. 30-day free trial; 100-day money-back guarantee on annual plans, with onboarding conditions. Verified against contractorforeman.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Small-to-mid construction and remodeling contractors that want a broad all-in-one project + business management platform at an affordable price
tools.weaknesses: Construction-project focused rather than a service-dispatch FSM; the broad feature set can feel busy; user caps per plan push growing teams up the ladder
tools.long_description:
Contractor Foreman is an all-in-one construction management platform for small and mid-size general contractors, remodelers and specialty contractors, founded in 2017 and based in Forest City, North Carolina. It says it serves contractors in more than 75 countries.

Its pitch is breadth for the money: estimating, project management, scheduling, daily logs, time tracking, invoicing and job costing in one platform, with integrations for QuickBooks Online and Desktop, Zapier, Stripe, Gusto, CompanyCam, Google and Outlook calendars, MS Project and Angi Leads.

Plans are priced per company with user caps, billed annually: Basic $49 a month (1 user), Standard $105 (3 users), Plus $166 (8 users), Pro $221 (15 users) and Unlimited $332 (unlimited users); quarterly billing costs more. There is a 30-day free trial, and annual plans carry a 100-day money-back guarantee if you complete its onboarding conditions.

The trade-offs: it's construction project management rather than a service-dispatch FSM like Jobber or ServiceTitan, so HVAC service calls and plumbing dispatch may find the workflow less tailored. The feature set is broad enough to feel busy, and the user caps mean a growing team moves up plans.

pros_detail.title: Breadth for the price
pros_detail.explanation: From $49/mo, Contractor Foreman bundles estimating, project management, scheduling, daily logs, time tracking and invoicing, far more capability per dollar than most construction platforms.

pros_detail.title: Long trial and money-back guarantee
pros_detail.explanation: A 30-day free trial, plus a 100-day money-back guarantee on annual plans if you complete a training session and use the core features.

pros_detail.title: True all-in-one for construction
pros_detail.explanation: Estimating, project management, scheduling, invoicing, and document/daily-log handling live in one place, so a small GC can run the whole project lifecycle without juggling separate tools.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks and other integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Integrates with QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop, plus Zapier, Stripe, Gusto, CompanyCam and Google and Outlook calendars.

pros_detail.title: Affordable entry for solos and small teams
pros_detail.explanation: The $49 Basic tier makes professional construction management accessible to solo contractors and very small teams who'd be priced out of Procore or Buildertrend.

cons_detail.title: Construction-PM, not service FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Contractor Foreman is built around construction project management, not service-call dispatch. HVAC/plumbing service businesses that live in scheduling and dispatch may prefer a purpose-built FSM like Jobber, Housecall Pro, or ServiceTitan.

cons_detail.title: Feature breadth can overwhelm
cons_detail.explanation: The huge feature set is a strength and a weakness: there's a lot to learn and configure, and some owners find the interface busy compared with a focused tool.

cons_detail.title: User caps by plan
cons_detail.explanation: Plans cap users at 1, 3, 8 and 15 before Unlimited, so the $49 entry is a one-person plan. Price the plan your team size forces, not the headline.

cons_detail.title: Less service-trade vertical depth
cons_detail.explanation: It's strongest for general construction and remodeling; service-trade-specific workflows (memberships, recurring service, GLS attribution) aren't its focus the way they are for HVAC-tuned FSMs.

cons_detail.title: Mid-market ceiling
cons_detail.explanation: Large commercial GCs needing enterprise-grade project controls will likely outgrow it toward Procore or BuildOps. It's built for small-to-mid, not enterprise construction.

tools.implementation_notes: Contractor Foreman is self-service to set up, but because it's broad, the main task is deciding which modules you'll actually use and configuring them: estimating templates, project setup, scheduling and your QuickBooks connection. Start by getting estimating and project management live, then layer in time tracking, daily logs and document management. Pick your plan by headcount (user caps are 1, 3, 8, 15 and unlimited), plan some training time given the breadth, and import customers, projects and price items early. If you buy annually, do the onboarding steps the money-back guarantee requires.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Contractor Foreman cost?
tool_faqs.a: Billed annually, plans run Basic $49/mo (1 user), Standard $105 (3 users), Plus $166 (8 users), Pro $221 (15 users) and Unlimited $332 (unlimited users); quarterly billing costs more. There is a 30-day free trial and a 100-day money-back guarantee on annual plans.

tool_faqs.q: Is Contractor Foreman an FSM or construction PM tool?
tool_faqs.a: It's primarily construction project management (estimating, PM, scheduling, daily logs, job costing) rather than a service-dispatch FSM. GCs and remodelers are the sweet spot. HVAC/plumbing/electrical service businesses focused on dispatch and recurring service calls may prefer a purpose-built FSM like Jobber, Housecall Pro, or ServiceTitan.

tool_faqs.q: Contractor Foreman vs Buildertrend or Procore?
tool_faqs.a: Contractor Foreman publishes low plan prices and aims at small and mid-size contractors who want broad capability per dollar. Buildertrend is custom-quoted and built around the residential homeowner experience, and Procore prices on construction volume for larger commercial work. Value-conscious small GCs lean Contractor Foreman.

tool_faqs.q: Does Contractor Foreman integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Contractor Foreman integrates with QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop (and Zapier). Confirm during the trial that the plan you choose includes the integration you need.

tool_faqs.q: Who is Contractor Foreman best for?
tool_faqs.a: Small-to-mid general contractors and remodelers who want an affordable, broad all-in-one for estimating, project management, scheduling, and accounting sync. It's less ideal for service-dispatch-heavy trades or large commercial GCs that need enterprise project controls.

tools.name: Workyard
tools.tagline: GPS time tracking and workforce management for construction and trades

pricing.pricing_note: Plans start at $6 per user/month billed annually; monthly billing is also available. Tiers: Starter, Pro, Autopilot and Enterprise (contact sales); Workyard publishes only the $6 starting rate. 14-day free trial, no credit card required. Verified against workyard.com/pricing 2026-09-10.

tools.best_for: Construction and trades contractors that want accurate GPS-based labor tracking and job costing to feed payroll, alongside their FSM
tools.weaknesses: A workforce, time-tracking and scheduling tool, not a full FSM (no invoicing or CRM, so pair it with one); geofenced clock-ins need tuning; construction ERP integrations are Enterprise-only
tools.long_description:
Workyard is a GPS-based workforce management platform for construction and skilled trades: the tool you add to get labor data you can trust before payroll runs. Founded in 2016 and based in San Mateo, California, it focuses on time tracking with GPS and geofenced clock-ins, crew scheduling, and job costing.

For a trades business, Workyard solves a specific, expensive problem: knowing which employee was on which job for how long, so labor gets costed to the right job and payroll is right the first time. Approved, GPS-verified hours, coded by job and cost code at clock-in, sync to payroll and accounting: QuickBooks Online and Desktop, ADP, Gusto and Paychex on every plan, with Procore, Sage 300 CRE, Sage Intacct, Foundation, Viewpoint Spectrum, Rippling and ComputerEase on Enterprise. That makes it a common add-on to a field service platform rather than a replacement for one.

The key thing to understand is scope: Workyard is time tracking and scheduling, not a full FSM. It doesn't do invoicing, CRM or customer-facing workflows the way Jobber or ServiceTitan do. Pricing is per user, with plans starting at $6 per user per month billed annually (Workyard publishes only that starting rate), and there is a 14-day free trial.

pros_detail.title: GPS-verified labor tracking
pros_detail.explanation: GPS and geofenced clock-ins record who was on which job and for how long, which is more rigorous than the basic time tracking bundled into most FSMs.

pros_detail.title: Job costing by cost code
pros_detail.explanation: Hours are coded by job and cost code at clock-in, so you see real labor cost per job before payroll runs, a major lever for protecting margins.

pros_detail.title: Payroll and accounting syncs
pros_detail.explanation: Approved hours sync natively to QuickBooks Online and Desktop, ADP, Gusto and Paychex on every plan, so payroll doesn't need re-keying.

pros_detail.title: Construction ERP integrations on Enterprise
pros_detail.explanation: Enterprise adds Procore, Sage 300 CRE, Sage Intacct, Foundation, Viewpoint Spectrum, Rippling and ComputerEase, which suits larger contractors.

pros_detail.title: Built for construction and trades crews
pros_detail.explanation: Unlike generic time trackers, Workyard is designed for field crews, so geofencing, scheduling and job costing map to how trades labor works.

cons_detail.title: Not a full FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Workyard is time tracking and scheduling, not field service management. It lacks invoicing, CRM and customer-facing workflows, so you'll run it alongside an FSM, not instead of one.

cons_detail.title: Geofenced clock-ins need tuning
cons_detail.explanation: Automatic clock-ins depend on phone location and geofence size, so a crew driving past a site can trigger one. Tune geofences at setup and review exceptions before payroll.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing adds up
cons_detail.explanation: Plans start at $6/user/month (billed annually) and Workyard publishes only that starting rate, so cost scales with crew size and sits on top of whatever FSM you also pay for; confirm your plan's per-user rate before committing (only Enterprise is marked contact-sales) and model the combined stack cost.

cons_detail.title: Not a project-management platform
cons_detail.explanation: Workyard is a labor and time tool; don't expect Procore-style project controls.

cons_detail.title: Adds another tool to the stack
cons_detail.explanation: Because it's a focused layer, Workyard means another login and another vendor alongside your FSM and accounting. Worth it for the labor data, but it's not consolidation.

tools.implementation_notes: Workyard deploys as a focused layer: set up your jobs and cost codes, draw geofences around job sites, add crew members, and connect your payroll or accounting system (QuickBooks, ADP, Gusto or Paychex; construction ERPs on Enterprise). The main adoption work is getting crews comfortable with the mobile app and clock-in flow and tuning geofences so automatic clock-ins are accurate. Because Workyard complements rather than replaces your FSM, decide up front how job and labor data will flow between Workyard, your FSM and your payroll system.

tool_faqs.q: Is Workyard a full field-service platform?
tool_faqs.a: No. Workyard is GPS time tracking, scheduling and job costing (a workforce-management layer), not a full FSM. It doesn't handle invoicing, CRM or customer-facing workflows, so contractors run it alongside their FSM (Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan) for accurate labor data.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Workyard cost?
tool_faqs.a: Plans start at $6 per user per month billed annually, with monthly billing also available; Workyard publishes only that starting rate across its Starter, Pro, Autopilot and Enterprise tiers. There's a 14-day free trial with no credit card required. Since it's on top of your FSM, factor the combined cost when deciding.

tool_faqs.q: What makes Workyard's time tracking better than my FSM's?
tool_faqs.a: Focus. Workyard records hours with GPS and geofenced clock-ins, codes them by job and cost code, and syncs approved hours to payroll. If labor cost accuracy and payroll precision matter, that focus is the reason contractors add it.

tool_faqs.q: Do the GPS clock-ins really work?
tool_faqs.a: They depend on phone location and how you draw geofences. Expect to tune geofences at setup and review the occasional false clock-in (for example, a crew driving past a site) before payroll. It's strong automation, not flawless.

tool_faqs.q: Who should use Workyard?
tool_faqs.a: Construction and trades contractors with field crews who need trustworthy labor tracking and job costing to feed payroll, and who are fine running it alongside their FSM. Solo operators or businesses that just need basic time tracking may be fine with what their FSM already includes.

tools.name: busybusy
tools.tagline: Construction time tracking, job costing, and equipment tracking

pricing.pricing_note: Free plan includes GPS time tracking, job costing, equipment tracking and unlimited users. Pro $9.99/user/mo billed annually ($11.99 monthly), Premium $14.99/user/mo annually ($17.99 monthly); each adds a $40 admin license (first user included). Zapier is listed on Premium. Part of AlignOps; still sold as busybusy.

tools.best_for: Construction and trades crews that want easy, accurate GPS time tracking with job costing and equipment tracking, including a genuine free tier
tools.weaknesses: Time-tracking-focused, not a full FSM (no invoicing/CRM); advanced project-management features are lighter than dedicated PM tools; pair with an FSM for customer-facing workflows
tools.long_description:
busybusy is a time-tracking app built for construction and field crews, sold by AlignOps as its field management product. busybusy's homepage counter showed 383,845,559 total time card hours tracked on 8 October 2026.

For trades and construction, busybusy covers GPS time tracking, job costing, equipment tracking, scheduling and reporting, with integrations that feed payroll and accounting: QuickBooks Online and Desktop, Procore, Sage, ADP and Zapier. The standout is a free plan, which makes digital time tracking accessible to small crews still on paper timecards.

Like Workyard, busybusy is a time and labor layer, not a full FSM: it doesn't do invoicing, CRM or customer-facing workflows, so contractors run it alongside their field-service platform. The free plan includes GPS time tracking, job costing and equipment tracking for unlimited users; scheduling and supervisor tools start on Pro ($9.99/user/month billed annually), and Premium ($14.99) includes documents, daily project reports, checklists, team messaging and Zapier (the first four are also sold as add-ons on Pro), each paid plan with a $40 admin license (first user included).

pros_detail.title: Genuine free tier
pros_detail.explanation: busybusy offers a real free plan, making accurate GPS time tracking accessible to small crews still on paper timecards, a low-risk way to digitize labor tracking and cut payroll errors.

pros_detail.title: Built for field crews
pros_detail.explanation: Clock-in and clock-out are designed for crews in the field, including remote sites, which is what makes or breaks time tracking adoption.

pros_detail.title: Job + equipment costing
pros_detail.explanation: Beyond time, busybusy tracks job costing and equipment, so contractors see labor and equipment cost per job, useful for protecting margins on construction and trades work.

pros_detail.title: Part of the AlignOps suite
pros_detail.explanation: AlignOps sells busybusy (field management) alongside ToolWatch (asset management), FleetWatcher (fleet and material management) and SafetyReports (risk management), so contractors already using one of those products can add crew time tracking from the same vendor.

pros_detail.title: Payroll and accounting integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Time and cost data sync to QuickBooks (Online or Desktop), Sage, ADP and Procore, reducing manual entry and speeding up pay runs.

cons_detail.title: Not a full FSM
cons_detail.explanation: busybusy is time tracking, job/equipment costing, and scheduling, not field service management. No invoicing, CRM, or customer workflows, so you'll pair it with an FSM rather than replace one.

cons_detail.title: Lighter advanced PM
cons_detail.explanation: Advanced project-management features are thinner than dedicated PM platforms. It's a labor/time tool, so don't expect deep project controls.

cons_detail.title: Another tool in the stack
cons_detail.explanation: As a focused layer, it adds a login and vendor alongside your FSM and accounting. Worth it for the labor data, but it's not all-in-one consolidation.

cons_detail.title: Crew management tools need a paid plan
cons_detail.explanation: The free plan covers GPS time tracking, job costing and equipment tracking, but scheduling, supervisor tools, GPS breadcrumbing, and photos and notes are on Pro ($9.99/user/month billed annually); documents, daily project reports, checklists, team messaging and Zapier are included on Premium ($14.99), and the first four are also sold as add-ons on Pro. Each paid plan adds a $40 admin license (first user included).

tools.implementation_notes: busybusy is easy to roll out: create your projects and jobs, add crew members, and have them install the mobile app to clock in and out with GPS. Connect QuickBooks, Sage, ADP or Procore to sync time and job-cost data. Start on the free plan, which includes job costing and equipment tracking, to validate the workflow, then move to Pro for scheduling and supervisor tools as needed. Because it complements rather than replaces your FSM, plan how labor and cost data will flow between busybusy, your FSM and accounting.

tool_faqs.q: Is busybusy free?
tool_faqs.a: busybusy has a free plan that covers GPS time tracking, job costing and equipment tracking for unlimited users. Pro ($9.99/user/month billed annually, $11.99 billed monthly) adds scheduling, supervisor tools and GPS breadcrumbing; Premium ($14.99 annually, $17.99 monthly) includes documents, daily project reports, checklists, team messaging and Zapier, and the first four are also sold as add-ons on Pro. Both paid plans add a $40 admin license (first user included) and offer a 14-day free trial.

tool_faqs.q: Is busybusy a full field-service platform?
tool_faqs.a: No. busybusy is construction time tracking, job costing, equipment tracking, and scheduling, not a full FSM. It doesn't handle invoicing, CRM, or customer workflows, so contractors typically run it alongside their field-service platform for accurate labor data.

tool_faqs.q: busybusy vs Workyard?
tool_faqs.a: Both are construction and trades time-tracking layers with GPS and job costing. busybusy has a free plan and is part of AlignOps; Workyard starts at $6/user/month billed annually and is known for geofencing. Crews wanting a free start lean busybusy; those wanting Workyard's geofencing lean Workyard. Both pair with an FSM.

tool_faqs.q: Does busybusy track equipment?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Alongside time and job costing, busybusy tracks equipment, so contractors can see equipment usage and cost per job. Combined with labor tracking, that helps cost jobs accurately and protect margins. The free plan includes equipment usage, equipment location, machine hours and the equipment list.

tool_faqs.q: Who is busybusy best for?
tool_faqs.a: Construction and trades crews that want dead-simple, accurate GPS time tracking with job and equipment costing, especially those moving off paper timecards who want a free tier to start. It's a labor-tracking layer, so pair it with an FSM for invoicing, CRM, and customer-facing work.

tools.name: Leap
tools.tagline: CRM and in-home sales platform for exteriors and remodeling contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Leap CRM Essential $79/mo (1 user); Leap CRM Team $298/mo (1 user) plus $99/mo per additional user; SalesPro $297/mo for 3 users plus $99/mo per additional user; SalesPro Premium $750/mo including 6 users plus $99/mo per additional user; Enterprise custom. One-year contracts paid monthly. Verified against leaptodigital.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Exteriors and remodeling contractors (roofing, siding, windows, painting) that sell in the home and want a CRM plus a field sales-and-proposal app with built-in financing
tools.weaknesses: Exteriors and remodeling sales focused, not a service-dispatch FSM; SalesPro is a separate product priced on top of the CRM; less fit for pure service trades (HVAC service calls, plumbing dispatch)
tools.long_description:
Leap is a CRM and in-home sales platform for home-improvement contractors who sell at the kitchen table: roofing, siding, windows and doors, remodeling, painting and other exterior trades. It pairs Leap CRM (lead-to-job management) with SalesPro, an in-home sales app where reps present, estimate, contract and collect payment on a tablet, including offline. Leap made the Inc. 5000 list of fast-growing private companies for the fifth year in a row in 2025.

The differentiator is the in-home sales motion. SalesPro lets a rep build a branded proposal, present financing, capture a signature and take payment at the point of sale; one financing application can put offers from several lenders (GreenSky, Aqua, Service Finance, Foundation Finance and others) in front of the homeowner at the appointment. Leap CRM connects to QuickBooks, EagleView, Hover, GAF QuickMeasure, CompanyCam, Angi Leads, Zapier and suppliers including ABC Supply, SRS and QXO.

The trade-offs: Leap is built for exteriors and remodeling sales, not service dispatch, so HVAC service and plumbing dispatch businesses won't find it tailored to their workflow. Pricing starts at $79/mo for Leap CRM Essential (1 user) and $298/mo for CRM Team; SalesPro is priced separately, from $297/mo for three users or $750/mo for SalesPro Premium with six, all on one-year contracts.

pros_detail.title: Purpose-built for in-home sales
pros_detail.explanation: SalesPro lets reps present, estimate, contract, and collect payment on a tablet at the kitchen table, even offline. For exteriors/remodeling businesses that close in the home, that integrated sales motion is the core advantage.

pros_detail.title: Multi-lender financing at the point of sale
pros_detail.explanation: One application in SalesPro can present offers from several lenders (GreenSky, Aqua, Service Finance, Foundation Finance and others), so reps can turn a big-ticket exterior job into a monthly payment on the spot. GreenSky financing is included in the Leap CRM subscription.

pros_detail.title: Exteriors/remodeling focus
pros_detail.explanation: Leap is tailored to roofing, siding, windows, remodeling, and painting workflows rather than generic, so the CRM and proposal tooling fit how these contractors actually sell.

pros_detail.title: Measurement and supplier integrations
pros_detail.explanation: EagleView, Hover and GAF QuickMeasure for measurements, CompanyCam for photos, and ABC Supply, SRS and QXO for suppliers, plus QuickBooks and Zapier.

pros_detail.title: End-to-end lead-to-payment
pros_detail.explanation: Leap CRM plus SalesPro covers lead management through proposal, contract, financing, and payment, so an exteriors contractor can run the sales lifecycle in one connected platform.

cons_detail.title: Sales/CRM, not service-dispatch FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Leap centers on selling and CRM for exteriors/remodeling, not service-call scheduling and dispatch. HVAC/plumbing/electrical service businesses will find a purpose-built FSM (Jobber, ServiceTitan, Workiz) a better fit for their day-to-day.

cons_detail.title: SalesPro is priced separately
cons_detail.explanation: The in-home sales app, SalesPro, costs $297/mo for three users (+$99 per additional user) or $750/mo for Premium with six users, on top of Leap CRM ($79/mo Essential, $298/mo Team). All plans are on one-year contracts.

cons_detail.title: Narrow vertical fit
cons_detail.explanation: Leap is strongest for exteriors and remodeling. Pure service trades or businesses that don't sell big-ticket in-home jobs will get less value than a generalist FSM.

cons_detail.title: Know the financing economics
cons_detail.explanation: Point-of-sale financing helps close, but lender programs carry merchant fees and, on some promotional plans, deferred-interest terms (see our financing category). Understand what each lender charges you and the homeowner before presenting it.

cons_detail.title: Two products to learn
cons_detail.explanation: Leap CRM and SalesPro are distinct products; getting the full lead-to-payment flow means adopting and configuring both, which is more setup than a single all-in-one.

tools.implementation_notes: Leap implementation centers on the sales motion.
