Set up Leap CRM for lead-to-job management first (pipeline, customers, jobs), then configure SalesPro for in-home selling: branded proposal templates and good/better/best options, your financing lenders, digital contracts and payment collection. The biggest training investment is getting field reps fluent in SalesPro on a tablet so they can present, finance, sign and collect smoothly, including offline. Decide up front whether you need both products or just Leap CRM, since SalesPro is priced separately.

tool_faqs.q: What is Leap (and SalesPro)?
tool_faqs.a: Leap is a CRM and in-home sales platform for home-improvement contractors. Leap CRM (from $79/mo) handles lead-to-job management, and SalesPro (from $297/mo for three users) is an in-home sales app where reps present, estimate, contract, present financing and collect payment on a tablet, even offline. It's built for exteriors and remodeling sales.

tool_faqs.q: Who is Leap best for?
tool_faqs.a: Exteriors and remodeling contractors (roofing, siding, windows and doors, painting, remodeling) that sell big-ticket jobs in the home and want a CRM plus an in-home sales-and-financing app. It's not designed for service-dispatch trades (HVAC service, plumbing) that need scheduling and dispatch.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Leap cost?
tool_faqs.a: Leap CRM Essential is $79/month for one user and Leap CRM Team $298/month plus $99 per additional user. SalesPro is $297/month for three users (+$99 per additional user) or $750/month for SalesPro Premium with six users. All plans are on one-year contracts paid monthly.

tool_faqs.q: Does Leap offer financing for customers?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. SalesPro can present offers from several lenders (GreenSky, Aqua, Service Finance, Foundation Finance and others) from one application during the in-home pitch, and GreenSky financing is included in the Leap CRM subscription. Understand each lender's fees and deferred-interest terms before you present them.

tool_faqs.q: Leap vs an FSM like Jobber or ServiceTitan?
tool_faqs.a: Different tools for different jobs. Leap is a sales and CRM platform built for the in-home exteriors and remodeling close; Jobber and ServiceTitan are field-service platforms built for scheduling, dispatch and service operations. Exteriors and remodeling sales teams lean Leap; service-dispatch trades lean an FSM. Some businesses use both.

tools.name: Jobber
tools.tagline: Field service management for growing service businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Prices shown are the annual-billed monthly equivalent at each plan's smallest team size, matching Jobber's 'Starting at' figures: Core $29, Connect $99, Grow $149, Plus $399. Prices rise with the team-size selector; the page headlines 'Jobber plans from $29 to $529/mo (billed annually)'. No-commitment (month-to-month) billing starts at $49 / $139 / $199 / $499, and a '1 year commitment' option (12-month minimum term, billed monthly) is priced between the two. Additional users $29/mo each. The August 2026 promotion ended 2026-08-31. 14-day free trial of the Grow plan, no card. Verified against getjobber.com/pricing 2026-09-10.

tools.best_for: Small and mid-size home service businesses (1-30 people) that want quoting, scheduling, invoicing and payments in one app
tools.weaknesses: No inventory management advertised on any plan; QuickBooks sync covers QuickBooks Online only and runs one way; built for small and mid-size crews rather than large multi-location operations
tools.long_description:
Jobber is field service management software for home service businesses, founded in 2011 in Edmonton, Canada by Sam Pillar and Forrest Zeisler. Jobber says more than 400,000 service pros across 50+ industries in 60+ countries use it. It puts quoting, scheduling, invoicing, payments and customer communication in one app, aimed at owner-operators and small crews rather than large enterprises.

The product's focus is day-to-day ease of use for small teams: a mobile app for field work, a client portal where customers can approve quotes and pay, online booking, and automated quote and invoice follow-ups from the Connect plan up. Newer additions include an AI Receptionist that answers calls and texts, and consumer financing through Wisetack, which Jobber adds automatically to eligible quotes for US businesses.

The four plans (Core, Connect, Grow and Plus) start at $29, $99, $149 and $399 a month billed annually at the smallest team size, or $49, $139, $199 and $499 month-to-month, and rise with team size; additional users are $29 a month each. The trade-offs to check before you buy: QuickBooks sync covers QuickBooks Online only and runs one way, from Jobber to QuickBooks; no plan advertises inventory management; and larger multi-location operations should test reporting and permissions during the 14-day trial.

pros_detail.title: Built for small crews
pros_detail.explanation: Jobber covers the core small-business workflow (quotes, scheduling, invoicing, payments) in one app, with a mobile app for field work and a client portal for customers. Ease of use is the product's main pitch, so judge it on your own jobs during the trial.

pros_detail.title: Broad trade coverage
pros_detail.explanation: Jobber says service pros across 50+ industries use it, from lawn care and cleaning to HVAC, plumbing and electrical, so it suits multi-trade shops without forcing one trade's workflow.

pros_detail.title: 14-day free trial, no credit card
pros_detail.explanation: The trial runs on the Grow plan with no credit card required. Use it seriously: schedule real jobs, send invoices, collect payments, and judge the actual workflow rather than the interface.

pros_detail.title: Consumer financing on quotes (US)
pros_detail.explanation: Through Wisetack, Jobber automatically adds financing offers to eligible quotes for US businesses, so customers can apply for monthly payments from the quote itself.

pros_detail.title: Transparent public pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan price is published, with a feature comparison and a team-size selector, so you can price your team without a sales call.

pros_detail.title: Integrations and API
pros_detail.explanation: Native integrations include QuickBooks Online, Xero, Gusto, Mailchimp, Google Local Services Ads booking and Google Calendar sync, with Zapier and a developer API for anything else.

pros_detail.title: Online booking and automated follow-ups
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can request or book work online on every plan, and automated quote and invoice follow-ups start on the Connect plan.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Online only, one-way sync
cons_detail.explanation: Jobber does not sync with QuickBooks Desktop, and its QuickBooks Online sync runs one way, from Jobber to QuickBooks (clients, products and services, invoices, payments and timesheets). QuickBooks Desktop users are limited to a manual CSV import.

cons_detail.title: An AI receptionist, not a phone system
cons_detail.explanation: Jobber's AI Receptionist answers calls and texts, but Jobber does not sell a full dispatcher phone system with call routing and recording. If you run a busy call desk, plan on a separate phone provider.

cons_detail.title: Built for small and mid-size crews
cons_detail.explanation: Plus is the top published plan. Larger multi-location operations should check reporting depth, user permissions and multi-location handling in a demo before committing.

cons_detail.title: No inventory management
cons_detail.explanation: No plan advertises inventory tracking. If you carry real parts inventory (HVAC equipment, plumbing fittings, appliance parts), plan on a third-party integration or a platform where inventory is built in.

cons_detail.title: Pricing scales directly with team size
cons_detail.explanation: Jobber prices plans by team size: the published $29/$99/$149/$399 annual rates are the smallest-team figures, additional users cost $29/mo each, and the page headlines plans from $29 to $529/mo billed annually. Budget from your headcount a year out, not today's, and price your actual team size in their calculator before committing.

cons_detail.title: Financing is US-only and excludes some trades
cons_detail.explanation: Wisetack financing through Jobber requires a US business and excludes pool and spa, residential and commercial cleaning, window washing and snow removal, so those shops need another lender.

tools.implementation_notes: Jobber is built for self-service setup. The setup flow walks you through importing clients (CSV upload), configuring services and prices, and connecting payments. Plan to spend the first week importing data and configuring the basics, then run it alongside your old system for a few weeks before cutting over. If you use QuickBooks Online, connect it once your products and services are set up; the sync runs one way, from Jobber to QuickBooks. If you are migrating from another FSM platform, budget extra time for data cleanup: historical job data and recurring service agreements rarely transfer cleanly.

tool_faqs.q: Should I pick Jobber or Housecall Pro?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on your team and trade. Both cover quoting, scheduling, invoicing, payments and Wisetack consumer financing on quotes. Compare the plan that fits your team size line by line, then run the same week of real jobs through both trials and pick the one your crew actually uses.

tool_faqs.q: Does Jobber have a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes: 14 days on the Grow plan, no credit card required. Use the trial to run real jobs end to end (schedule, dispatch, invoice, payment) rather than just clicking around the interface.

tool_faqs.q: What tier should I start on?
tool_faqs.a: Start on the smallest plan that has what you need. Core ($29/mo billed annually, $49 month-to-month) covers the basics at the smallest team size; Connect ($99/mo billed annually, $139 month-to-month) adds automated quote and invoice follow-ups; Grow and Plus add more users and features such as job costing and, on Plus, the AI Receptionist. Check the current plan comparison before you buy, since features move between plans.

tool_faqs.q: Can Jobber replace QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: No. Jobber isn't an accounting platform. It syncs clients, products and services, invoices, payments and timesheets one way to QuickBooks Online (not QuickBooks Desktop), and it also integrates with Xero. Keep your accounting package for the general ledger, payables and tax.

tool_faqs.q: How does Jobber handle recurring service agreements?
tool_faqs.a: Jobber supports recurring jobs and visits. It doesn't sell a dedicated membership-plan module like ServiceTitan's, so if maintenance agreements drive your business, test renewals and plan billing during the trial.

tools.name: Housecall Pro
tools.tagline: All-in-one platform for home service pros

pricing.pricing_note: Annual-billed monthly equivalents: Basic $59 (1 user), Essentials $149 (5 users included), Max $299 (8 users included, additional users $35/mo each). Monthly billing runs $79 / $189 / $329. 14-day free trial, no card. Verified against housecallpro.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Home service businesses that want payments, consumer financing, online booking and review requests built into one platform
tools.weaknesses: QuickBooks sync starts on Essentials and QuickBooks Desktop sync is one way; user limits per plan push growing teams to higher tiers; residential-first
tools.long_description:
Housecall Pro is field service software for home service businesses, founded in 2013 and based in San Diego. Housecall Pro says 45,000+ businesses and 180,000+ pros use it, concentrated in HVAC, plumbing, electrical and cleaning. Its focus is the customer-facing side of the job: online booking, in-app payments, consumer financing through Wisetack, a Google Local Services Ads booking integration, and automated review requests.

Every plan includes scheduling and dispatch, quotes, invoicing and payments (card processing from 2.59%), online booking, review management, live phone and chat support, and access to consumer financing. Essentials adds QuickBooks Online sync, flat-rate pricing, GPS tracking and commissions; Max adds recurring service plans, route optimization, a sales proposal tool, open API access and dedicated onboarding.

Plans are Basic ($59 a month billed annually or $79 monthly, 1 user), Essentials ($149 or $189, 5 users) and Max ($299 or $329, 8 users, then $35 a month per additional user), so the real cost depends on your headcount. Map the features you need to a plan before comparing prices: QuickBooks sync, for example, is not on Basic.

Housecall Pro fits residential service shops that want payments, financing, booking and reviews in one place. Commercial contractors that need project tracking and progress billing should look at platforms built for that work.

pros_detail.title: Consumer financing built in (Wisetack)
pros_detail.explanation: Financing offers can be added to estimates and invoices through Housecall Pro's native Wisetack integration, and customers apply with a soft credit check. Housecall Pro's help center lists a flat 3.9% fee on the financed amount and jobs from $500 to $25,000, with higher limits rolling out.

pros_detail.title: Google Local Services Ads booking
pros_detail.explanation: Businesses running Local Services Ads can add a Schedule button to those ads at no extra cost; those bookings, and Reserve with Google bookings, land in Housecall Pro's job inbox.

pros_detail.title: Payments built in
pros_detail.explanation: In-app card processing from 2.59% per transaction is on every plan, with instant payouts available, so you don't need a separate processor account.

pros_detail.title: Review requests on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Review management is included on every plan, so review requests can go out automatically after each job.

pros_detail.title: Online booking on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can book online on every plan; Max adds recurring service plans for maintenance memberships.

pros_detail.title: 14-day free trial with no credit card
pros_detail.explanation: Run real jobs through the system end to end before committing. No credit card required to start. Use the trial seriously rather than just clicking around.

pros_detail.title: Live phone and chat support on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: The pricing page lists live phone and chat support on all plans, not just the top tier.

cons_detail.title: Card fees are Housecall Pro's rates
cons_detail.explanation: Card processing starts at 2.59% per transaction. Compare it at your volume with a standalone processor (Stripe publishes 2.9% + 30 cents for online card payments), and check what instant payouts cost.

cons_detail.title: Key features sit on higher plans
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online sync, flat-rate pricing and GPS tracking start on Essentials; recurring service plans, route optimization and API access are Max-only. Map the features you need to a plan before you compare prices.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Desktop sync is one way
cons_detail.explanation: The QuickBooks Desktop integration (US Windows versions, through the Web Connector) syncs one way from Housecall Pro to QuickBooks. Changes made in QuickBooks are overwritten on the next sync, and edits to imported jobs don't sync.

cons_detail.title: User limits per plan
cons_detail.explanation: Plans include 1, 5 and 8 users, and Max charges $35 a month for each additional user. Price your actual headcount, and the plan it forces you onto, before you commit.

cons_detail.title: Residential-first
cons_detail.explanation: Housecall Pro is built around residential service calls. Commercial contractors that need project tracking, progress billing or AIA billing should look at platforms built for commercial work, such as BuildOps.

tools.implementation_notes: Housecall Pro is set up for self-service, and the Max plan includes dedicated onboarding. A small shop can typically be running jobs within a couple of weeks: import customers by CSV, configure services and prices, set up payments, and train the team on the mobile apps (iOS and Android, in English and Spanish). Run it alongside your old system for a few weeks before cutting over. Consumer financing needs a separate Wisetack application, and the Google Local Services booking integration requires your business to be Google Guaranteed, so start both early.

tool_faqs.q: Is Housecall Pro better than Jobber for HVAC?
tool_faqs.a: Both cover the core workflow and both offer Wisetack consumer financing on quotes, and both integrate with Google Local Services Ads. Housecall Pro includes review management on every plan. Compare which features sit on the plan your team size needs, then run the same week of jobs through both 14-day trials.

tool_faqs.q: What's included in Housecall Pro's payments?
tool_faqs.a: In-app card processing from 2.59% per transaction on every plan, instant payouts, and consumer financing through Wisetack. Check the current rate card for ACH and instant-payout fees before you compare it with a standalone processor.

tool_faqs.q: Does Housecall Pro work for commercial trade work?
tool_faqs.a: Not well. Housecall Pro is residential-first. If most of your work is commercial (project tracking, progress billing, AIA billing), look at platforms built for commercial contractors, such as BuildOps or ServiceTitan.

tool_faqs.q: How long is the contract?
tool_faqs.a: Every plan can be billed monthly or annually, and annual billing is cheaper ($59 instead of $79 a month on Basic). The 14-day free trial needs no credit card.

tool_faqs.q: What happens if I outgrow Housecall Pro?
tool_faqs.a: If you need deeper reporting, multi-location controls or commercial project features, compare Max with platforms such as ServiceTitan or BuildOps in a demo before you migrate.

tools.best_for: Established residential and commercial trades businesses with larger teams that want depth in dispatch, marketing attribution and reporting
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (per-technician pricing, quoted on request)
tools.long_description:
ServiceTitan is an all-in-one software platform for trades contractors (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, garage door, roofing and more), built for established shops with office staff and several technicians. It was incorporated in 2007, as LinxLogic, by Ara Mahdessian and Vahe Kuzoyan, the sons of trades business owners, and later took the ServiceTitan name. Its annual report counts approximately 10,800 active customers as of January 31, 2026.

What sets ServiceTitan apart isn't any single feature: it's the integrated depth. Beyond scheduling, dispatching and invoicing, ServiceTitan adds flat-rate pricebooks that can pull supplier price changes through Pricebook Connect; Marketing Pro, which ties calls, booked jobs and revenue back to the campaign, ad group or keyword; Dispatch Pro, which assigns jobs using technician skills, location, recent sales performance and conversion rates; payroll and commission management; in-app consumer financing (GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance); and KPI reporting. Several of these are separately named "Pro" products, so confirm which ones your quote includes.

The trade-off is significant: ServiceTitan publishes no prices. Its pricing page says pricing is per technician, and every package shows 'Request Pricing', so you need a written quote for your team size. ServiceTitan does not publish an implementation timeline, so ask for a go-live date in writing. Smaller shops that won't use that depth can compare tools that publish their prices, such as Jobber (Core from $29 a month billed annually, 1 user) or Housecall Pro (Basic, $59 a month billed annually, 1 user).

pros_detail.title: Marketing attribution down to the ad keyword
pros_detail.explanation: ServiceTitan's call-tracking integration with Google Ads, Facebook, and inbound channels attributes every booked job back to the specific ad that drove the call. This lets you calculate true cost-per-job by source and shift budget between channels with booked-job data.

pros_detail.title: Pricebook Pro automates flat-rate pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Every job gets the same price for the same work regardless of which technician runs it. Pricebook Pro updates pricing automatically when material costs change, generates upsell suggestions on-screen during tech visits, and ensures techs don't undercharge under customer pressure.

pros_detail.title: AI dispatcher with skill and history matching
pros_detail.explanation: The dispatching engine recommends the optimal tech for each call based on certifications, historical close rate on that job type, current location, and drive time. Especially valuable for shops running 10+ techs where manual dispatching becomes a bottleneck during peak hours.

pros_detail.title: Deep membership and maintenance plan management
pros_detail.explanation: Recurring maintenance plans (service agreements) get first-class treatment: automated billing, renewal reminders, technician notifications when a member calls, plan-level pricing differentiation.

pros_detail.title: Built-in consumer financing (GreenSky, Financeit, Service Finance)
pros_detail.explanation: In-app financing offers for high-ticket repairs (replacements, full system installs), so customers see monthly payment options at the moment of decision rather than after they've slept on it. ServiceTitan's help center documents GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance integrations.

pros_detail.title: KPI reporting with technician and CSR scorecards
pros_detail.explanation: ServiceTitan's reporting tracks revenue and trends by day, week or month; its technician scorecard shows revenue generated and memberships sold for each tech, and its CSR scorecard shows incoming calls and conversions. If you're planning to sell or have outside investors, check that these reports cover what they ask for.

cons_detail.title: Pricing is custom-quoted with no public floor
cons_detail.explanation: ServiceTitan publishes no prices. Its pricing page says pricing is per technician, and every package shows 'Request Pricing'. The lack of transparency makes it impossible to budget without going through their sales process.

cons_detail.title: No published implementation timeline
cons_detail.explanation: ServiceTitan does not publish an implementation timeline. Ask for the onboarding steps, a go-live date and any implementation fee in writing before you sign, and plan who in your office will run the project.

cons_detail.title: A broad mobile app to learn
cons_detail.explanation: The mobile app covers work orders, parts ordering, time tracking, customer communication and payment collection, so plan training time for technicians before you switch.

cons_detail.title: Overkill for small shops
cons_detail.explanation: If your team won't use marketing attribution, pricebooks, payroll and advanced dispatch, you pay for depth you don't need. Jobber (from $29 a month billed annually) and Housecall Pro (from $59 a month billed annually) cover the core workflows at published prices; ServiceTitan's pricing is per technician and quoted on request.

cons_detail.title: Commercial work is supported but not specialized
cons_detail.explanation: ServiceTitan is built for residential. If you're 50%+ commercial mechanical or commercial HVAC, BuildOps is purpose-built for that work and handles project tracking, sub-contractor management, and progress billing better.

cons_detail.title: Check the contract terms
cons_detail.explanation: Ask whether the contract auto-renews and whether features added mid-contract carry new fees. Read the contract carefully before signing; a multi-year commitment reduces your leverage if the product direction changes or you outgrow it.

tools.implementation_notes: ServiceTitan does not publish an implementation timeline. Ask for the onboarding steps, a go-live date and any implementation fee in writing before you sign; its onboarding page says you get your own customer success manager after you go live. Plan for these steps in order. Data migration: clean up and import customer records, equipment history, recurring service agreements and historical work orders. Pricebook setup: if you hire a pricebook consultant, get that fee quoted. Office staff training and a parallel run, where dispatchers and CSRs learn the new system while the old one stays running; marketing attribution (Google Ads, call tracking) gets configured in this window. Then field technicians move onto the mobile app. Don't cut over the old system until every tech is using the mobile app for active work.

tool_faqs.q: Is ServiceTitan worth the price?
tool_faqs.a: It can be for larger shops that will use its depth. Marketing attribution lets you shift ad budget between campaigns based on booked-job data, Pricebook Pro standardizes flat-rate pricing, and built-in financing helps close high-ticket jobs. ServiceTitan's pricing page claims customers see a 15% average yearly increase in revenue; that is the vendor's figure, not an independent one. Smaller shops that won't use those features can compare tools that publish their prices, such as Jobber (from $29 a month billed annually at the smallest team size) or Housecall Pro (from $59 a month billed annually); ServiceTitan's pricing is per technician and quoted on request.

tool_faqs.q: How long is the contract?
tool_faqs.a: Ask ServiceTitan for the term length, whether it auto-renews and whether a longer term changes the price. A multi-year term reduces your leverage if the product direction changes or you outgrow it. Always negotiate cancellation terms and price-lock provisions before signing, and ask whether fees can rise automatically during the term.

tool_faqs.q: Can ServiceTitan replace my existing accounting software?
tool_faqs.a: No. ServiceTitan integrates with QuickBooks and Sage for accounting but isn't an accounting platform itself. It syncs transactions to your accounting system rather than replacing it; its integrations page lists QuickBooks Online and Desktop, Sage Intacct, Sage 50, NetSuite, Xero, Acumatica and Viewpoint, among others. You keep that system for the general ledger and tax reporting.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between ServiceTitan and BuildOps?
tool_faqs.a: Both serve residential and commercial trades but with different priorities. ServiceTitan is residential-first with deep features for inbound calls, marketing attribution, and consumer financing. BuildOps is commercial-first with deeper project tracking, sub-contractor management, and progress billing. If you're 50%+ residential service work, ServiceTitan fits better. If you're 50%+ commercial mechanical or commercial HVAC, BuildOps is the right choice.

tool_faqs.q: Can I try ServiceTitan before signing a contract?
tool_faqs.a: No free trial. You'll need to go through their sales process, which starts with a discovery call to assess fit. Ask for a guided demo with your real data (or sample data from a similar-sized shop) rather than just a generic product tour, and talk to current customers in your vertical and team size; ServiceTitan can connect you with reference contractors.

tools.best_for: On-demand service businesses (locksmiths, garage door, junk removal, appliance repair)
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing; built around inbound, same-day calls rather than recurring scheduled work; short 7-day trial; AI features depend on plan or add-ons
tools.long_description:
Workiz is field service software for on-demand service businesses, founded in 2015 in San Diego by Idan Kadosh, Erez Marom and Saar Kohanovitch; Kadosh and Marom had worked as locksmiths, and the product grew out of that same-day work. It serves locksmiths, garage door, junk removal and appliance repair businesses as well as HVAC, plumbing and electrical, and it raised a $5 million Series A in 2019 and a $13 million Series B in 2021.

The product treats the inbound phone call as the center of the workflow. Genius Phone transcribes and summarizes calls and pulls job details from them, and Genius Answering (an AI assistant called Jessica) answers missed calls and turns them into scheduled jobs. Lead integrations bring in work from Google Local Services Ads and Reserve with Google, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp, and payments run through Stripe, with Sunbit for customer financing.

Workiz no longer publishes prices: its Standard, Pro and Ultimate plans are quoted on request, annual billing is cheaper than monthly, and plans differ by automation count, Genius AI features, service plans, inventory and API access. There is a 7-day free trial with no credit card. Shops whose work is mostly scheduled maintenance and recurring service agreements should compare platforms built around the calendar.

pros_detail.title: Built for on-demand service
pros_detail.explanation: Founded by former locksmiths, Workiz is designed around businesses where customers call and want service the same day: locksmiths, garage door, junk removal, appliance repair, emergency plumbing.

pros_detail.title: AI call handling
pros_detail.explanation: Genius Phone transcribes and summarizes calls and extracts job details; Genius Answering answers missed calls in English, Spanish or French, can live-transfer to your team, and books jobs. Check which plan or add-on your quote includes.

pros_detail.title: Lead-source integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Leads from Google Local Services Ads and Reserve with Google, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp flow into Workiz, which suits trades that rely on those channels.

pros_detail.title: Payments and financing
pros_detail.explanation: Payments are operated by Stripe, with Sunbit for customer financing, so collecting on the spot doesn't need a separate processor.

pros_detail.title: Service plans and price book
pros_detail.explanation: Recurring service plans and a price book (with a Pro version) are available for shops that also sell maintenance work.

pros_detail.title: Free trial with no credit card
pros_detail.explanation: The 7-day trial needs no credit card. Plan your test calls and jobs in advance so you can run them end to end in that window.

cons_detail.title: Built around inbound calls
cons_detail.explanation: Workiz is designed around inbound, same-day work. If most of your jobs are scheduled weeks out under maintenance agreements, compare platforms built around the calendar before committing.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: All three plans are quoted on request, so you need a sales conversation to get a number.

cons_detail.title: Short trial
cons_detail.explanation: The free trial is 7 days, half the 14 days Jobber and Housecall Pro offer.

cons_detail.title: Features vary by plan and add-on
cons_detail.explanation: Automation counts, Genius AI features, service plans, inventory and API access vary by plan, and some Genius features are add-ons. Get them itemized in the quote.

tools.implementation_notes: Workiz is set up for self-service onboarding. The main work is on the call side: port or connect your phone numbers, set up call handling and Genius Answering, connect your lead sources (Google Local Services, Angi, Thumbtack, Yelp), then train dispatchers on the inbound call workflow. Field tech training is lighter, since the mobile app is mainly for accepting jobs, updating status and taking payment. If you are moving from a calendar-first platform, expect to rethink how jobs enter the system, because Workiz starts from the call.

tool_faqs.q: Is Workiz only for locksmiths?
tool_faqs.a: No. Its founders were locksmiths and it is built for on-demand work generally (garage door, junk removal, appliance repair, emergency plumbing), and it also markets to HVAC, plumbing and electrical. Shops whose work is mostly scheduled maintenance should compare calendar-first platforms.

tool_faqs.q: What's Genius Answering?
tool_faqs.a: Workiz's AI answering assistant (named Jessica). It answers the calls you miss, handles inbox messages from email, SMS, web forms and lead sources, supports English, Spanish and French, can live-transfer to your team, and turns calls into scheduled jobs. Pricing is quote-based, so ask which plan or add-on includes it.

tool_faqs.q: Can Workiz replace my CSR team?
tool_faqs.a: Partially. AI answering covers missed calls, after-hours and overflow; complex calls, custom quotes and first-time customers still benefit from people. Plan on using it alongside a human team rather than instead of one.

tool_faqs.q: Does Workiz work for HVAC or plumbing?
tool_faqs.a: Workiz markets to HVAC and plumbing, and its call-handling features suit emergency-heavy work. If you mostly run maintenance plans and scheduled tune-ups, compare it with calendar-first platforms.

tool_faqs.q: How does Workiz handle Google Local Services Ads?
tool_faqs.a: Workiz integrates with Google Local Services Ads and Reserve with Google, so leads and bookings from Google flow into Workiz alongside Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp leads.

tools.name: FieldEdge
tools.tagline: Service management built for HVAC, plumbing, and electrical

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing: all three plans (Select, Premier, Elite) say "Request Pricing", and FieldEdge says price depends on how many technicians or employees you have and which add-ons you choose. The plans include 2, 4 and 6 mobile app licenses. FieldEdge does not offer a free trial. Verified against fieldedge.com/pricing 2026-09-26.

tools.best_for: HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors who run QuickBooks and want service agreements and flat-rate pricing
tools.weaknesses: HVAC, plumbing and electrical focus only; no published pricing and no free trial; plans include a small number of mobile licenses
tools.long_description:
FieldEdge is a field service management platform built specifically for HVAC, plumbing, and electrical contractors, known above all for its QuickBooks integration. Tracing its history to Coastal Computer Corporation, founded in Fort Myers in 1980 (renamed dESCO in 2006 and FieldEdge in 2017, and part of Xplor since Clearent and TSG merged to create it in 2021), the platform has long been sold to contractors who keep QuickBooks as their accounting system.

The QuickBooks integration is the central differentiator. FieldEdge markets it as real-time and two-way, and calls it the only real-time sync between QuickBooks and a field service platform (that is FieldEdge's claim, not an independent test). Field and office transactions post to QuickBooks as they happen, which matters for shops whose accountants live in QuickBooks, including Desktop users.

FieldEdge publishes no prices: its three plans (Select, Premier, and Elite) are quoted after a demo, and FieldEdge says the price depends on team size and add-ons. The platform covers scheduling and dispatching, invoicing, service agreements with renewal and billing automation, a pricebook with flat-rate pricing, lead-source tracking for incoming calls, consumer financing through GreenSky and the Optimus marketplace, and mobile field workflows.

The trade-off: FieldEdge is built for HVAC, plumbing and electrical, not for multi-trade shops that also do landscaping or cleaning.

pros_detail.title: Real-time QuickBooks integration
pros_detail.explanation: FieldEdge markets a real-time, two-way QuickBooks integration and calls it the only one of its kind among field service platforms (a vendor claim). Transactions sync as they happen rather than in batches, which suits shops whose accountants run QuickBooks, including Desktop.

pros_detail.title: Built specifically for HVAC, plumbing, and electrical
pros_detail.explanation: Trade-specific workflows: a pricebook with flat-rate pricing, service agreement management, and service history, aimed at the three core residential trades.

pros_detail.title: Lead-source tracking on calls
pros_detail.explanation: Unique phone numbers identify the lead source of every incoming call, so you can connect marketing spend to the revenue each channel produces.

pros_detail.title: Consumer financing through GreenSky and Optimus
pros_detail.explanation: FieldEdge partners with GreenSky and the Optimus financing marketplace, so techs can offer monthly payment options on high-ticket jobs such as system replacements.

pros_detail.title: Long track record
pros_detail.explanation: FieldEdge traces its history to Coastal Computer Corporation, founded in Fort Myers in 1980 (dESCO from 2006, FieldEdge from 2017), and has been part of Xplor since 2021.

pros_detail.title: Onboarding and support in every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes an onboarding specialist. Support is chat on Select, email or phone on Premier, and a dedicated customer success representative on Elite. The plans include 2, 4, and 6 mobile app licenses, so larger crews should ask how additional licenses are priced.

cons_detail.title: HVAC/plumbing/electrical only, not multi-vertical
cons_detail.explanation: Not designed for landscaping, cleaning, pest control, or other trades outside the core three. Multi-vertical shops need to look at Jobber, Housecall Pro, or specialty platforms for the other trades.

cons_detail.title: Custom-quoted pricing with no public floor
cons_detail.explanation: FieldEdge publishes no prices; every plan says "Request Pricing", and the price depends on team size and add-ons. You need a demo call to get a number, which makes initial budgeting harder than with published-price competitors.

cons_detail.title: No free trial
cons_detail.explanation: FieldEdge does not offer a free trial, so evaluation runs through a demo rather than your own jobs.

cons_detail.title: Few mobile licenses per plan
cons_detail.explanation: Select, Premier and Elite include 2, 4 and 6 mobile app licenses. Larger crews should get the price of additional licenses in writing.

tools.implementation_notes: Every FieldEdge plan includes an onboarding specialist. Get the QuickBooks integration right first: agree the setup with your accountant before going live with anything else. Then import customers and equipment history, configure the pricebook and service agreements, train office staff on dispatching and invoicing, and roll the mobile app out to technicians in waves, most comfortable first. Plan a few weeks of parallel running with your old system before cutting over; shops moving from QuickBooks-only operations face the bigger change, because techs are adopting new workflows.

tool_faqs.q: Is FieldEdge worth it for a QuickBooks Desktop shop?
tool_faqs.a: It is one of the strongest candidates. FieldEdge markets a real-time, two-way QuickBooks integration, and it supports Desktop as well as Online, so an HVAC, plumbing or electrical shop can keep its accountant's setup. Confirm the Desktop setup and any server requirements in the demo.

tool_faqs.q: How does FieldEdge compare to ServiceTitan?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceTitan offers more depth in marketing attribution, pricebook tools and reporting for larger shops. FieldEdge centers on its QuickBooks integration and HVAC, plumbing and electrical workflows. Neither publishes prices, so get written quotes from both and compare them against the features you will actually use.

tool_faqs.q: Does FieldEdge handle commercial HVAC work?
tool_faqs.a: FieldEdge is built mainly for residential HVAC, plumbing and electrical. If most of your work is commercial mechanical, look at platforms built for commercial contractors, such as BuildOps.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between FieldEdge and Sera Systems?
tool_faqs.a: Both target HVAC, plumbing and electrical shops. FieldEdge has a long track record (history back to 1980) and centers on its QuickBooks integration; Sera is newer (out of beta in early 2022), publishes its pricing, and builds in marketing attribution. Pick on QuickBooks needs and on a side-by-side demo.

tool_faqs.q: Can FieldEdge handle membership and maintenance plans?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. FieldEdge's service agreement tools track renewals, billing cycles and scheduled visits in one place, and automate reminders and invoices.

tools.name: ServiceTrade
tools.tagline: Commercial service contractor platform

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote: the Select, Premium and Enterprise suites all show 'Request pricing'. ServiceTrade prices mainly by technician count, plus the suite you choose, and every suite includes unlimited office users. Verified against servicetrade.com/pricing 2026-10-08.

tools.best_for: Commercial HVAC/refrigeration/fire-life-safety contractors with recurring service agreements
tools.weaknesses: Not designed for residential; plan training time on its service-agreement and deficiency workflows
tools.long_description:
ServiceTrade is field service software for commercial service contractors (commercial HVAC, refrigeration, fire and life safety, plumbing and other building services) whose business runs on recurring service agreements. It was founded in 2012 by Billy Marshall and Brian Smithwick and is based in Durham, North Carolina.

What separates it from general FSM is how it models commercial service. Service agreements generate scheduled visits, every piece of equipment at every site has its own service history, and deficiencies found on inspections and maintenance visits are recorded and turned into quotes, with photos and AI-assisted summaries, for the customer to approve. The Service Portal gives facility managers their work history, asset details, upcoming visits, quotes awaiting approval, invoices and job documents.

ServiceTrade publishes no prices: its Select, Premium and Enterprise suites are quoted, pricing is driven mainly by the number of technicians, and every suite includes an unlimited number of office users. The accounting integrations are broad for an FSM platform: QuickBooks (Online, Online Advanced and Desktop), Sage Intacct and Sage 100, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, Acumatica, Vista, Trimble Spectrum and ComputerEase, plus Avalara for tax and Zapier.

The trade-off: ServiceTrade is built for commercial work. Residential service operations would pay for features they won't use and miss homeowner-focused ones.

pros_detail.title: Built around commercial service agreements
pros_detail.explanation: Service agreements generate scheduled visits and recurring work, the way commercial maintenance contracts actually run, instead of forcing them into residential job templates.

pros_detail.title: Deficiencies turned into quotes
pros_detail.explanation: Deficiencies recorded on inspections and maintenance visits become quotes, with photos and AI-assisted summaries, that customers can approve.

pros_detail.title: Asset-level service history
pros_detail.explanation: Every piece of equipment at every customer site has its own record and service history, which commercial facility work depends on.

pros_detail.title: Service Portal for facility managers
pros_detail.explanation: Customers see work history, asset details, upcoming visits, quotes awaiting approval, invoices and job documents in one portal.

pros_detail.title: Broad accounting integrations
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks (Online, Online Advanced, Desktop), Sage Intacct, Sage 100, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, Acumatica, Vista, Trimble Spectrum and ComputerEase, which suits commercial contractors with heavier accounting needs.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited office users
pros_detail.explanation: ServiceTrade says pricing is driven mainly by the number of technicians, and every suite includes an unlimited number of office users, so your plan does not cap dispatchers and admins.

cons_detail.title: Commercial-only (wrong fit for residential)
cons_detail.explanation: Residential service contractors won't use service agreements, deficiency workflows or asset-level histories the way commercial shops do. Residential-focused operations should evaluate Housecall Pro, FieldEdge or ServiceTitan instead.

cons_detail.title: Plan training time for non-commercial teams
cons_detail.explanation: If your office staff come from residential FSM, budget training time for the service-agreement and deficiency workflows.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: All three suites say "Request Pricing", so you need a sales conversation to get a number for your technician count.

cons_detail.title: No free trial
cons_detail.explanation: Evaluation runs through demos with the sales team rather than a self-serve trial.

cons_detail.title: Migrating agreements takes work
cons_detail.explanation: Moving service agreements and building the asset library are the longest steps in a commercial rollout, especially coming from a platform that models jobs rather than agreements.

tools.implementation_notes: Treat a commercial rollout as a project. Configure the system and import customers and properties first, then migrate service agreements (the hardest step, because agreement data rarely maps cleanly between platforms), then build the asset library, since every piece of equipment at every site needs a record. Train office staff on agreements and the deficiency-to-quote workflow, then field techs on the mobile app and deficiency capture, and finally launch the Service Portal to customers and connect your accounting system.

tool_faqs.q: Can ServiceTrade handle residential service operations?
tool_faqs.a: Technically yes, but it's the wrong fit. ServiceTrade's core features (service agreements, deficiency tracking, asset hierarchies, facility-manager portals) are built for commercial workflows. Residential operations should evaluate Housecall Pro, FieldEdge, ServiceTitan, or Jobber instead. Mixed residential-commercial operations typically run two platforms or compromise with general FSM.

tool_faqs.q: How does ServiceTrade compare to ServiceTitan?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceTrade is built for commercial service contractors with recurring agreements, deficiency workflows and a facility-manager portal. ServiceTitan serves residential and commercial trades with deeper marketing and residential sales tools. Neither publishes prices, so get written quotes from both. For commercial-only service work, ServiceTrade is the more focused fit; for mixed residential and commercial work, ServiceTitan covers both.

tool_faqs.q: What's the deficiency-tracking workflow?
tool_faqs.a: Field techs record deficiencies during inspections and maintenance visits (failed equipment, code issues, recommended replacements). ServiceTrade turns them into quotes, with photos and AI-assisted summaries, that facility managers can review and approve, including through the Service Portal.

tool_faqs.q: Does ServiceTrade integrate with Sage Intacct or NetSuite?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. ServiceTrade integrates with Sage Intacct and NetSuite (syncing customers, items, jobs, AR invoices, payments and clock events), and also with QuickBooks, Sage 100, Microsoft Dynamics, Acumatica, Vista, Trimble Spectrum and ComputerEase.

tool_faqs.q: Is ServiceTrade worth it for a 20-tech commercial HVAC operation?
tool_faqs.a: It is built for exactly that kind of shop. Pricing is driven mainly by technician count, and every suite includes an unlimited number of office users, so get a written quote for your 20 technicians and weigh it against the time your office spends on agreements, deficiency follow-up and customer updates today.

tools.tagline: All-in-one field service software

pricing.pricing_note: Flat per-company pricing with unlimited users at every tier: Starter $208/mo, Plus $325/mo, Pro $533/mo billed annually ($245/$382/$627 month-to-month). Verified against servicefusion.com/pricing 2026-09-10.

tools.best_for: Growing service businesses that want unlimited users on a flat monthly price
tools.weaknesses: Higher entry price than per-seat plans for small teams; inventory, job costing and integrated voice start on Plus; GPS tracking and some document features are add-ons; no free trial listed
tools.long_description:
Service Fusion is field service management software founded in 2014 and based in Irving, Texas; EverCommerce acquired it in December 2020. Its differentiator is pricing: every plan includes unlimited users, for a flat $208, $325 or $533 a month billed annually ($245, $382 or $627 month-to-month).

That flat price changes the math as a team grows. Jobber and Housecall Pro price by team size or charge for users beyond each plan's allowance, so Service Fusion costs more than they do for a small team and can cost less for a large one. Price your own headcount on each vendor's current pricing page before deciding; the crossover depends on which plans you'd need.

Starter covers customer management, estimates, scheduling and dispatching, invoicing, integrated payments, QuickBooks integration, reporting and text messaging. Plus adds inventory management, job costing, job photos and integrated voice and text; Pro adds an open API, eSign and custom documents, a customer web portal and progressive billing. GPS fleet tracking and the ServiceCall.ai call tracker are add-ons, and homeowner financing runs through Acorn Finance inside estimates, jobs and invoices.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes unlimited users at a flat monthly price, so adding technicians doesn't raise the bill. For larger teams that can undercut per-seat pricing; price your own headcount to check.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online and Desktop
pros_detail.explanation: Service Fusion integrates with both QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop: invoices and payments created in Service Fusion sync to QuickBooks, and customer records stay aligned. Useful if your accountant still runs Desktop.

pros_detail.title: Voice, text and call tracking
pros_detail.explanation: Plus adds integrated voice and text, and the ServiceCall.ai add-on records and transcribes calls and tracks call reasons and outcomes.

pros_detail.title: Core workflow on the entry plan
pros_detail.explanation: Starter ($208/month billed annually) already includes scheduling and dispatching, estimates, invoicing, integrated payments, QuickBooks integration, reporting and text messaging.

pros_detail.title: Homeowner financing through Acorn Finance
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can apply for financing while reviewing estimates, jobs or invoices, and Service Fusion advertises $0 dealer fees for the contractor.

pros_detail.title: Progressive billing and eSign on Pro
pros_detail.explanation: Pro adds progressive billing, eSign and custom documents and a customer web portal, useful for larger or project-style jobs.

cons_detail.title: Higher entry price for small teams
cons_detail.explanation: Starter is $208/mo billed annually ($245 month-to-month), several times Jobber Core ($29/mo billed annually). The flat price only pays off once your team is large enough; solo and very small shops are usually cheaper on per-seat plans.

cons_detail.title: Key features sit on Plus, Pro or add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: Inventory, job costing and integrated voice start on Plus; eSign, the customer portal and progressive billing are Pro features or add-ons; GPS fleet tracking is an add-on. Price the plan and add-ons you'll actually use.

cons_detail.title: No free trial listed
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page doesn't list a self-serve free trial, so expect to evaluate it through a demo.

tools.implementation_notes: Service Fusion advertises personalized onboarding. Plan the usual phases: import customers and data (CSV or QuickBooks), configure services, pricing and workflows, train office staff on dispatching and invoicing, then train field techs on the mobile app and run in parallel with your old system before cutting over. If you add integrated voice or ServiceCall.ai, number porting and call-flow setup add time; if you use QuickBooks, agree the sync settings with your accountant before the first sync.

tool_faqs.q: When does Service Fusion become cheaper than Jobber or Housecall Pro?
tool_faqs.a: Once your team is big enough that the others' team-size pricing passes Service Fusion's flat fee. Service Fusion is $208, $325 or $533 a month billed annually with unlimited users; Jobber prices plans by team size, and Housecall Pro includes 1, 5 or 8 users per plan, with extra users on Max at $35 a month. Price your actual headcount on each current pricing page, since the crossover depends on which plan you'd need.

tool_faqs.q: Does Service Fusion work for solo contractors?
tool_faqs.a: Technically yes, but the math rarely favors it. Starter is $245/mo month-to-month ($208/mo billed annually), about five times Jobber Core's month-to-month price ($49/mo). Solo contractors and very small shops are usually better served by per-seat plans.

tool_faqs.q: Does Service Fusion work with QuickBooks Desktop?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Service Fusion supports both QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Online. Invoices and payments created in Service Fusion sync to QuickBooks, and customer records stay aligned between the two systems.

tool_faqs.q: Can I add unlimited techs without paying more?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Every plan includes unlimited users. Plus and Pro add features (inventory, job costing, voice, eSign, customer portal, progressive billing), not seats.

tool_faqs.q: How does Service Fusion compare to ServiceTitan?
tool_faqs.a: They serve different buyers. ServiceTitan publishes no prices (its pricing page says pricing is per technician) and sells deep marketing attribution, pricebook and dispatch tools to larger shops. Service Fusion publishes flat pricing ($208-$533/mo billed annually) with unlimited users for shops that want the core workflow without per-seat costs.

tools.name: BuildOps
tools.tagline: All-in-one platform for commercial subcontractors

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote only; BuildOps publishes no prices. Quotes depend on company size, modules (service, project or both) and integrations.

tools.best_for: Commercial mechanical, electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors running both service and project work
tools.weaknesses: Built for commercial work, not residential; no published pricing; rolling out service and project workflows is a phased project
tools.long_description:
BuildOps is an operations platform for commercial contractors (mechanical, electrical, plumbing, HVAC and other specialty trades that work on commercial buildings), founded in 2018 and based in Los Angeles. In March 2025 it raised a $127 million Series C led by Meritech Capital Partners at a $1 billion valuation; earlier backers include Founders Fund, 01A and B Capital.

It combines service and project work in one system. The service side covers scheduling and dispatch, service agreements and recurring maintenance, and asset records with service history, specs and warranty data for every unit. The project side covers project management, materials and subcontract change orders, and billing: time and materials, fixed price, progress billing, AIA pay applications, service agreement billing and milestone billing. OpsAI, its AI layer, handles smart dispatch, turns technician voice notes into structured field notes and scans purchase orders.

BuildOps publishes no prices; quotes depend on company size, modules and integrations. It connects to accounting and ERP systems including QuickBooks, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Viewpoint Spectrum and Viewpoint Vista.

The trade-off: BuildOps is built for commercial work. Residential service shops fit better on ServiceTitan, Jobber or Housecall Pro, and general contractors managing every trade on a project fit better on Procore.

pros_detail.title: Built for commercial trade contractors
pros_detail.explanation: Designed around commercial mechanical, electrical, plumbing and HVAC work rather than residential service calls or general construction.

pros_detail.title: Service and project work in one platform
pros_detail.explanation: Commercial trade contractors often run both project work (installations, buildouts) and service work (maintenance contracts). BuildOps handles both, so you don't need two systems.

pros_detail.title: Commercial billing, including AIA pay apps
pros_detail.explanation: Supports time-and-materials, fixed-price, progress, milestone and service agreement billing, plus AIA-format pay applications.

pros_detail.title: Asset history on every unit
pros_detail.explanation: Service history, specs and warranty data are tracked per unit, so techs arrive at a rooftop unit or chiller with its history in hand.

pros_detail.title: Service agreements and recurring maintenance
pros_detail.explanation: Recurring maintenance workflows and service agreement billing are built in, which suits commercial maintenance contracts.

pros_detail.title: OpsAI
pros_detail.explanation: AI tools for smart dispatch, turning technician voice notes into structured field notes, and scanning purchase orders.

pros_detail.title: ERP integrations
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Viewpoint Spectrum and Viewpoint Vista integrations keep job costs aligned with accounting.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: BuildOps publishes no prices, so get a written quote that itemizes modules, integrations and any implementation fees, and compare it with ServiceTitan and other commercial platforms.

cons_detail.title: Phased implementation
cons_detail.explanation: Rolling out both service and project workflows is a phased project that needs an internal lead from operations. BuildOps doesn't publish a timeline, so ask for the plan in writing.

cons_detail.title: Wrong fit for residential trades
cons_detail.explanation: BuildOps is built for commercial work. If you also do residential service, you'll likely need a separate FSM (ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro) for that side.

cons_detail.title: Lien waivers and COIs are manual for now
cons_detail.explanation: Lien waiver and certificate-of-insurance tracking are handled as attachments today; BuildOps says fuller support is planned.

tools.implementation_notes: BuildOps doesn't publish an implementation timeline, and rolling out both service and project work is a phased project. Start by mapping your customer and building structure, importing equipment lists with serial numbers and service history, and setting up project templates; then roll out project workflows, then service workflows to field techs, where cutover risk concentrates. Name an internal owner (an operations lead or project manager) for the whole rollout, and keep historical data in your old systems as an archive rather than migrating all of it.

tool_faqs.q: Is BuildOps better than ServiceTitan for commercial work?
tool_faqs.a: For commercial mechanical, electrical and plumbing work, BuildOps is built for the job: service and project workflows, AIA pay applications and asset history in one system. ServiceTitan is strongest in residential service. If most of your work is commercial, start with BuildOps; if it's mostly residential, start with ServiceTitan.

tool_faqs.q: How does BuildOps compare to Procore?
tool_faqs.a: Procore is general commercial construction, used by GCs, large multi-family, industrial across all trades. BuildOps is MEP-specific (mechanical, electrical, plumbing trades). If you're a commercial GC managing multiple trades on commercial projects, Procore. If you're a commercial MEP trade contractor doing both project work and ongoing service, BuildOps. Some operations run both: Procore for project coordination, BuildOps for trade-specific operations.

tool_faqs.q: Does BuildOps handle residential work?
tool_faqs.a: It isn't built for it. If you do mixed commercial and residential work, you'll likely need a separate FSM (ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro) for the residential side.

tool_faqs.q: What's the typical BuildOps implementation timeline?
tool_faqs.a: BuildOps doesn't publish one. Rolling out both project and service workflows is a phased project, so ask for the implementation plan, the named contacts and any implementation fees in writing before you sign.

tool_faqs.q: How is BuildOps pricing structured?
tool_faqs.a: Custom-quoted. BuildOps publishes no prices; the quote depends on company size, modules (service, project or both) and integrations. Get it in writing, including implementation fees, and compare it with ServiceTitan and other commercial platforms.

tools.name: Knowify
tools.tagline: Construction and contractor management built on QuickBooks

pricing.pricing_note: Core $99/mo billed annually ($149 monthly), 1 user included; Advanced $329/mo billed annually ($399 monthly), 10 users included; additional users $29/mo each on both. Enterprise custom, with unlimited users. Add-ons include Service Pro (dispatching, inventory) and equipment tracking. Free trial on Core and Advanced. Verified against knowify.com/pricing 2026-10-08.

tools.best_for: Trade contractors and subcontractors on QuickBooks who need job costing, change orders and AIA progress billing
tools.weaknesses: Key features (job costing, client portal, subcontracts) start on Advanced and QuickBooks Desktop sync on Enterprise; per-user charges beyond each plan's included users; less homeowner-facing than Buildertrend
tools.long_description:
Knowify is construction and project management software built for trade contractors, especially subcontractors, founded in 2012 in New York by Daniel de Roulet Jr. and Marc Visent. It is built around QuickBooks: with QuickBooks Online, nearly all operational and financial data syncs both ways in real time, and QuickBooks Desktop (on the Enterprise plan) syncs both ways on demand.

Core covers estimates and proposals, fixed-price contracts, scheduling, time tracking, change orders, progress billing and AIA pay applications (G702/G703), payment processing and QuickBooks Online sync. Advanced adds cost-plus and time-and-materials contracts, subcontracts, project budgets, daily logs, work orders, a client portal, custom workflows, job costing with real-time WIP reporting, advanced reporting and Zapier. Enterprise adds RFIs and submittals, document markup, QuickBooks Desktop and Intuit Enterprise Suite integration, and equipment management. A Service Pro add-on brings dispatching and inventory for service work.

Pricing: Core is $99 a month billed annually ($149 monthly) with one user, Advanced $329 ($399 monthly) with ten users, and additional users are $29 a month each; Enterprise is custom-quoted with unlimited users. There is a free trial on Core and Advanced.

The trade-off: Knowify is built for trade contractors' project and financial workflows rather than the homeowner-facing experience, so custom home builders who want selections and a polished homeowner portal should compare Buildertrend.

pros_detail.title: Real-time QuickBooks Online sync
pros_detail.explanation: With QuickBooks Online, nearly all operational and financial data syncs both ways in real time; QuickBooks Desktop syncs both ways on demand on the Enterprise plan.

pros_detail.title: AIA G702/G703 progress billing on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Core already includes progress billing and AIA-format pay applications, which matters for subcontractors billing GCs on commercial-style projects.

pros_detail.title: Change orders tied to the budget
pros_detail.explanation: Change orders are part of the core plan and tie back to the project, instead of living in email and spreadsheets.

pros_detail.title: Job costing and WIP on Advanced
pros_detail.explanation: Advanced adds project budgets, job costing and real-time work-in-progress reporting, so you can see margins before a job closes.

pros_detail.title: Built for subcontractors
pros_detail.explanation: Knowify was built for trade contractors, especially subcontractors, with contract types (fixed price, cost plus, T&M) and subcontracts that fit how they work.

pros_detail.title: Time tracking with job costing
pros_detail.explanation: Field time tracking is on every plan and feeds job costing on Advanced, so labor lands on the right project.

cons_detail.title: Key features sit on higher plans
cons_detail.explanation: Job costing, subcontracts, the client portal and Zapier start on Advanced; QuickBooks Desktop sync, RFIs and submittals are Enterprise features. Map what you need to a plan before comparing prices.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing beyond included seats
cons_detail.explanation: Core includes one user and Advanced ten, with each additional user at $29 a month; only Enterprise includes unlimited users.

cons_detail.title: Less homeowner-facing than Buildertrend
cons_detail.explanation: For custom home work where selections and a homeowner portal matter most, Buildertrend is built more around that experience.

cons_detail.title: Service work needs an add-on
cons_detail.explanation: Dispatching and inventory come with the Service Pro add-on, so contractors running service calls alongside projects should price it in.

tools.implementation_notes: Get the QuickBooks connection right first: agree the setup with your accountant, then import customers and active projects. Next, set up estimates, contract types, change orders and progress billing, and train office staff; then roll out time tracking to field crews and run your first projects alongside your old process before cutting over. Moving from spreadsheets or QuickBooks-only operations, most of the work is adopting structured project workflows that QuickBooks doesn't enforce.

tool_faqs.q: Should I use Knowify or Buildertrend for residential remodeling?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on what matters more. Buildertrend is built around the homeowner-facing experience (selections, client portal) for custom builders and remodelers. Knowify is built for trade contractors and subcontractors that live in QuickBooks and need job costing, change orders and AIA progress billing. Compare both on your own projects.

tool_faqs.q: Does Knowify replace QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: No. Knowify handles projects, change orders, time tracking and progress billing, and syncs with QuickBooks for accounting: QuickBooks Online syncs both ways in real time, and QuickBooks Desktop syncs both ways on demand on the Enterprise plan. Keep QuickBooks for the general ledger, payables, payroll and tax.

tool_faqs.q: How does Knowify handle commercial GC work?
tool_faqs.a: Knowify is aimed at trade contractors and subcontractors on commercial and residential projects, with AIA pay applications on every plan and RFIs and submittals on Enterprise. General contractors running large multi-trade commercial projects should compare Procore.

tool_faqs.q: What's in Knowify's plans?
tool_faqs.a: Core ($99/month billed annually, $149 monthly, 1 user) covers estimates, contracts, scheduling, time tracking, change orders, AIA progress billing, payments and QuickBooks Online sync. Advanced ($329/month billed annually, $399 monthly, 10 users) adds subcontracts, budgets, job costing and WIP, daily logs, a client portal and Zapier. Enterprise (custom, unlimited users) adds RFIs and submittals and QuickBooks Desktop. Extra users are $29/month.

tool_faqs.q: Can I track time directly in QuickBooks instead of Knowify?
tool_faqs.a: You can but you'll lose the job-costing visibility that Knowify provides. Knowify's value is connecting field time tracking to specific project budgets in real-time. QuickBooks Time (formerly TSheets) handles time tracking but doesn't have the project management context. Most Knowify customers use Knowify time tracking and rely on the QB sync for payroll processing.

tools.name: Joist
tools.tagline: Estimating and invoicing app for solo contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Free plan discontinued. Billed annually, as a monthly equivalent that includes 2 months free: Basics $8.34/mo (up to 5 documents/mo), Pro $14.17/mo, Elite $26.67/mo and the new Run plan (adds jobs and scheduling) $58.33/mo, which also includes an introductory 30% off. Billed monthly: Basics $10/mo, Pro $17/mo, Elite $32/mo and Run $70/mo (introductory 30% off its $100/mo list price). Pro has unlimited documents and clients. Monthly plans carry no long-term contract. AI Receptionist add-on from $49/mo, billed monthly. 14-day free trial with access to all Run features, no credit card required. Verified against joist.com/pricing 2026-10-08.

tools.best_for: Solo contractors and small 1-2 person operations needing only estimates and invoicing
tools.weaknesses: Scheduling and jobs only on the new Run plan ($100/mo list, offered at an introductory $58.33/mo billed annually or $70/mo billed monthly); below that it is quote-and-invoice only with no dispatching. Outgrown quickly past 3 techs.
tools.long_description:
Joist is an estimating and invoicing app for solo contractors and small trade businesses, based in Toronto and owned by EverCommerce since 2018. Joist says more than 1.3 million contractors across 20+ industries use it. It focuses on quotes, invoices, payments and signatures, the work an owner-operator does between jobs.

What separates Joist from broader FSM platforms is the narrow focus and low price. Apart from the jobs and scheduling in its Run plan, it doesn't try to handle dispatching or team management. The free plan has been discontinued: Basics is the entry plan (up to 5 documents a month) at $8.34/month billed annually or $10 billed monthly, Pro is $14.17/month billed annually ($17 monthly), Elite $26.67/month ($32 monthly), and Run, which adds jobs and scheduling, lists at $100/month and is offered at an introductory 30% off: $58.33/month billed annually or $70 billed monthly. Even Basics includes online payments through Joist Payments and homeowner financing, with offers from 30+ lenders on estimates.

Pro adds unlimited documents and work orders, and Elite adds change orders, business reports and review management. QuickBooks Online sync is available on Pro, Elite and Run. The 14-day free trial includes all Run features and needs no credit card.

The trade-off: Joist is outgrown as a business adds people. Past two or three people, the lack of dispatching and team management (outside Run) becomes a real limit, and growing operations typically move to Jobber, Housecall Pro or Workiz.

pros_detail.title: Low-cost entry plan
pros_detail.explanation: Basics costs $8.34/month billed annually or $10 billed monthly, for up to 5 documents a month; the old free tier has been discontinued.

pros_detail.title: Simple, inexpensive upgrade path
pros_detail.explanation: Pro at $14.17/month and Elite at $26.67/month billed annually ($17 and $32 billed monthly) keep the upgrade cost small, and the new Run plan adds jobs and scheduling for operations that outgrow quote-and-invoice.

pros_detail.title: Focused feature set works for solo operators
pros_detail.explanation: Estimating + invoicing + payments + signatures is exactly what solo contractors need. No overwhelming feature ladder, no upsell pressure for unused features.

pros_detail.title: Strong mobile experience for field use
pros_detail.explanation: Built mobile-first for solo contractors doing quotes and invoices on-site. Photo attachments, client signatures, payment collection all work cleanly from the mobile app.

pros_detail.title: 14-day free trial
pros_detail.explanation: A 14-day free trial with access to all Run features and no credit card required allows full evaluation, including setting up Joist Payments.

pros_detail.title: Payments and financing on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Joist Payments is built into invoicing even on Basics, and homeowner financing from 30+ lenders can be offered on estimates.

cons_detail.title: Scheduling only on the top plan
cons_detail.explanation: Below the new Run plan ($100/month list; at the introductory 30% off, $58.33/month billed annually or $70 billed monthly), Joist is quote-and-invoice only, with no appointment scheduling or calendar management; Run adds jobs and scheduling. Operations needing scheduling or dispatch should price Run against Jobber, Housecall Pro, or Workiz.

cons_detail.title: No team management features
cons_detail.explanation: Single-user platform design. Past 2-3 person operations, no way to manage team schedules, assign jobs to specific techs, or track multi-user activity.

cons_detail.title: Outgrown as the team grows
cons_detail.explanation: Joist's narrow focus means growing operations move to a broader FSM once they need multi-person scheduling and dispatch.

cons_detail.title: Limited integrations
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online sync (on Pro, Elite and Run) is the main integration; there are no CRM, calendar or parts-management connections.

cons_detail.title: Light marketing and customer tools
cons_detail.explanation: Elite adds review management, but there is no email marketing or full customer portal; active marketers need separate tools.

tools.implementation_notes: Joist takes a day or two to set up. Download the app, enter your business details, logo, services and prices, then send your first estimates and invoices to real customers and switch on Joist Payments. Connect QuickBooks Online if you're on Pro, Elite or Run. Coming from paper there is nothing to import. If you're approaching three or more people who need scheduling, price Joist's Run plan against Jobber or Housecall Pro before you outgrow it.

tool_faqs.q: Does Joist still have a free plan?
tool_faqs.a: No. Joist's free plan is no longer available. Basics is the entry plan (up to 5 documents a month) at $8.34/month billed annually or $10 billed monthly; Pro is $14.17/month billed annually ($17 monthly) and Elite $26.67/month billed annually ($32 monthly). Every user can try Joist with a 14-day free trial that includes all Run features, no credit card required.

tool_faqs.q: How does Joist compare to Jobber or Housecall Pro?
tool_faqs.a: Joist is quote-and-invoice software (its new Run plan adds jobs and scheduling); Jobber and Housecall Pro are full FSM platforms with scheduling, dispatching, team management, and marketing automation. For solo contractors needing only estimates and invoices, Joist costs less: from $8.34/month billed annually ($10 billed monthly), against Jobber from $29/month and Housecall Pro from $59/month, both billed annually. For operations needing scheduling, dispatching, or team management, Jobber or Housecall Pro fit better despite higher cost.

tool_faqs.q: When should I migrate away from Joist?
tool_faqs.a: Typical triggers: hiring your first employee or subcontractor who needs scheduling and dispatch, wanting a customer portal for self-booking, wanting marketing automation, or growing past about three people. Joist's Run plan adds jobs and scheduling, so price Run against Jobber, Housecall Pro or Workiz at that point.

tool_faqs.q: Does Joist integrate with QuickBooks Desktop?
tool_faqs.a: No. Joist syncs with QuickBooks Online (on Pro, Elite and Run). QuickBooks Desktop users would need to move to QuickBooks Online or enter invoices manually, which works at solo-operator scale.

tool_faqs.q: Can Joist handle credit card payments?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Joist Payments is built into invoicing on every plan, including Basics, so customers can pay online and you save a reconciliation step. Homeowner financing from 30+ lenders can also be offered on estimates. Check the current processing rates in the app.

tools.name: Connecteam
tools.tagline: All-in-one workforce management for deskless teams

pricing.pricing_note: Pricing is for first 30 users; scales up after. Free tier is genuinely useful for sub-10-user teams.

tools.best_for: Teams of 10-100 deskless workers needing time tracking + communication + scheduling in one app
tools.weaknesses: Not a full FSM (no quotes, invoicing or customer portal); pair it with Jobber, Housecall Pro or another FSM for customer work
tools.long_description:
Connecteam is a workforce management app for deskless teams, founded in 2016 in Tel Aviv, with an office in New York. It raised a $120 million Series C in 2022 and serves construction, retail, hospitality, healthcare, trades and other industries whose staff work away from a desk. Unlike FSM tools that focus on customer-facing work (dispatching, invoicing, customer portal), Connecteam focuses on the employee side: time clock, scheduling, internal communication, training and documents.

For trades businesses it fills a gap FSM platforms often leave: managing the team itself. The GPS time clock records where techs clock in, shift scheduling handles rotating crews, chat and announcements replace WhatsApp groups, onboarding workflows train new hires, and document storage keeps certifications and licenses in one place. Time data flows to payroll through QuickBooks Online, Gusto, Xero, Paychex and ADP integrations.

Pricing is per hub (Operations, Communications, HR & Skills): a flat monthly price covers the first 30 users, then a small fee per extra user, and the free plan covers up to 10 users with every hub.

The trade-off: Connecteam isn't a full FSM. Most trades shops run it alongside their FSM: Connecteam for the team, the FSM for customers.

pros_detail.title: Free plan for up to 10 users
pros_detail.explanation: The free plan includes every hub and feature for up to 10 users, with no time limit, which covers many small crews.

pros_detail.title: Flat pricing for the first 30 users
pros_detail.explanation: Each hub has a flat monthly price for the first 30 users (Operations Basic from $29), then a small per-user fee, which keeps costs predictable for mid-size crews.

pros_detail.title: GPS-verified time clock
pros_detail.explanation: Techs clock in/out from job sites with GPS verification. Reduces time-theft (clocking in from home, not the job site) and dispute resolution. Critical for trades shops with hourly field workers.

pros_detail.title: In-app chat and announcements
pros_detail.explanation: Replaces WhatsApp/SMS groups for team communication. Searchable history, file sharing, channel organization. Keeps work communication separate from personal phones and creates audit trail.

pros_detail.title: Training and onboarding workflows
pros_detail.explanation: Built-in training modules for safety procedures, equipment use, customer service standards. New hire onboarding paths track completion automatically. Useful for shops with frequent turnover or new-hire compliance requirements.

pros_detail.title: Compliance document storage with expiration alerts
pros_detail.explanation: Centralized storage for tech certifications, licenses, vehicle docs, safety training records. Notifications when documents are expiring. Important for OSHA compliance, EPA Section 608 tracking, state licensing audits.

cons_detail.title: Not a full FSM
cons_detail.explanation: No customer scheduling, no dispatching, no invoicing, no customer portal. Trades shops run Connecteam ALONGSIDE primary FSM (Jobber, Housecall Pro), not as a replacement. Two-platform overhead.

cons_detail.title: Multi-vertical generic focus
cons_detail.explanation: Built for deskless workers across many industries (retail, hospitality, healthcare, construction). Trade-specific workflows (work orders, equipment tracking, pricebook) aren't here. Use trade-specific FSM for those.

cons_detail.title: Scheduling lacks dispatching intelligence
cons_detail.explanation: Shift scheduling is basic: assign techs to time blocks. Doesn't optimize routes, match skills to jobs, or handle on-demand dispatch like Workiz or ServiceTitan. Use a real FSM for dispatch.

cons_detail.title: UI can feel cluttered with many modules
cons_detail.explanation: Lots of modules in the platform (time clock + scheduling + chat + training + forms + documents + payroll). Can feel like a Swiss army knife. Some teams find this overwhelming compared to focused tools.
