tools.implementation_notes: Connecteam is self-service. Invite team members to the app, set up the GPS time clock and job sites, and build scheduling templates for your usual week. Frame the app as replacing WhatsApp groups, not adding another app, when you train field techs. Then set up chat channels, training and onboarding for new hires, and connect payroll (QuickBooks Online, Gusto, Xero, Paychex or ADP) so time data flows without re-keying.

tool_faqs.q: Can Connecteam replace Jobber or Housecall Pro?
tool_faqs.a: No. Connecteam is workforce management, not field service management. It handles the EMPLOYEE side (time clock, scheduling, chat, training, compliance) but lacks the CUSTOMER side (scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, customer portal). Most trades shops run Connecteam alongside their primary FSM. They solve different problems.

tool_faqs.q: How does Connecteam's pricing work?
tool_faqs.a: Each hub (Operations, Communications, HR & Skills) is priced separately. A flat monthly price covers the first 30 users, and each user after that adds a small per-user fee; Operations Basic starts at $29 a month for the first 30 users. The free plan covers up to 10 users with every hub. Price the hubs you'd actually use at your headcount.

tool_faqs.q: How does GPS-verified time clock work?
tool_faqs.a: Techs clock in/out from the mobile app; Connecteam captures GPS coordinates at clock-in/out. Settings can require techs to be within a geofence of an assigned job site before clocking in, or just record location as evidence. Reduces time-theft and helps dispute resolution.

tool_faqs.q: Is Connecteam's free tier really free?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The free plan covers up to 10 users and includes all hubs and features, with no time limit. Larger teams move to a paid plan, priced per hub.

tool_faqs.q: How does Connecteam compare to When I Work or Deputy?
tool_faqs.a: All three handle scheduling and time tracking; Connecteam bundles more in one app (chat, training, documents, forms) across its three hubs. Its pricing is a flat price per hub for the first 30 users plus a per-user fee after that, so compare the hubs you need with per-user alternatives at your headcount.

tools.name: Buildertrend
tools.tagline: Construction project management for builders and remodelers

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote: one subscription with unlimited users, every feature, onboarding and support; optional business services extra. No published tiers (the former Essential / Advanced / Complete plans started at $199/mo). 10% off when paying an annual plan upfront (limited-time offer). Verified against buildertrend.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Custom home builders, remodelers, and specialty contractors running multi-month projects
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (custom quotes); built for residential projects, so overkill for pure service work
tools.long_description:
Buildertrend is construction project management software for residential builders, remodelers and specialty contractors, founded in 2006 in Omaha, Nebraska by Dan Houghton and brothers Jeff and Steve Dugger. It is still based in Omaha and was reported in 2026 to have more than 20,000 customers across 100 countries. In 2021 it acquired CoConstruct, a competing residential construction platform, with a growth investment from Bain Capital Tech Opportunities and HGGC, and moved CoConstruct customers onto Buildertrend.

The product focuses on the homeowner-facing experience as much as the contractor workflow: scheduling, selections for custom work (colors, fixtures, finishes), change orders with homeowner approval, a client portal for schedules, photos and selections, daily logs, subcontractor coordination, budgeting and job costing. It integrates with QuickBooks (Online and Desktop), Xero, Gusto, Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive and The Home Depot.

Buildertrend no longer publishes prices: one custom-quoted subscription includes unlimited users, every feature, onboarding and support, and paying an annual plan upfront currently earns a 10% discount.

The trade-off: Buildertrend is built for residential projects. Commercial GCs, large multi-family and industrial work fit better on Procore, and short service-style jobs fit better on a field service tool.

pros_detail.title: Client portal for homeowners
pros_detail.explanation: Homeowners can follow schedules, photos, selections, change orders and budget updates in one portal, which cuts down on email back-and-forth and helps win custom-home and major-remodel clients.

pros_detail.title: Selections management for custom home work
pros_detail.explanation: Captures and tracks the hundreds of small decisions in a custom home build (paint colors, cabinet finishes, fixture brands, flooring options, hardware). Customers approve selections in the portal; selections drive purchase orders to suppliers. Reduces dispute risk from picked-wrong-product scenarios.

pros_detail.title: Scheduling for multi-month projects
pros_detail.explanation: Project schedules with linked tasks let you see how one trade's delay affects the rest and keep subs informed, which beats spreadsheets on long projects.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users, every feature
pros_detail.explanation: One subscription covers unlimited users and every feature, with onboarding and support included, so you don't pay per seat as the office and crews grow.

pros_detail.title: Change orders with homeowner approval
pros_detail.explanation: Change orders are captured with the homeowner's approval and tied to the project budget, instead of living in email and spreadsheets.

pros_detail.title: Subcontractor coordination
pros_detail.explanation: Subs get schedules, communication and document sharing through the platform, matched to residential projects.

cons_detail.title: Residential-focused only
cons_detail.explanation: Not designed for commercial GCs, large multi-family, or industrial. Procore, BuildOps, or specialty commercial platforms fit those better. Buildertrend's strengths (homeowner-facing portal, selections management) don't apply to commercial work.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Buildertrend quotes each account, so get a written quote and compare it with JobTread, which publishes its price, before committing.

cons_detail.title: Plan training time
cons_detail.explanation: Buildertrend covers a lot (schedules, selections, change orders, budgets, client portal), so plan training time for project managers, office staff and subs.

cons_detail.title: CoConstruct migration history
cons_detail.explanation: Former CoConstruct customers were moved onto Buildertrend after the 2021 acquisition; if you came from CoConstruct, check that the workflows you relied on are covered.

tools.implementation_notes: Onboarding is included in the subscription. Plan the rollout in stages: account and user setup, the accounting integration (QuickBooks or Xero), and importing customers and active projects; then project and selections templates for your common project types, subs with portal access, and office training; then invite homeowners on active projects to the client portal. Start new projects in Buildertrend and leave historical project data in your old system as an archive unless you are coming from CoConstruct.

tool_faqs.q: Should a remodeling business use Jobber or Buildertrend?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on project length and complexity. Short, service-style remodeling jobs fit a field service tool like Jobber. Project-based remodeling (whole-house remodels, additions, kitchens and baths running for weeks) fits Buildertrend, because of schedules, subcontractor coordination, change orders, selections and the client portal.

tool_faqs.q: What happened to CoConstruct?
tool_faqs.a: Buildertrend acquired CoConstruct in February 2021 and moved its customers onto Buildertrend. There is no separate CoConstruct product anymore.

tool_faqs.q: Is Buildertrend worth it for a small remodeling business?
tool_faqs.a: For project-based remodeling with selections, change orders and homeowner communication, it can be. Buildertrend no longer publishes prices, so get a quote (it includes unlimited users) and compare it with JobTread's published pricing before deciding.

tool_faqs.q: How does Buildertrend compare to Procore?
tool_faqs.a: Buildertrend is residential-focused (custom home builders, remodelers, residential GCs). Procore is commercial construction-focused (commercial GCs, large multi-family, industrial). Buildertrend has stronger client portal for homeowner-facing communication and selections management. Procore has stronger sub-coordination, AIA progress billing, and commercial-specific features (BIM, safety modules, quality control). Pick by primary work mix.

tool_faqs.q: Can Buildertrend replace QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: No. Buildertrend handles project management, budgets, change orders and selections, and syncs cost codes, bills, invoices and payments with QuickBooks (Online or Desktop) or Xero. Keep your accounting system for the general ledger, payables and tax.

tools.name: mHelpDesk
tools.tagline: Field service software for small businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote only; mHelpDesk publishes no prices on its site (/pricing returns 404; the Get a Quote link emails support@mhelpdesk.com, or call 888-558-6275). The homepage offers a free trial but states no length. Verified against mhelpdesk.com 2026-10-08.

tools.best_for: Small home-service shops needing QuickBooks-tight FSM
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (custom quote only) and no stated free-trial length; long-established product that newer platforms often out-publish on features
tools.long_description:
mHelpDesk is field service management software for small home-service businesses, founded in 2007 in Virginia by Vincent Wong and Khoa Ho. HomeAdvisor took a majority stake in 2014, and mHelpDesk now sits under Angi. It serves HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, handyman and appliance repair businesses with scheduling, dispatching, estimates, invoicing, a customer portal, inventory and recurring jobs.

Its QuickBooks coverage is broad: QuickBooks Desktop, QuickBooks Enterprise, QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Online Advanced, plus Google Calendar sync.

mHelpDesk publishes no prices: its pricing page returns 404 and buyers request a quote by email or phone. The homepage offers a free trial but states no length.

The trade-off: it is a long-established product, and newer platforms (Jobber, FieldPulse, Sera Systems) publish more about their features and pricing. Compare a written quote and a hands-on trial before choosing.

pros_detail.title: Broad QuickBooks coverage
pros_detail.explanation: Integrates with QuickBooks Desktop, Enterprise, Online and Online Advanced, which suits shops that keep QuickBooks as their financial system of record.

pros_detail.title: Multi-trade coverage
pros_detail.explanation: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, handyman, appliance repair all supported. Multi-trade operations avoid the dual-platform problem. Established workflow patterns for each trade reflecting long product evolution.

pros_detail.title: Long track record
pros_detail.explanation: Founded in 2007 and backed by Angi (through HomeAdvisor) since 2014.

pros_detail.title: Customer portal built in
pros_detail.explanation: Customer-facing portal for invoice viewing, payment, and service history access. Standard among modern FSM but worth noting for mHelpDesk's mid-tier positioning.

pros_detail.title: Free trial offered
pros_detail.explanation: The homepage offers a free trial but states no length; ask mHelpDesk how to start one and whether it includes the QuickBooks integration.

cons_detail.title: Test the interface and mobile app
cons_detail.explanation: It is a long-established product; compare its interface and mobile app with newer platforms during a trial before you commit.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: mHelpDesk publishes no prices; its pricing page returns 404 and quotes come by email or phone, so get a written quote for your team size.

cons_detail.title: Limited integration list
cons_detail.explanation: Beyond QuickBooks and Google Calendar, integrations are few, so shops relying on CRM, marketing or specialty tools should check connections first.

tools.implementation_notes: Confirm what implementation support your quote includes. Set up the account and configure the QuickBooks integration first (Desktop or Online, matching your accounting), import customers, build the service catalog and roll the mobile app out to techs. Then set up dispatching and roles, migrate recurring service contracts, and launch the customer portal, running in parallel with your old process for a few weeks.

tool_faqs.q: Is mHelpDesk worth choosing for new operations in 2026?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on your QuickBooks setup and budget. mHelpDesk publishes no prices and has a long track record with QuickBooks (Desktop, Enterprise and Online). Newer platforms such as FieldPulse, Workiz, Jobber or Sera Systems publish more about their products and pricing, so compare quotes and trials before deciding.

tool_faqs.q: How does mHelpDesk compare to FieldPulse or Jobber?
tool_faqs.a: mHelpDesk is established FSM with mature QuickBooks integration and a dated UI, and it publishes no prices (quote only). FieldPulse (founded 2015) is modern multi-trade FSM with better UX, online booking and mobile depth, also quote-only. Jobber publishes plans from $29/month billed annually at the smallest team size and has the strongest US user community. For new operations, FieldPulse and Jobber typically win on modern UX and feature pace. For operations with deep mHelpDesk legacy workflows, switching cost may not justify the upgrade.

tool_faqs.q: Does mHelpDesk support QuickBooks Desktop?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. mHelpDesk integrates with QuickBooks Desktop, QuickBooks Enterprise, QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Online Advanced. Other platforms support Desktop too (Service Fusion, FieldPulse and JobNimbus, for example), so compare how each handles your setup.

tool_faqs.q: What's mHelpDesk best for?
tool_faqs.a: Small home-service shops that rely on QuickBooks (Desktop or Online) and value a long-established platform. New operations should compare it with FieldPulse, Jobber, Workiz or RazorSync before committing.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns mHelpDesk?
tool_faqs.a: mHelpDesk was founded in 2007 in Virginia. HomeAdvisor, then part of IAC, took a majority stake in 2014, and it now sits under Angi, the company formed from HomeAdvisor and Angie's List.

tools.name: Synchroteam
tools.tagline: Field service management software available in six languages

pricing.pricing_note: Two per-user plans: Standard from $39 and Premium from $64 per user/month (the page shows a second, higher figure for each plan, $49 and $79, for the other billing term). One free administrator account, QuickBooks Online two-way sync, free setup and training. 14-day free trial, no credit card; month-to-month, cancel anytime. Verified against synchroteam.com/pricing.php 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Service businesses with international clients or multi-language teams
tools.weaknesses: European-rooted, so US-specific integrations are thinner; per-user pricing; fewer native integrations than US-rooted platforms
tools.long_description:
Synchroteam is cloud field service management software from Synchroteam SAS, based in Paris with an office in Miami. It covers scheduling, dispatching, GPS tracking, a customer database, invoicing, reporting and a mobile app, and it is available in six languages (English, French, Spanish, German, Italian and Portuguese), which makes it a fit for multi-language teams.

Pricing is per user: Standard from $39 and Premium from $64 per user per month, with one free administrator account, two-way QuickBooks Online sync, and free setup and training. There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card, and billing is month-to-month. Other accounting integrations include Sage and FreshBooks.

The trade-off: Synchroteam's roots are European. US-only businesses on QuickBooks with English-only teams may find Jobber or Housecall Pro stronger on US-specific features; teams working across languages are where Synchroteam stands out.

pros_detail.title: Six language versions
pros_detail.explanation: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian and Portuguese, so office staff and field techs can work in their own language.

pros_detail.title: Multi-currency billing built in
pros_detail.explanation: Operations billing in multiple currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD) get native multi-currency support. Includes locale-specific tax structures (VAT, GST, sales tax) handled correctly per region.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online two-way sync included
pros_detail.explanation: Two-way QuickBooks Online sync comes with the plans, and Sage and FreshBooks integrations cover other accounting setups.

pros_detail.title: Published pricing with a free admin seat
pros_detail.explanation: Standard from $39 and Premium from $64 per user per month, one free administrator account, free setup and training, and month-to-month billing.

pros_detail.title: Time-zone-aware scheduling
pros_detail.explanation: Operations with techs across multiple time zones get scheduling that handles zone differences correctly. Critical for multi-region service operations or operations dispatching from one country to another.

cons_detail.title: European-rooted
cons_detail.explanation: US-specific integrations (payroll, local tools) are thinner than those of US-rooted competitors; check what you need before you buy.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Every field user is a paid seat (apart from the free administrator account), so costs scale with headcount.

cons_detail.title: Fewer native integrations
cons_detail.explanation: Beyond QuickBooks Online, Sage and FreshBooks, check that the tools you rely on connect before committing.

tools.implementation_notes: Synchroteam includes free setup and training. Configure language and currency, set up users and roles, import customers, and connect QuickBooks Online (or your accounting system). Then roll the mobile app out to techs in their language, set up scheduling and dispatch, and run a few weeks in parallel with your old system. Teams working across countries should allow extra time to configure time zones, currencies and taxes.

tool_faqs.q: Is Synchroteam suitable for US-based service businesses?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with caveats. The core workflows (scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, mobile app) work for US operations, and QuickBooks Online syncs two ways. Its roots are European, so compare US-specific needs (payroll and local integrations) against Jobber, Housecall Pro and Workiz. For teams working in several languages, Synchroteam's six language versions are its clearest advantage.

tool_faqs.q: What languages does Synchroteam support?
tool_faqs.a: Synchroteam is available in English, French, Spanish, German, Italian and Portuguese, so office staff and field techs can work in their own language.

tool_faqs.q: How does Synchroteam compare to Jobber for an international service operation?
tool_faqs.a: For US-only operations on QuickBooks, Jobber has the larger US user base and US-focused features. For teams that work in several languages, Synchroteam's six language versions and European roots are the reason to shortlist it.

tool_faqs.q: What accounting software does Synchroteam integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: QuickBooks Online with two-way sync (included on its plans), plus Sage and FreshBooks. Confirm the connector for your accounting system and country before you buy.

tool_faqs.q: Is Synchroteam's per-user pricing worth it?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on whether you need its multi-language support. At $39 per user per month for Standard (with one free administrator seat), it sits above Jobber Core ($29/month billed annually) and similar entry plans, so for English-only US teams the case rests on features rather than price.

tools.name: FieldPulse
tools.tagline: All-in-one platform for service contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote only, seat-based: seats are bought upfront for the contract term and the rate depends on what each seat needs access to; the vendor publishes no plan names or dollar figures. Premium add-ons (Engage VoIP, Operator AI, Chat AI, Pricebook, Payments, Financing, Fleet Tracking, Custom Forms) are priced separately (some flat-rate, some consumption-based, some seat-based). No free trial, per the vendor's pricing FAQ. Verified against fieldpulse.com/pricing 2026-10-08.

tools.best_for: Growing multi-trade service businesses that want custom workflows, maintenance agreements and inventory in one platform
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing and no free trial (evaluation is by sales demo); payments, financing, VoIP, AI, fleet tracking and other premium features are priced as add-ons
tools.long_description:
FieldPulse is field service management software founded in 2015 in Dallas, Texas by Gabriel Pinchev. It raised a $21 million Series B led by Fulcrum Equity Partners in October 2023 and says it serves thousands of field service businesses. It lists HVAC, electrical, plumbing, garage door, locksmith, property management, appliance repair, commercial equipment, fire and security, general contracting, septic and A/V installation among the trades it serves.

The platform covers scheduling and dispatching, work orders, estimates and invoices, a mobile app, project management, dashboards and reporting, inventory and asset management, maintenance agreements, a customer portal and a booking portal. ClearPath lets you design your own job workflows, and Operator AI captures leads and books jobs.

FieldPulse publishes no prices: seats are bought upfront for the contract term, the rate depends on what each seat needs access to, and premium add-ons (Engage VoIP, Operator AI, Chat AI, Pricebook, Payments, Financing, Fleet Tracking, Custom Forms) are priced separately. Its pricing FAQ says there is no free trial.

Integrations include QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Time, Zapier, Google Calendar, CompanyCam, NiceJob, HighLevel, Marketing 360 and Angi.

pros_detail.title: Broad trade coverage
pros_detail.explanation: FieldPulse lists a dozen trades, from HVAC, plumbing and electrical to locksmith, septic, fire and security and A/V installation, so a multi-trade shop can run every service line in one system.

pros_detail.title: Custom workflows (ClearPath)
pros_detail.explanation: ClearPath lets you design your own job workflows, useful when different services need different steps.

pros_detail.title: Booking portal and customer portal
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can book through a booking portal and manage their account in a customer portal. Confirm both are in your quote, since FieldPulse prices by seat access and add-ons.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online and Desktop
pros_detail.explanation: FieldPulse integrates with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Time, which helps shops whose accountants still run Desktop.

pros_detail.title: Maintenance agreements, inventory and assets
pros_detail.explanation: Maintenance agreements, inventory and asset management are part of the platform, which suits HVAC and commercial equipment service work.

cons_detail.title: No free trial
cons_detail.explanation: FieldPulse's pricing FAQ answers 'Does FieldPulse offer a free trial?' with 'No', so evaluation runs through a sales demo rather than hands-on testing with your own jobs.

cons_detail.title: Seat-based pricing you have to be quoted
cons_detail.explanation: FieldPulse sells seats upfront for the contract term, priced by what each seat needs access to. With no published rates, get a full quote for your headcount before comparing against Jobber or Housecall Pro.

cons_detail.title: Many features are paid add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: Payments, financing, VoIP, AI, the pricebook, fleet tracking and custom forms are premium add-ons priced separately, some by consumption. Get every add-on you need into the quote before comparing totals.

tools.implementation_notes: FieldPulse's onboarding scope is set in the quote, so confirm whether guided implementation is included. Plan the usual phases: account setup and customer and property import, service catalog and pricing, workflow setup in ClearPath, mobile rollout to techs, office training, then a parallel run with your old system before cutting over. Customer data exported from another FSM tool usually imports by CSV; recurring maintenance agreements often need rebuilding by hand because data structures differ between platforms.

tool_faqs.q: How does FieldPulse compare to Jobber and Housecall Pro?
tool_faqs.a: FieldPulse publishes no prices (seat-based quotes) and sells premium features as add-ons. Jobber publishes plans from $29/mo billed annually at the smallest team size and Housecall Pro from $59/mo billed annually, and both offer 14-day free trials, while FieldPulse evaluates through a sales demo. FieldPulse's case is multi-trade coverage, custom workflows and maintenance agreements; get a full quote before comparing.

tool_faqs.q: Is FieldPulse worth the cost?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on the quote. FieldPulse does not publish prices, so get a quote for your seat mix and every add-on you'll use, then compare the total with published plans such as Jobber and Housecall Pro. Its case is strongest for multi-trade shops that need custom workflows and maintenance agreements.

tool_faqs.q: Does FieldPulse handle online customer booking?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. FieldPulse lists a booking portal among its features. Confirm it is included in your quote.

tool_faqs.q: Can FieldPulse handle garage door operations specifically?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Garage door is one of the trades FieldPulse lists, alongside HVAC, plumbing, electrical, locksmith, appliance repair and others. Compare it with other multi-trade platforms that serve garage door companies before you decide.

tool_faqs.q: Does FieldPulse work for solo contractors?
tool_faqs.a: It can, but FieldPulse does not publish prices or offer a free trial, so you need a sales demo and quote before knowing the cost. Solo contractors who don't need multi-trade workflows may find options with published prices adequate, such as Jobber Core ($29/mo billed annually) or Joist Basics ($8.34/mo billed annually, $10 billed monthly).

tools.name: Smart Service
tools.tagline: QuickBooks-based scheduling and dispatch for service businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote only; Smart Service publishes no prices. Its pricing page says the quote is built on the product you pick (Smart Service Cloud or Smart Service Desktop), the size of your team, how you pay (annual billing saves 20%) and what it takes to bring over your existing customer and QuickBooks data. The page also names SmartFlow Advanced Workflow Automation and Smart Service Dynamic Systems Design. Budget the quote plus your QuickBooks subscription. Verified against smartservice.com/pricing 2026-10-03.

tools.best_for: HVAC, plumbing and other service shops that run on QuickBooks and want scheduling and dispatch built around it
tools.weaknesses: Built around QuickBooks, so not for businesses on other accounting systems; no public pricing
tools.long_description:
Smart Service is field service software from My Service Depot, based in Dublin, Ohio, for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, pest control and other service trades. It is built around QuickBooks: the company says it is designed for use with QuickBooks Pro, Premier, Enterprise and QuickBooks Online, so jobs, customers and invoices flow through QuickBooks rather than a separate accounting setup.

It covers scheduling, dispatching, a mobile app, service agreements and route optimization. Built-in integrations include QuickBooks, Twilio for messaging and AI assistants (ChatGPT and Claude), with custom API integrations for Sage and SAP.

Pricing is custom-quoted with no published tiers, so budget from a quote plus your QuickBooks subscription.

The trade-off: Smart Service only makes sense if QuickBooks is your accounting system. Shops on other accounting software, or wanting a broader platform, should compare Sera Systems, FieldEdge or ServiceTitan.

pros_detail.title: Built around QuickBooks
pros_detail.explanation: Designed for QuickBooks Pro, Premier, Enterprise and Online, so scheduling, dispatch and invoicing flow through the accounting system you already use.

pros_detail.title: Works with QuickBooks Enterprise and Online
pros_detail.explanation: Covers QuickBooks Enterprise for larger Desktop users as well as QuickBooks Online, so a move between editions doesn't force a new FSM.

pros_detail.title: Service agreement workflows
pros_detail.explanation: Recurring service agreement management for HVAC/plumbing maintenance contracts. Mature feature reflecting decades of service industry workflow refinement.

pros_detail.title: Route optimization built in
pros_detail.explanation: Built-in route optimization for tech dispatching across service calls. Standard among mid-tier FSM but worth noting for Smart Service's specialty category positioning.

pros_detail.title: AI and messaging integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Built-in ChatGPT, Claude and Twilio integrations, with custom API connections to Sage and SAP.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks required
cons_detail.explanation: Smart Service is built for QuickBooks (Pro, Premier, Enterprise or Online); businesses on other accounting systems can't use it as designed.

cons_detail.title: No public pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Quotes come from sales, so comparison shopping means talking to the vendor; add your QuickBooks subscription to the total.

cons_detail.title: Smaller user community than modern FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Niche positioning means smaller online community, fewer tutorials, fewer third-party guides. Affects troubleshooting speed when implementation issues arise.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with the QuickBooks connection, since it is the center of the product: match users and roles to your QuickBooks setup and import your items and customers. Then configure service agreements and dispatch (including route optimization), train office staff, roll the mobile app out to techs, and run in parallel with your old process until invoices and reports reconcile with QuickBooks.

tool_faqs.q: Do I need QuickBooks to use Smart Service?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Smart Service is designed for use with QuickBooks: Pro, Premier, Enterprise or QuickBooks Online. It is built around QuickBooks as your accounting system, so it isn't a fit if you don't use QuickBooks.

tool_faqs.q: How does Smart Service compare to FieldEdge?
tool_faqs.a: Both target HVAC and plumbing businesses that run on QuickBooks. FieldEdge markets a real-time two-way QuickBooks integration and is quote-only; Smart Service is built specifically around QuickBooks (Pro, Premier, Enterprise or Online). Compare both on your QuickBooks edition and workflow in demos.

tool_faqs.q: Does Smart Service work with QuickBooks Online?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Smart Service lists QuickBooks Online alongside QuickBooks Pro, Premier and Enterprise, so moving from Desktop to Online doesn't rule it out; confirm the setup for your edition with the vendor.

tool_faqs.q: What does Smart Service cost?
tool_faqs.a: Smart Service doesn't publish prices, so get a quote for your number of users and the features you need, and add the cost of your QuickBooks subscription to compare it fairly.

tool_faqs.q: What's Smart Service best for?
tool_faqs.a: HVAC, plumbing, electrical and pest control businesses that run on QuickBooks (Pro, Premier, Enterprise or Online) and want scheduling, dispatch and service agreements tied tightly to it. Businesses not on QuickBooks should look at other FSM platforms.

tools.name: ServSuite
tools.tagline: Pest, lawn and arbor software from ServicePro, now sold as ServSuite by FieldRoutes (a ServiceTitan company)

pricing.pricing_note: No published pricing. FieldRoutes' ServSuite page lists no plans or prices and its demo button reads 'Demo FieldRoutes'; ServicePro's own site (servicepro.com) no longer loads. Any price comes from FieldRoutes' sales team. Verified against fieldroutes.com/servsuite-by-fieldroutes 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Existing ServSuite customers, and pest, lawn or arbor companies that want to compare it with FieldRoutes' main platform
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing; FieldRoutes' ServSuite page steers new buyers to a FieldRoutes demo, and ServicePro's old website no longer loads, so current features are hard to confirm.
tools.long_description:
ServSuite is pest control software built by ServicePro, which ServiceTitan described as a software solution for the pest, lawn and arbor industries. ServiceTitan acquired ServicePro in 2021. When ServiceTitan agreed to acquire FieldRoutes in January 2022, it said ServicePro would be managed under FieldRoutes, and the product is now sold as ServSuite by FieldRoutes. It is a ServiceTitan product, not a WorkWave product.

FieldRoutes' ServSuite page says 'there is no change to your software or service' for existing customers. The page offers a 'Log in to ServSuite' link for current users, but its demo button reads 'Demo FieldRoutes', and it lists no ServSuite features, plans or prices. ServicePro's own website (servicepro.com) did not load when we checked on September 29, 2026.

ServicePro's former product pages described ServSuite as web-based software with drag-and-drop scheduling, intelligent routing, invoicing, a mobile app for technicians, commercial barcode scanning, GPS vehicle tracking, inventory management, reporting, and a branded customer login portal where customers can make payments and view upcoming services. Confirm in a demo which of these are still offered.

There is no published pricing. Any price comes from a conversation with FieldRoutes' sales team.

The trade-off: ServSuite now sits beside FieldRoutes, the same company's main pest and lawn platform, and FieldRoutes' own ServSuite page promotes FieldRoutes demos. If you are a new buyer, ask FieldRoutes directly whether ServSuite is still offered to new customers and how its roadmap compares with FieldRoutes. Existing ServSuite users can keep logging in through FieldRoutes' site.

pros_detail.title: Backed by ServiceTitan
pros_detail.explanation: ServicePro, the maker of ServSuite, was acquired by ServiceTitan in 2021 and is now part of FieldRoutes, a ServiceTitan company.

pros_detail.title: No change for existing customers
pros_detail.explanation: FieldRoutes says the move to the ServSuite by FieldRoutes name brought no change to customers' software or service.

pros_detail.title: Built for pest, lawn and arbor work
pros_detail.explanation: ServiceTitan described ServicePro as a software solution for the pest, lawn and arbor industries, so its workflows target those trades rather than general contracting.

pros_detail.title: Field and customer tools
pros_detail.explanation: ServicePro's product pages described a technician mobile app, commercial barcode scanning, GPS vehicle tracking and a branded customer portal for payments and upcoming services.

cons_detail.title: Unclear status for new buyers
cons_detail.explanation: FieldRoutes' ServSuite page offers a ServSuite login and a 'Demo FieldRoutes' button. Ask whether ServSuite is still sold to new customers.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Pricing is by quote only, and no plans are listed.

cons_detail.title: Hard to verify features
cons_detail.explanation: ServicePro's old website no longer loads and the FieldRoutes page lists no ServSuite features, so you need a demo to confirm what is included today.

cons_detail.title: Overlaps with FieldRoutes
cons_detail.explanation: The same company sells FieldRoutes for pest control and lawn care. Whether both products stay side by side long term is unclear.

tools.implementation_notes: Contact FieldRoutes (the ServSuite page lists a support line) and ask first whether ServSuite or FieldRoutes is the product offered to new customers. If you already use ServSuite, log in through FieldRoutes' ServSuite page and ask your account contact about the product roadmap before investing in new setup work. If you are evaluating it fresh, request a demo and a written quote, confirm which features (routing, mobile app, barcode scanning, customer portal, accounting connection) are included today, and ask how your customer records, service history and recurring schedules would be imported.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns ServSuite?
tool_faqs.a: ServSuite was built by ServicePro, which ServiceTitan acquired in 2021. After ServiceTitan agreed to acquire FieldRoutes in January 2022, ServicePro moved under FieldRoutes, and the product is now sold as ServSuite by FieldRoutes. It is a ServiceTitan product, not a WorkWave product.

tool_faqs.q: Is ServSuite still available?
tool_faqs.a: Existing customers can still log in through FieldRoutes' ServSuite page, and FieldRoutes says the rebrand brought no change to customers' software or service. The page's demo button is for FieldRoutes, so new buyers should ask FieldRoutes whether ServSuite is still offered to them.

tool_faqs.q: How much does ServSuite cost?
tool_faqs.a: No price is published, and no plans are listed. Pricing comes from FieldRoutes' sales team.

tool_faqs.q: Should I choose ServSuite or FieldRoutes?
tool_faqs.a: Both come from FieldRoutes, a ServiceTitan company. FieldRoutes publishes its package names (Growth and Corporate) and a current feature list, while the FieldRoutes site lists no ServSuite features. Ask FieldRoutes to demo both and explain which one it recommends for your size and trade.

tool_faqs.q: How does ServSuite compare to PestPac?
tool_faqs.a: PestPac is a competing product from WorkWave. Both are quote-only. Compare them in demos using your own routes, recurring services and termite work.

tools.name: GorillaDesk
tools.tagline: Field service software for pest control, lawn care, cleaning and other route-based home service businesses, priced per route

pricing.pricing_note: Per route (schedule) per month, billed monthly: Basic $49, Pro $99, Growth $149. Paid annually: $539, $1,089 and $1,639 a year (about $44.92, $90.75 and $136.58 a month). Only schedules need a paid seat: a solo technician needs one, a crew needs one for its leader, and admin users and mobile devices are unlimited on every plan. Month-to-month, no contracts or setup fees, free data import. Text messaging is extra: $5/month plus message packs ($50 for 1,000, $100 for 2,500, $200 for 8,000). 14-day free trial, no credit card. Verified against gorilladesk.com/pricing and gorilladesk.com/industries/pest-control-software 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Small pest control, lawn care, cleaning and other route-based service businesses that want published, month-to-month pricing
tools.weaknesses: QuickBooks Online sync, the customer portal, e-signatures and Zapier start on the $99 Pro plan; every solo technician needs a paid schedule; no QuickBooks Desktop or payroll integration is listed.
tools.long_description:
GorillaDesk is field service software for pest control, lawn care, landscaping, tree care, pool service, cleaning and similar route-based home service businesses. The company says it was started by people who ran a pest control and lawn business, and its site says more than 4,500 local service companies use it. We found no announcement that it has been acquired.

Pricing is published and charged per route (schedule), not per office user. Basic is $49 a month, Pro $99 and Growth $149, or $539, $1,089 and $1,639 a year when paid annually. A technician who works solo needs a schedule; a crew that rides together needs one only for its leader. Admin users and mobile devices are unlimited on every plan, plans are month-to-month with no contract or setup fee, and GorillaDesk says its team will import data from another system at no charge. There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card. Text messaging costs extra: $5 a month plus prepaid message packs.

Every plan includes invoices, estimates and work orders, job and customer mapping, basic routing (up to 25 stops on Basic), Stripe and Square payments, broadcast messaging, material tracking and reporting, triggered automations, and automated emails and texts. Pro adds routing with a drive-time matrix, the customer portal, online booking, review requests, documents and e-signatures, device tracking and barcoding, multi-dwelling unit support, commission tracking, QuickBooks Online sync, GPS tracking, email inbox sync, Zapier, open API access and time clocking. Growth adds map-based estimating, dynamic estimates and estimate packages, a sales pipeline, custom fields and job statuses, and multi-branch support.

For pest control, GorillaDesk's pest page lists chemical data and templates, material use reports, device scanning and tracking in the field, and tracking of individual units in multi-unit buildings. Its integrations library lists QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Square, Zapier, Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Maps, Google My Business, Yelp, Waze, Mapbox, SalesRabbit, Weather Underground and Adobe.

The trade-off: the cheapest plan leaves out the customer portal, e-signatures, QuickBooks Online sync and Zapier, so many growing companies will need Pro at $99 per route. Every solo technician adds a paid schedule, and the integrations list has no QuickBooks Desktop or payroll connection. Pest companies that want a larger, quote-based platform can compare FieldRoutes or PestPac.

pros_detail.title: Published, month-to-month pricing
pros_detail.explanation: $49, $99 or $149 per route a month, with annual prepay options, no contracts and no setup fees.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited free office users
pros_detail.explanation: Admin users and mobile devices are unlimited on every plan; you pay only for the schedules that technicians or crews run.

pros_detail.title: Pest control tools
pros_detail.explanation: The pest control page lists chemical data and templates, material use reports and device scanning and tracking, and material tracking is on every plan.

pros_detail.title: Free trial and free data import
pros_detail.explanation: There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card, and GorillaDesk says its customer success team will import data from another system at no charge.

pros_detail.title: Covers several trades
pros_detail.explanation: Pest control, lawn care, landscaping, tree care, pool service and cleaning businesses are all listed among the industries it serves.

cons_detail.title: Key features start on Pro
cons_detail.explanation: The customer portal, online booking, e-signatures, QuickBooks Online sync, Zapier and GPS tracking are not on the $49 Basic plan.

cons_detail.title: Each solo technician needs a paid schedule
cons_detail.explanation: A company with ten technicians who ride solo pays for ten schedules.

cons_detail.title: No QuickBooks Desktop or payroll integration listed
cons_detail.explanation: For accounting, the integrations library lists QuickBooks Online only, and it lists no payroll app.

cons_detail.title: Texting costs extra
cons_detail.explanation: Text messaging is a $5 monthly add-on plus prepaid packs ($50 for 1,000 messages, $100 for 2,500, $200 for 8,000).

cons_detail.title: Sales and multi-branch tools only on Growth
cons_detail.explanation: Map estimation, dynamic estimates, the sales pipeline, custom fields and multi-branch support need the $149 Growth plan.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 14-day free trial, then work out how many schedules you need: one per technician who works alone, or one per crew leader if technicians ride together. Ask GorillaDesk's customer success team to import your customers and service history from your current system (it says this is free). Set up your chemical and material records, service templates and recurring invoice frequencies, then connect Stripe or Square for payments. On Pro or Growth, connect QuickBooks Online and set up the customer portal and online booking before inviting customers. Roll out the mobile app to technicians and run a few routes before you switch over fully.

tool_faqs.q: How much does GorillaDesk cost?
tool_faqs.a: Basic is $49 a month, Pro $99 and Growth $149, per route (schedule). Paid annually they are $539, $1,089 and $1,639 a year. Admin users are unlimited and free, plans are month-to-month with no setup fee, and text messaging is an add-on.

tool_faqs.q: What counts as a route or schedule?
tool_faqs.a: GorillaDesk charges for each schedule that work is assigned to. A technician who rides solo needs their own schedule; when technicians ride together, only the supervisor or crew leader needs one. Office admins do not need a paid seat.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. GorillaDesk offers a 14-day free trial with no credit card required.

tool_faqs.q: Does GorillaDesk integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: It syncs with QuickBooks Online on the Pro and Growth plans, pushing customers, invoices and payments. QuickBooks Desktop is not listed in its integrations library.

tool_faqs.q: Does GorillaDesk work for lawn care and cleaning as well as pest control?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. GorillaDesk lists pest control, lawn care, landscaping, tree care, pool service, cleaning services and some contracting trades among the industries it serves.

tool_faqs.q: How does GorillaDesk compare to PestPac and FieldRoutes?
tool_faqs.a: GorillaDesk publishes its prices and bills per route. PestPac (WorkWave) and FieldRoutes (ServiceTitan) are quote-only, and FieldRoutes prices on your number of active customers. Small companies that want to see the price up front can start with GorillaDesk's trial; larger pest companies may also want to demo the quote-based platforms.

tools.name: Service Autopilot
tools.tagline: Scheduling, routing and automation software for lawn care, landscaping, snow and other route-based services

pricing.pricing_note: Flat monthly price per company (not per user), based on annual subscription rates, plus a sign-up fee whose amount is not published. Startup $49 a month (1 mobile and 1 business user license), Pro $199 (2 mobile, 1 business), Pro Plus $499 (5 mobile, 1 business on the plan card; the comparison chart shows 2 business users), Elite priced on request (8 mobile, 2 business). The comparison chart marks QuickBooks integration, two-way texting, the client portal, Smart Maps, email integration and FleetSharp GPS as call-for-pricing on Pro Plus and Elite. No trial length is published. Verified against serviceautopilot.com/pricing/ and /pricing/comparison-chart/ 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Lawn care, landscaping, snow removal, cleaning, pest control and pool service businesses with recurring routes that want scheduling, dispatch, routing and billing in one system, with automations on the higher plans
tools.weaknesses: Annual subscription plus a sign-up fee whose amount is not published; QuickBooks sync, two-way texting, the client portal and email integration are upper-tier items priced on request; the Elite price is not published; the plan cards, comparison chart and QuickBooks page disagree on some details
tools.long_description:
Service Autopilot is field service software for route-based service businesses. Its website targets lawn care, landscaping, snow removal, cleaning, pest control, pool service and arbor and tree care companies. It is part of Xplor Technologies: the member agreement names an Xplor entity as the contracting party, the site links to Xplor's terms and privacy policy, and payments run through Xplor Pay. The site lists an address at 950 East Paces Ferry Rd NE in Atlanta, Georgia. Service Autopilot says it has helped thousands of business owners and has more than 80 developers, trainers, support, marketing and sales staff.

The Startup plan covers scheduling and dispatch, invoicing and integrated payments, expense tracking, and customer and lead management. Pro adds multi-day job management, route optimization, a dispatch calendar, job costing and analysis, asset, expense and employee tracking, and customized reporting; the comparison chart also lists chemical tracking from Pro. Pro Plus adds Service Autopilot's Automations (workflows that run on their own once set up), marketplace access and extra software training. For snow work, Service Autopilot offers pre-built master routes, lets you add or cancel jobs during a snow event, and bills flat rate, per push, per event, per inch or hourly.

Prices are flat per company, based on annual subscription rates, plus a sign-up fee whose amount is not published. Startup is $49 a month with 1 mobile and 1 business user license, Pro is $199 with 2 mobile and 1 business, and Pro Plus is $499 with 5 mobile and 1 business (the comparison chart shows 2 business users). Elite is priced on request and includes 8 mobile and 2 business licenses. The Elite card lists two-way texting, email integration, Smart Maps, a client portal, QuickBooks integration, onboarding and training specialists and multi-location management. The comparison chart shows those items, plus the FleetSharp GPS integration, as call-for-pricing on Pro Plus and Elite.

Service Autopilot's QuickBooks page describes a two-way sync with QuickBooks Online and Windows versions of QuickBooks Desktop (Pro, Premier and Enterprise), sold as a $29-a-month add-on for Pro and Pro Plus members. That page and the current plan chart disagree, so confirm the price and plan requirement before you buy. The member agreement renews automatically for the same period unless you cancel 30 days before the term ends.

The trade-off: the lower plans are inexpensive and flat-priced, but the features many offices expect (QuickBooks sync, two-way texting and a client portal) sit on the upper tiers at prices you have to request, and every plan carries an annual subscription and a sign-up fee.

pros_detail.title: Low published entry price
pros_detail.explanation: Startup is $49 a month and Pro $199, flat per company rather than per user, based on annual subscription rates.

pros_detail.title: Snow billing options
pros_detail.explanation: Pre-built master routes, adding or cancelling jobs mid-storm, and billing flat rate, per push, per event, per inch or hourly suit snow contractors.

pros_detail.title: Automations
pros_detail.explanation: The plan cards list Service Autopilot's Automations from Pro Plus: workflows you set once that run on their own until you stop them.

pros_detail.title: Job costing and chemical tracking from Pro
pros_detail.explanation: Pro adds job costing and analysis, and the comparison chart lists chemical tracking from Pro as well, which lawn treatment companies need.

pros_detail.title: Several route-based trades
pros_detail.explanation: The site has industry pages for lawn care, landscaping, snow removal, cleaning, pest control, pool service and tree care, so a mixed service company can run on one system.

cons_detail.title: Sign-up fee and annual terms
cons_detail.explanation: Every plan adds a sign-up fee whose amount is not published, prices are based on annual subscriptions, and the agreement auto-renews unless cancelled 30 days before the term ends.

cons_detail.title: Common integrations on upper tiers
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks integration, two-way texting, the client portal and email integration are listed on Elite, or as call-for-pricing on Pro Plus and Elite.

cons_detail.title: Few licenses included
cons_detail.explanation: Startup includes 1 mobile user and Pro 2. A five-person field crew needs Pro Plus ($499 a month) or extra app users added through customer success.

cons_detail.title: Inconsistent plan details
cons_detail.explanation: The plan cards, comparison chart and QuickBooks page disagree on business-user counts and on how QuickBooks is sold, so get the details in writing.

cons_detail.title: Elite price and trial not published
cons_detail.explanation: Elite is priced on request, and no free trial length is published; evaluation is through a demo.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with a demo, since Service Autopilot publishes no trial length. Count your field and office staff first, because each plan includes a fixed number of licenses (1 mobile on Startup, 2 on Pro, 5 on Pro Plus, 8 on Elite), and customer success can add app users. Before signing, ask for the sign-up fee and, if you need them, the prices of QuickBooks sync, two-way texting and the client portal. Set up customers, properties, services and recurring routes, then decide whether to take payments through Xplor Pay. Snow contractors should build master routes and pick their billing method (flat, per push, per event, per inch or hourly) before the first storm.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Service Autopilot?
tool_faqs.a: Service Autopilot is part of Xplor Technologies. Its member agreement names an Xplor entity as the contracting party, payments run through Xplor Pay, and the site lists an Atlanta, Georgia address.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Service Autopilot cost?
tool_faqs.a: Startup is $49 a month, Pro $199 and Pro Plus $499, based on annual subscription rates, plus a sign-up fee whose amount is not published. Elite is priced on request. Each plan includes a set number of mobile and business user licenses.

tool_faqs.q: Does Service Autopilot integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with QuickBooks Online and Windows versions of QuickBooks Desktop through a two-way sync. The pricing pages list QuickBooks integration on the upper tiers (priced on request), while an older QuickBooks page sells it as a $29-a-month add-on for Pro and Pro Plus, so confirm the cost in a demo.

tool_faqs.q: Can Service Autopilot handle snow removal?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. It offers pre-built master routes, lets you add or cancel jobs during a snow event, and can bill flat rate, per push, per event, per inch or hourly. The comparison chart lists snow dispatch on every plan.

tool_faqs.q: Is Service Autopilot only for lawn care?
tool_faqs.a: No. Its website targets lawn care, landscaping, snow removal, cleaning, pest control, pool service and tree care businesses.

tool_faqs.q: Service Autopilot or Aspire?
tool_faqs.a: Service Autopilot publishes flat per-company prices ($49 to $499 a month on annual rates, plus a sign-up fee) with a fixed number of user licenses per plan. Aspire publishes no prices and quotes a single monthly license fee with unlimited users, aimed at larger landscaping and commercial cleaning companies.

tools.name: Aspire

tiers: Custom quote (single license fee, unlimited users)

A single license fee billed monthly covers all contracted functionality with no limit on users, priced by company size, complexity and solution fit; implementation, training, post-implementation support and future upgrades are included, and the price is protected through the contract term. Electronic payments, payroll services and GPS fleet management are quoted in addition to the software. The demo form asks for annual revenue (Under $1M to Over $8M). No free trial is published. Verified against youraspire.com/aspire-plans 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Established landscaping, snow and ice management, and commercial cleaning companies with multiple crews that want estimating, scheduling, job costing, purchasing and reporting in one system with unlimited users
tools.weaknesses: No published prices; payments, payroll and GPS fleet management are quoted on top of the software; built for established multi-crew companies rather than small residential shops; no published free trial
tools.long_description:
Aspire is business management software for landscaping companies, covering grounds maintenance, landscape construction, and snow and ice management, and since 2021 for commercial cleaning companies. Mark Tipton and Kevin Kehoe began building it in 2013, and its home office is in Chesterfield, Missouri. In 2021 Aspire signed a definitive agreement to be acquired by ServiceTitan, and it now operates as a ServiceTitan company alongside FieldRoutes. Aspire's about page says it is trusted by more than 800 clients with more than 100,000 users in over 2,200 locations, managing more than $6.5 billion in client revenue.

The platform covers estimating built from historical data and approved profit margins, drag-and-drop scheduling, a CRM with sales pipeline visibility and email integration, job costing with drill-down reporting, purchasing with inventory visibility, equipment maintenance and repair tracking, and invoicing. The crew mobile app for iOS and Android provides job checklists and geo-tagged time tracking and works offline. For snow and ice work, Aspire offers scheduling across crews with visual routing and text updates to clients about schedule changes due to weather.

Aspire's accounting integrations are QuickBooks and Acumatica, with API options for enterprise-tier clients to connect other accounting systems. Its partner marketplace lists Inova Payroll, Azuga telematics (sold as Aspire Integrated Telematics), SiteOne Landscape Supply for material quotes, Marketing Pro for targeted email and direct mail campaigns, and Scorpion for marketing.

Aspire does not publish prices. Its plans page says pricing depends on company size, complexity and solution fit, with a single license fee billed monthly that covers all contracted functionality and no limit on users. Every client gets unlimited user licenses, implementation and training, post-implementation support and future upgrades, and the price is protected through the contract term. Electronic payments, payroll services and GPS fleet management are quoted separately. The demo form asks for annual revenue, from under $1M to over $8M.

The trade-off: you cannot compare Aspire's cost without a sales conversation, add-on services are quoted on top of the license, and the platform is designed around established multi-crew companies. A small residential lawn or landscape business may be better served by a lighter tool with published prices.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on one license
pros_detail.explanation: Aspire charges a single monthly license fee with no limit on users, so adding office staff and crew members does not add seat fees.

pros_detail.title: Estimating tied to job costing
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates are built from historical data and approved profit margins, and job costing with drill-down reporting shows how jobs perform against them.

pros_detail.title: Purchasing and equipment built in
pros_detail.explanation: Purchasing with inventory visibility and equipment maintenance and repair tracking are part of the platform rather than separate tools.

pros_detail.title: Implementation included
pros_detail.explanation: Implementation, training, post-implementation support and future upgrades are included in the license fee, and you work with an implementation specialist.

pros_detail.title: Offline crew app
pros_detail.explanation: The crew mobile app for iOS and Android has checklists and geo-tagged time tracking and works offline.

pros_detail.title: Accounting and payroll connections
pros_detail.explanation: Aspire integrates with QuickBooks and Acumatica, offers API options on its enterprise tier, and lists Inova Payroll and Azuga telematics in its marketplace.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: Aspire quotes every customer based on size and complexity, so you need a sales conversation to learn the cost.

cons_detail.title: Add-on services cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Electronic payments, payroll services and GPS fleet management are quoted in addition to the software license.

cons_detail.title: Built for larger operations
cons_detail.explanation: The feature set and sales process are aimed at established multi-crew companies; a small residential lawn or landscape business may find it more than it needs.

cons_detail.title: Price protection ends with the term
cons_detail.explanation: Aspire protects the price through the contract term. Ask what happens at renewal and get any increase limits in writing.

cons_detail.title: No published trial
cons_detail.explanation: There is no self-serve trial; evaluation is through a demo.

tools.implementation_notes: Aspire includes implementation and training in the license fee, and you work with an implementation specialist. Before kickoff, gather your customer and property list, crew structure, equipment list, service catalog, and the historical costs and margin targets you want estimates built on. Decide early whether you will connect QuickBooks or Acumatica, or use the API on the enterprise tier, and ask for quotes on payments, payroll and GPS fleet services if you want them, since those are priced separately. Roll out the crew mobile app (iOS and Android, with offline access) once jobs and schedules are set up, so crews track time against the right jobs from the first day.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Aspire?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceTitan. Aspire signed a definitive agreement in 2021 to be acquired by ServiceTitan and now operates as a ServiceTitan company. Its home office is in Chesterfield, Missouri.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Aspire cost?
tool_faqs.a: Aspire does not publish prices. It quotes a single license fee billed monthly, based on company size and complexity, with unlimited users. Implementation, training and upgrades are included; payments, payroll and GPS fleet services are quoted separately.

tool_faqs.q: Which accounting systems does Aspire integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: QuickBooks and Acumatica. Enterprise-tier clients can also use Aspire's API to connect other accounting systems.

tool_faqs.q: Does Aspire handle snow and ice management?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Snow and ice management is one of Aspire's core segments, with crew scheduling and visual routing, text updates to clients about weather changes, and an offline-capable mobile app.

tool_faqs.q: Does Aspire work for commercial cleaning companies?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Aspire expanded into the commercial cleaning industry in 2021 and markets to commercial cleaning companies alongside landscapers.

tool_faqs.q: Aspire or Service Autopilot?
tool_faqs.a: Aspire quotes a single monthly license with unlimited users and targets established landscaping and commercial cleaning companies. Service Autopilot publishes flat plans from $49 to $499 a month on annual rates, plus a sign-up fee, with a fixed number of user licenses per plan.

tools.name: RealGreen
tools.tagline: Lawn care, landscaping, irrigation and tree care business software, sold as RealGreen by WorkWave

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote. The pricing page lists three packages with no prices: Small Business ('Ideal for 3 crews or more': CRM, scheduling, routing, mobile app, marketing tools), Professional (adds pay-over-time and capital solutions, advanced reporting, API integration) and Enterprise (unlimited licenses, advanced API and analytics integrations, professional services). RealGreen says it offers 'both usage and user-based' pricing options. Free demo; no free trial advertised. Verified against realgreen.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Lawn care, landscaping, irrigation and tree care companies with several crews that want scheduling, routing, billing and built-in marketing in one system
tools.weaknesses: No published prices or trial; QuickBooks is a one-way file export; integrated payments run through WorkWave's own payment service.
tools.long_description:
RealGreen is business management software for lawn care, landscaping, irrigation and arbor (tree) care companies, now sold as RealGreen by WorkWave. It comes from Real Green Systems, founded by Joe Kucik, and RealGreen says it was created by lawn professionals and has served the green industry since 1984. WorkWave, a field service software company headquartered in Holmdel, New Jersey, announced its acquisition of Real Green Systems, then based in Walled Lake, Michigan, on June 22, 2021, and said RealGreen and its pest control product PestPac would remain separate.

The core program is Service Assistant 5, which runs customer records, scheduling, billing and crew coordination. Around it, RealGreen offers Dynamic Routing for route optimization, Measurement Assistant for measuring properties and producing estimates and quotes, Mobile Live for crews in the field, Customer Assistant websites where customers can request service and pay, an Automated Marketing Assistant for automated emails, texts and customer communications, custom digital forms, and Wavelytics for business analytics. RealGreen says nine of the top 10 lawn care franchises choose it.

Payments run through WorkWave's payment service, which supports credit card auto-billing, prepayment discounts, ACH, online payments, invoice consolidation and payments by text. For accounting, RealGreen offers a one-way export: you export the general ledger report from Service Assistant as an IIF file and import it into QuickBooks. Reports can also be exported to Excel, CSV, PDF, XML and Constant Contact. Listed partners include Wisetack, Coalmarch, Waypoint Analytical (soil testing), Voice for Turf, Slingshot, YouLend, Applause and American Profit Recovery.

Pricing is by quote. The pricing page lists three packages with no prices: Small Business (which RealGreen says is ideal for 3 crews or more), Professional and Enterprise (unlimited licenses), and says it offers 'both usage and user-based' pricing options. Small Business includes CRM, scheduling, routing, the mobile app and marketing tools; Professional adds pay-over-time and capital solutions, advanced reporting and API integration; Enterprise adds advanced API and analytics integrations and professional services. RealGreen offers a free demo; no free trial is advertised.

The trade-off: you need a sales call to see a price, the QuickBooks link is a manual one-way file export rather than a live sync, and integrated payments run through WorkWave's own service. RealGreen's comparison page names Service Autopilot, LMN, Jobber, Yardbook, Aspire and FieldRoutes as alternatives, and lawn and landscape companies may want to demo one or two of them alongside it.

pros_detail.title: Long history in lawn care
pros_detail.explanation: RealGreen says it was created by lawn professionals in 1984, and it says nine of the top 10 lawn care franchises choose it.

pros_detail.title: Marketing built in
pros_detail.explanation: The Automated Marketing Assistant sends automated emails, texts and customer communications from the same system that runs your schedule and billing.

pros_detail.title: Measuring, estimating and routing
pros_detail.explanation: Measurement Assistant produces estimates and quotes from property measurements, and Dynamic Routing builds optimized routes.

pros_detail.title: Autopay and prepay tools
pros_detail.explanation: Credit card auto-billing, prepayment discounts, ACH and online payments through Customer Assistant websites. RealGreen says companies using the portal have 12% more customers on autopay.

pros_detail.title: Owned by WorkWave
pros_detail.explanation: WorkWave, which also makes PestPac, owns RealGreen and says it has served more than 8,000 companies across its products.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: All three packages are quote-based, and RealGreen advertises a free demo rather than a free trial.

cons_detail.title: One-way QuickBooks export
cons_detail.explanation: You export an IIF general ledger file from Service Assistant and import it into QuickBooks. There is no live sync, and no other accounting package is listed.

cons_detail.title: Payments tied to WorkWave
cons_detail.explanation: Integrated payments run through WorkWave's payment service; Stripe and other outside processors are not listed as partners.

cons_detail.title: API and advanced reporting cost more
cons_detail.explanation: API integration and advanced reporting start on the Professional package, and advanced API and analytics integrations need Enterprise.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and ask for quotes on the Small Business, Professional or Enterprise package, and ask whether your price will be usage-based or user-based. Before migrating, export customers, properties, service programs, service history and balances from your current system and ask RealGreen what its team handles during import and training. Set up service programs, routes and billing (auto-billing, prepay discounts and the Customer Assistant website) before go-live, and plan a regular general ledger export to QuickBooks if you use it. Then roll out Mobile Live to crews and turn on the marketing automation once your customer data is clean.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns RealGreen?
tool_faqs.a: WorkWave. WorkWave announced its acquisition of Real Green Systems, then based in Walled Lake, Michigan, on June 22, 2021, and the product now trades as RealGreen by WorkWave. WorkWave is headquartered in Holmdel, New Jersey, and also makes PestPac, which it said would remain a separate product.

tool_faqs.q: How much does RealGreen cost?
tool_faqs.a: RealGreen does not publish prices. Its pricing page lists Small Business, Professional and Enterprise packages, says its pricing options are both usage-based and user-based, and asks you to contact sales for a custom quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does RealGreen integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Only through a one-way export. You export the general ledger report from Service Assistant as an IIF file and import it into QuickBooks.

tool_faqs.q: What trades does RealGreen serve?
tool_faqs.a: Lawn care, irrigation, landscaping and arbor care. When WorkWave bought it in 2021, it described Real Green Systems as serving lawn care, landscaping, arbor care and pest control companies.

tool_faqs.q: How does RealGreen compare to Service Autopilot?
tool_faqs.a: Both serve lawn and landscape companies. RealGreen is quote-only and includes marketing automation, measuring and routing modules. RealGreen's own comparison page names Service Autopilot, LMN, Jobber, Yardbook, Aspire and FieldRoutes as alternatives; check each one's current pricing on its own site.

tool_faqs.q: Does RealGreen handle commercial landscaping?
tool_faqs.a: RealGreen markets to lawn care, landscaping, irrigation and arbor businesses from single locations to multi-franchise operations. Commercial landscape contractors may also want to compare Aspire, which ServiceTitan describes as software for commercial landscaping businesses.
