Verified against razorsync.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Small-to-mid service businesses that want capped, per-company pricing instead of paying per user
tools.weaknesses: User caps per plan (2, 7, 15) force plan jumps as the team grows; QuickBooks sync is an add-on on Solo; route optimization and inventory need Pro
tools.long_description:
RazorSync is field service management software for small and mid-size service businesses, serving HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, handyman and appliance repair operations. It was founded in 2010 and is based in Minnesota.

Its pricing is per company with user caps rather than per user: Solo covers up to 2 users ($85 a month billed annually, $90 monthly), Team up to 7 ($195 or $225), Pro up to 15 ($439 or $499), and Enterprise has unlimited users on a quote. Annual billing saves 15%, and there is a 14-day free trial of the Enterprise package.

QuickBooks sync (Desktop and Online) is included from Team and is a $20/month add-on on Solo. Route optimization is included on Pro (a $50/month add-on below), and inventory management comes with Pro and Enterprise; scheduling, dispatching, estimates, invoicing, GPS tracking and customer history are part of the core product.

The trade-off: the user caps mean a growing team jumps plans (for example from 7 to 8 users moves you from Team to Pro), and competitors with larger communities, such as Jobber and Housecall Pro, publish more features. RazorSync's case is predictable pricing for a team that fits a cap.

pros_detail.title: Capped per-company pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Solo (2 users), Team (7) and Pro (15) are flat monthly prices, so adding users within a cap doesn't raise the bill.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Desktop and Online
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks sync covers Desktop and Online, included from Team and a $20/month add-on on Solo.

pros_detail.title: Multi-trade coverage
pros_detail.explanation: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, handyman, appliance repair all supported with relevant workflows. Multi-trade operations avoid the dual-platform problem of running separate FSM per service line.

pros_detail.title: Route optimization and inventory on Pro
pros_detail.explanation: Pro includes route optimization and inventory management; lower plans can add route optimization for $50/month.

pros_detail.title: 14-day trial of the full package
pros_detail.explanation: The trial runs on the Enterprise package, so you can test everything, including QuickBooks sync, before choosing a plan.

pros_detail.title: GPS tracking built in
pros_detail.explanation: Tech location tracking with route history. Included at all paid tiers (not premium-only). Important for operations dispatching across service areas and tracking actual vs scheduled service times.

cons_detail.title: Plan jumps at each user cap
cons_detail.explanation: Going from 7 to 8 users moves you from Team ($195/month billed annually) to Pro ($439), more than double, so plan ahead before crossing a cap.

cons_detail.title: Key features are add-ons on lower plans
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks sync is an add-on on Solo, and route optimization is an add-on below Pro; price the plan plus add-ons you need.

cons_detail.title: Smaller community than the market leaders
cons_detail.explanation: Jobber and Housecall Pro have larger user communities and more third-party guides, which helps with self-service learning.

tools.implementation_notes: RazorSync is largely self-service. Set up the account, import customers (manually or by CSV), build the service catalog and roll the mobile app out to techs with GPS tracking. Then set up dispatching and roles, connect QuickBooks (Desktop or Online), and migrate recurring contracts, which is usually the slowest step. Run a few weeks in parallel with your old system and confirm invoices flow into QuickBooks correctly before cutting over.

tool_faqs.q: How does RazorSync compare to Jobber or Housecall Pro?
tool_faqs.a: RazorSync prices per company with user caps (2, 7, 15, then unlimited on Enterprise); Jobber prices plans by team size and Housecall Pro includes 1, 5 or 8 users per plan. For a team of around 5-15, compare the RazorSync plan your headcount needs with the others at the same headcount. Jobber and Housecall Pro have larger user communities and publish more features; RazorSync's case is predictable, capped pricing.

tool_faqs.q: Does RazorSync work with QuickBooks Desktop?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. RazorSync syncs with QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Online; the sync is included from the Team plan and is a $20/month add-on on Solo.

tool_faqs.q: What's the user count for each tier?
tool_faqs.a: Solo covers up to 2 users, Team up to 7, Pro up to 15, and Enterprise is unlimited. Billed annually they cost $85, $195 and $439 a month ($90, $225 and $499 monthly), and Enterprise is quoted.

tool_faqs.q: Is RazorSync's per-company pricing actually cheaper?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on your headcount. At 10 techs you'd need Pro ($439/month billed annually). Housecall Pro Max is $299/month billed annually for 8 users plus $35 for each additional user, about $369 for 10; Jobber prices by team size. Price your actual team on each vendor's current pricing page; capped plans favor teams near the top of a cap.

tool_faqs.q: What's RazorSync best for?
tool_faqs.a: Small-to-mid service businesses (5-15 techs) running multi-trade workflows (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, handyman, appliance repair) where per-company pricing math matters and modern UX is less important than predictable cost. Operations on QuickBooks Desktop specifically get added value from the QB Desktop integration. Operations prioritizing modern features should evaluate Jobber, FieldPulse, or Workiz instead.

tools.name: Tradify
tools.tagline: Job management for trade businesses (UK/AU/NZ-rooted)

pricing.pricing_note: Three tiers per-user/month: Lite $47, Pro $51, Plus $61 (USD); Custom tier by request.

tools.best_for: 1-10 person trade businesses needing quote-to-invoice flow at a low price point
tools.weaknesses: Roots and most customers are in NZ/AU/UK, so US-specific integrations are thinner; timesheets, job photos and purchase orders sit on higher plans; no advanced dispatching for larger teams
tools.long_description:
Tradify is job management software for small trade businesses, founded in 2013 in Auckland, New Zealand by Curtis Bailey, who came to software from electrical engineering. The UK's Access Group acquired Tradify in October 2024; at the time it had about 20,000 customers across New Zealand, Australia and the UK, and it also sells in the United States.

It targets 1-10 person trade businesses with a tight quote-to-invoice workflow and accounting sync: Xero (two-way) and QuickBooks Online everywhere, MYOB in Australia and New Zealand, and Sage in the UK and Ireland, with Stripe for online payments.

Pricing is per user per month in USD: Lite $47 covers job management, scheduling, quotes, invoices, online payments and accounting sync; Pro $51 adds branding, enquiry forms, job photos, recurring jobs, progress invoicing, timesheets and subcontractor scheduling; Plus $61 adds AI SmartTools, service reminders, job tasks, purchase orders, bulk invoicing, kit bundles, staff activity tracking and reporting. A Custom plan is available by request, and there is a 14-day free trial with full access.

The trade-off: Tradify is built for small crews where the owner also works on the tools. Larger operations should check whether it covers their dispatching and reporting needs.

pros_detail.title: Simple per-user pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Three published per-user tiers (Lite $47, Pro $51, Plus $61 per user per month, USD) with a custom tier by request. Predictable, with no sales call needed for small teams.

pros_detail.title: Two-way Xero sync, plus QuickBooks, MYOB and Sage
pros_detail.explanation: Payments recorded in Xero sync back to Tradify and mark invoices paid; QuickBooks Online, MYOB (AU/NZ) and Sage (UK/IE) are supported too.

pros_detail.title: Low entry price
pros_detail.explanation: Lite at $47/user/month (USD) keeps the entry cost low for solo operators and small crews, with Pro and Plus only a few dollars more per user.

pros_detail.title: Tight quote-to-invoice flow
pros_detail.explanation: Quote → approval → job → time tracking → invoice flow is optimized for small trade businesses where the owner needs visibility from quote to payment in one workflow.

pros_detail.title: Strong mobile app for working tradespeople
pros_detail.explanation: Built for operations where the owner is a working tradesperson. Mobile app handles real fieldwork (time tracking, materials capture, customer signatures, photo attachments) without office reliance.

pros_detail.title: 14-day free trial with full access
pros_detail.explanation: The trial includes every feature, including accounting sync setup, so you can test the whole quote-to-invoice flow.

cons_detail.title: US is a secondary market
cons_detail.explanation: Most of Tradify's customers are in New Zealand, Australia and the UK, so US-specific integrations (payroll, local tools) are thinner than those of US-rooted competitors like Jobber or Housecall Pro.

cons_detail.title: Per-user cost scales with headcount
cons_detail.explanation: Every tier is priced per user, so a 10-person crew on Pro runs about $510/month (USD). Larger operations should also check whether the feature set covers advanced dispatching, reporting, or multi-region needs.

cons_detail.title: Limited marketing automation
cons_detail.explanation: No built-in marketing automation, review request workflows, or campaign management. Operations needing marketing automation need to layer Mailchimp or similar through Zapier.

cons_detail.title: Key features sit on higher plans
cons_detail.explanation: Timesheets, job photos and recurring jobs start on Pro; purchase orders, service reminders and reporting are Plus features. Check which plan your workflow needs.

tools.implementation_notes: Tradify is self-service. Set up the account, connect your accounting system (Xero, QuickBooks Online, MYOB or Sage), import customers, build your price book and materials, and install the mobile app for every user. Then run your first jobs end to end: quote, approval, job, time tracking, invoice and accounting sync. Map your chart of accounts carefully during the accounting connection, since that is where most setup mistakes happen.

tool_faqs.q: Is Tradify suitable for US-based trade businesses?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with caveats. The core workflow (quote, schedule, track time, invoice) works for US operations, and Tradify integrates with QuickBooks Online as well as Xero. Its roots and most of its 20,000 customers are in New Zealand, Australia and the UK, so compare US-specific needs (payroll, local integrations) against Jobber or Housecall Pro.

tool_faqs.q: How does Tradify compare to Jobber?
tool_faqs.a: Tradify and Jobber serve similar small-business segments but with different positioning. Tradify: three per-user tiers (Lite $47, Pro $51, Plus $61 per user per month in USD), Xero-first, international roots. Jobber: four plans from $29 to $399/mo billed annually at the smallest team size and priced up by team size, QuickBooks-first, US-rooted, deeper marketing features. Pure cost comparison: at 1 user, Tradify Lite $47 vs Jobber Core $29 billed annually ($49 month-to-month); at 5 users Tradify Lite is $235, while Jobber prices every plan by team size, so compare your actual headcount in both calculators. The trade-off is feature depth versus pricing model.

tool_faqs.q: Does Tradify have an enterprise tier?
tool_faqs.a: Tradify publishes three per-user plans (Lite $47, Pro $51, Plus $61 per user per month in USD) and a Custom plan by request that includes every Plus feature. Larger operations needing multi-region controls or advanced dispatching should also evaluate enterprise platforms. Tradify is built for small trade businesses.

tool_faqs.q: What accounting software does Tradify integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Xero (two-way sync) and QuickBooks Online everywhere, MYOB in Australia and New Zealand, and Sage in the UK and Ireland. There is no QuickBooks Desktop integration, so Desktop users would need to move to QuickBooks Online.

tool_faqs.q: Is Tradify's per-user pricing competitive?
tool_faqs.a: It is mid-priced rather than cheap: Tradify's plans run $47 (Lite), $51 (Pro) and $61 (Plus) per user per month, so a solo operator pays from $47/month and a 5-person team from $235/month. Jobber Core starts lower at $29/month billed annually, and for 5+ user operations, plans with included seats (such as Housecall Pro Essentials, which includes 5 users at $149/mo billed annually) can be cheaper on absolute cost.

tools.best_for: Mid-large field service organizations 25+ techs running mixed fleet + service operations
tools.weaknesses: UK/EU-centered; no published pricing in any region; fleet depth is more than small shops need
tools.long_description:
BigChange is a job management and field service platform founded in Leeds in 2013 by Martin Port. Great Hill Partners invested in 2021, and in October 2024 Simpro Group, another field service software company, acquired BigChange. It serves mid-size and larger field service organizations, with CRM, scheduling, a mobile app for engineers, financial management, stock control, vehicle tracking and business analytics in one platform.

What sets it apart from US-rooted platforms is fleet integration: vehicle tracking sits alongside the job workflow, which suits operations where fleet costs matter. Integrations center on UK accounting (Xero and Sage), with APIs for ERPs and other systems.

Pricing is custom-quoted: the pricing page publishes no plans or rates, lists what all plans include (support, CRM, job scheduling, a mobile app, live tracking, quote and invoice, business intelligence and a collaboration network) and sends buyers to a 'Request pricing' demo request.

The trade-off: BigChange is built for mid-size and larger operations with fleets, and its community and integrations lean UK. Small US shops usually fit better on Jobber, Housecall Pro or FieldPulse.

pros_detail.title: Vehicle tracking with job management
pros_detail.explanation: Fleet location and job workflows in one platform, useful where vehicles are a major cost.

pros_detail.title: AI features
pros_detail.explanation: BigChange markets AI across scheduling and job workflows; see what is live in a demo.

pros_detail.title: Core modules in every plan
pros_detail.explanation: BigChange's pricing page says all plans include support, CRM, job scheduling, the mobile app, live tracking, quote and invoice, business intelligence and the collaboration network. It lists AI Dashcams, Fleet, Fuel Cards, DaaS and Unlimited Data and Smartphone as extras, so ask which extras your quote includes.

pros_detail.title: Xero and Sage integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Native Xero and Sage integrations suit businesses in the UK, Australia and New Zealand on those systems.

pros_detail.title: Stock control built in
pros_detail.explanation: Parts and equipment inventory management integrated with FSM workflows. Important for service operations with significant parts handling, since operations can avoid running separate inventory management software.

pros_detail.title: Established, now part of Simpro Group
pros_detail.explanation: Founded in 2013 and acquired by Simpro Group in 2024, BigChange sits inside one of the larger field service software groups.

cons_detail.title: US market presence still growing
cons_detail.explanation: Originated in UK; US user community is smaller than ServiceTitan, FieldEdge, or BuildOps. US-specific features (US payroll integrations, US change order workflows) less mature than US-rooted competitors.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing in any region
cons_detail.explanation: BigChange publishes no plans or rates; the pricing page sends buyers to a 'Request pricing' demo request, so get a written quote for your headcount and any extras you need.

cons_detail.title: Implementation is a project
cons_detail.explanation: Mid-size and larger deployments, especially with fleet tracking, take real configuration and training time; get the implementation plan and any fees in writing.

cons_detail.title: Fleet features overkill for small operations
cons_detail.explanation: Operations under 25 techs without significant fleet management needs pay for vehicle tracking depth they won't use. Smaller operations get better fit from FSM platforms without the fleet integration premium.

cons_detail.title: Smaller US user community
cons_detail.explanation: Most case studies, tutorials, and YouTube content come from UK market. US-specific guidance is thinner than for US-rooted competitors. Self-service learning ecosystem is UK-leaning.

tools.implementation_notes: Plan a phased deployment. Start with discovery and configuration: accounting integration (Xero or Sage), user roles and permissions, and vehicle onboarding with tracking devices if you use them. Then migrate customers, recurring contracts and stock, configure dispatch, train office staff, then field engineers on the mobile app, and run in parallel with your old system before cutting over. Moving from a US-rooted FSM usually needs more reconstruction than moving from paper or spreadsheets.

tool_faqs.q: Is BigChange suitable for US-based service operations?
tool_faqs.a: Yes for mid-large US operations (25+ techs) with significant fleet management needs. BigChange publishes no prices, so compare its written quote with quotes from US-rooted platforms at your headcount. US-specific features (US payroll integrations, US tax handling, US-style change order workflows) are less mature than US-rooted competitors. For US operations without significant fleet needs or under 25 techs, evaluate Jobber, Housecall Pro, FieldPulse, or Sera Systems instead.

tool_faqs.q: How does BigChange compare to ServiceTitan?
tool_faqs.a: Neither vendor publishes prices: BigChange's pricing page sends buyers to a 'Request pricing' demo request, and ServiceTitan's pricing page says its pricing is per technician, with every package showing 'Request Pricing'. ServiceTitan has the larger US presence and US-specific depth; BigChange, now part of Simpro Group, is strongest in the UK and in fleet-heavy operations. Get quotes from both at your headcount.

tool_faqs.q: What's BigChange's fleet management capability?
tool_faqs.a: BigChange includes vehicle tracking alongside its job management, so fleet location and job workflows live in one system. If fleet costs matter to your business, ask in the demo exactly which fleet reports (fuel, driver behavior, maintenance) are included in your quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does BigChange integrate with Xero?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. BigChange integrates with Xero and Sage, and offers APIs for ERPs and other systems. US businesses on QuickBooks should confirm how BigChange connects to it before buying.

tool_faqs.q: What's the AI in BigChange?
tool_faqs.a: BigChange markets AI features across its platform. Ask for a demo of what is live today (job assignment suggestions, scheduling help, customer messages) versus on the roadmap, and whether it's included in your quote.

tools.name: MrTask (formerly Field Complete)
tools.tagline: Field service management with a job-sharing network

pricing.pricing_note: Per company/month: Solo $39.99/mo (1 user +1 bonus), Team $99.99/mo (limited-time 50% off at $49.99; +5 users), Business $199.99/mo (+10 users), Enterprise custom-quoted; additional users $19.99/user/mo. Prices are billed monthly; the pricing page gives no annual price. Verified against mrtask.com/pricing 2026-10-03.

tools.best_for: Small and mid-size service businesses that want affordable FSM, with the option to join a job-sharing network
tools.weaknesses: QuickBooks Desktop and Zapier only on the Business plan; per-user fees beyond included seats
tools.long_description:
MrTask, formerly Field Complete, is field service management software for small and mid-size service businesses, based in Sandy Springs, Georgia. It covers scheduling, dispatching, estimates and invoicing, and every plan includes Job Sharing, a network you can join to receive more jobs.

Pricing is per company with included users: Solo $39.99 a month (1 user plus 1 bonus user), Team $99.99 (currently 50% off at $49.99; 5 users), Business $199.99 (10 users) and Enterprise on a quote, with additional users at $19.99 a month each. There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card.

QuickBooks Online is on every plan; QuickBooks Desktop and Zapier come with Business, and Stripe handles payments.

The trade-off: MrTask is smaller than Jobber or Housecall Pro, with fewer case studies and third-party guides. Its case is a low entry price and the job-sharing network.

pros_detail.title: Job Sharing network
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes Job Sharing, which lets you join MrTask's network and receive more jobs.

pros_detail.title: Low entry price
pros_detail.explanation: Solo is $39.99/month for 1 user plus a bonus user, and Team is currently $49.99/month for 5 users, so small operations can start cheaply.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online sync is included on all plans, with QuickBooks Desktop and Zapier on Business.

pros_detail.title: 14-day free trial, no credit card
pros_detail.explanation: Test scheduling, dispatch and invoicing on real jobs before you pay.

cons_detail.title: Smaller user base
cons_detail.explanation: MrTask has a smaller user community than Jobber, Housecall Pro or ServiceTitan, with fewer case studies and third-party guides.

cons_detail.title: Seat costs beyond included users
cons_detail.explanation: Plans include a set number of users (Solo 1 plus a bonus user, Team 5, Business 10), and additional users are $19.99/month each, so larger teams should model the total.

cons_detail.title: Some integrations need Business
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Desktop and Zapier are Business-plan features, so shops that depend on them should price that plan.

tools.implementation_notes: Onboarding is largely self-service; confirm what help your plan includes. Import customers and properties, set up your service catalog and prices, roll the mobile app out to techs, and connect QuickBooks. Decide whether to join the Job Sharing network, then run a few weeks of jobs alongside your old process before cutting over.

tool_faqs.q: Who is MrTask best for?
tool_faqs.a: Small and mid-size service businesses that want affordable scheduling, dispatch and invoicing, and that may want extra work through the Job Sharing network included on every plan.

tool_faqs.q: What is MrTask's Job Sharing?
tool_faqs.a: Job Sharing lets you become part of MrTask's network and receive more jobs. Ask MrTask how jobs are shared, who they come from and what fees apply before relying on it for revenue.

tool_faqs.q: How does MrTask compare to general FSM platforms?
tool_faqs.a: It covers the core FSM workflow at a low price, with QuickBooks Online on every plan. Larger platforms such as Jobber or Housecall Pro have bigger communities and more published features; compare trials.

tool_faqs.q: Is MrTask the same as Field Complete?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Field Complete was renamed MrTask; older guides and reviews use the Field Complete name.

tool_faqs.q: Is MrTask worth the price?
tool_faqs.a: At $39.99/month for Solo or $49.99/month for Team (currently discounted), it is inexpensive. Use the 14-day free trial to check whether the workflow fits and whether Job Sharing brings work in your area.
