pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote; AccuLynx publishes no prices.

tools.best_for: Established roofing companies (5-100 employees) running insurance claims and storm restoration work
tools.weaknesses: Roofing-specific, not for general trades; no published pricing; no Xactimate integration listed
tools.long_description:
AccuLynx is CRM and project management software for residential roofing and exterior contractors, founded in 2008 by Rich Spanton in Beloit, Wisconsin. It is privately held; Verisk agreed to buy it for $2.35 billion in 2025 but later called the deal off.

The product follows a roofing job from lead to payment: sales and door-to-door workflows, measurements ordered from EagleView, Hover, Geospan or GAF QuickMeasure that populate the estimate, material ordering through QXO (Beacon), ABC Supply and SRS, production scheduling and crews, photo documentation, insurance jobs with supplements and documents in the job file, commissions, and AccuPay card and ACH payments. Other integrations include QuickBooks, Sage Intacct, CompanyCam, GreenSky financing, Angi, SalesRabbit and Spotio.

AccuLynx publishes no prices; quotes come from sales. Xactimate is not listed among its integrations, so insurance-heavy shops should check how estimates from carriers fit their workflow.

Best for residential roofing companies running retail and insurance work. Commercial roofing and general trades fit better elsewhere.

pros_detail.title: Built around the roofing job
pros_detail.explanation: Sales, measurements, estimates, material orders, production, insurance supplements and payments in one system designed for roofing contractors.

pros_detail.title: Measurement ordering built in
pros_detail.explanation: Order EagleView, Hover, Geospan or GAF QuickMeasure reports from AccuLynx, with measurements flowing straight into the estimate.

pros_detail.title: Supplier ordering
pros_detail.explanation: Direct integrations with QXO (Beacon), ABC Supply and SRS Distribution turn measurements into material orders without re-keying.

pros_detail.title: Door-to-door sales workflow for storm-chasers
pros_detail.explanation: Mobile workflow designed for D2D sales: rep walks neighborhood post-storm, captures damage photos, drafts signed agreements at the door, schedules inspections. Lead flows automatically to project managers and install crews.

pros_detail.title: AccuPay payments
pros_detail.explanation: Card and ACH payments can be requested and processed inside AccuLynx, with GreenSky available for homeowner financing.

pros_detail.title: Commission and lead-source tracking
pros_detail.explanation: Multi-tier commissions (sales rep + project manager + installer crews) and lead-source attribution help operators track per-channel CAC and optimize sales workflows. Critical for storm-chaser commission structures.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: AccuLynx quotes each account, so budgeting starts with a sales call; get the quote, contract length and any implementation fees in writing.

cons_detail.title: Residential roofing focus
cons_detail.explanation: Commercial roofing that runs like construction projects, and trades outside roofing and exteriors, fit better on other platforms.

cons_detail.title: Roofing insurance workflow to learn
cons_detail.explanation: The insurance workflow uses terminology and process specific to roofing (supplements, scope adjustments, approved vs requested billing), so plan training time for office staff without roofing experience.

cons_detail.title: No Xactimate integration listed
cons_detail.explanation: Insurance-heavy shops that want to import Xactimate estimates should confirm how AccuLynx handles carrier estimates before buying.

tools.implementation_notes: Plan a phased rollout. Import contacts and open jobs from your old CRM, then connect measurements (EagleView, Hover, GAF QuickMeasure), your supplier and QuickBooks. Train office staff on the job workflow, insurance supplements and material ordering, then field crews on photo documentation, then sales reps on the mobile workflow before cutting over. The biggest change for shops coming from spreadsheets is adopting a structured job file and photo standards.

tool_faqs.q: Is AccuLynx good software for storm restoration roofing?
tool_faqs.a: It is built for residential roofing, including insurance and storm work: claim details, supplements and documents live in the job file, measurements order straight from EagleView, Hover, Geospan or GAF QuickMeasure, and materials order through QXO, ABC Supply and SRS. JobNimbus is the closest alternative; compare both on your own insurance workflow.

tool_faqs.q: How does AccuLynx compare to JobNimbus?
tool_faqs.a: Both are built for residential roofing and both connect to aerial measurements and suppliers. AccuLynx is roofing-specialty with commission tracking and AccuPay payments; JobNimbus adds restoration and other exterior work and owns SumoQuote proposals. Compare them on your workflow and get written quotes from both, since neither publishes prices.

tool_faqs.q: Does AccuLynx handle commercial roofing?
tool_faqs.a: It is built around residential roofing. Commercial roofing that is project-based, with progress billing and subcontractor management, should check the fit in a demo or look at construction project platforms.

tool_faqs.q: Does AccuLynx integrate with Xactimate?
tool_faqs.a: Xactimate is not listed among AccuLynx's integrations. AccuLynx keeps supplements and insurance documents in the job file, but if you need to import Xactimate estimates directly, confirm how AccuLynx handles it in a demo, or compare JobNimbus, which connects to Xactimate on its legacy financials.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns AccuLynx?
tool_faqs.a: AccuLynx is a privately held company in Beloit, Wisconsin, founded in 2008 by Rich Spanton. Verisk agreed to acquire it for $2.35 billion in 2025 but later called the deal off.

tools.name: JobNimbus
tools.tagline: CRM and project management for contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote; pricing based on plan tier (Essentials/Pro/Premium/Enterprise), user count, and add-ons; prices not published on vendor site.

tools.best_for: Roofing, exterior and restoration contractors that want a CRM and project management system built around the roofing sales cycle
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing; Xactimate integration works only with legacy financials; roofing-first, so other trades may find it a loose fit
tools.long_description:
JobNimbus is a CRM and project management platform for roofing and exterior contractors, founded in 2013 in Lehi, Utah by Ben Hodson, Nick Wood and Jason Wood. In November 2024 Sumeru Equity Partners made a $330 million strategic investment in the company, and in January 2024 JobNimbus acquired SumoQuote, the roofing estimate and proposal tool.

The product covers the roofing sales and production cycle: lead capture, a CRM with contact history and pipelines, estimates and proposals, project management with task automation, invoicing and payments, and photo documentation. Its integration list is broad for the trade: aerial measurements from EagleView and Hover, supplier ordering and pricing through Beacon, ABC Supply and SRS, QuickBooks (Desktop, Online and Server), CompanyCam, Zapier and more than 50 tools in all. Xactimate and XactAnalysis connect too, but only with JobNimbus's legacy financials.

JobNimbus doesn't publish prices; plans (Essentials, Pro, Premium and Enterprise) are quoted by tier, user count and add-ons. It competes most directly with AccuLynx for residential roofing, and restoration contractors use it for the same project-based workflow.

The trade-off: it is built around roofing and exterior work. Commercial roofing and trades outside exteriors should check that the workflow fits before committing.

pros_detail.title: Built around the roofing sales cycle
pros_detail.explanation: Lead capture, CRM pipelines, proposals, production and invoicing in one system, designed for roofing and exterior contractors.

pros_detail.title: Measurement and supplier integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Order EagleView reports and use Hover measurements from inside JobNimbus, and build estimates with Beacon, ABC Supply and SRS pricing and ordering.

pros_detail.title: SumoQuote proposals
pros_detail.explanation: JobNimbus owns SumoQuote, the roofing estimate and proposal tool, which it acquired in January 2024.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Desktop, Online and Server
pros_detail.explanation: Contacts, jobs, products and services, estimates, invoices and payments sync with QuickBooks, including Desktop and Server editions.

pros_detail.title: CRM with task automation
pros_detail.explanation: Contact history, pipelines and automated tasks suit longer sales cycles such as insurance and storm work.

pros_detail.title: Restoration work in the same system
pros_detail.explanation: Restoration uses the same project-based workflow (photos, insurance coordination, multi-step jobs), so a roofing and restoration contractor can run both in one platform.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: JobNimbus quotes by plan, user count and add-ons, so get a written quote for your team before comparing it with AccuLynx or other roofing CRMs.

cons_detail.title: Xactimate only with legacy financials
cons_detail.explanation: JobNimbus's help center says the Xactimate / XactAnalysis integration works only with its legacy financials, so insurance-heavy shops should confirm how it fits their setup.

cons_detail.title: Roofing-first
cons_detail.explanation: The workflow is built around roofing and exterior sales. Other trades, and commercial roofing with complex progress billing, should check the fit in a demo.

tools.implementation_notes: Plan a phased rollout. Import contacts and open jobs from your old CRM, then connect the integrations you rely on (EagleView or Hover for measurements, your supplier, QuickBooks, Xactimate if you use legacy financials). Train office staff on the CRM pipeline and task automation, then field crews on photo documentation, then sales reps on the mobile workflow before you cut over. Moving from another roofing CRM is usually simpler than moving from spreadsheets, because the data models are similar.

tool_faqs.q: Should I use JobNimbus or AccuLynx for residential roofing?
tool_faqs.a: Both are built for residential roofing, and both connect to aerial measurement and supplier tools. Compare them on your own workflow: the insurance process, supplier ordering, commission tracking and reporting. Neither publishes prices, so get written quotes from both for your team size.

tool_faqs.q: Can JobNimbus handle commercial roofing?
tool_faqs.a: It is built around residential roofing and exterior work. Commercial roofing that is project-based, with progress billing and subcontractor management, should check the fit in a demo or look at construction project platforms.

tool_faqs.q: How does JobNimbus pricing compare to AccuLynx?
tool_faqs.a: Neither publishes prices. JobNimbus quotes by plan (Essentials, Pro, Premium, Enterprise), user count and add-ons; AccuLynx also quotes per account. Get written quotes from both for the same team and feature set.

tool_faqs.q: Does JobNimbus have a referral program?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, for existing customers only: customers who refer other contractors to JobNimbus earn credit.

tool_faqs.q: How does JobNimbus handle restoration work alongside roofing?
tool_faqs.a: Restoration (water, fire and mold jobs) uses a similar project-based workflow: photo documentation, insurance coordination and multi-step project management. JobNimbus runs it in the same CRM and project tools as roofing, so a contractor doing both doesn't need two platforms.

tools.name: FieldRoutes
tools.tagline: Pest control and lawn care field service software from FieldRoutes, a ServiceTitan company

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote. Growth ('Ideal for Small Businesses') and Corporate ('Perfect for Scaling') both show 'Request Pricing'; the subscription is based on the number of active customers, not a per-user rate. Both packages list the same features (route optimization, tech mobile app, mobile sales, lead management, customer payment portal, premium API, real-time reporting, Sentricon). No free trial; free demo only. Verified against fieldroutes.com/company/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Pest control and lawn care companies running recurring service routes that want scheduling, routing, sales and billing in one system
tools.weaknesses: No published prices and no free trial; the price scales with your number of active customers. Built for pest control and lawn care, so other trades get a weaker fit.
tools.long_description:
FieldRoutes is field service software for pest control and lawn care companies. It grew out of two businesses: PestRoutes, route and sales software for pest control, and Lobster Marketing, a pest control marketing agency. FieldRoutes' own timeline traces PestRoutes to TextRoutes, a door-to-door sales app Jared Green built in 2009, and the 2022 acquisition announcement says the platform was co-founded in 2013 by CTO Rubens Basso. Mainsail Partners acquired both companies in 2018, Gryphon Investors invested in 2020, and in 2021 the combined business rebranded as FieldRoutes and expanded into lawn care.

ServiceTitan announced its agreement to acquire FieldRoutes on January 4, 2022. As part of that deal, ServicePro, which ServiceTitan had bought the year before, moved under FieldRoutes, and its product is now sold as ServSuite by FieldRoutes. FieldRoutes is not part of WorkWave, which makes the competing PestPac and RealGreen. FieldRoutes lists its address in Chesterfield, Missouri; at the time of the acquisition it was based in McKinney, Texas.

The core product, which FieldRoutes calls the Operations Suite, covers drag-and-drop scheduling, route optimization, recurring services, automated reminders, billing with AutoPay, card and ACH payments, a customer payment portal, a mobile app for technicians, mobile sales tools, lead management and real-time reporting. Its pest control pages also list chemical and product tracking and Sentricon integration for termite work. Two ServiceTitan products plug in: Marketing Pro for email and direct mail campaigns built from FieldRoutes data, and Fleet Pro for fleet management. QuickBooks and other accounting systems sync through its integrations, and an open API is available. FieldRoutes names large pest brands such as Aptive and Fox Pest Control among its customers.

Pricing is by quote. The pricing page shows two packages, Growth (pitched at small businesses) and Corporate (for companies that are scaling), both marked 'Request Pricing'. FieldRoutes says the subscription is based on your number of active customers rather than a per-user rate, and both packages list the same core features. There is no free trial; FieldRoutes offers a free demo instead.

The trade-off: you cannot see a price until you talk to sales, and because the fee is tied to active customers, your cost grows with your book of business. Marketing Pro and Fleet Pro are separate products to budget for. The software is built around pest control and lawn care, so HVAC, plumbing or electrical shops will find better-fitting tools elsewhere. Small pest companies that want to see prices up front can compare GorillaDesk, which publishes its plans.

pros_detail.title: Built for recurring pest and lawn routes
pros_detail.explanation: Recurring services, route optimization, drag-and-drop scheduling and automated reminders are core features, matching how pest control and lawn care companies run repeat service.

pros_detail.title: Sales and lead tools included
pros_detail.explanation: Both packages include mobile sales capabilities and lead management, useful for pest companies that sell door to door. The product traces back to a door-to-door sales app.

pros_detail.title: Termite and chemical tools
pros_detail.explanation: Sentricon integration is listed on both packages, and FieldRoutes' pest control page lists chemical and product tracking.

pros_detail.title: Payments and customer portal built in
pros_detail.explanation: Card and ACH payments, AutoPay, batch payments and a customer payment portal are part of the Operations Suite.

pros_detail.title: ServiceTitan add-ons and accounting sync
pros_detail.explanation: As a ServiceTitan company, FieldRoutes connects to ServiceTitan Marketing Pro for email and direct mail campaigns and to Fleet Pro. QuickBooks sync and an open API are also available.

pros_detail.title: Priced on customers, not seats
pros_detail.explanation: FieldRoutes prices the subscription on your number of active customers rather than per user, and both packages list the same features.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: Both packages show 'Request Pricing', so you need a sales call to get a number.

cons_detail.title: No free trial
cons_detail.explanation: FieldRoutes offers a free demo but no trial, so you cannot test it with your own data before you sign.

cons_detail.title: Cost grows with your customer count
cons_detail.explanation: Because the fee is based on active customers, a growing customer list can raise your bill even if your team size stays the same.

cons_detail.title: Narrow trade focus
cons_detail.explanation: It is designed for pest control and lawn care. HVAC, plumbing and electrical companies are better served by general field service tools.

cons_detail.title: Marketing and fleet tools are separate products
cons_detail.explanation: Email and direct mail campaigns (Marketing Pro) and fleet management (Fleet Pro) are ServiceTitan products outside the core Operations Suite, so price them separately.

tools.implementation_notes: Start by booking a demo, since there is no free trial. Ask for a quote based on your current active customer count and ask how the price changes as that count grows. Before moving over, export your customer list, recurring service schedules, service history and open balances from your current system, and ask FieldRoutes what its team handles during data import and training. Set up routes and service intervals, chemical and product records, Sentricon if you use it, and payment settings (AutoPay and the customer portal) before go-live. If you use QuickBooks, confirm how the sync handles invoices and payments, and if you want Marketing Pro or Fleet Pro, price them in the same conversation.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns FieldRoutes, and is it part of WorkWave?
tool_faqs.a: FieldRoutes is a ServiceTitan company, not part of WorkWave. ServiceTitan announced its agreement to acquire FieldRoutes (formerly PestRoutes and Lobster Marketing) on January 4, 2022. ServicePro, which ServiceTitan bought in 2021, moved under FieldRoutes, so ServSuite is now sold as ServSuite by FieldRoutes. WorkWave is a separate company that makes the competing PestPac and RealGreen.

tool_faqs.q: How much does FieldRoutes cost?
tool_faqs.a: FieldRoutes does not publish prices. Its pricing page lists two packages, Growth and Corporate, both marked 'Request Pricing', and says the subscription is based on your number of active customers. There is no free trial, only a free demo.

tool_faqs.q: How does FieldRoutes compare to PestPac?
tool_faqs.a: They come from competing companies: FieldRoutes from ServiceTitan, PestPac from WorkWave. Both are quote-only and cover routing, mobile apps, customer portals and Sentricon. FieldRoutes sells two packages priced on active customers; PestPac sells three packages (Small Business, Professional and Enterprise). Demo both with your own route data and compare written quotes.

tool_faqs.q: Does FieldRoutes handle termite work?
tool_faqs.a: FieldRoutes lists Sentricon integration on both of its packages. Ask in the demo how it handles the termite and WDO paperwork your state requires.

tool_faqs.q: Does FieldRoutes serve lawn care companies?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. FieldRoutes expanded from pest control into lawn care when it rebranded in 2021, and it markets to both industries.

tool_faqs.q: Does FieldRoutes integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. FieldRoutes says QuickBooks and other accounting systems sync with it, and it offers an open API for other connections.

tools.name: PestPac
tools.affiliate_note: Applied through parent company WorkWave's referral program; no decision received. We earn nothing from this tool today.
tools.tagline: Pest control software from WorkWave, sold in three quote-based packages

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote. The pricing page lists three packages with no prices and asks buyers to speak with a consultant: Small Business (basic scheduling and routing, termite inspection, mobile app, billing and payments, basic accounting, customer portal), Professional (adds smart scheduling and route optimization, IPM and multi-unit support, general ledger export, lead management, marketing automation) and Enterprise (adds multi-branch and API integrations). No free trial is advertised. Verified against pestpac.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Pest control companies, from small shops to multi-branch operations, that want termite, commercial and chemical tracking tools in one pest-specific system and are comfortable buying by quote
tools.weaknesses: No published prices or trial; route optimization, marketing automation and the general ledger export start on the Professional package; the QuickBooks connection is an export, not a live sync.
tools.long_description:
PestPac is pest control management software from WorkWave, a field service software company headquartered in Holmdel, New Jersey. WorkWave says it has served the field service industry for more than 40 years and has served more than 8,000 companies across its products, which also include RealGreen for lawn care. PestPac is not related to FieldRoutes or ServSuite, which belong to ServiceTitan.

PestPac covers scheduling, routing and route optimization, a technician mobile app, customer management, billing and accounting, integrated payments, chemical tracking and inventory, digital forms and proposals, business analytics, and a customer portal called CustomerConnect where customers can view their accounts, run reports, schedule service and pay bills. For commercial work it offers integrated pest management (IPM) and multi-unit support, and its marketing tools handle email marketing and drip campaigns. PestPac also includes a website builder.

Termite work is a focus. PestPac says it can automatically submit Sentricon reports, lets technicians scan and inspect Sentricon bait stations from a phone or tablet, and fills in WDI/WDO and NPMA-33 forms, including California WDO forms, with account information in the field.

Pricing is by quote. The pricing page lists three packages with no prices. Small Business covers customer management, basic scheduling and routing, termite inspection, the mobile app, billing and payments, basic accounting and reporting, and the customer portal. Professional adds smart scheduling and route optimization, IPM and multi-unit support, digital forms, a general ledger export, custom reporting, lead management, eCommerce and marketing automation. Enterprise adds multi-branch management, auditor reports and API integrations. Payments run through WorkWave Payments (cards, ACH and online invoice payment links), with WorkWave Pay Over Time customer financing for jobs from $500 to $25,000. For accounting, PestPac exports financial totals to QuickBooks rather than syncing live. Its partner list includes Avalara, Azuga, Verizon Connect, Linxup, CallTrackingMetrics, Coalmarch and Waypoint Analytical, and a cloud API is available for custom integrations.

The trade-off: you need a sales call to see any price, several of the most useful tools (route optimization, marketing automation, the general ledger export) sit in the Professional package or above, and the QuickBooks connection is a periodic export. Payment processing is tied to WorkWave's own service rather than Stripe or Square. Companies that want published prices can compare GorillaDesk, and larger operations may also want to demo FieldRoutes.

pros_detail.title: Termite and Sentricon tools
pros_detail.explanation: Automatic Sentricon report submission, bait station scanning from phones and tablets, and WDI/WDO and NPMA-33 forms that pre-fill in the field.

pros_detail.title: Pest-specific features
pros_detail.explanation: Chemical tracking and inventory, IPM and multi-unit support for commercial accounts, digital templates and proposals, and a technician mobile app.

pros_detail.title: Customer self-service
pros_detail.explanation: The CustomerConnect portal lets customers access their accounts, run reports, schedule service and pay bills.

pros_detail.title: Built-in payments and financing
pros_detail.explanation: WorkWave Payments handles cards, ACH and online payment links inside PestPac, and Pay Over Time offers customer financing for jobs from $500 to $25,000.

pros_detail.title: Packages that scale to multiple branches
pros_detail.explanation: The Enterprise package adds multi-branch management and API integrations, and the PestPac Cloud API allows custom integrations.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: All three packages are quote-only, and no free trial is advertised.

cons_detail.title: Key tools in higher packages
cons_detail.explanation: Route optimization, smart scheduling, marketing automation and lead management start on Professional; multi-branch management and API integrations need Enterprise.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks is an export
cons_detail.explanation: PestPac exports financial totals to QuickBooks for your general ledger; it is not a live two-way sync, and the general ledger export is listed from the Professional package.

cons_detail.title: Payments tied to WorkWave
cons_detail.explanation: PestPac's integrated payments run through WorkWave Payments; Stripe and Square are not listed as options.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and ask for quotes on the package you need (Small Business, Professional or Enterprise); check whether route optimization, marketing automation and the general ledger export, which start on Professional, matter to you. Before migrating, export customers, service agreements, service history, termite records and open balances from your current system, and ask WorkWave what its team handles during data import and training. Set up chemical and inventory records, termite and WDO form templates, and Sentricon reporting if you use it. Plan your accounting routine around a regular export to QuickBooks, set up WorkWave Payments for cards and ACH, and roll out the mobile app to technicians before go-live.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns PestPac?
tool_faqs.a: WorkWave, which is headquartered in Holmdel, New Jersey and also owns RealGreen. PestPac is not part of ServiceTitan, which owns the competing FieldRoutes and ServSuite.

tool_faqs.q: How much does PestPac cost?
tool_faqs.a: PestPac does not publish prices. Its pricing page lists Small Business, Professional and Enterprise packages and asks you to speak with a consultant for a quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does PestPac integrate with Sentricon?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. PestPac says it can automatically submit Sentricon reports and lets technicians scan and inspect Sentricon devices and manage bait stations from a phone or tablet.

tool_faqs.q: Does PestPac work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: PestPac exports financial totals to QuickBooks, which then acts as your general ledger. It is an export you run on your own schedule, not a live sync, and the general ledger export is listed from the Professional package.

tool_faqs.q: How does PestPac compare to FieldRoutes?
tool_faqs.a: They come from competing companies: PestPac from WorkWave, FieldRoutes from ServiceTitan. Both are quote-only and cover routing, mobile apps, customer portals and Sentricon. PestPac sells three packages; FieldRoutes sells two and prices on your number of active customers. Demo both with your own route and termite data.

tool_faqs.q: How does PestPac handle payments?
tool_faqs.a: Through WorkWave Payments: credit and debit cards, ACH and online invoice payment links, plus WorkWave Pay Over Time customer financing for jobs from $500 to $25,000.

tools.name: ZenMaid
tools.tagline: Scheduling, reminders and payments software for maid services and residential cleaning companies

pricing.pricing_note: Per-company monthly plans: Starter $19/month for up to 40 appointments a month; Pro $39/month and Pro Max $49/month with unlimited appointments. Month to month with no commitment; no annual price is published. SMS charges are not included. QuickBooks integration from Pro; Mailchimp, Zapier and custom-branded booking forms on Pro Max. 14-day free trial. Verified against get.zenmaid.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential cleaning and maid service businesses that want scheduling, automated client reminders, booking forms and card payments at a low flat monthly price
tools.weaknesses: Text message charges are extra on every plan; Starter caps you at 40 appointments a month and has no GPS tracking; QuickBooks needs Pro and Mailchimp or Zapier need Pro Max; built for maid services rather than multi-trade or commercial janitorial work
tools.long_description:
ZenMaid is scheduling and business software for residential cleaning and maid service companies. Co-founder and CEO Amar Ghose started it in April 2013 after running his own maid service, Fast Friendly Spotless. The company's site says it is made in Palo Alto, California, and its team is spread across several countries. ZenMaid says more than 3,000 cleaning businesses use it.

The core is a drag-and-drop scheduling calendar with dispatch and map views, automated appointment confirmations and reminders by text and email, on-my-way notifications, invoicing with billing reminders, and card payments through Stripe or Square. The cleaner app for iOS and Android shows the schedule, entry instructions and job notes, handles clock-in and clock-out, lets cleaners add notes and photos, and has an SOS button that alerts the office.

Pricing is per company, not per user. Starter is $19 a month and covers up to 40 appointments a month. Pro is $39 a month and Pro Max $49 a month, both with unlimited appointments. Plans are month to month with a 14-day free trial, and text message charges are billed on top. Pro adds digital checklists, GPS tracking in the app, online booking forms, reports and payroll, QuickBooks integration and a tool ZenMaid calls Spotfinder for fitting in recurring customers. Pro Max adds Mailchimp and Zapier integrations, booking forms with your own branding, cleaner availability and PTO tracking, service ratings, data export and priority support. ZenMaid also advertises free migration help.

The trade-off: ZenMaid is built for maid services, so businesses that mix cleaning with other trades, or that run commercial janitorial contracts with site inspections, may be better served by a general field service tool or a commercial cleaning platform. Starter's 40-appointment cap and missing GPS tracking push most working teams to Pro, and texts cost extra on every plan. We did not find in-app team chat or a customer self-service portal on ZenMaid's product pages, so ask about those if you need them.

pros_detail.title: Built for maid services
pros_detail.explanation: Scheduling, reminders, booking forms and the cleaner app are designed around residential cleaning work, and the founder ran his own maid service before building the software.

pros_detail.title: Low flat price per company
pros_detail.explanation: Plans run $19 to $49 a month for the whole business rather than per cleaner, so adding staff does not raise the subscription. Only Starter limits volume (40 appointments a month).

pros_detail.title: Automated client messages
pros_detail.explanation: Appointment confirmations, reminders, on-my-way notifications and billing reminders go out by text and email from templates, which cuts down on phone calls from the office.

pros_detail.title: Practical cleaner app
pros_detail.explanation: Cleaners see their schedule, entry instructions and pet notes, clock in and out, add notes and photos, and can press an SOS button to alert the office. GPS tracking and digital checklists come with Pro.

pros_detail.title: Easy to try and to leave
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan has a 14-day free trial and runs month to month with no commitment, and ZenMaid offers free migration help from your current system.

cons_detail.title: Text messages cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: SMS charges are not included in any plan, so a business that leans on text reminders pays more than the headline price. Estimate your monthly text volume before choosing.

cons_detail.title: Integrations depend on plan
cons_detail.explanation: Stripe and Square work on every plan, but QuickBooks needs Pro and Mailchimp or Zapier need Pro Max. The native list is short, so other tools usually go through Zapier.

cons_detail.title: Starter is limited
cons_detail.explanation: Starter caps you at 40 appointments a month, leaves out GPS tracking, checklists and booking forms, and offers chat-only support.

cons_detail.title: Narrow focus
cons_detail.explanation: ZenMaid is aimed at maid services. Companies that combine cleaning with other trades, or that need inspection and quality-control tools for commercial contracts, may find gaps.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 14-day trial and ask ZenMaid about its free migration help before importing clients yourself. Set up your services, cleaners and recurring appointments first, then connect Stripe or Square so client cards can be stored and charged. Write your confirmation, reminder and on-my-way templates, and estimate how many texts you send each month, since SMS is billed separately. Have cleaners install the mobile app and practice clock-in, notes and photos on a few real jobs. Choose Pro if you need QuickBooks, GPS tracking or checklists, and Pro Max if you need Mailchimp, Zapier or booking forms with your own branding. Add the booking form to your website last, once your pricing and availability are set.

tool_faqs.q: How much does ZenMaid cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starter is $19 a month for up to 40 appointments a month, Pro is $39 a month and Pro Max is $49 a month, both with unlimited appointments. Prices are per company, plans are month to month, and text message charges are extra. There is a 14-day free trial.

tool_faqs.q: Does ZenMaid integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, on Pro and Pro Max. Stripe and Square card payments are available on every plan, and Mailchimp and Zapier integrations are included with Pro Max.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a mobile app for cleaners?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. ZenMaid's app is on iOS and Android. Cleaners can see their schedule and job notes, clock in and out, send on-my-way texts, add notes and photos, and use an SOS alert. GPS tracking in the app starts on Pro.

tool_faqs.q: Can ZenMaid handle commercial janitorial work?
tool_faqs.a: ZenMaid markets itself to maid services and residential cleaning companies. We did not find commercial janitorial tools such as site inspections or client quality surveys on its site, so commercial contract cleaners may want an inspection-focused platform such as Otuvy (formerly CleanTelligent).

tool_faqs.q: Is there a contract or free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Every plan comes with a 14-day free trial and is billed month to month with no commitment, according to ZenMaid's pricing page.

tools.name: JobTread
tools.tagline: Modern construction project management software

pricing.pricing_note: $199/mo base including 1 internal user. Additional internal users per month: $20 each for users 2-10, $15 for 11-20, $10 for 21-30, $5 for 31+ ($16/$12/$8/$4 on annual billing, which saves 20%). Unlimited customer and vendor portal users are free. Every feature included; no contract, no setup fees; free implementation, training and support. No free trial; monthly subscriptions carry a 30-day money-back guarantee. Verified against jobtread.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Home builders, remodelers and specialty contractors that want estimating, job costing, selections and client portals in one system
tools.weaknesses: No free trial (a 30-day money-back guarantee instead); per-user charges after the first internal user; no native QuickBooks Desktop integration; newer than Buildertrend
tools.long_description:
JobTread is construction management software for builders and contractors, founded in 2019 by Eric Fortenberry and based in Dallas. It is built for home builders, remodelers, pool builders, outdoor living contractors, roofers, specialty contractors and commercial contractors, and it ranked #155 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of fast-growing private companies.

It covers estimating, job costing, scheduling, change orders, purchase orders, vendor management, selections and client and vendor portals in one system, and every feature comes at one price.

Pricing is a $199 monthly base that includes one internal user, with each additional internal user from $20 a month (less at higher counts, and 20% off with annual billing). Customer and vendor portal users are free and unlimited, implementation and support are free, and there is no contract. There is no free trial, but monthly subscriptions carry a 30-day money-back guarantee.

Native integrations include QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Plaid, Gusto, Zapier, Slack, CompanyCam, EagleView, Hover and NiceJob, supplier integrations with The Home Depot, SRS Distribution, QXO, PoolCorp and Heritage Pool Supply, and Acorn Finance and HFS Financial for customer financing; Xero connects through a partner integration. There is no native QuickBooks Desktop integration.

The trade-off: JobTread has a shorter track record than Buildertrend, and it is built for construction projects rather than service calls, so HVAC, plumbing and electrical service shops should look at field service tools instead.

pros_detail.title: Every feature on one price
pros_detail.explanation: JobTread includes every feature at every size: you pay the $199 base plus internal users, with no feature tiers, setup fees or contract.

pros_detail.title: Free customer and vendor portal users
pros_detail.explanation: Clients and vendors get portal access without counting as paid users, so you can bring homeowners and subs into a project at no extra cost.

pros_detail.title: Selection management
pros_detail.explanation: Handles the client-decision process that custom building and remodeling depend on (fixtures, finishes, appliances), alongside change orders and purchase orders.

pros_detail.title: Supplier and measurement integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Integrations with The Home Depot, SRS Distribution, QXO, PoolCorp and Heritage Pool Supply, plus EagleView and Hover, are unusual in construction software and useful for remodelers, roofers and pool builders.

pros_detail.title: Free implementation and support
pros_detail.explanation: Implementation, training and support are included at no charge.

pros_detail.title: 30-day money-back guarantee
pros_detail.explanation: Monthly subscriptions carry a 30-day money-back guarantee, which is how you test JobTread on real projects in place of a free trial.

cons_detail.title: No free trial
cons_detail.explanation: JobTread doesn't offer a free trial; the 30-day money-back guarantee on monthly subscriptions is the way to test it with real projects.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing after the first seat
cons_detail.explanation: The base includes one internal user, and each additional user costs $20 a month for users 2-10 on monthly billing, so a 10-person team pays $199 plus $180, or $379 a month, before annual savings.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Online first
cons_detail.explanation: JobTread's native accounting integration is QuickBooks Online, with Xero through a partner. QuickBooks Desktop users should ask how JobTread's published Desktop workflow fits their setup before committing.

cons_detail.title: Construction-only positioning
cons_detail.explanation: Built for builders, remodelers and specialty contractors. HVAC, plumbing and electrical service shops should evaluate field service platforms instead.

cons_detail.title: Shorter track record
cons_detail.explanation: Founded in 2019, JobTread is newer than Buildertrend and other established construction platforms; ask for references from companies of your size and type.

tools.implementation_notes: JobTread includes free implementation, training and support. Plan the usual phases: account setup and data import, cost codes and templates for your common project types, selection templates, the QuickBooks Online connection, office training, then running your first projects alongside your old process before cutting over. Selection templates take the most care, since each project type needs its own default list.

tool_faqs.q: How does JobTread compare to Buildertrend?
tool_faqs.a: JobTread charges a $199 monthly base with one internal user plus a tiered per-user price, includes every feature, gives customers and vendors free portal access, and offers a 30-day money-back guarantee instead of a free trial. Buildertrend has the longer track record. Price your actual team on both vendors' current pricing before deciding.

tool_faqs.q: Is JobTread worth the cost?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on your team size and how much you'll use job costing, selections and the portals. Work out the monthly cost for your internal users on the pricing page, then use the 30-day money-back guarantee to test it on live projects.

tool_faqs.q: Does JobTread integrate with QuickBooks Desktop?
tool_faqs.a: Not natively. JobTread's native accounting integration is QuickBooks Online, and Xero connects through a partner integration. JobTread publishes a QuickBooks Desktop workflow in its help center, so ask how it works for your setup.

tool_faqs.q: How do JobTread's supplier integrations work?
tool_faqs.a: JobTread's catalog lets you pull items from The Home Depot into estimates and material lists, and it lists supplier integrations with SRS Distribution, QXO, PoolCorp and Heritage Pool Supply. Lowe's is not on its integrations page.

tool_faqs.q: Can JobTread handle commercial construction?
tool_faqs.a: JobTread lists commercial contractors among the companies it serves. Larger commercial operations with complex progress billing and vendor management should compare it with dedicated commercial platforms such as Procore.

tools.name: Houzz Pro
tools.tagline: Business software for remodelers, builders and designers, with 3D floor plans, estimating, project management and Houzz marketing

pricing.pricing_note: Free plan: 3D Floor Planner, estimates and invoicing. Design $99 a month and Pro $199 a month, each with 1 user included and additional users at $50 per user per month; Teams from $399 a month with unlimited users. Advertising packages on Houzz from $499 a month, sold separately. Paid plans start with a 30-day free trial, and Houzz's FAQ says the annual subscription begins at the end of the trial unless you cancel; no month-to-month price is shown. Verified against houzz.com/houzz-pro/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Remodelers, builders, interior designers and architects who want design tools, estimates, project management and marketing on Houzz in one app
tools.weaknesses: Paid plans become an annual subscription after the 30-day trial; lead-generation tools sit on the Teams plan or in advertising sold separately; built for project-based work, not service-call dispatch; a short list of named integrations
tools.long_description:
Houzz Pro is business software for construction and design professionals from Houzz, the home remodeling and design platform founded by Adi Tatarko and Alon Cohen. Houzz launched Houzz Pro in April 2020 and added online takeoffs by acquiring ConX in December 2021. Houzz says Houzz Pro serves residential and commercial new construction and remodeling companies and interior design firms, and its site lists builders, remodelers, interior designers, architects and painters.

The planning tools include a 3D Floor Planner (which added elevations, annotations and AI-generated custom finishes in 2026), mood boards, a product clipper, selections, takeoffs, bid management and contracts. Financial tools cover estimates, proposals, change orders, invoices, online payments by credit card, debit card or ACH, budget management and financial reports. Project management includes schedules, daily logs, time tracking and a 24/7 client dashboard where clients see their documents. The iOS and Android app added AI call and meeting recording, video daily logs, message translation in 10 languages and an offline mode in June 2026.

Marketing is the part tied to Houzz itself. Houzz says more than 70 million homeowners and home design enthusiasts and more than 3 million professionals use Houzz. The Teams plan adds a Premium Profile, email marketing and a custom website, and targeted advertising packages on Houzz are sold separately starting at $499 a month.

The Free plan includes the 3D Floor Planner, estimates and invoicing. Design is $99 a month and Pro is $199 a month; each includes one user, with additional users at $50 per user per month. Teams starts at $399 a month with unlimited users and dedicated support. Paid plans start with a 30-day free trial, and Houzz's FAQ says the annual subscription begins when the trial ends unless you cancel; the pricing page does not show a month-to-month option. The integrations Houzz names are QuickBooks Online, calendar apps, Gmail and Zoom, with a Gusto integration in beta from the Pro plan up.

The trade-off: the marketing value depends on how much work you win through Houzz, and the lead tools cost extra (the Teams plan or paid advertising). Houzz Pro is built for project-based remodeling, building and design, not for dispatching technicians to service calls, and its named integration list is short, so check that it connects to the other tools you rely on.

pros_detail.title: Design tools built in
pros_detail.explanation: The 3D Floor Planner, mood boards, product clipper and selections let designers and remodelers show clients what they are buying without a separate design program.

pros_detail.title: Estimate to invoice in one place
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates, proposals, takeoffs (Pro and up), change orders, invoices and online payments by card or ACH run in the same system as the project.

pros_detail.title: Free plan, and unlimited users on Teams
pros_detail.explanation: The Free plan covers the 3D Floor Planner, estimates and invoicing. Teams (from $399 a month) includes unlimited users, which can cost less than adding $50 seats to Design or Pro once a team grows.

pros_detail.title: Client dashboard and permissions
pros_detail.explanation: The 24/7 client dashboard gives clients access to their project documents, and you control what team members and subcontractors can view or manage.

pros_detail.title: Marketing on Houzz
pros_detail.explanation: Teams adds a Premium Profile, email marketing and a custom website, and advertising packages on Houzz start at $499 a month for businesses that win work there.

pros_detail.title: Mobile app with AI tools
pros_detail.explanation: The iOS and Android app includes AI call and meeting recording, video daily logs, translation in 10 languages and an offline mode.

cons_detail.title: Trial rolls into an annual plan
cons_detail.explanation: Houzz's FAQ says the annual subscription begins at the end of the 30-day trial unless you cancel, and the pricing page shows no month-to-month option.

cons_detail.title: Lead tools cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: The Premium Profile and email marketing are only on Teams (from $399 a month), and advertising on Houzz is a separate package starting at $499 a month.

cons_detail.title: Seat fees on Design and Pro
cons_detail.explanation: Design and Pro include one user, and each extra user is $50 a month. At five users, Pro ($199 plus four extra users) reaches the $399 starting price of Teams.

cons_detail.title: Not for service dispatch
cons_detail.explanation: It is built for project-based remodeling, building and design, not for dispatching technicians to service calls.

cons_detail.title: Short integration list
cons_detail.explanation: Houzz names QuickBooks Online, calendar apps, Gmail, Zoom and a Gusto integration in beta. Businesses on other accounting systems should confirm fit before buying.

tools.implementation_notes: Start on the Free plan or the 30-day trial of Design or Pro, and set a reminder before day 30, because the trial rolls into an annual subscription unless you cancel. Set up your company branding for proposals, estimates and invoices, connect QuickBooks Online, turn on online payments, and link your calendar, Gmail and Zoom. Build estimate templates for your common job types, invite team members and subcontractors with the permissions they need, and open the client dashboard on a first project. If Houzz leads matter to you, weigh the Teams plan's Premium Profile and any advertising package against the number of jobs you actually win through Houzz.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Houzz Pro cost?
tool_faqs.a: There is a Free plan. Design is $99 a month and Pro is $199 a month, each with one user included and extra users at $50 per user per month. Teams starts at $399 a month with unlimited users. Advertising packages on Houzz start at $499 a month and are sold separately.

tool_faqs.q: Does the free trial turn into a paid plan?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Houzz's FAQ says you can cancel anytime during the 30-day free trial, and that the annual subscription begins at the end of the trial.

tool_faqs.q: Does Houzz Pro include leads from Houzz?
tool_faqs.a: Not on every plan. The Teams plan includes a Premium Profile, email marketing and a custom website, and targeted advertising packages are sold separately from $499 a month.

tool_faqs.q: What does Houzz Pro integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Houzz names QuickBooks Online, calendar apps, Gmail and Zoom, and lists a Gusto integration in beta on the Pro plan and up.

tool_faqs.q: Is Houzz Pro a field service (FSM) tool?
tool_faqs.a: No. It is built for project-based remodeling, construction and design work, with estimates, schedules, daily logs and client dashboards. Service trades that dispatch technicians to calls are better served by field service software.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Houzz Pro has apps for iOS and Android, with AI call and meeting recording, video daily logs, translations and an offline mode.

tools.name: Method:CRM
tools.tagline: CRM with real-time two-way QuickBooks sync, for small businesses including contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Per user per month: CRM Quick Start $35, CRM Pro $59, CRM Enterprise $97; 10% off when you prepay 12 months. At the time of checking, a promotion offered 25% off for three months on accounts with 3+ users. Method:Field Services is priced separately (from $15 a month per field crew technician license and $45 per dispatcher license). Free 10-day trial with CRM Pro features, no credit card. A separate CRM is sold for Xero users. Verified against method.me/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Small businesses and contractors that run their books in QuickBooks (Online, Desktop or Enterprise) and want leads, estimates, a customer portal and workflows tied to that data
tools.weaknesses: Per-user pricing adds up as the team grows; technician scheduling and dispatch are a separate Method:Field Services product; a general small-business CRM that needs configuring for your trade; 10-day trial
tools.long_description:
Method CRM is customer relationship management software from Method Integration, a company with its office in downtown Toronto. It is built around a two-way, real-time sync with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Enterprise: Method says its patented integration instantly syncs customers, invoices, payments and more between the CRM and QuickBooks. Method also sells a separate CRM for Xero users. It targets several industries, including construction contractors, field services, manufacturing, distribution and professional services, and says more than 18,000 users rely on it.

Core tools cover lead management, customer records, and estimates that customers can accept online and that convert to sales orders and invoices with a click, syncing to QuickBooks. The customer portal lets customers view and pay invoices, approve documents, update their details and submit support requests. Method stresses customization: you can track the data your business needs, use custom transaction templates and build workflows that follow your own process. It connects with Gmail, Google Calendar and Outlook, and Method says Zapier links it to more than 8,000 other apps. The mobile app for iPhone, iPad and Android shows your pipeline and lets you add leads, send estimates and take payments.

Pricing is per user per month: CRM Quick Start $35, CRM Pro $59 and CRM Enterprise $97, with 10% off for paying 12 months up front. All three plans include QuickBooks integration, lead management, online portals, reports and customization; Pro and Enterprise add financial management and the sales pipeline, and Enterprise adds professional customization services. The free trial is 10 days, needs no credit card and includes all CRM Pro features. When we checked, Method also advertised 25% off for three months on accounts with three or more users.

Field service tools are a separate product, Method:Field Services, which Method prices from $15 a month per field crew technician license and $45 a month per dispatcher license.

The trade-off: Method fits best when QuickBooks (or Xero, through the separate Xero CRM) already holds your customer and invoice data. It is a general small-business CRM rather than a trade-specific job management system, per-user pricing grows with headcount, and scheduling and dispatch need the separate Field Services product.

pros_detail.title: Two-way, real-time QuickBooks sync
pros_detail.explanation: Method says customers, invoices, payments and more sync instantly in both directions, so the office does not re-key data between the CRM and the books.

pros_detail.title: Works with QuickBooks Desktop too
pros_detail.explanation: Method supports QuickBooks Online, Desktop and Enterprise, and says its mobile app brings QuickBooks Desktop data into the cloud so you can reach it away from the office.

pros_detail.title: Estimates to invoices
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can accept estimates online, and an accepted estimate converts to a sales order or invoice with a click and syncs to QuickBooks.

pros_detail.title: Customer portal on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Online portals are included from Quick Start up, so customers can view and pay invoices, approve documents and update their details themselves.

pros_detail.title: Built to be customized
pros_detail.explanation: You can track the data your business needs, use custom transaction templates and set up workflows that match how you sell.

pros_detail.title: No-card trial with Pro features
pros_detail.explanation: The 10-day free trial needs no credit card and includes all CRM Pro features, so you can test the QuickBooks sync on your own data.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Plans run $35 to $97 per user per month (10% off with annual prepay), so costs rise with every seat.

cons_detail.title: Dispatch is a separate product
cons_detail.explanation: Technician scheduling and dispatch come from Method:Field Services, priced separately per field technician ($15 a month) and dispatcher ($45 a month) license.

cons_detail.title: Not built only for trades
cons_detail.explanation: Method also sells to manufacturers, distributors and professional services firms, so plan to configure it around your trade's workflow.

cons_detail.title: Customization takes setup
cons_detail.explanation: Much of the value comes from tailoring fields, templates and workflows. Enterprise includes professional customization services; on the other plans you configure it yourself.

cons_detail.title: Short trial
cons_detail.explanation: The free trial is 10 days, which is short for testing a QuickBooks sync, estimates and portal end to end.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 10-day trial (no credit card; it includes CRM Pro features) and connect your QuickBooks Online, Desktop or Enterprise company file first, since customers, invoices and payments sync from it. Check that customer and transaction data came across correctly before adding users. Then set up estimate templates, custom fields and workflows for how you sell, add sales pipeline stages if you are on Pro or Enterprise, turn on the customer portal, and connect Gmail or Outlook and Google Calendar. Install the mobile app for staff who quote on site. If you need technician scheduling and dispatch, trial Method:Field Services alongside the CRM, and consider Enterprise's professional customization services for a complex setup.

tool_faqs.q: Do I need QuickBooks to use Method?
tool_faqs.a: The main Method CRM is built for QuickBooks Online, Desktop and Enterprise. Method also sells a separate CRM for Xero users, which also uses a two-way sync.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Method CRM cost?
tool_faqs.a: CRM Quick Start is $35, CRM Pro $59 and CRM Enterprise $97 per user per month, with 10% off if you prepay 12 months. Method:Field Services is priced separately. There is a 10-day free trial with no credit card.

tool_faqs.q: What is the difference between the plans?
tool_faqs.a: All plans include QuickBooks integration, lead management, online portals, reports and customization. Pro and Enterprise add financial management and the sales pipeline, and Enterprise adds professional customization services.

tool_faqs.q: Does Method handle scheduling and dispatch?
tool_faqs.a: Not in the CRM plans. Method sells Method:Field Services separately, from $15 a month per field crew technician license and $45 a month per dispatcher license.

tool_faqs.q: Does it work with QuickBooks Desktop?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Method supports QuickBooks Desktop as well as QuickBooks Online and Enterprise, with a two-way sync of customers, invoices and payments.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Method has a mobile CRM app for iPhone, iPad and Android that lets you view your pipeline, add leads, send estimates and take payments.

tools.name: Simpro
tools.tagline: Job, project and service management software for commercial and residential trade contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Simpro does not publish prices. Its pricing page says pricing is tailored to team size (office and field users) and the add-ons chosen, with monthly or annual billing; add-ons include Maintenance Planner, Takeoffs, Digital Forms, Simtrac fleet tracking, Data Feed and SMS. Simpro says an initial setup fee covers onboarding, training and data migration. No self-serve trial; a tailored demo and a self-guided product tour are offered. Verified against simprogroup.com/pricing and simprogroup.com/demo (read through search; the pages block direct fetches) 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Electrical, HVAC, plumbing, security and fire protection contractors that mix service, maintenance and project work and want quoting, stock and job costing in one system
tools.weaknesses: No published prices or self-serve trial; setup fee on top of the subscription; several add-ons cost extra and some integrations (Salesforce, NetSuite) come from partners
tools.long_description:
Simpro is job and project management software for trade contractors. It started in Brisbane, Australia in 2002, when an electrical business owner teamed up with a software engineering student. Today it is part of Simpro Group, a K1 Investment Management portfolio company that also owns AroFlo, ClockShark and BigChange (acquired in October 2024). Simpro Group named Miami, Florida its North America headquarters in December 2025, and its own company summary now lists Miami as its headquarters, with offices in Brisbane, Auckland, Reading (UK) and several US states. Simpro Group says its four brands serve more than 24,000 businesses and 450,000 users.

The main product, Simpro Premium, targets electrical, HVAC, plumbing, security and fire protection businesses. It covers quoting (with supplier price updates, set labor rates and online quote acceptance), scheduling, job costing (estimated versus actual), stock tracking across vans and storage locations, ordering materials from supplier catalogs, and workflows for service, asset maintenance and projects. For project work it supports progress claims, and US customers on Simpro Premium get an AIA Preparation Form for requests for payment. Add-ons include Maintenance Planner (service levels and testing frequencies for customer assets), Takeoffs, Digital Forms, Simtrac fleet tracking, Data Feed and SMS messaging.

Simpro does not publish prices. Its pricing page says the price is tailored to your team size (office and field users) and the add-ons you choose, with monthly or annual billing, and Simpro says an initial setup fee covers onboarding, training and data migration. There is no self-serve trial: Simpro offers a tailored demo with a consultant and a self-guided online product tour.

Accounting links include Xero, QuickBooks Online, MYOB, Sage 50, Sage 200 and Sage Intacct, with NetSuite and Acumatica through partner connectors. Simpro Payments runs on Stripe for card payments in the field, by payment link or in the customer portal. Simpro's marketplace lists more than 240 integrations, including HubSpot and a Salesforce connector built by partner SyncEzy.

The trade-off: Simpro is priced and sold like a larger system. You need a sales call to get a price, a setup fee applies, and useful pieces such as Maintenance Planner and Digital Forms are add-ons, so compare full quotes (subscription, add-ons and setup) against other commercial FSM tools. Simpro Group also has a new chairman and CEO (Fred Voccola, appointed in October 2025) and is adding AI features, so ask what is on the roadmap for your plan.

pros_detail.title: Service, maintenance and projects in one system
pros_detail.explanation: Simpro Premium runs service jobs, asset maintenance and project work in the same platform, with quoting, scheduling, job costing and invoicing shared across them.

pros_detail.title: Stock and purchasing built in
pros_detail.explanation: Track stock held in vans, warehouses and on site, move it with desktop or mobile barcode scanning, and order materials against supplier catalogs.

pros_detail.title: Progress billing for project work
pros_detail.explanation: Progress claims and requests for claim handle staged billing, and US Simpro Premium users get an AIA Preparation Form for requests for payment.

pros_detail.title: Wide accounting coverage
pros_detail.explanation: Xero, QuickBooks Online, MYOB, Sage 50, Sage 200 and Sage Intacct are supported, with NetSuite and Acumatica through partner connectors.

pros_detail.title: Large integration marketplace
pros_detail.explanation: Simpro's marketplace lists more than 240 integrations, including supplier catalogs, HubSpot and a Salesforce connector from partner SyncEzy.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: Pricing is tailored to team size and add-ons, so you need a sales conversation to get a number.

cons_detail.title: Setup fee and paid add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: Simpro says an initial setup fee covers onboarding, training and data migration, and features such as Maintenance Planner, Takeoffs and Digital Forms are add-ons.

cons_detail.title: No self-serve trial
cons_detail.explanation: You evaluate through a tailored demo or the self-guided product tour rather than a free trial account.

cons_detail.title: Some integrations come from partners
cons_detail.explanation: The Salesforce, NetSuite and Acumatica connectors are built by third parties (SyncEzy, Integration Fox), so check who supports them and whether they cost extra.

cons_detail.title: A broad system to set up
cons_detail.explanation: Simpro covers quoting, stock, projects, maintenance and accounting links; plan time for office staff to set up price lists, stock locations and workflows before go-live.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with a demo and ask for a written quote that lists user counts (office and field), add-ons, billing term and the setup fee. Before go-live, prepare your customer and site list, supplier price files, labor rates, stock locations and chart of accounts, then connect your accounting package (Xero, QuickBooks Online, MYOB or Sage) and test that invoices and payments sync. If you run maintenance contracts, set up Maintenance Planner service levels for customer assets; if you do projects, build quote templates and test progress claims (and the AIA form for US jobs). Train office staff on scheduling and job costing first, then roll out the mobile app to techs. Simpro's help guide includes pre-implementation checklists and accounting requirements.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Simpro?
tool_faqs.a: Simpro is part of Simpro Group, a K1 Investment Management portfolio company. The group also owns AroFlo, ClockShark and BigChange, which it acquired in October 2024. Fred Voccola became chairman and CEO in October 2025.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Simpro cost?
tool_faqs.a: Simpro does not publish prices. Its pricing page says pricing depends on your team size (office and field users) and the add-ons you choose, with monthly or annual billing, and Simpro says an initial setup fee covers onboarding, training and data migration. Ask for a written quote with every line item.

tool_faqs.q: Does Simpro have a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: No self-serve trial. Simpro offers a tailored demo with one of its consultants, and a self-guided product tour on its website.

tool_faqs.q: Can Simpro handle both project work and recurring service?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Simpro Premium has workflows for service, asset maintenance and projects, with progress claims for staged billing and the Maintenance Planner add-on for recurring asset maintenance under service-level agreements.

tool_faqs.q: Which accounting software does Simpro work with?
tool_faqs.a: Xero, QuickBooks Online, MYOB, Sage 50, Sage 200 and Sage Intacct, plus NetSuite and Acumatica through partner connectors. Check the Simpro marketplace for your specific version.

tool_faqs.q: Is Simpro a good fit for US contractors?
tool_faqs.a: Simpro sells in the US and Canada, and Simpro Group named Miami its North America headquarters in December 2025. US-specific features include the AIA Preparation Form for Simpro Premium users. Compare it with US-based commercial FSM tools such as ServiceTitan and BuildOps on a full written quote.

tools.name: Commusoft
tools.tagline: Job management software for UK and US trade and service businesses with six or more staff

pricing.pricing_note: Commusoft does not publish prices; its FAQ says to speak to the team. Pricing is per license per month: contracted licenses run on a 12-month contract, monthly rolling licenses can be added for seasonal staff, and daily licenses (no storage included) suit subcontractors and are billed by days used. Storage is pooled per contracted and rolling license. Add-ons: Fleet+ and Sales+ (AI:den+ and Analytics+ listed as coming soon). Onboarding is included. A free trial is available on request after a demo; length not published. Verified against commusoft.com/en-us/plans and commusoft.com/en-us/faqs 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Heating, plumbing, electrical, commercial HVAC, building maintenance and generator service companies with 6 or more staff that run service contracts and planned maintenance
tools.weaknesses: No published prices; standard plans need a 12-month contract; aimed at businesses with 6 or more staff; trial only after a demo
tools.long_description:
Commusoft is job management software for trade and field service businesses. Jason Morjaria started it in London in 2006, building custom software for a field service company while still at university. The company is still based in London, opened a Chicago office in 2019 to serve North America, and has offices in Chennai and Nasik, India. Commusoft says more than 1,000 trades businesses and 10,000 trades professionals use it.

The core product, Commusoft Jobs, covers scheduling and dispatch, job tracking and costing, quotes, invoicing and payments, a customer database, service contracts, asset maintenance, stock control, digital forms and a customer portal. It has deep roots in UK heating work: engineers complete gas safety records (CP12s) and other certificates on the mobile app, and service contract workflows send service reminders, let customers book their next visit online and automate invoicing for boiler service plans. The customer portal lets clients see job and invoice history, view asset details, download certificates, accept quotes and pay online. The iOS and Android apps work offline.

Commusoft does not publish prices. It charges per license per month, and standard plans run on a 12-month contract. You can add monthly rolling licenses for seasonal staff and daily licenses for subcontractors, billed by the days used. Add-ons include Fleet+ (GPS tracking and driver behavior) and Sales+ (pipeline management and automated follow-ups). Onboarding with a dedicated trainer is included, and a free trial is available on request after a demo.

Integrations include QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage and FreeAgent for accounting, Stripe and GoCardless for payments, HubSpot and Pipedrive for CRM, Gmail, Outlook and their calendars, Mailchimp, naturalForms, Zapier and an API.

The trade-off: Commusoft is built for established businesses. It says it is designed for companies with 6 or more staff, prices are quote-only, and the standard plan needs a 12-month commitment, so a solo trader or a very small crew will find simpler, month-to-month tools easier to start with.

pros_detail.title: Certificates and service contracts for heating work
pros_detail.explanation: Engineers fill in gas safety records (CP12s) and other certificates on the app, and service contract workflows handle reminders, online rebooking and invoicing for service plans.

pros_detail.title: Asset maintenance and planned maintenance
pros_detail.explanation: Asset records hold make, model and service history, and you can automate planned preventative maintenance schedules against them.

pros_detail.title: Customer portal
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can see job and invoice history and asset details, download certificates, accept quotes and pay online.

pros_detail.title: Flexible license types
pros_detail.explanation: Alongside contracted licenses, you can add monthly rolling licenses for seasonal hires and daily licenses for subcontractors, billed by the days used.

pros_detail.title: Broad integration list
pros_detail.explanation: QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage, FreeAgent, Stripe, GoCardless, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Gmail, Outlook, Mailchimp and Zapier are listed on its integrations page.

pros_detail.title: Onboarding included
pros_detail.explanation: Commusoft says every new client is onboarded by a dedicated trainer, with support teams in London and Chicago.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: Commusoft asks you to speak to its team for pricing, so you cannot compare costs before a sales call.

cons_detail.title: 12-month contract on standard plans
cons_detail.explanation: Contracted licenses lock in your price for 12 months; only the extra rolling and daily licenses are month to month.

cons_detail.title: Not built for very small teams
cons_detail.explanation: Commusoft says the platform is designed for businesses with 6 or more staff.

cons_detail.title: No free plan, trial by request
cons_detail.explanation: There is no free plan, and the free trial is set up after a demo with a product expert. The trial length is not published.

cons_detail.title: Some add-ons still coming
cons_detail.explanation: AI:den+ and Analytics+ are listed as coming soon, so confirm what is live before you count on them.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo, then ask for a written quote covering contracted licenses, any rolling or daily licenses, add-ons (Fleet+, Sales+) and storage. Onboarding is included: a dedicated trainer takes you through setup, with follow-up sessions and business reviews. Before go-live, gather your customer and property list, asset details (make, model, install dates), active service contracts and renewal dates, price list and stock, then connect QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage or FreeAgent and test that invoices and payments sync. Set up the certificate templates your engineers need (for example gas safety records), load service contract reminders, and train engineers on the offline mobile app before switching over.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Commusoft cost?
tool_faqs.a: Commusoft does not publish prices. It charges per license per month on a 12-month contract, with optional monthly rolling licenses for seasonal staff and daily licenses for subcontractors. Add-ons such as Fleet+ and Sales+ cost extra. Ask for a written quote.

tool_faqs.q: Does Commusoft have a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, on request. Commusoft sets up a free trial after an online demo with a product expert, tailored to your industry and customer types. The trial length is not published, and there is no free plan.

tool_faqs.q: Is Commusoft suitable for US businesses?
tool_faqs.a: Commusoft opened a Chicago office in 2019, won its first US client in 2020 and has US-based sales and support staff. It integrates with QuickBooks Online, Stripe and HubSpot, among others. Compare it with US-based tools on the features you need, such as certificates, service contracts and asset maintenance.

tool_faqs.q: What does Commusoft do for heating and gas engineers?
tool_faqs.a: Engineers complete gas safety records (CP12s) and other certificates on the mobile app; they are saved, emailed to the customer and stored in the customer portal. Service contract workflows send service reminders, let customers book online and automate invoicing for service plans.

tool_faqs.q: Does Commusoft work offline?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The iOS and Android apps let technicians see job history, complete digital certificates and capture photos and signatures without a signal.

tool_faqs.q: Who is Commusoft for?
tool_faqs.a: Trade and service businesses with 6 or more staff, including commercial HVAC, plumbing, electrical, gas and heating, building maintenance and generator installation and maintenance companies.

tools.tagline: Pool service software for routes, chemical readings, billing and customer updates, priced per serviced pool

pricing.pricing_note: Priced per serviced location per month, not per user: Getting Started is $1 per location with a $49 monthly minimum (covers 49 locations); Scaling Up is $2 per location with a $98 minimum; Skimmer for Enterprise is custom pricing for businesses servicing over 1,000 pools a month. All plans include unlimited technicians, admins, customers and visits. Route optimization, quotes, job management, the Orenda LSI and dosing calculator, the LaMotte integration and unlimited service texts start on Scaling Up. Add-ons: service texts on Getting Started ($0.029 per message), AI Phone ($99 a month), Marketing Suite ($150 a month), Skimmer Bookkeeping (from $198 a month). No annual plan is listed. The first month of Scaling Up is free, and the FAQ allows a refund if you cancel within the first 30 days. Verified against getskimmer.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Pool and spa service companies, from solo operators to multi-location groups, that want routing, chemistry logging and recurring billing in one pool-specific app with unlimited users
tools.weaknesses: Pool and spa service only; the bill grows with the number of serviced pools; route optimization and the LSI calculator need the Scaling Up plan; the accounting integration is QuickBooks Online only
tools.long_description:
Skimmer is pool and spa service software that covers routes, scheduling, chemical readings, billing and customer communication. According to its about page, the first version launched in Phoenix in 2017, when software engineer Ronny Hash teamed up with a pool pro. Pete Freeland and Jack Nelson joined in 2020, Mainsail Partners invested $74 million in 2024, and the company is now based in Austin, Texas. Skimmer says more than 35,000 pool service professionals use it to service more than 1 million pools across North America.

The technician app for iOS and Android records readings and dosages, service checklists and photos, works offline and syncs when the connection returns. Each body of water keeps a service history with the tech, readings, dosages, checklist items and notes. In the office, Skimmer offers a route builder and route optimizer, work orders, office alerts, quotes, job management and reports. Completed work flows into invoices, which can go out in bulk by email or text, and customers can pay by card, ACH, Apple Pay or Google Pay (payments run through Stripe), use AutoPay, or apply for Sunbit financing on bigger jobs. Customers also get service emails and a customer portal.

Pricing is per serviced location, not per user. Getting Started costs $1 per location a month with a $49 monthly minimum. Scaling Up costs $2 per location a month with a $98 minimum and adds route optimization, quotes, job management, the Orenda LSI and dosing calculator, the LaMotte integration and unlimited service texts. Skimmer for Enterprise is custom priced for businesses servicing more than 1,000 pools a month and adds custom reports, custom integrations through a public REST API and a dedicated success manager. Every plan includes unlimited technicians, admins and customers. Paid add-ons include AI Phone ($99 a month), a Marketing Suite ($150 a month) and Skimmer Bookkeeping (from $198 a month).

Integrations include QuickBooks Online (a one-way sync from Skimmer into QBO), Stripe for payments, Heritage Pool Supply for product costs and ordering, LaMotte and Orenda. In August 2026 Skimmer announced that it had acquired Pool Builder Geek and Poologics, two pool construction software companies, to extend its platform to pool builders.

The trade-off: because the price follows your pool count, a company with many pools per tech pays more than it would under a per-technician price, and the entry plan leaves out route optimization and the LSI calculator. Skimmer's integration list names QuickBooks Online but not QuickBooks Desktop, and the software is built only for pool and spa work, so a company that also runs other trades needs a second system for them.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes unlimited technicians, admins, customers and visits, so hiring a tech or adding office staff does not change the subscription price.

pros_detail.title: Pool-specific chemistry tools
pros_detail.explanation: Techs log readings and dosages in the app. Scaling Up adds the Orenda LSI and dosing calculator and the LaMotte integration for importing test results.

pros_detail.title: Proof of service for customers
pros_detail.explanation: Photo upload on every visit (5 per visit on Getting Started, 20 on Scaling Up), service emails and a customer portal show homeowners what was done.
