pros_detail.title: Billing built for recurring service
pros_detail.explanation: Completed work, chemicals and installed items flow into invoices. Skimmer supports bulk invoicing, AutoPay, card, ACH, Apple Pay and Google Pay, credit card surcharging where legal, and Sunbit financing.

pros_detail.title: Offline mobile app
pros_detail.explanation: The iOS and Android app keeps working without signal and syncs with the office when the connection returns.

pros_detail.title: An upgrade path for large operators
pros_detail.explanation: Skimmer for Enterprise adds a public REST API, custom reports, a dedicated success manager and multi-location tools for rollups and franchise groups.

cons_detail.title: Cost follows pool count
cons_detail.explanation: At $1 or $2 per serviced location a month, a large route costs more even with a small team. Compare it with per-technician tools using your own pool count.

cons_detail.title: Key tools need Scaling Up
cons_detail.explanation: Route optimization, quotes, job management, the LSI calculator, the LaMotte integration and unlimited service texts are not on the Getting Started plan.

cons_detail.title: Paid add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: AI Phone, the Marketing Suite, Skimmer Bookkeeping and, on Getting Started, service texts are billed on top of the plan price.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Online only
cons_detail.explanation: Skimmer lists QuickBooks Online, not QuickBooks Desktop, and the sync runs one way, from Skimmer into QBO.

cons_detail.title: Pool and spa only
cons_detail.explanation: Skimmer is built for pool and spa service. A company that also does landscaping or other trades needs separate software for that work.

tools.implementation_notes: Start on Scaling Up if you want route optimization: the first month of that plan is free, and Skimmer's FAQ says you can cancel and request a refund within the first 30 days. Import your customer list, set up each service location with its bodies of water, equipment and gate codes, then build routes and assign techs. Connect Stripe to take card and ACH payments, turn on AutoPay for recurring customers, and connect QuickBooks Online if you use it (the sync runs from Skimmer into QBO). If you buy from Heritage Pool Supply, link your Heritage account to sync product costs. Have techs install the iOS or Android app and practice logging readings, dosages, checklists and photos on a few stops before the full route goes live. Enterprise customers get onboarding and migration help and a dedicated success manager.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Skimmer cost?
tool_faqs.a: Skimmer charges per serviced location each month. Getting Started is $1 per location with a $49 minimum, Scaling Up is $2 per location with a $98 minimum, and Skimmer for Enterprise (over 1,000 pools a month) is custom priced. AI Phone, the Marketing Suite and Skimmer Bookkeeping cost extra.

tool_faqs.q: Does Skimmer charge per technician?
tool_faqs.a: No. Every plan includes unlimited technicians, admins and customers. The price depends on how many locations you service, not on how many people use the software.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: The pricing page offers the first month of the Scaling Up plan free, and the FAQ says you can cancel and request a refund within the first 30 days.

tool_faqs.q: Does Skimmer work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with QuickBooks Online on every plan. The sync is one way, from Skimmer into QBO. Skimmer does not list a QuickBooks Desktop integration, so ask before switching if you use Desktop.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Skimmer?
tool_faqs.a: Skimmer is an independent company based in Austin, Texas, led by CEO Jack Nelson. Mainsail Partners invested $74 million in 2024. In August 2026 Skimmer bought Pool Builder Geek and Poologics, two pool construction software companies.

tool_faqs.q: Can Skimmer handle a large or multi-location pool company?
tool_faqs.a: Skimmer for Enterprise is aimed at companies servicing more than 1,000 pools a month, with custom reports, a public REST API, custom integrations, a dedicated success manager and tools for multi-location and franchise groups.

tools.name: Vonigo
tools.tagline: Field service software for franchise systems and multi-location home service businesses

pricing.pricing_note: No prices published. Vonigo's help page says pricing varies based on the features and number of users and asks buyers to contact sales for a quote; vonigo.com/pricing resolves to the homepage. We found no free trial offer on the site; evaluation starts with a demo. Verified against vonigo.com/help and vonigo.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Franchise systems and multi-location home service companies, such as cleaning, junk removal, moving and handyman brands, that want central control of pricing and standards with a separate workspace for each location
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing and no free trial offer found; the only named third-party integration is QuickBooks, with other connections through Vonigo's API; setup involves configuring locations, pricing and workflows, so expect a sales-led onboarding
tools.long_description:
Vonigo is cloud field service software from Vonigo Software Ltd., based in Vancouver, British Columbia. It is aimed mainly at franchise systems and multi-location service businesses, and its site lists industries such as home, carpet, window and air duct cleaning, junk removal, moving, mobile pet grooming, handyman, appliance repair and garage door service. Brands shown on its site include ServiceMaster, Frogbox, Sir Grout, Aussie Pet Mobile and Furniture Medic. Vonigo's privacy policy directs privacy and compliance requests to Fullsteam Operations LLC of Auburn, Alabama.

The franchise and multi-location setup is the core of the product. Corporate teams set pricing, service menus and operating standards from one dashboard and see job volume, revenue, technician activity and customer metrics for every location. Each franchisee or branch gets its own secure workspace for scheduling, dispatch, work orders, invoicing and customer communication. Around that sit a CRM, online appointment booking for customers, estimates and quotes, and a technician app for viewing schedules, updating jobs and taking payments.

Vonigo does not publish prices. Its help page says pricing varies based on the features and number of users, and it asks buyers to contact sales for a quote. We found no free trial offer on the site; evaluation starts with a demo.

For accounting, Vonigo syncs sales records, invoices and quotes with QuickBooks Online or QuickBooks Desktop and links payments to their invoices. Beyond that, it offers a read-and-write API and UI plugins for connecting other systems rather than a list of named integrations. Vonigo says it trains franchise teams during onboarding; its contact page lists phone support on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Pacific, and its help page describes 24/7 support by live chat and email.

The trade-off: Vonigo is built for businesses with several locations or franchisees, so a single-location company pays for structure it may not use and has to go through a sales process to see a price. Confirm pricing, onboarding scope and any integration you depend on before you sign.

pros_detail.title: Built for franchises and multi-location
pros_detail.explanation: Corporate sets pricing, service menus and standards centrally, while each franchisee or branch works in its own secure workspace.

pros_detail.title: Cross-location reporting
pros_detail.explanation: One dashboard shows job volume, revenue, technician activity and customer metrics for every location.

pros_detail.title: Online booking and CRM
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can book appointments online, and every customer, job, quote and interaction sits in one CRM.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online and Desktop sync
pros_detail.explanation: Sales records, invoices and quotes sync to QuickBooks, and customer payments are linked to their invoices automatically.

pros_detail.title: API and plugins
pros_detail.explanation: A read-and-write API and UI plugins let larger systems connect Vonigo to their own tools and trigger workflows from actions in Vonigo.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Vonigo says pricing depends on features and number of users and asks buyers to contact sales, so you cannot compare costs without a demo.

cons_detail.title: No free trial
cons_detail.explanation: The site offers demos rather than a self-serve trial, so evaluation runs through the sales team.

cons_detail.title: Few named integrations
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks is the only third-party product Vonigo names; other connections rely on its API or custom plugins.

cons_detail.title: More than a single location needs
cons_detail.explanation: The franchise and multi-location structure is the main reason to choose Vonigo; a one-location business may find simpler, self-serve tools easier to adopt.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with a demo and ask for a written quote that covers every location and user, since Vonigo prices by features and user count. Decide which settings corporate controls (pricing, service menus, standards) and which each location manages, then set up one pilot location first. Configure services, pricing, online booking and technician schedules for that location, connect QuickBooks Online or Desktop, and train the office team and technicians on the app. Use Vonigo's onboarding training for franchise teams, then roll out the remaining locations one at a time. If you need other systems connected, scope the API or plugin work with Vonigo before signing.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Vonigo cost?
tool_faqs.a: Vonigo does not publish prices. Its help page says pricing varies based on the features and number of users, and you need to contact sales for a quote.

tool_faqs.q: Is Vonigo a good fit for a single-location business?
tool_faqs.a: Vonigo is built mainly for franchise systems and multi-location companies, although it also markets a small-business version. A single-location business should compare it with self-serve field service tools, since Vonigo requires a demo and quote to get started.

tool_faqs.q: How does Vonigo handle franchises?
tool_faqs.a: The franchisor sets pricing, service menus and standards from one dashboard and sees each location's performance. Each franchisee gets its own secure workspace for scheduling, dispatch, invoicing and customer communication.

tool_faqs.q: What does Vonigo integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Vonigo syncs with QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop. For other systems it offers an API and UI plugins; its integrations page lists categories such as payments, calendars and marketing tools but does not name specific products.

tool_faqs.q: Where is Vonigo based?
tool_faqs.a: Vonigo Software Ltd. lists its office at 333 Seymour Street in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its privacy policy directs privacy and compliance requests to Fullsteam Operations LLC in Auburn, Alabama.

tools.name: ServiceM8
tools.tagline: iPhone-first job management app for small service businesses, priced by jobs per month

pricing.pricing_note: Per company per month by job volume, unlimited users on paid plans: Free $0 (1 user, 30 jobs a month), Starter $29 (50 jobs), Growing $79 (150 jobs), Premium $149 (500 jobs), Premium Plus $349 (1,500 jobs, then 20 cents per extra job). 14-day free trial on paid plans. SMS free on Starter and above (10 cents each on Free). ServiceM8 Phone add-on from $19 a month. Verified against servicem8.com/us/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Small trade and home service businesses (electricians, plumbers, HVAC, cleaners, locksmiths, pool and pest control) whose managers use iPhones or iPads and who want pricing by job volume rather than per user
tools.weaknesses: Built iPhone and iPad first; the Android app lacks some iOS features; price climbs with monthly job volume
tools.long_description:
ServiceM8 is job management software for small service businesses. It is an Australian company founded in 2009 by Kim Ford and his son Ben Ford, a software engineer; the first version shipped in 2010 as an iPhone and web app, and ServiceM8 officially launched in the United States in 2016. ServiceM8 says it has managed more than 50 million jobs for businesses in more than 40 countries.

The product is built around its iPhone and iPad app, which covers scheduling and dispatch, quotes and invoices, card payments (including Tap to Pay on iPhone), forms and certificates, photos, time tracking and asset management, and works offline. Office staff use the online dashboard in a web browser or the desktop apps for Windows and Mac. An Android app launched in 2024 as ServiceM8 Lite for technicians and subcontractors; ServiceM8's help center now says the Android app offers almost all the same functionality as iOS, but Room Scan, AR measurement, diagrams and PDF editing remain iPhone and iPad features. Other features include online booking with deposits, two-way SMS, AI quoting and writing tools, and the ServiceM8 Phone add-on (an integrated phone system that records and transcribes calls).

Pricing is per company by jobs per month, with unlimited users on paid plans. The Free plan covers 1 user and 30 jobs a month. Paid plans are Starter ($29 a month, 50 jobs), Growing ($79, 150 jobs), Premium ($149, 500 jobs) and Premium Plus ($349, 1,500 jobs, then 20 cents per extra job). Paid plans come with a 14-day free trial. ServiceM8 Phone starts at $19 a month, and text messages are free on Starter and above (10 cents each on the Free plan).

Accounting integrations cover Xero, QuickBooks Online and MYOB. ServiceM8 also connects to Mailchimp and Deputy, to other apps through Zapier, Workato or n8n, and offers an open API and SDK for custom add-ons. A directory of independent ServiceM8 partners (bookkeepers, accountants and consultants who charge for their services) can help with setup and training.

The trade-off: ServiceM8 gets the most out of iPhones and iPads, so a team that mostly runs Android should test the Android app first. Job-based pricing is cheap for a larger team doing a modest number of jobs, but a busy month or a growing job count moves you up a plan, so price it on your real monthly job count.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on paid plans
pros_detail.explanation: Plans are priced by jobs per month, not per user, so adding techs or office staff does not add cost.

pros_detail.title: Usable free plan
pros_detail.explanation: The Free plan covers 1 user and 30 jobs a month with no time limit, which suits a solo operator starting out.

pros_detail.title: Polished iPhone and iPad app
pros_detail.explanation: The iOS app includes scheduling, quotes, invoices, forms, photos, offline access, Tap to Pay on iPhone, Apple Watch support and tools such as Room Scan and AR measurement.

pros_detail.title: Online booking and customer messaging
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can book online with deposits, and ServiceM8 handles two-way SMS, on-the-way messages and arrival tracking.

pros_detail.title: Xero, QuickBooks Online and MYOB
pros_detail.explanation: All three accounting packages are supported, plus Zapier, Workato and n8n for other apps and an open API for custom add-ons.

cons_detail.title: iPhone-first design
cons_detail.explanation: Managers get the full app on iPhone and iPad. The Android app (launched in 2024 as ServiceM8 Lite) covers core job work, but some iOS features, such as Room Scan, AR measurement and diagrams, are not available on Android.

cons_detail.title: Price rises with job volume
cons_detail.explanation: A busy month or a growing job count pushes you to a higher plan, and above 1,500 jobs a month each extra job costs 20 cents.

cons_detail.title: Some tools sit in add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: ServiceM8 Phone is a paid add-on from $19 a month, and features such as recurring jobs and job costing are listed under add-ons, so check what your plan includes.

cons_detail.title: Built for small businesses
cons_detail.explanation: Its feature list is aimed at small service businesses; contractors that need tools for large, multi-location operations should compare bigger platforms.

cons_detail.title: Support by email and chat
cons_detail.explanation: ServiceM8 lists email and chat support and a help centre; for hands-on setup you hire an independent partner.

tools.implementation_notes: Start on the Free plan or a paid plan's 14-day trial. Install the iPhone or iPad app for anyone in a management role and the Android app for techs who use Android; office staff can work in the online dashboard or the Windows and Mac desktop apps. Import your customer list, set up your services, prices and quote and invoice templates, connect Xero, QuickBooks Online or MYOB, and turn on card payments. Build any forms or certificates your techs need, then run a few real jobs from booking to payment before moving everyone over. Count your typical monthly jobs so you pick the right plan, and use the ServiceM8 partner directory if you want paid help with setup and training.

tool_faqs.q: Does ServiceM8 work on Android?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with limits. ServiceM8 launched an Android app in 2024 as ServiceM8 Lite for technicians and subcontractors. Its help center says the Android app now offers almost all the same functionality as iOS, including scheduling, job history, quotes, invoices and payments, but Room Scan, AR measurement, diagrams and PDF editing are iOS-only. Office staff can use the web dashboard or the Windows and Mac desktop apps.

tool_faqs.q: How does ServiceM8 pricing work?
tool_faqs.a: You pay per company based on jobs per month, with unlimited users on paid plans: Free (1 user, 30 jobs), Starter $29 (50 jobs), Growing $79 (150), Premium $149 (500) and Premium Plus $349 (1,500 jobs, then 20 cents per extra job). Paid plans have a 14-day free trial.

tool_faqs.q: How does ServiceM8 pricing compare to Jobber?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceM8 charges by monthly job volume with unlimited users on paid plans, so its cost depends on how many jobs you run, not how many people you have. Check Jobber's current pricing page and compare both at your real team size and monthly job count.

tool_faqs.q: Which accounting software does ServiceM8 connect to?
tool_faqs.a: Xero, QuickBooks Online and MYOB. ServiceM8 also connects to Mailchimp and Deputy, and to other apps through Zapier, Workato or n8n.

tool_faqs.q: Does ServiceM8 work for HVAC or plumbing shops?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceM8 has industry pages for electricians, plumbers, HVAC, cleaning, locksmiths, pool service, pest control, lawn care and appliance repair. It includes asset management with service history, forms and certificates, and recurring jobs, which suit small service and maintenance work. Larger contractors running membership programs or complex projects should compare heavier platforms.

tool_faqs.q: Can I get help setting it up?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceM8 lists email and chat support and a help centre, plus a directory of independent partners (bookkeepers, accountants and consultants) who charge for consultation, setup, training and customization.

tools.name: Powered Now
tools.tagline: Quotes, invoices, certificates and job management for UK trade businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Business £28 a month (single user only), Professional £32 and Premium £40 per user per month, all excluding VAT, rolling subscription with no contract; annual billing gives 2 months free (£280, £320 and £400 per user per year). USD figures are approximate at 1.3263 USD per GBP (frankfurter.dev, 2026-09-28). 14-day free trial, no card required. Add-ons: PN Receptionist £29 (speech) or £39 (speech and text) a month. Verified against powerednow.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: UK sole traders and small trade teams (plumbers, electricians, gas and heating engineers, builders, landscapers) who want quoting, invoicing, certificates and Making Tax Digital in one app
tools.weaknesses: Built for UK businesses (GBP, VAT, HMRC); accounting integrations limited to Xero and QuickBooks and not on the single-user plan; customer portal only on Premium
tools.long_description:
Powered Now is job management software for UK trade businesses. The company, Powered Now Ltd, is registered in England and Wales (company number 07647786, incorporated in 2011). Powered Now says more than 4,000 UK trade businesses use it and that more than £2.2 billion has been invoiced through the app. It targets plumbers, electricians, gas and heating engineers, builders, landscapers, roofers, decorators and other trades.

It is built around UK rules. Every plan supports Making Tax Digital (Powered Now says it is HMRC-recognised), Professional and Premium can submit VAT returns, and it supports CIS and the domestic reverse charge for construction work. Core tools include quotes and estimates, invoices and part invoicing, online payments and payment links, a work diary, job sheets, projects, expense tracking, supplier invoices and purchase orders, plus compliant certificates and custom forms on Professional and above. Apps run on iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac and PC, and work offline.

Pricing is published in pounds, excluding VAT, on a rolling subscription with no contract. Business is £28 a month for a single user; Professional is £32 and Premium £40 per user per month. Annual billing gives two months free (£280, £320 and £400 a year). In US dollars that is roughly $37, $42 and $53 a month. There is a 14-day free trial with no card required. Add-ons include PN Receptionist (£29 a month for speech, £39 for speech and text) and Here Is My Work, a website tool with a free tier; its Premium version (£100 a year) is included in the Premium plan.

Integrations are Xero and QuickBooks for accounting (Professional and above) and SumUp for online card payments, plus what3words for job locations. Professional adds unlimited team members, staff location and time tracking, team chat and permissions, job routing, deposits, automatic quote and invoice chasing and recurring invoices. Premium adds a customer portal, drag-and-drop scheduling, appointment reminders, drawings and annotations, and AI tools for writing and receipt scanning. Support is by phone (Monday to Friday, 9am to 5:30pm), email and live chat.

The trade-off: Powered Now is built for UK tax and trade conventions, so it is a poor fit for US businesses. The single-user Business plan leaves out certificates, accounting integrations and VAT returns, so most VAT-registered trades will need Professional or Premium.

pros_detail.title: UK tax built in
pros_detail.explanation: Making Tax Digital on every plan, VAT return submission on Professional and Premium, and CIS and domestic reverse charge support for construction work.

pros_detail.title: Transparent published pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Prices from £28 a month are on the website, excluding VAT, with no contract and two months free on annual billing.

pros_detail.title: Certificates and custom forms
pros_detail.explanation: Professional and Premium include compliant certificates and custom forms that engineers complete on site.

pros_detail.title: Works on any device, offline
pros_detail.explanation: Apps for iPhone, iPad, Android, Mac and PC, with offline working.

pros_detail.title: Xero and QuickBooks sync
pros_detail.explanation: Professional and Premium connect to Xero and QuickBooks, so invoices and payments do not need re-keying.

pros_detail.title: 14-day free trial, no card
pros_detail.explanation: You can test quoting, invoicing and certificates for two weeks without entering card details.

cons_detail.title: UK only in practice
cons_detail.explanation: Pricing in pounds, VAT, HMRC Making Tax Digital and CIS support make it a UK product; US businesses should look elsewhere.

cons_detail.title: Business plan is limited
cons_detail.explanation: The £28 single-user plan excludes certificates, team features, VAT returns, accounting integrations, the customer portal and automatic chasing.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing for teams
cons_detail.explanation: Professional (£32) and Premium (£40) are charged per user, so costs grow with every team member.

cons_detail.title: Few integrations
cons_detail.explanation: Accounting links are limited to Xero and QuickBooks, and online card payments run through SumUp.

cons_detail.title: Customer portal on Premium only
cons_detail.explanation: The customer portal, drag-and-drop scheduling and appointment reminders need the top plan.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 14-day free trial (no card needed) on the app or website. Enter your business details, VAT status and CIS settings, add your price list or product catalogue, and set up quote and invoice templates. If you are VAT registered, pick Professional or Premium so you can submit VAT returns and connect Xero or QuickBooks, then test that invoices and payments sync. Set up SumUp for online card payments, add the certificate or form templates your trade needs, and invite team members so you can test scheduling and staff tracking. Powered Now offers one-to-one training sessions through its support portal, plus phone support Monday to Friday, 9am to 5:30pm.

tool_faqs.q: Is Powered Now suitable for US-based trade businesses?
tool_faqs.a: Not really. It prices in pounds and is built around UK VAT, HMRC Making Tax Digital and CIS, so US businesses are better served by US-focused tools.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Powered Now cost?
tool_faqs.a: Business is £28 a month for one user; Professional is £32 and Premium £40 per user per month, all excluding VAT (roughly $37, $42 and $53). Annual billing gives two months free. There is no contract, and the 14-day trial needs no card.

tool_faqs.q: Does Powered Now handle Making Tax Digital?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Powered Now says it is HMRC-recognised for Making Tax Digital on every plan, and Professional and Premium can submit VAT returns.

tool_faqs.q: Which accounting and payment tools does it connect to?
tool_faqs.a: Xero and QuickBooks on Professional and Premium, and SumUp for online card payments and payment links.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between Business, Professional and Premium?
tool_faqs.a: Business is single-user and covers quotes, invoices, online payments, diary, job sheets, expenses and MTD. Professional adds certificates and forms, VAT returns, Xero and QuickBooks, unlimited team members, staff tracking, team chat, deposits, automatic chasing and recurring invoices. Premium adds the customer portal, drag-and-drop scheduling, appointment reminders, drawings and AI tools.

tools.name: Procore
tools.tagline: All-in-one construction management platform

pricing.pricing_note: Custom-quoted: an annual fee per product based on annual construction volume (ACV), with unlimited users, unlimited storage and support included. Multi-year volume pools are available. Verified against procore.com 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Commercial general contractors, specialty contractors and owners managing complex multi-trade projects
tools.weaknesses: Priced by annual construction volume rather than seats; overkill for residential or small commercial work
tools.long_description:
Procore is construction management software for general contractors, specialty contractors and owners, founded in 2002 in Carpinteria, California by Tooey Courtemanche. It is a public company (NYSE: PCOR) and says more than 3 million people use it, with more than three million projects run on the platform across 150+ countries.

It grew from project management into a multi-product platform: project management, quality and safety, financial management (budgets, commitments, change orders and invoicing), design coordination with BIM tools, and workforce management. RFIs, submittals, drawings with revision history, daily logs and change orders are core, and because every contract includes unlimited users, subcontractors, owners and designers can work in the same project.

Pricing is custom: Procore charges an annual fee per product based on your annual construction volume (the total value of the work you run through it), with unlimited users, storage and support included. Cost follows your volume, not your headcount.

The trade-off: Procore is more than most residential builders and remodelers need (Buildertrend and JobTread are built around the homeowner-facing workflow), and a full rollout across projects, subcontractors and accounting is a phased project that needs an internal lead.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every contract
pros_detail.explanation: Because Procore prices on construction volume, GCs can bring subcontractors, owners and designers into the same project without per-seat costs.

pros_detail.title: RFIs, submittals and daily logs
pros_detail.explanation: RFI and submittal workflows, daily logs and change orders are core project tools, shared with everyone on the project.

pros_detail.title: Financial management in the project
pros_detail.explanation: Budgets, commitments, change orders and invoicing (subcontractor invoices and owner billing) live alongside the project, with connectors to construction ERPs.

pros_detail.title: Document version control with markup
pros_detail.explanation: Drawing markup history, RFI workflow, submittal logs all integrated. When an architect issues a revised drawing set, the system flags affected RFIs and tracks distribution to subs automatically. Reduces wrong-drawing rework dramatically on multi-month projects.

pros_detail.title: Design coordination and BIM tools
pros_detail.explanation: Model coordination and BIM viewing help MEP trades and GCs catch clashes during design and preconstruction rather than during installation.

pros_detail.title: Quality and safety tools
pros_detail.explanation: Inspections, observations, incidents and daily logs support safety programs and the documentation owners ask for in prequalification.

pros_detail.title: Broad ERP connectors
pros_detail.explanation: Procore's ERP integrations cover QuickBooks Desktop, Sage 300 CRE, Sage 100 Contractor, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Acumatica, CMiC and Viewpoint Spectrum and Vista, plus Autodesk, Bluebeam, DocuSign and Dropbox connections.

cons_detail.title: Priced on construction volume
cons_detail.explanation: Procore charges per product based on annual construction volume, not seats, so a contractor with a small team but large projects pays accordingly. Get a written quote for the products you need and settle volume terms before signing.

cons_detail.title: Overkill for residential GCs
cons_detail.explanation: Residential custom builders and remodelers are usually better served by Buildertrend, JobTread or Knowify, which are built around the homeowner-facing workflow; Procore's commercial depth doesn't pay off there.

cons_detail.title: Training across multiple roles
cons_detail.explanation: Project managers, accounting staff, schedulers and subcontractor coordinators all need training on Procore, so plan for dedicated change management.

cons_detail.title: Phased implementation
cons_detail.explanation: A go-live across all products and projects is a phased rollout that needs a dedicated internal lead (or implementation partner); Procore's team helps but doesn't replace your own.

cons_detail.title: Negotiate the contract terms
cons_detail.explanation: Contracts run annually or over multiple years on committed volume. Procore offers multi-year volume pools and up-front pricing for added volume, so negotiate those terms, plus renewal and cancellation, before signing.

cons_detail.title: Limited service-work support
cons_detail.explanation: Procore is project-based. If you do both commercial GC work AND ongoing service work (commercial HVAC service contracts, ongoing electrical service for property managers), you'll need separate service FSM (ServiceTitan, Service Fusion, BuildOps) alongside Procore.

tools.implementation_notes: Plan a phased rollout. Start with system configuration: map your chart of accounts and cost codes, set up project templates and approval workflows for RFIs, submittals and change orders. Pilot on one or two active projects while running your old process in parallel, then roll out across all projects, onboarding subcontractors and switching on the ERP integration, where most cutover risk sits. Add quality, safety and design coordination tools once the core is stable. Name an internal owner for the whole rollout.

tool_faqs.q: Is Procore worth the cost for a small commercial GC?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on your construction volume and how many companies you coordinate. Procore prices on annual construction volume with unlimited users, so a small GC with modest volume gets a smaller quote, but its depth (subcontractor collaboration, RFIs and submittals, financials) pays off most on complex multi-trade projects. If your work is residential or light commercial, compare quotes from Buildertrend or Knowify.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between Procore and Buildertrend?
tool_faqs.a: Procore is commercial construction-focused (commercial GCs, large multi-family, industrial). Buildertrend is residential-focused (custom home builders, remodelers, residential GCs). Procore has deeper sub-coordination, AIA progress billing, and commercial-specific features (BIM, safety modules). Buildertrend has stronger client portal for homeowner-facing communication and selections management. Pick based on primary work mix.

tool_faqs.q: How long is the Procore contract?
tool_faqs.a: Contracts are annual or multi-year, priced on committed construction volume. Procore offers multi-year volume pools and up-front pricing for additional volume; negotiate those, plus renewal and cancellation terms, before you sign.

tool_faqs.q: Can Procore replace my accounting software?
tool_faqs.a: No. Procore's financial tools handle project-level budgets, commitments, change orders and invoicing, but it isn't a general ledger, payables or tax system. Keep your accounting or ERP system (QuickBooks, Sage, Viewpoint, NetSuite, Acumatica, CMiC) and connect it through Procore's ERP integrations.

tool_faqs.q: Does Procore integrate with Sage or Viewpoint?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Procore's ERP integrations cover Sage 300 CRE, Sage 100 Contractor, Sage Intacct, Viewpoint Spectrum and Viewpoint Vista (through Ryvit), as well as QuickBooks Desktop, NetSuite, Acumatica and CMiC. Confirm which records sync, and in which direction, for your ERP during the sales process.

tools.name: Automaid (formerly Launch27)
tools.tagline: Online booking and scheduling software for residential cleaning businesses, formerly Launch27

pricing.pricing_note: Per-company monthly plans with unlimited users and bookings: Base $75/month, Pro $150/month, Plus $299/month. Launch27.com's pricing page lists annual billing at 15% off ($765, $1,530 and $3,049.80 a year); automaidsoftware.com shows monthly prices only. Integrations (QuickBooks, Zapier, Google Calendar, Google Analytics, Twilio SMS) start on Pro; mobile apps, card pre-authorization and multi-location support are Plus only. 14-day free trial, no credit card required. Card processing rates are not published. Verified against automaidsoftware.com/pricing and launch27.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential cleaning companies that sell through an online booking form with instant pricing and want unlimited users at a flat monthly price
tools.weaknesses: Mobile apps for cleaners are only on the $299 Plus plan; integrations such as QuickBooks, Zapier and Twilio SMS start on Pro; card processing rates are not published; the May 2026 rename means some login, docs and pricing pages still say Launch27
tools.long_description:
Automaid, known as Launch27 until May 2026, is booking and scheduling software for residential cleaning businesses. The company says Launch27 was founded in 2013, and its privacy policy names Fullsteam Operations LLC of Auburn, Alabama as the parent company. Automaid says it is trusted by more than 3,000 home cleaners. The rename was a rebrand of the same product: logins still run through launch27.com.

The product is built around an online booking form that shows customers a price as they enter their home details and pick a frequency. You can price by bedrooms and bathrooms, by the hour, by square footage or with custom rules, and offer discounts for recurring cleanings. Behind the form sit a customer database, team scheduling and dispatch, email and text reminders, invoicing, card processing, a payroll calculator and a customer login where clients manage bookings, update cards and rebook. Automaid's homepage also says you can assign jobs and optimize routes from the scheduler.

Pricing is per company with unlimited users and bookings on every plan. Base is $75 a month, Pro is $150 a month and Plus is $299 a month. Launch27's pricing page lists annual billing at 15% off ($765, $1,530 and $3,049.80 a year). There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card required. Pro adds an unbranded booking form, time tracking reports, gift cards, satisfaction ratings, automated review requests and integrations with QuickBooks, Zapier, Google Calendar, Google Analytics and Twilio for SMS. Plus adds mobile apps for cleaners and staff, automatic card pre-authorization and charging, a referral engine, Spanish language support, photos and multi-location support.

Card payments run through the vendor's own Launch27Pay processing or a connected Stripe account. Other tools, such as Mailchimp, connect through Zapier.

The trade-off: the headline $75 plan covers booking, scheduling and payments, but the cleaner mobile apps are only on Plus at $299 a month and every integration starts on Pro, so compare the plan lists against how your team works before you choose. Card processing rates are not published, so ask for them in writing.

pros_detail.title: Online booking with instant pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Customers enter their home details and frequency and see a price before they book. Pricing can be set by bedrooms and bathrooms, hourly, square footage or custom rules, with frequency discounts for recurring cleanings.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: All three plans are priced per company and include unlimited users and bookings, so adding cleaners or office staff does not raise the subscription.

pros_detail.title: Customer self-service login
pros_detail.explanation: Even the Base plan includes a customer portal where clients manage bookings, update their card and book again with one click.

pros_detail.title: Free trial without a card
pros_detail.explanation: The 14-day free trial does not require a credit card, so you can build the booking form and test it on your own site before paying.

pros_detail.title: Established product, new name
pros_detail.explanation: Launch27 has been sold since 2013 and is backed by Fullsteam; the Automaid rename in 2026 kept the same product and accounts.

cons_detail.title: Mobile apps only on the top plan
cons_detail.explanation: Mobile apps for cleaners, admins and staff, real-time app alerts and job photos are listed only under Plus at $299 a month.

cons_detail.title: Integrations start on Pro
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks, Zapier, Google Calendar, Google Analytics and Twilio SMS integrations are Pro features ($150 a month). Mailchimp and other tools connect only through Zapier.

cons_detail.title: Processing rates not published
cons_detail.explanation: Card processing is included, but the vendor does not publish its Launch27Pay rates. Get them in writing before you move your payments.

cons_detail.title: Rename in progress
cons_detail.explanation: Automaid and Launch27 websites both remain live, and the login and help docs still use the Launch27 name, which can be confusing when you look for support articles.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 14-day trial (no card needed) and set up your service list and pricing rules first, since the booking form's instant price depends on them. Import your customer list, create your teams and enter recurring customers with their frequency. Connect card processing through Launch27Pay or Stripe and ask for the processing rates before charging real customers. If you need QuickBooks, Zapier, Google Calendar or SMS reminders through Twilio, choose Pro; if your cleaners need the mobile app, choose Plus. Test the booking form on your own website with a few real addresses before you publish it, and use the Launch27 help docs (docs.launch27.com) for setup steps until they carry the Automaid name.

tool_faqs.q: Are Launch27 and Automaid the same product?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Launch27 announced in May 2026 that it had become Automaid. It is the same software and accounts, and logins still run through launch27.com. Launch27's privacy policy names Fullsteam Operations LLC as its parent company.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Automaid cost?
tool_faqs.a: Base is $75 a month, Pro $150 a month and Plus $299 a month, each with unlimited users and bookings. Launch27's pricing page lists annual billing at 15% off. There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card required.

tool_faqs.q: Does Automaid have a mobile app for cleaners?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, but only on the Plus plan. The pricing page lists mobile apps for cleaners, admins and staff, real-time alerts and photos as Plus features.

tool_faqs.q: What does Automaid integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: The Pro and Plus plans include integrations with QuickBooks, Zapier, Google Calendar, Google Analytics and Twilio for SMS. Card payments run through the vendor's Launch27Pay processing or a connected Stripe account, and tools such as Mailchimp connect through Zapier.

tool_faqs.q: Is Automaid suited to commercial janitorial work?
tool_faqs.a: Automaid is built around online booking for home cleaning, with pricing by bedrooms, bathrooms, hours or square footage. Commercial contract cleaners who need site inspections and client quality reporting may want an inspection-focused platform such as Otuvy (formerly CleanTelligent).

tools.name: Markate
tools.tagline: Affordable field service software for small service businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Owner Operator $45.95/mo billed annually (one yearly payment of $551.40) or $49.95/mo month-to-month; the pricing page says annual billing saves 8%. Team plan: the same base price plus $5 per additional employee per month. Many features are paid add-ons, most at $10/mo each (e.g. online booking, the fully branded customer portal, and the Zapier, CompanyCam, NiceJob and ResponsiBid integrations); API and developer access $50/mo; Kate-AI receptionist $1 per call; on annual billing, add-ons are billed annually too. No contract; no refunds for early cancellation within a billing period. No free tier; 14-day free trial with full access, no credit card required. Verified against markate.com/pricing 2026-10-08.

tools.best_for: Solo contractors and small teams wanting affordable FSM with scheduling, dispatch and invoicing
tools.weaknesses: Small company; several features (such as online booking) are paid add-ons; per-employee fee on top of the plan; built for very small teams
tools.long_description:
Markate is field service software for solo operators and small service businesses, founded in 2015 as a bootstrapped company and based in Scottsdale, Arizona. It covers the core workflow: customer database, job scheduling, dispatching, invoicing with payments, automated appointment reminders and a mobile app for field work, with some features, such as online booking ($10/month), sold as add-ons.

Pricing: the Owner Operator plan is $45.95 a month billed annually (one yearly payment of $551.40) or $49.95 month-to-month, and the Team plan adds $5 per additional employee per month to that base price. Several features are paid add-ons, many of them $10 a month each. There is no contract and no free tier; Markate offers a 14-day free trial with no credit card required. Compared with Joist, which is mainly estimating and invoicing, Markate adds scheduling and dispatching.

Integrations include QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Payroll, Square and PayPal for payments, Wisetack for customer financing, Google Calendar and Contacts, CompanyCam, NiceJob for reviews, ResponsiBid, Twilio and Zapier. The CompanyCam, NiceJob, ResponsiBid and Zapier integrations are each listed as a $10-a-month add-on.

The trade-off: Markate is built for very small teams. Growing crews that need deeper team management, reporting or membership programs usually move to a larger FSM.

pros_detail.title: Full FSM workflow at a small-business price
pros_detail.explanation: Scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, automated reminders, and a mobile app on the Owner Operator plan at $45.95/month billed annually ($49.95 month-to-month), plus $5 per additional employee per month on the Team plan. Some features, such as online booking ($10/month), are paid add-ons.

pros_detail.title: Low entry price
pros_detail.explanation: The Owner Operator plan is $45.95/month billed annually ($49.95 month-to-month), and the Team plan adds $5 per additional employee per month, which keeps the total affordable for small teams.

pros_detail.title: Multi-trade coverage in one platform
pros_detail.explanation: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, cleaning, handyman, landscaping, appliance repair, supported with relevant workflows. Avoids the dual-platform problem for operations doing multiple service lines.

pros_detail.title: Online booking available as an add-on
pros_detail.explanation: A customer-facing online booking widget is available as a $10/month add-on for operations that take website-driven bookings.

pros_detail.title: Mobile app for field work
pros_detail.explanation: Mobile app handles real fieldwork (time tracking, customer signatures, photo attachments, invoice generation on-site). Functional and suitable for solo contractors doing quotes and invoices on customer premises.

pros_detail.title: Financing and payment options
pros_detail.explanation: Wisetack customer financing, plus Square and PayPal for payments, so small shops can take cards and offer monthly payments without a separate setup.

cons_detail.title: Small company
cons_detail.explanation: Markate is a small, bootstrapped company. Ask about support hours and the product roadmap if you plan to run your business on it for years.

cons_detail.title: Paid add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: Several features, including online booking ($10/month), are sold as add-ons on top of the $45.95/month (billed annually) Owner Operator plan and the $5 per-employee fee, so price your full configuration before committing.

cons_detail.title: Per-employee fee
cons_detail.explanation: On top of the plan price, each additional employee adds $5 a month, so price your full team plus the add-ons you need.

cons_detail.title: Built for very small teams
cons_detail.explanation: Growing past a handful of employees usually brings needs (deeper dispatching, reporting, membership programs) that a larger FSM such as Jobber, Housecall Pro or Workiz covers better.

tools.implementation_notes: Markate is self-service to set up; start on the 14-day free trial. Import customers (manually or by CSV), set up your service catalog and prices, install the mobile app, and run your first jobs end to end (quote, schedule, invoice, payment). Connect QuickBooks Online and your payment processor, switch on appointment reminders, and add online booking if you buy that add-on.

tool_faqs.q: How does Markate compare to Joist?
tool_faqs.a: Joist is estimating-and-invoicing software (its Run plan adds jobs and scheduling). Markate covers scheduling, dispatching and invoicing, and sells a client portal as a $10/month add-on. For solo contractors who only need quotes and invoices, Joist (from $8.34/month billed annually, $10 billed monthly) is cheaper and simpler; for scheduling and dispatching to techs, Markate (from $45.95/month billed annually, $49.95 month-to-month) is more capable.

tool_faqs.q: Does Markate have a free tier?
tool_faqs.a: No. Markate's entry plan is Owner Operator at $45.95/month billed annually ($49.95 month-to-month), plus $5 per additional employee per month on the Team plan, and some features such as online booking are $10/month add-ons. It offers a 14-day free trial with no credit card required.

tool_faqs.q: When should I outgrow Markate?
tool_faqs.a: Typical triggers: your team grows past a handful of employees, you need advanced dispatching with route optimization, you want recurring service or membership management, or you need a wider integration set. At that point Jobber, Housecall Pro, FieldPulse or Workiz usually fit better despite the higher cost.

tool_faqs.q: Does Markate handle online customer booking?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, as a $10/month add-on. The customer-facing online booking widget integrates with Markate scheduling, so customers can book through your website or a Markate-hosted page and bookings flow into Markate and route to available techs.

tool_faqs.q: How is Markate priced?
tool_faqs.a: The Owner Operator plan is $45.95/month billed annually ($49.95 month-to-month); the Team plan is the same base price plus $5 per additional employee per month. Several features are paid add-ons (for example, online booking at $10/month); on annual billing, add-ons are billed annually too. There is no contract, and Markate does not refund early cancellations within a billing period. There is no free tier, but a 14-day free trial is available. Check Markate's pricing page for current add-on prices before budgeting.

tools.name: Sera Systems
tools.tagline: HVAC, plumbing, and electrical management software with modern UX

pricing.pricing_note: Core Essentials $399/mo incl. unlimited admins + up to 4 technicians; $149/mo per additional technician.

tools.best_for: Small-to-medium HVAC/plumbing/electrical shops wanting modern UX and published pricing without ServiceTitan's complexity
tools.weaknesses: Newer platform (out of beta in early 2022) with a smaller customer base; less mature than ServiceTitan; onboarding fee not published
tools.long_description:
Sera Systems is an HVAC, plumbing, and electrical management platform built for residential service shops that have outgrown entry-tier FSM but don't need ServiceTitan's enterprise complexity or its quote-only pricing. It was created by Billy Stevens, who built two plumbing and HVAC companies in the Dallas/Fort Worth area; the software came out of beta in early 2022 and the company is based in Dallas. It combines ServiceTitan-style features (marketing attribution, membership management, consumer financing, KPI dashboards) with a modern UX.

What separates Sera from competitors is the deliberate mid-market positioning. ServiceTitan's enterprise feature set and quote-only pricing are a poor fit for a 5-tech HVAC shop. Jobber and Housecall Pro at entry-tier pricing don't have the marketing attribution, membership management, or KPI reporting that growing shops need to scale past 10 techs. Sera targets exactly this gap.

Pricing is published: Core Essentials is $399/month including unlimited admins and up to 4 technicians, with each additional technician at $149/month. Sera also charges an onboarding fee for its hands-on setup (one-on-one setup help, live team training and data migration support) but does not publish the amount, so get it quoted. ServiceTitan publishes no prices; its pricing page says pricing is per technician. Model the per-technician cost at your team size early in evaluation, since it drives the buy-vs-ServiceTitan decision.

Sera's integrations page lists QuickBooks for accounting, Global Payments and Stax for payments, Service Finance for consumer financing, HighLevel, RingCentral, pulseM, CAMP Digital, JB Warranties, Broccoli AI and Zapier.

The trade-off: Sera is newer, with a smaller customer base than ServiceTitan and a smaller third-party implementation partner ecosystem.

pros_detail.title: Growth features at a published price
pros_detail.explanation: Sera ships marketing attribution, membership management, consumer financing and KPI dashboards at a published $399/month for up to 4 technicians plus $149 per additional technician, plus an onboarding fee it does not publish, while ServiceTitan's per-technician pricing is quoted on request.

pros_detail.title: Modern platform
pros_detail.explanation: A newer platform, out of beta in early 2022, built as a modern alternative to legacy enterprise FSM.

pros_detail.title: Marketing and reputation integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Sera's integrations page lists HighLevel for marketing automation, pulseM for reviews and CAMP Digital, which complement its built-in marketing attribution.

pros_detail.title: Built-in consumer financing (Service Finance)
pros_detail.explanation: Sera's Service Finance integration lets techs present multiple lending options without leaving the Sera app, useful for residential HVAC system replacements.

pros_detail.title: Hands-on onboarding with ongoing check-ins
pros_detail.explanation: Sera's onboarding includes one-on-one setup help, live team training and data migration support, with check-ins at least quarterly afterwards. It is a paid service and the fee is not published.

pros_detail.title: KPI dashboards built for HVAC/plumbing/electrical KPIs
pros_detail.explanation: Average ticket, close rate, conversion rate by lead source, technician profitability: the metrics that residential trade operations actually run on. Different from generic FSM reporting.

cons_detail.title: Newer platform (out of beta in early 2022)
cons_detail.explanation: Smaller customer base, fewer case studies, smaller implementation partner ecosystem than ServiceTitan. Some operations prioritize maturity and won't switch from established platforms.

cons_detail.title: Per-technician cost adds up
cons_detail.explanation: Core Essentials is $399/month including up to 4 technicians, then $149/month for each additional technician, so a 10-tech shop pays about $1,293/month.

cons_detail.title: HVAC/plumbing/electrical specific
cons_detail.explanation: Not designed for general FSM or trades outside residential HVAC/plumbing/electrical. Multi-trade operations need to evaluate whether Sera serves all their trades adequately or if a multi-trade FSM fits better.

cons_detail.title: Limited integration ecosystem versus enterprise platforms
cons_detail.explanation: Sera's integrations page lists 11 integrations (QuickBooks, Global Payments, Stax, Service Finance, HighLevel, RingCentral, pulseM, CAMP Digital, JB Warranties, Broccoli AI, Zapier), a smaller footprint than ServiceTitan's. Custom integrations may require Zapier.

cons_detail.title: Paid, sales-led onboarding (no self-service tier)
cons_detail.explanation: Onboarding is a paid service with an unpublished fee, and there is no self-service signup option for very small operations wanting immediate access without a sales process.

tools.implementation_notes: Sera does not publish an implementation timeline. Its onboarding, a paid service with an unpublished fee, includes one-on-one setup help, live training for your team, data migration support and check-ins at least quarterly afterwards. For a 10-tech HVAC operation leaving a legacy FSM, expect the usual phases: system configuration (user roles, service catalog, good-better-best pricing), customer and membership data migration, office staff training on dispatching, memberships and dashboards, field tech training on the mobile app, then a short parallel run before cutover with the QuickBooks integration verified. Recurring contract (membership) reconstruction is usually the longest pole. Ask Sera for the go-live plan in writing. For operations migrating from ServiceTitan, the data structures are more similar than for migrations from Jobber or Housecall Pro.

tool_faqs.q: How does Sera Systems compare to ServiceTitan?
tool_faqs.a: Sera is the mid-market alternative to ServiceTitan. Pricing: Sera publishes $399/month for up to 4 technicians plus $149 per additional technician, plus an onboarding fee it does not publish; ServiceTitan publishes no prices; its per-technician pricing is quoted on request. Implementation: neither publishes a timeline, so ask each for a go-live date in writing. Features: both have marketing attribution, membership management, consumer financing and KPI dashboards. Differences: ServiceTitan has more integration depth, a larger user community and more case studies.

tool_faqs.q: Is Sera Systems worth the price for a 5-tech HVAC operation?
tool_faqs.a: Borderline. At 5 techs, Core Essentials costs $548/month ($399 including 4 technicians, plus $149 for the fifth), before the onboarding fee. That's a real commitment for a sub-$1M revenue shop. The features (marketing attribution, membership, financing) only pay back if you actually use them. Sera's pricing page reports customer gains such as a 24% increase in revenue and a 53% increase in memberships sold; those are the vendor's figures, not independent ones. Operations that just need basic scheduling and invoicing are better served by Jobber or Housecall Pro at lower cost.

tool_faqs.q: What's Sera Systems best for?
tool_faqs.a: Small-to-medium residential HVAC, plumbing, and electrical shops (Sera's own description of its customers) that have outgrown entry-tier FSM but don't need ServiceTitan's enterprise feature set or its quote-only pricing. Specifically: operations running consumer financing on installs, and operations with established membership programs that need automation. Very small operations and large multi-trade companies typically fit better with other platforms.

tool_faqs.q: Does Sera Systems handle consumer financing?
tool_faqs.a: Yes: Sera integrates with Service Finance, so techs can present multiple lending options without leaving the Sera app, and customers can apply for financing for repair and replacement projects through it.

tool_faqs.q: How does Sera compare to FieldEdge?
tool_faqs.a: Different positioning. FieldEdge is QuickBooks-centric, custom-quoted (FieldEdge publishes no prices), established (company history back to 1980) with strong QuickBooks Desktop integration. Sera is modern UX with marketing attribution + consumer financing built in, with published pricing from $399/month including up to 4 technicians plus $149/month per additional technician, newer (out of beta in early 2022). FieldEdge wins for QuickBooks Desktop shops prioritizing accounting integration. Sera wins for growing shops prioritizing marketing/sales features. Both are reasonable mid-market options.

tools.name: LMN by Granum
tools.tagline: Budget-based estimating, scheduling and crew time tracking for landscaping companies

pricing.pricing_note: Per-company plans in USD, billed monthly, after a one-time onboarding fee whose amount is not published. Starter $297 a month (companies under 10 employees; 1 office or crew lead license and 5 crew member licenses). Professional $648 a month (10+ employees; 3 office or crew lead licenses and 15 crew member licenses). Enterprise is priced by sales, starts at 100 users and targets multi-location companies. Additional licenses are available for a fee; Greenius crew training is an add-on. No free trial is published. Verified against granum.com/lmn/pricing/ 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Landscaping companies (maintenance, design and build, and snow and ice) that want budget-based estimating tied to scheduling, crew time tracking and job costing
tools.weaknesses: Plans are billed monthly after a one-time onboarding fee whose amount is not published; real-time job costing, Zapier and QuickBooks Desktop need the $648 Professional plan; focused on landscaping; no published free trial
tools.long_description:
LMN (Landscape Management Network) is business software for landscaping companies, covering full-service landscaping, design and build, maintenance, tree care, and snow and ice work. It was founded by Mark Bradley and says it has served landscapers since 2009. In November 2024 LMN merged with SingleOps, alongside a growth investment from FTV Capital with participation from Five Elms Capital. In October 2025 the combined company launched Granum as its parent brand, so the product is now sold as LMN by Granum. LMN's legal pages give an address in Markham, Ontario, and LMN says more than 3,000 North American landscaping companies have adopted it.

LMN is built around budget-based estimating: you set up a company budget and use it to price estimates to a target margin. It also covers drag-and-drop scheduling with crew routing, a CRM, SMS messaging, a customer portal where clients see service information, invoices and schedules and can approve and sign proposals, and invoicing with online payments through LMN Pay (powered by Stripe, card or ACH). The LMN Crew app, in English and Spanish, lets crews track hours with GPS timestamps, add photos, weather notes and vendor receipts, and see job notes and checklists. That time feeds payroll and estimate-versus-actual job cost reports.

Prices are per company in US dollars, billed monthly after a one-time onboarding fee whose amount is not published. Starter is $297 a month for companies with fewer than 10 employees and includes 1 office or crew lead license and 5 crew member licenses. Professional is $648 a month for companies with 10 or more employees, includes 3 office or crew lead licenses and 15 crew member licenses, and adds real-time job costing, Zapier integrations, files and photos on documents, and equipment and material costing. Enterprise is priced by sales for multi-location companies and starts at 100 users. LMN says additional licenses are available for a fee, and Granum's Greenius crew-training software is an add-on.

LMN integrates with QuickBooks: the plan comparison lists QuickBooks Online on Starter and QuickBooks Online or Desktop on Professional and Enterprise, and you can import customers from QuickBooks or a CSV file. LMN's terms let either party cancel on 30 days' written notice, with no refund of fees already paid.

The trade-off: LMN costs more to start than simple scheduling apps, the onboarding fee is unpublished, and job costing, Zapier and QuickBooks Desktop sit on the $648 Professional plan. It is built for landscaping; Granum sells SingleOps as its tree care product, and multi-trade businesses need a general tool.

pros_detail.title: Budget-based estimating
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates are priced from your company budget to hit a target margin, rather than from a flat price list.

pros_detail.title: Licenses included per company
pros_detail.explanation: Starter includes 6 licenses (1 office or crew lead plus 5 crew members) and Professional 18 (3 plus 15), so a crew can join without a per-user fee until you pass the plan's count.

pros_detail.title: Bilingual crew app
pros_detail.explanation: LMN Crew works in English and Spanish and captures hours with GPS timestamps, photos, weather notes and receipts, feeding payroll and job costing.

pros_detail.title: Customer portal with e-signature
pros_detail.explanation: Clients can see service information, invoices and schedules, and approve and sign proposals in the portal.

pros_detail.title: Built-in payments
pros_detail.explanation: LMN Pay, powered by Stripe, takes card or ACH payments with no monthly minimum, and LMN says most payouts arrive within 2 business days.

cons_detail.title: Unpublished onboarding fee
cons_detail.explanation: Both Starter and Professional are billed monthly after a one-time onboarding fee, and LMN does not publish the amount.

cons_detail.title: Big step to Professional
cons_detail.explanation: Real-time job costing, Zapier, and equipment and material costing need Professional at $648 a month, more than twice Starter's $297.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Desktop on higher plans
cons_detail.explanation: Starter connects to QuickBooks Online only; QuickBooks Desktop needs Professional or Enterprise.

cons_detail.title: Landscaping focus
cons_detail.explanation: LMN is built for landscaping companies; Granum sells SingleOps as its tree care product, and multi-trade shops need a general field service tool.

cons_detail.title: No published free trial
cons_detail.explanation: LMN offers demos rather than a self-serve trial.

tools.implementation_notes: LMN starts with a one-time onboarding (LMN Launch) that includes dedicated new-customer training. Before it begins, gather your overhead costs, labor rates and equipment costs, because LMN's estimating works from a company budget, and export your customer list so it can be imported from QuickBooks or a CSV file. Connect QuickBooks (Online on Starter, Online or Desktop on Professional and Enterprise) and, if you want online payments, set up LMN Pay. Count office and crew licenses before choosing a plan, since Starter includes 6 and Professional 18. Then roll out the LMN Crew app in English or Spanish so hours, photos and notes flow into each job.

tool_faqs.q: Is LMN part of the same company as SingleOps?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. LMN and SingleOps merged in November 2024, with investment from FTV Capital and Five Elms Capital, and the combined company became Granum in October 2025. LMN is now sold as LMN by Granum and SingleOps as SingleOps by Granum.

tool_faqs.q: How much does LMN cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starter is $297 a month (under 10 employees, 6 licenses) and Professional $648 a month (10+ employees, 18 licenses), billed monthly after a one-time onboarding fee whose amount is not published. Enterprise is priced by sales and starts at 100 users.

tool_faqs.q: Does LMN integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Starter connects to QuickBooks Online, and Professional and Enterprise connect to QuickBooks Online or Desktop. Professional also adds Zapier.

tool_faqs.q: Does LMN have a crew app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. LMN Crew is available in English and Spanish and lets crews track hours with GPS timestamps, upload photos and receipts, and see job notes and checklists.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: LMN does not publish a free trial. You book a demo, and new customers go through a paid one-time onboarding.

tool_faqs.q: LMN or Aspire?
tool_faqs.a: LMN publishes per-company prices ($297 and $648 a month, plus an onboarding fee) with a set number of licenses. Aspire publishes no prices and quotes a single monthly license fee with unlimited users, aimed at established multi-crew landscaping and commercial cleaning companies.

tools.name: MarketSharp
tools.tagline: CRM for home improvement and remodeling contractors, from lead to production

pricing.pricing_note: Per company plus per-user fees. Prices include 1 account and 1 user, billed annually: Standard $182/mo, Pro $319/mo, Ultimate $457/mo ($199, $349 and $499 billed monthly). Additional users $40, $50 or $55 per user per month by plan. All plans are annual contracts; annual pay is discounted. Includes up to 3 hours of onboarding, up to 4 hours of data conversion and 5 GB storage per user; more onboarding, conversion, storage and databases cost extra; texting overages $0.05 per message. No trial listed. Verified against marketsharp.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Remodelers, window and door, roofing, siding and other home improvement contractors that sell through in-home appointments and want lead tracking, marketing campaigns and production tracking in one CRM
tools.weaknesses: Every plan is an annual contract, and each user after the first costs $40-$55 a month. Texting, marketing campaigns, quoting, payments and the QuickBooks connector are not on the Standard plan.
tools.long_description:
MarketSharp is CRM software for home improvement contractors. Its site names remodelers, window and door installers, roofers, painters, deck builders, drywall and insulation contractors, and siding and gutter pros. The company says the software was first built in 1988 for a Midwestern window business and was taken to market in 1996, and that it has helped thousands of remodeling businesses. MarketSharp is owned by EverCommerce. Its contact page lists an office in Denver, Colorado, and its privacy policy names Advanced Marketing Concepts, LLC (doing business as MarketSharp) in La Crosse, Wisconsin.

Every plan covers lead, account and contact management, search and filtering, a calendar with scheduling and appointment tracking, document and photo storage, basic document generation, and reporting and analytics. The plans above Standard add sales appointment routing, two-way text conversations, text alerts and reminders, and marketing campaigns: recovery, repeat and referral marketing, geographic and demographic targeting, jobsite radius marketing, targeted direct mail and email automation. They also add point-of-sale and production tools: quoting and estimating, payments, commissions, job costing, production management, a QuickBooks connector and an API. MarketSharp describes Ultimate as adding advanced tools and reports and the ability to create, send and e-sign documents.

MarketSharp's integrations page lists QuickBooks, PaySimple and GreenSky, lead sources such as Angi Leads, Modernize, CraftJack, Networx and Zillow, sales tools such as Five9, SalesRabbit and Spotio, and marketing and reputation tools such as GuildQuality, Listen360 and Constant Contact. A MarketSharp app on Zapier can submit new leads into the system.

Prices are published. Each plan includes one account and one user: Standard is $182 a month billed annually ($199 monthly), Pro $319 ($349) and Ultimate $457 ($499). Extra users cost $40, $50 or $55 each a month depending on the plan. All plans are annual contracts, and paying annually gets the lower rate. Plans include up to 3 hours of dedicated onboarding, up to 4 hours of data conversion and 5 GB of storage per user. More onboarding, conversion, storage or extra databases cost more, and text messages over the allowance are $0.05 each.

The trade-off: the tools that take MarketSharp beyond a contact manager (texting, marketing campaigns, quoting, payments, production and QuickBooks) start on Pro, and every plan is a yearly commitment with per-user fees after the first seat. It suits contractors who sell through in-home appointments and want marketing, sales and production tracking in one place. A small crew that mainly needs scheduling and invoicing may find a field service app a closer fit.

pros_detail.title: Built for home improvement sales
pros_detail.explanation: Lead, appointment and sales tracking is set up for contractors who sell remodeling, windows, roofing and siding through in-home appointments.

pros_detail.title: Published prices
pros_detail.explanation: Plan prices and per-user fees are on the pricing page ($182, $319 or $457 a month billed annually for the first user), so you can budget before a sales call.

pros_detail.title: Marketing campaigns built in
pros_detail.explanation: Pro and Ultimate include recovery, repeat and referral marketing, jobsite radius marketing, targeted direct mail and email automation.

pros_detail.title: Goes past the sale
pros_detail.explanation: Pro and Ultimate add quoting, payments, commissions, job costing and production management, so sold jobs can be tracked through production.

pros_detail.title: Many lead-source integrations
pros_detail.explanation: The integrations page lists lead sources such as Angi Leads, Modernize, CraftJack, Networx and Zillow, plus QuickBooks and a Zapier lead action.

pros_detail.title: Onboarding hours included
pros_detail.explanation: Plans include up to 3 hours of dedicated onboarding and up to 4 hours of data conversion.

cons_detail.title: Annual contract on every plan
cons_detail.explanation: All plans are annual contracts. Paying monthly costs more but does not remove the yearly commitment.

cons_detail.title: Per-user fees after the first seat
cons_detail.explanation: Each plan includes one user. Every additional user costs $40 (Standard), $50 (Pro) or $55 (Ultimate) a month.

cons_detail.title: Standard is basic
cons_detail.explanation: Standard covers the CRM, calendar, documents and reports. Texting, marketing campaigns, quoting, payments and the QuickBooks connector need Pro or Ultimate.

cons_detail.title: Extra fees beyond the included amounts
cons_detail.explanation: Additional onboarding, data conversion, storage over 5 GB per user, extra databases and texting overages ($0.05 per message) are billed separately.

tools.implementation_notes: Before signing, decide which plan you need (texting, marketing, quoting, payments and QuickBooks start on Pro) and how many users, because each user after the first adds $40-$55 a month and every plan is an annual contract. Plans include up to 3 hours of dedicated onboarding and up to 4 hours of data conversion, so clean up your customer and lead lists before the first session and ask what extra conversion time would cost if your history is large. List your lead sources and check each one against MarketSharp's integrations page or its Zapier lead action. Then set up appointment scheduling, sales appointment routing and your sales stages, and connect QuickBooks if you are on Pro or Ultimate.

tool_faqs.q: How much does MarketSharp cost?
tool_faqs.a: Standard is $182 a month billed annually ($199 monthly), Pro is $319 ($349) and Ultimate is $457 ($499). Each includes one user; extra users cost $40, $50 or $55 a month depending on the plan. All plans are annual contracts.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns MarketSharp?
tool_faqs.a: MarketSharp is owned by EverCommerce. Its contact page lists an office in Denver, Colorado, and its legal entity, Advanced Marketing Concepts, LLC, has an address in La Crosse, Wisconsin.

tool_faqs.q: Is MarketSharp only for sales, or does it handle production too?
tool_faqs.a: Every plan includes the CRM, calendar and scheduling, documents and reports. Pro and Ultimate add quoting, payments, commissions, job costing and production management, so jobs can be tracked after the sale.

tool_faqs.q: What does MarketSharp integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Its integrations page lists QuickBooks (the connector is on Pro and Ultimate), PaySimple, GreenSky and lead sources such as Angi Leads, Modernize, CraftJack, Networx and Zillow, plus sales and marketing tools such as Five9, SalesRabbit, Spotio, GuildQuality and Constant Contact. A Zapier app can submit leads.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: No free trial is listed on the pricing page. Plans are annual contracts and include up to 3 hours of onboarding and up to 4 hours of data conversion.

tool_faqs.q: Who is MarketSharp for?
tool_faqs.a: Home improvement contractors such as remodelers, window and door installers, roofers, painters, deck builders, drywall and insulation contractors, and siding and gutter pros, especially those who sell through in-home appointments and run marketing campaigns.

tools.name: OptimoRoute
tools.tagline: Route planning and scheduling optimization for field service businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Per-driver pricing: Lite $35.10 and Pro $44.10 per driver/mo billed annually (paying a year upfront gives a 10% discount); Custom plan quote-based. Lite up to 700 orders, Pro up to 1,000; multi-day routes and pickup-and-delivery are Custom features. 30-day free trial, no credit card. Verified against optimoroute.com/pricing 2026-09-28.

tools.best_for: Multi-route service businesses (pest control, landscaping, cleaning, pool service, delivery) that want dedicated route optimization alongside their FSM
tools.weaknesses: Route optimization only, not a full FSM, so it pairs with separate invoicing and CRM; per-driver pricing adds up at scale; multi-day routes need the Custom plan
tools.long_description:
OptimoRoute is route planning and scheduling software for businesses that run many stops a day, founded in 2012 by Goran Kukolj and Marin Saric and based in Palo Alto, California. It serves delivery and field service operations, including pest control, landscaping, cleaning and pool service, where route density drives the economics.

It optimizes routes around time windows, driver skills and vehicle capacity, tracks drivers live, and re-plans when jobs change. Lite covers the mobile app, live tracking, route history, exports and API access for up to 700 orders; Pro adds weekly planning, real-time order tracking, proof of delivery, customer feedback and analytics for up to 1,000 orders; the Custom plan adds multi-day routes, pickup and delivery, commercial routing and dynamic depots.

Pricing is per driver: Lite $35.10 and Pro $44.10 a month billed annually (paying a year upfront gives a 10% discount), with Custom quoted. There is a 30-day free trial with no credit card. It connects to other systems through its REST API and Zapier, with integrations for Shopify, WooCommerce, Salesforce, HubSpot and NetSuite.

The trade-off: OptimoRoute is routing only, not a full FSM, so it sits beside your quoting, invoicing and customer records. Shops with a handful of stops a day usually get enough from their FSM's built-in routing.

pros_detail.title: Dedicated route optimization
pros_detail.explanation: Routes are optimized around time windows, driver skills and vehicle capacity, with live tracking and re-planning when jobs are added or cancelled, which goes deeper than most FSM-bundled routing.

pros_detail.title: 30-day free trial, no credit card
pros_detail.explanation: Long enough to plan several weeks of real routes on your own data and compare the results with how you route today.

pros_detail.title: Pairs with existing FSM
pros_detail.explanation: OptimoRoute isn't a replacement; it's the routing-specialty layer on top of whatever FSM you use. No platform migration required to adopt. Pest control operations on PestPac/FieldRoutes/GorillaDesk can add OptimoRoute as the routing specialty without changing their core platform.

pros_detail.title: Proof of delivery and customer feedback on Pro
pros_detail.explanation: Pro adds real-time order tracking, proof of delivery, customer feedback and weekly planning.

pros_detail.title: API and Zapier connections
pros_detail.explanation: A REST API plus Zapier, Shopify, WooCommerce, Salesforce, HubSpot and NetSuite integrations let it take orders from the systems you already use.

cons_detail.title: Route optimization only, not a full FSM
cons_detail.explanation: OptimoRoute doesn't handle quotes, invoicing, billing or a customer portal. It sits on top of your FSM or CRM, adding another monthly subscription.

cons_detail.title: Per-driver pricing adds up at scale
cons_detail.explanation: At $35.10-$44.10 per driver per month (billed annually), 50 drivers cost roughly $1,755-$2,205 a month on top of your FSM. Measure the route savings during the trial.

cons_detail.title: Less trade-specific than HVAC- or plumbing-focused FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Routing-specialty positioning means no trade-specific workflows for HVAC repair quoting, plumbing service contracts, or electrical inspection workflows. HVAC operations get the routing benefit but lose trade-specific FSM depth.

cons_detail.title: Multi-day routes need Custom
cons_detail.explanation: Multi-day route planning, pickup-and-delivery and dynamic depots are Custom-plan features, so recurring multi-day route operations should get a quote.

cons_detail.title: Best fit is high-density routing
cons_detail.explanation: Pest control, lawn care, pool service and delivery benefit most. HVAC and plumbing service shops with a few calls a day usually get enough from their FSM's routing.

tools.implementation_notes: OptimoRoute is largely self-service.
