Import customers and orders (CSV from your FSM or spreadsheets, or through the API or Zapier), set up drivers, vehicles, skills, capacities and depots, then describe your real constraints: time windows, service durations and which driver can do which job. Getting those constraints right is what makes the optimization good. Roll the mobile app out to drivers, train dispatchers on re-planning during the day, and compare optimized routes with your current ones during the 30-day trial.

tool_faqs.q: How does OptimoRoute compare to routing built into FSM platforms?
tool_faqs.a: FSM-bundled routing covers basic scheduling and route order. OptimoRoute is dedicated routing software that optimizes around time windows, skills, capacity and live changes. For a few service calls a day, FSM routing is usually enough; for dense daily routes (pest control, lawn care, pool service), test OptimoRoute on your own routes during the trial.

tool_faqs.q: Do I need to switch FSM to use OptimoRoute?
tool_faqs.a: No. OptimoRoute pairs with whatever FSM you currently use. Customer data and route assignments flow between OptimoRoute and your FSM via Zapier workflows or CSV imports. The architecture is intentionally layered: OptimoRoute as the routing specialty, your existing FSM as the customer/billing/invoicing core.

tool_faqs.q: What types of operations benefit most from OptimoRoute?
tool_faqs.a: Operations with many stops per route: pest control, lawn care, pool service, route-based cleaning and delivery. Shops with a few service calls a day (HVAC, plumbing repair) get less from dedicated routing, since their FSM's routing usually copes.

tool_faqs.q: Is the 30-day free trial enough to evaluate OptimoRoute?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Use it as a production test: configure your constraints (time windows, capacity, driver skills), optimize two or three weeks of real routes, and compare miles and stops per day with your current routing.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between Lite, Pro and Custom?
tool_faqs.a: Lite ($35.10/driver/mo billed annually) covers the mobile app, live tracking, route history, exports and API access for up to 700 orders. Pro ($44.10) adds weekly planning, real-time order tracking, proof of delivery, customer feedback and analytics for up to 1,000 orders. Custom is quoted and adds multi-day routes, pickup and delivery, commercial routing and dynamic depots.

tools.name: CompanyCam
tools.tagline: Photo documentation and communication platform for contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Core $63/mo billed annually (1 user included; +$29/mo per additional user on annual billing); Crew $129/mo billed annually (3 users); Scale $199/mo billed annually (3 users); Enterprise custom for 50+ users. The pricing page says annual billing saves 20% against month-to-month; month-to-month Core is $79 and Scale $249, and Crew's month-to-month price was not confirmed on 2026-10-03. Verified against companycam.com/pricing 2026-10-03.

tools.best_for: Contractors needing structured photo documentation for insurance claims, customer trust, or marketing portfolios
tools.weaknesses: Photo platform only, not a full FSM; adds another monthly subscription on top of FSM; extra users cost $29/mo each (annual) beyond each plan's included seats
tools.long_description:
CompanyCam is a photo documentation and communication app for contractors, started in 2014 in Lincoln, Nebraska by Luke Hansen, who built it while working at his family's roofing company. A 2025 funding round led by B Capital valued it at $2 billion, and local reporting put it at about 50,000 customers.

It fills a gap that FSM photo features often leave: every photo is location- and time-stamped and filed into a project, with annotations, comments, tags, documents and customer-facing galleries. AI features come with monthly credits (20 on Core, 100 on Crew, unlimited on Scale), and storage is unlimited on every plan.

Pricing is per plan with included seats: Core at $63/month billed annually (1 user), Crew at $129/month (3 users) and Scale at $199/month (3 users), with additional users at $29/month each on annual billing, month-to-month rates about 25% higher, and custom Enterprise pricing for 50+ users. There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card.

Integrations include ServiceTitan, JobNimbus, AccuLynx, Jobber, JobTread, SumoQuote, QuickBooks Online and Zapier, so photos can flow into the job record in your main system. CompanyCam sits alongside your FSM rather than replacing it.

The trade-off: CompanyCam is photo-only, not a full FSM, so it is an extra subscription. It pays off where photo evidence matters most: roofing, insurance restoration and general contracting, and anywhere disputes or warranty claims turn on what the job looked like.

pros_detail.title: GPS-tagged photo organization
pros_detail.explanation: Every photo automatically tied to location, project, customer, and date. Eliminates the 'which job was this photo from?' problem that kills contractor photo libraries. Critical for insurance restoration documentation.

pros_detail.title: AI features on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: AI features for working with photos come with 20 credits a month on Core, 100 on Crew and unlimited use on Scale.

pros_detail.title: Integrations with major contractor platforms
pros_detail.explanation: ServiceTitan, JobNimbus, AccuLynx, Jobber and JobTread integrations link CompanyCam projects to jobs and sync photos and documents to the job record.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited storage
pros_detail.explanation: Every photo, video and document your team captures is stored with no storage cap on any plan.

pros_detail.title: Customer-facing galleries
pros_detail.explanation: Share project galleries with customers as live links. Builds trust during the project and creates marketing assets after completion. Roofing and general contracting customers particularly value this transparency.

pros_detail.title: 14-day free trial, no credit card
pros_detail.explanation: Test it on live jobs with your crew before you pay; no credit card is required to start.

cons_detail.title: Photo platform only, not full FSM
cons_detail.explanation: CompanyCam doesn't handle scheduling, dispatching, invoicing, or customer billing. Sits on top of your FSM as a photo layer. Additional monthly subscription rather than replacement.

cons_detail.title: Seat costs scale with team size
cons_detail.explanation: Core includes 1 user and Crew and Scale include 3; extra users are $29/month each on annual billing ($34 month-to-month), so a large crew pays well above the headline plan price. Cost-benefit depends on photo discipline actually paying back through faster claims and better marketing.

cons_detail.title: Roofing-centric positioning
cons_detail.explanation: Highest value for roofing contractors and operations doing insurance restoration. HVAC, plumbing, electrical operations get value from photo documentation but the ROI math is less compelling than for roofing.

tools.implementation_notes: Plan for one to three weeks. Onboarding is largely self-service. Connect CompanyCam to your main platform first (ServiceTitan, JobNimbus, AccuLynx, Jobber or JobTread) so projects match your jobs, invite the team and install the app on every field phone. Then agree photo standards for each job stage (arrival, before, work in progress, completion) and train the office on galleries, tags and sharing. The hard part is habit: expect to remind crews for several weeks before photographing every stage becomes routine.

tool_faqs.q: Is CompanyCam worth the extra subscription on top of my FSM?
tool_faqs.a: It depends on how much your work relies on photo evidence. Roofing, insurance restoration and general contracting get the most from it (claims, disputes, warranty questions, marketing portfolios). For HVAC, plumbing and electrical shops that take few photos, the photo tools in their FSM may be enough. Use the 14-day trial on real jobs to judge it.

tool_faqs.q: How does CompanyCam compare to taking photos with my phone's camera?
tool_faqs.a: Native phone photos lack: GPS tagging tied to a specific project, automatic organization into project galleries, annotations and comments tied to specific images, structured before/after pairing, AI content tagging, customer-facing galleries, and integration with your FSM. CompanyCam is essentially the office discipline layer on top of phone photos: same photos, but searchable, organized, and tied to business records. The discipline matters more than the photos themselves.

tool_faqs.q: Does CompanyCam integrate with ServiceTitan?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. CompanyCam can create a matching project from an in-progress or dispatched ServiceTitan job, sync photos and documents back to ServiceTitan, and archive the project automatically once the job is done.

tool_faqs.q: Can CompanyCam handle drone footage?
tool_faqs.a: You can upload photos and videos from drones through the app or the web interface into the same project gallery. Location tagging depends on the drone writing GPS data into its files, so test it with your own drone before relying on it.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between CompanyCam's plans?
tool_faqs.a: Core ($63/month billed annually, $79 month-to-month) includes 1 user; Crew ($129/month billed annually) and Scale ($199/month annual, $249 monthly) each include 3 users; additional users are $29/month on annual billing ($34 month-to-month); Enterprise is custom for 50+ users. Feature differences between plans are listed on CompanyCam's pricing page, so confirm the features you need (such as AI photo tagging) are on the plan you choose.

tools.name: Buildxact
tools.tagline: Estimating and project management for residential builders and remodelers

pricing.pricing_note: Foundation $169/mo billed annually ($2,030/yr; $199 month-to-month); free Go tier with 5 complimentary estimate credits; Pro $339/mo, Master $509/mo (annual billing).

tools.best_for: Residential custom home builders and remodelers wanting strong estimating with project management
tools.weaknesses: Smaller US user community than Buildertrend; Australian heritage with a growing US presence; AI add-ons cost extra
tools.long_description:
Buildxact is estimating and project management software for residential builders and remodelers, founded in 2011 in Melbourne, Australia, with a North American base in Austin, Texas. It serves builders in Australia, New Zealand, North America and the UK.

Estimating is the focus: digital takeoffs from plans, supplier price connections for current material costs, labor estimating, change orders and budgets tracked against actuals. AI "Blu" tools can generate estimates, assist with takeoffs and review estimates as paid add-ons.

Pricing is per company with unlimited users on every plan: a free Go tier with 5 estimate credits, Foundation at $169 a month billed annually ($199 monthly, with digital takeoffs and lead management), Pro at $339 ($399 monthly, adding the Blu Estimate Generator and job management) and Master at $509 ($599 monthly, adding user access controls and priority support). There is a 14-day free trial. Integrations include QuickBooks Online, Xero, MYOB and Deputy, plus supplier price connections.

The trade-off: Buildxact is smaller in the US than Buildertrend, and it is built for residential construction rather than commercial projects.

pros_detail.title: Estimating depth for residential construction
pros_detail.explanation: Materials takeoffs from drawings, supplier pricing integration, labor estimating by trade and skill level, change order cost impact analysis. The granularity residential construction needs for accurate bidding versus general FSM's line-item quote approach.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Foundation $169, Pro $339 and Master $509 per month (billed annually) all include unlimited users, so adding estimators or project managers doesn't raise the bill.

pros_detail.title: Supplier price connections
pros_detail.explanation: Supplier connections bring current material prices into estimates, so bids reflect today's costs rather than a stale spreadsheet. Confirm your suppliers are connected.

pros_detail.title: Digital takeoffs from Foundation
pros_detail.explanation: Measure and count from PDF or image plans on every paid plan, with the quantities flowing straight into the estimate.

pros_detail.title: Free Go tier and 14-day trial
pros_detail.explanation: Start free with 5 estimate credits, or trial a paid plan for 14 days before committing.

cons_detail.title: Smaller US community than Buildertrend
cons_detail.explanation: Buildertrend has the longer US track record and larger community; Buildxact's roots and much of its base are in Australia and New Zealand.

cons_detail.title: AI features cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: The Blu Estimate Generator, Takeoff Assistant and Estimate Reviewer are paid add-ons ($99-$149/month each), so price the plan plus the add-ons you want.

cons_detail.title: Check US supplier coverage
cons_detail.explanation: Supplier price connections matter most for estimating accuracy, so confirm the suppliers you buy from are connected in your area.

cons_detail.title: Roofing fit is weak
cons_detail.explanation: Built for residential construction; roofing operations get a thinner feature set than dedicated roofing platforms (AccuLynx, JobNimbus, Roofr). Listed in roofing vertical because some general contractors do roofing, but pure roofing operations should use roofing-specialty alternatives.

tools.implementation_notes: Set up your company profile, project templates for common job types, pricing and markup rules, supplier price connections and your accounting integration. Then practice digital takeoffs from real plans (the highest-value skill), build estimating templates for your cost structure, and run your first projects from estimate through change orders to completion. Expect to refine material rates and labor pricing over the first few months as you compare estimates with actual results.

tool_faqs.q: How does Buildxact compare to Buildertrend and JobTread?
tool_faqs.a: Buildxact is estimating-focused residential construction software with unlimited users on every plan ($169-$509/month billed annually). Buildertrend is custom-quoted with unlimited users. JobTread publishes a $199/month base including one user plus per-user fees. For estimating and takeoffs specifically, Buildxact is the most focused of the three; compare all three on your projects.

tool_faqs.q: What's the takeoff feature in Buildxact?
tool_faqs.a: Digital takeoffs from plans are included from the Foundation plan: upload PDF or image plans, measure and count items, and the quantities flow into the estimate. Blu AI add-ons (Takeoff Assistant, Estimate Generator, Estimate Reviewer) cost extra.

tool_faqs.q: Is Buildxact good for US-based builders?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with caveats. Buildxact has a North American base in Austin, Texas, and its estimating and project workflows suit US residential builders. Check that the supplier price connections and accounting integration you need (QuickBooks Online is supported) cover your area.

tool_faqs.q: Does Buildxact handle commercial construction?
tool_faqs.a: Limited. Buildxact is built for residential construction (custom homes, remodels, renovations). Commercial construction operations doing significant new construction with AIA progress billing, complex vendor management, RFI workflows, and submittals typically need Procore, Simpro, or other commercial-construction PM platforms. Small commercial builders doing work similar in scope to large residential projects can use Buildxact; larger commercial operations outgrow its feature set.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between Buildxact's plans?
tool_faqs.a: Go is free with 5 estimate credits. Foundation ($169/month billed annually, $199 monthly) adds lead management and digital takeoffs; Pro ($339, $399 monthly) adds the Blu Estimate Generator and job management; Master ($509, $599 monthly) adds user access controls and priority support. All plans include unlimited users, and AI add-ons cost extra.

tools.name: Yardbook
tools.tagline: Landscaping business software with a free plan and low-cost paid upgrades

pricing.pricing_note: Starter is free (customers, jobs and scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, expenses, reports, card payments), but Yardbook charges a 1% processing fee on each online customer payment for free and trial accounts, on top of Stripe's fees. Business $34.99/month adds bulk email and text, GPS tracking and automatic invoice reminders, and waives the 1% fee. Enterprise $49.99/month adds QuickBooks sync, a branded company portal and no ads. Verified against yardbook.com/pages/pricing and /pages/tos 2026-09-10.

tools.best_for: Solo landscapers and small lawn and landscape crews that want scheduling, estimates, invoices and routing without a monthly fee to start
tools.weaknesses: The free plan charges a 1% fee on online customer payments; QuickBooks sync and the branded portal are on the $49.99 Enterprise plan only; little public information about the company; no app found in the App Store
tools.long_description:
Yardbook is business management software for lawn care and landscaping companies, built for small operations. It covers the core office work of a lawn and landscape business: customers, jobs and scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, expenses and reports, with card payments from customers.

Its main draw is price. The Starter plan is free with no subscription fee. The catch is a 1% processing fee that Yardbook charges on each online customer payment made through a free or trial account, on top of Stripe's own card fees. Business costs $34.99 a month, adds bulk email and text messaging, GPS tracking and automatic invoice reminders, and waives the 1% fee. Enterprise costs $49.99 a month and adds QuickBooks sync, a branded company portal for your customers and no ads. Prices are per company, not per user.

For a business that takes a steady volume of card payments online, the 1% fee can cost more than the Business plan that removes it: at $3,500 a month in online payments, the fee is $35, about the price of Business.

The trade-off: Yardbook publishes little about the company behind it, its only named integrations are Stripe for payments and QuickBooks on the top plan, and we could not find a Yardbook app in Apple's App Store. Test how your crews would use it on their phones before you rely on it in the field.

pros_detail.title: Free plan to start
pros_detail.explanation: Starter costs nothing and covers customers, jobs and scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, expenses, reports and card payments.

pros_detail.title: Low-cost paid plans
pros_detail.explanation: Business is $34.99 a month and Enterprise $49.99 a month, priced per company rather than per user.

pros_detail.title: Paid plans drop the payment fee
pros_detail.explanation: Business and Enterprise waive the 1% fee that Yardbook charges on online customer payments made through free and trial accounts.

pros_detail.title: Built for lawn and landscape work
pros_detail.explanation: Scheduling, estimates, invoicing and routing are set up for small lawn care and landscaping businesses.

cons_detail.title: 1% fee on the free plan
cons_detail.explanation: Free and trial accounts pay Yardbook 1% of each online customer payment, on top of Stripe's card fees. At higher payment volumes a paid plan costs less.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks only on Enterprise
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks sync, the branded customer portal and removing ads all require the $49.99 Enterprise plan.

cons_detail.title: Few integrations
cons_detail.explanation: Stripe for payments and QuickBooks on Enterprise are the only integrations Yardbook names.

cons_detail.title: No App Store app found
cons_detail.explanation: We could not find a Yardbook app in Apple's App Store, so confirm how crews would use it on a phone before you switch.

tools.implementation_notes: Start on the free Starter plan, enter your customers and services, and run a few real jobs from estimate to invoice. Connect your Stripe account for card payments and watch the 1% fee on online payments: once it adds up to more than $34.99 a month, Business costs less. Move to Enterprise if you need QuickBooks sync or a branded portal for customers, and check how your crews will use Yardbook on their phones before you depend on it in the field.

tool_faqs.q: Is Yardbook really free?
tool_faqs.a: The Starter plan has no subscription fee and covers customers, jobs and scheduling, estimates, invoices, routing, expenses, reports and card payments. Yardbook does charge a 1% processing fee on each online customer payment made through a free or trial account, on top of Stripe's fees.

tool_faqs.q: What do the paid plans add?
tool_faqs.a: Business ($34.99 a month) adds bulk email and text, GPS tracking and automatic invoice reminders, and waives the 1% fee. Enterprise ($49.99 a month) adds QuickBooks sync, a branded company portal and no ads.

tool_faqs.q: When does a paid plan pay for itself?
tool_faqs.a: When your online customer payments reach about $3,500 a month, the 1% fee on the free plan is about $35, roughly the price of the Business plan that waives it.

tool_faqs.q: Does Yardbook work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, on the $49.99 Enterprise plan. The free Starter and $34.99 Business plans do not include QuickBooks sync.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a Yardbook mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: We could not find a Yardbook app in Apple's App Store. Ask Yardbook how crews should use it on their phones before you switch.

tools.name: Roofr
tools.tagline: Roofing software that combines its own roof measurement reports with a CRM, proposals and payments

pricing.pricing_note: Per company; every plan card lists unlimited users. Starter is free ($19 measurement reports, 1 job board, 10 trial proposals and invoices, 5 automated actions). Prices shown are monthly billing: Measure+ from $109/mo (6-hour or 2-hour report delivery, $13 reports, ESX files $10 per report), Essentials $249/mo ($209/mo on annual billing), Scale $349/mo ($299/mo annual). Paid plans get $13 measurement reports. Month-to-month or annual contract; Roofr says annual billing saves up to 15% and there are no setup or onboarding fees. Instant Estimator, Roofr Sites and AI Receptionist are paid add-ons. Verified against roofr.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential roofing contractors who want measurement reports, proposals, e-signatures, payments and material ordering in one system, with unlimited users on every plan
tools.weaknesses: Built for roofing only. There is no App Store or Google Play app (Roofr runs as a web app you add to your home screen), and QuickBooks, crew management and job costing start on the $349-a-month Scale plan.
tools.long_description:
Roofr is software for roofing contractors that combines roof measurement reports with a CRM, proposals, invoicing, payments and material ordering. Roofr says CEO Richard Nelson, a third-generation roofer, started the company in 2016 with CTO Kevin Redman, and that it joined Y Combinator in 2017. The company says thousands of roofing contractors across North America use it.

Roofr Reports are roof measurement reports that give pitch and roofing squares and calculate materials from your waste factor. Roofr says paid subscribers get reports in 2 hours or less, and Measure+ subscribers choose 2-hour or 6-hour delivery. Proposals pull measurements from the report and support custom templates, several options for the homeowner to pick from, discounts, change orders and on-the-spot e-signatures, and Roofr shows when a proposal has been opened. A signed proposal becomes a material list, and Roofr can check prices and stock and send orders to ABC Supply, QXO (formerly Beacon) and SRS Distribution.

The CRM side has drag-and-drop job boards, automated actions (such as changing a job's status or assigning tasks), a calendar, invoicing, SMS texting with templates and performance reporting. Roofr Payments takes cards and ACH: Roofr lists 2.8% plus 30 cents for Visa, Mastercard and Discover, 3.25% plus 30 cents for American Express and 0.5% for ACH (capped at $40), and you can pass these fees on to the customer. Paid add-ons include the Instant Estimator (a link where homeowners get a price based on your own pricing, measured from satellite imagery), Roofr Sites and an AI Receptionist. On phones, Roofr runs as a web app added to the home screen rather than an App Store or Google Play download.

Pricing is per company, and every plan card lists unlimited users. Starter is free, with $19 measurement reports, 1 job board, 10 trial proposals and invoices and 5 automated actions. Measure+ starts at $109 a month billed monthly and lowers reports to $13 with faster delivery. Essentials is $249 a month ($209 on annual billing) and adds unlimited proposals, invoices and work orders, card and ACH payments, unlimited e-signatures and SMS texting. Scale is $349 a month ($299 annual) and adds 7 job boards, crew management, 25+ automated actions, a performance dashboard, profit margins and job costs, QuickBooks integration and role-based permissions. Roofr says there are no setup or onboarding fees, and you can pay month to month or sign an annual contract.

The trade-off: Roofr is built only for roofing, and several tools a growing company may want (QuickBooks, crew management, job costing, role permissions) start on Scale. Teams that rely on a native mobile app should test the web app on their crews' phones before switching.

pros_detail.title: Measurements, proposals and payments in one place
pros_detail.explanation: Measurement data flows into proposals, a signed proposal becomes a material list, and invoices and card or ACH payments run in the same system.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Roofr says it does not charge per seat, so adding sales reps or office staff does not change the monthly price.

pros_detail.title: Free plan to start
pros_detail.explanation: The Starter plan costs nothing and includes a job board, 10 trial proposals and invoices and pay-per-report measurements, so you can test it on real jobs.

pros_detail.title: Supplier ordering built in
pros_detail.explanation: Roofr pulls material pricing and sends orders to ABC Supply, QXO (formerly Beacon) and SRS Distribution from the field.

pros_detail.title: Month-to-month billing, no setup fee
pros_detail.explanation: You can pay monthly without a contract, or annually to save up to 15%, and Roofr says there are no setup or onboarding fees.

pros_detail.title: Instant Estimator for lead capture
pros_detail.explanation: The Instant Estimator add-on gives homeowners a price from your own pricing based on satellite imagery of their roof, and creates a job card for follow-up.

cons_detail.title: Roofing only
cons_detail.explanation: Roofr is designed for roofing contractors. Companies that also sell siding, windows or general remodeling get a roofing-focused workflow.

cons_detail.title: Key tools on the top plan
cons_detail.explanation: QuickBooks integration, crew management, job costing and role-based permissions are on Scale at $349 a month billed monthly.

cons_detail.title: No native mobile app
cons_detail.explanation: Roofr runs in the phone's browser and can be added to the home screen, but it is not an App Store or Google Play download.

cons_detail.title: Reports and add-ons cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Measurement reports are billed per report ($19 on Starter, $13 on paid plans), and the Instant Estimator, Roofr Sites and AI Receptionist are paid add-ons.

cons_detail.title: Payment processing fees
cons_detail.explanation: Roofr Payments charges 2.8% plus 30 cents per card payment (3.25% plus 30 cents for American Express) and 0.5% for ACH, unless you pass the fees to customers.

tools.implementation_notes: Start on the free Starter plan and run a few measurement reports and proposals, then choose a paid plan: Essentials for unlimited proposals, invoices and card or ACH payments, Scale for QuickBooks, crew management and job costing. Build proposal templates with your branding, options and terms, and set your waste factor and material choices so signed proposals produce accurate material lists. If you buy from ABC Supply, QXO or SRS, connect those accounts for pricing and ordering. Turn on Roofr Payments if you want to collect by card or ACH, and decide whether to pass processing fees to customers. Have field staff add the Roofr web app to their phone home screens. Use the Zapier app if you need to send new leads or proposal events to other tools.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Roofr cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starter is free. Measure+ starts at $109 a month billed monthly, Essentials is $249 a month ($209 on annual billing) and Scale is $349 a month ($299 annual). Measurement reports are $13 each on paid plans and $19 on Starter. Add-ons such as the Instant Estimator cost extra.

tool_faqs.q: Does Roofr charge per user?
tool_faqs.a: No. Roofr says it does not charge per seat, and every plan card lists unlimited users.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free version of Roofr?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The Starter plan is free and includes 1 job board, 10 trial proposals and invoices, 5 automated actions and measurement reports at $19 each. Roofr describes it as the way to try the software before paying.

tool_faqs.q: Does Roofr have a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: Not a native one. Roofr runs in the browser on iOS and Android and can be added to the home screen, with push notifications, the job board, measurements and proposals available on the phone.

tool_faqs.q: What does Roofr integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Material ordering and pricing connect to ABC Supply, QXO (formerly Beacon) and SRS Distribution. QuickBooks integration is on the Scale plan. A Roofr app on Zapier sends events such as new leads, job stage changes and signed proposals to other tools, and can create jobs and customers in Roofr.

tool_faqs.q: How fast are Roofr measurement reports?
tool_faqs.a: Roofr says paid subscribers get reports in 2 hours or less, and Measure+ subscribers can choose 2-hour or 6-hour delivery. Reports include pitch, roofing squares and material quantities based on your waste factor.

tools.name: GoCanvas
tools.tagline: Mobile forms and workflow automation for field service businesses

pricing.pricing_note: Essentials $29, Pro $39 and Max $49 per user a month, billed annually, with a 3-user minimum. Free trial: GoCanvas's trial page says a product specialist activates it after a setup call, and its pricing, trial and FAQ pages state no length; its release notes of 24 November 2025 say the trial messaging was updated to a 14-day duration. Verified against gocanvas.com/pricing, gocanvas.com/free-trial and help.gocanvas.com 2026-10-05.

tools.best_for: Trades businesses needing custom mobile forms beyond what their primary FSM provides, such as inspection forms, safety checklists, equipment audits, custom work order templates
tools.weaknesses: Centered on forms and field data rather than quoting, invoicing and payments, so you may need an FSM beside it; per-user pricing with a 3-user minimum; custom forms take someone on your team to build
tools.long_description:
GoCanvas is a mobile forms and field operations platform, founded in 2008 and based in Reston, Virginia. Since July 2024 it has been part of the Nemetschek Group, in the same Build & Construct division as Bluebeam. Trades businesses use it for the forms their main FSM doesn't cover well: inspection forms, safety checklists, equipment audits, custom work orders and trade-specific data collection.

The form builder is the core: conditional logic, calculation fields, photo capture with annotations, GPS tagging, signatures, barcode scanning and offline use for techs in low-signal areas, with a template library to start from. Essentials also includes dispatch and scheduling and configurable PDF reports; Pro adds multi-user workflows, customer and project management and API access; Max adds departments, follow-up tasks, live data sources and single sign-on.

Pricing is per user, billed annually with a 3-user minimum: Essentials $29, Pro $39 and Max $49 per user per month. GoCanvas offers a free trial, which a product specialist activates after a setup call; its release notes put it at 14 days (November 2025). Integrations include QuickBooks, Salesforce, Procore (two-way), Zapier, Microsoft Power Automate, Box, Dropbox and Google Drive.

The trade-off: GoCanvas centers on forms and field data, not quoting, invoicing and payments, so most trades run it beside an FSM. Building good forms takes someone with an eye for logic and workflow.

pros_detail.title: Custom mobile form builder with depth
pros_detail.explanation: Conditional logic, calculation fields, photo capture with annotations, GPS tagging, signature capture, barcode scanning, offline mode. Operations build trade-specific data collection workflows that pre-built FSM templates can't match.

pros_detail.title: Template library to start from
pros_detail.explanation: Pre-built templates for inspections, service calls, audits and safety checks mean you customize rather than build every form from scratch.

pros_detail.title: Offline mode for low-signal environments
pros_detail.explanation: Forms work offline and sync when connectivity returns. Useful for techs working in basements, rooftops, remote rural locations, or other low-signal areas. Many FSM-bundled form features lack this depth.

pros_detail.title: Free trial with every feature
pros_detail.explanation: GoCanvas's help center says you can use "any and all features and functions" during the trial, with unlimited form building, devices and users. Its release notes put the trial at 14 days (November 2025), and a product specialist activates it after a setup call.

pros_detail.title: Procore, Salesforce and QuickBooks integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Push completed forms into Procore Documents and pull Procore data into forms, sync with Salesforce and QuickBooks, and file PDFs to Box, Dropbox or Google Drive.

pros_detail.title: Dispatch and scheduling included
pros_detail.explanation: Even Essentials includes dispatch and scheduling, so forms can go out to techs as job assignments.

cons_detail.title: Not a full FSM
cons_detail.explanation: GoCanvas handles forms, dispatch and field data, but not the quoting, invoicing and payments of a full FSM, so most trades run it beside one. Weigh it against the forms your FSM already has.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing adds up at scale
cons_detail.explanation: At $29-$49 per user per month (billed annually), large operations (25+ users) pay roughly $725-$1,225 per month for GoCanvas alone. For operations adopting GoCanvas just to extend FSM form functionality, the cost-benefit math requires justification.

cons_detail.title: Custom forms take time to build
cons_detail.explanation: Custom forms with conditional logic, calculation fields and workflow steps need someone on your team to build them, so plan who will do it, or start from pre-built templates.

cons_detail.title: Overlaps with FSM-bundled mobile forms
cons_detail.explanation: Most modern FSM platforms ship some mobile form capability. Operations should genuinely need custom forms beyond FSM-bundled features to justify GoCanvas; operations that use FSM-bundled forms for everything don't need GoCanvas's depth.

tools.implementation_notes: Deployment time depends on how many custom forms you build. Start from the template library and adapt templates rather than building from scratch, then test each form with field techs and iterate. Connect the integrations you need (QuickBooks, Salesforce, Procore, cloud storage) once the forms are stable. Moving from paper is mostly a habit change; moving from another forms tool usually means rebuilding forms. Make the GoCanvas forms a required step, not an optional one.

tool_faqs.q: Do I need GoCanvas if my FSM has mobile forms?
tool_faqs.a: Depends on your form complexity needs. Most modern FSM platforms (Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan) ship basic mobile form capability, sufficient for simple inspections and standard work order completion. GoCanvas's specialty is custom forms with conditional logic, calculation fields, and complex workflows. If you find yourself wishing your FSM forms could do more, GoCanvas extends the capability. If your FSM forms handle your workflows, you don't need GoCanvas.

tool_faqs.q: How does GoCanvas compare to Mitti (formerly SafetyCulture)?
tool_faqs.a: Both are mobile-forms platforms with overlapping uses. Mitti is inspection and safety focused, with a free plan for up to 10 seats. GoCanvas covers inspections plus general data collection, work orders, equipment audits, dispatch and scheduling, with per-user plans from $29/user/month (3-user minimum). For a pure safety and compliance focus, Mitti fits; for custom forms across many workflows, GoCanvas.

tool_faqs.q: What kinds of forms do operations build in GoCanvas?
tool_faqs.a: Common form types: HVAC equipment inspection checklists, plumbing service call documentation, electrical audit forms, roofing damage assessment forms, vehicle inspection forms, safety pre-work checklists, equipment maintenance logs, customer signature acceptance forms, time tracking with project codes, and many trade-specific data collection workflows. GoCanvas's template library has pre-built forms to start from, such as daily field reports, estimates, risk assessments and work orders.

tool_faqs.q: Does GoCanvas work offline?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Offline access is on every plan: forms, photos and signatures can be completed without a connection and sync when connectivity returns, which matters for basements, rooftops and rural sites.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between GoCanvas's plans?
tool_faqs.a: GoCanvas publishes three per-user plans billed annually with a 3-user minimum: Essentials at $29/user/month, Pro at $39 and Max at $49. Compare the feature lists on GoCanvas's pricing page to see what Pro and Max add.

tools.name: Mitti (formerly SafetyCulture)
tools.tagline: Inspection and safety checklist platform, originally the iAuditor app

pricing.pricing_note: Free plan covers up to 10 seats with 5 active inspection templates (unlimited inspections), basic analytics, training, tasks, and issue reporting; Mitti's FAQ at mitti.com/safetyculture says the free plan has no time limit. Premium $24/seat/mo billed annually ($29 monthly) adds unlimited seats and active inspection templates, advanced analytics, extended data history, integrations, and SSO. Enterprise custom-quoted. Every plan includes AI credits per full seat each month: up to 300 on Free, from 500 on Premium and from 800 on Enterprise. Multi-site operations can instead get a quoted location-based price: one fixed price per site with unlimited users. Premium has a 30-day free trial, per Mitti's preventive maintenance software guide (mitti.com/apps/preventive-maintenance-software, checked 2026-10-05); the pricing page FAQ says card details are collected when the trial starts and you are not charged if you return to the Free plan before it ends. SafetyCulture rebranded as Mitti on 2026-08-11; safetyculture.com now redirects to mitti.com. Verified against mitti.com/pricing and help.mitti.com/000867 2026-10-05.

tools.best_for: Trades businesses needing structured safety inspections, code compliance documentation, and audit-ready checklists for OSHA or insurance requirements
tools.weaknesses: Not a full FSM (inspection and operations focused); integrations need a paid plan; renamed twice (iAuditor to SafetyCulture in 2022, SafetyCulture to Mitti in August 2026), so older guides use old names
tools.long_description:
Mitti (formerly SafetyCulture, and before that iAuditor) is an inspection, safety and frontline operations platform. Luke Anear started the business in 2004 in Townsville, Australia; it is now headquartered in Sydney, and the company says more than 2 million frontline workers across 80,000 organizations use it. SafetyCulture rebranded to Mitti on 11 August 2026; Mitti's developer changelog calls it the same platform and team with a new name, and safetyculture.com now redirects to mitti.com.

For trades, the core is structured inspections: custom checklist templates (plus a public library of ready-made ones), photo evidence with annotations, issue and incident reporting, asset tracking, dashboards and audit-ready records. That makes it useful where OSHA, insurers or customers expect documented inspections, such as commercial property service, facility maintenance or government contracting.

The Free plan covers up to 10 seats with 5 active inspection templates at a time (unlimited inspections), and Mitti says it has no time limit. Premium, at $24 per seat per month billed annually ($29 monthly), adds unlimited seats and active templates, advanced analytics, extended data history, integrations and single sign-on; Enterprise is custom-quoted. Premium comes with a 30-day free trial; Mitti collects card details when it starts and does not charge you if you return to the Free plan before it ends.

Integrations, available on Premium and Enterprise, include a two-way Salesforce integration built by the partner OpSmooth, Procore, Zapier, Workato, Microsoft Power BI, Power Automate and SharePoint, and file tools such as Google Drive, Dropbox and OneDrive.

The trade-off: Mitti is not a full FSM. It schedules inspections, but its plans list no job dispatch, quoting or customer invoicing, and shops without formal inspection or compliance requirements usually get enough from the photo and checklist features in their FSM.

pros_detail.title: Free plan (up to 10 seats)
pros_detail.explanation: The Free plan covers up to 10 seats with 5 active inspection templates at a time, unlimited inspections, basic analytics, training, tasks and issue reporting. Mitti says the Free plan has no time limit.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited custom checklist templates on Premium
pros_detail.explanation: Build inspection forms for your own trade workflows (HVAC equipment inspections, roofing pre-work safety checks, electrical compliance forms), or start from the public template library.

pros_detail.title: Audit-ready inspection records
pros_detail.explanation: Mitti says each inspection keeps a complete record, including date and time stamps, GPS location and user attribution, alongside photo evidence: the documentation OSHA inspectors, insurers and compliance-minded customers ask for. It replaces paper forms that get lost or filled in after the fact.

pros_detail.title: Widely used
pros_detail.explanation: The company says more than 2 million frontline workers across 80,000 organizations use it, so ready-made templates exist for most trades and staff may already know the app.

pros_detail.title: 30-day free trial of Premium
pros_detail.explanation: Mitti offers a 30-day free trial of Premium. It collects card details when the trial starts; return to the Free plan before the trial ends and you are not charged.

pros_detail.title: Salesforce, Procore and BI integrations
pros_detail.explanation: A two-way Salesforce integration, built by the partner OpSmooth, creates Mitti inspections from Salesforce jobs and writes the results back to the job record; Procore, Zapier, Workato and Power BI round out the list on Premium and Enterprise.

cons_detail.title: Not a full FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Mitti schedules inspections, but its plans list no job dispatch, customer billing or invoicing, so you need an FSM platform for those workflows. That adds another monthly subscription on top of the FSM for operations needing both.

cons_detail.title: Can feel overkill for shops without compliance requirements
cons_detail.explanation: Operations without OSHA inspections, insurance audit requirements, or customer compliance documentation needs may find SafetyCulture's depth excessive. General FSM with built-in photo documentation handles simpler trade workflow needs without the safety-platform overhead.

cons_detail.title: Two renames in four years
cons_detail.explanation: The platform was renamed from iAuditor to SafetyCulture in 2022 and from SafetyCulture to Mitti on 11 August 2026 (safetyculture.com now redirects to mitti.com). Long-time users may still use the old names, and older documentation and tutorials carry old branding.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing scales with team size
cons_detail.explanation: At $24/seat/month billed annually ($29 monthly) once you outgrow the Free plan, 50 full seats come to $1,200 a month for Mitti alone; Premium includes free guest seats for occasional users. Cost-benefit depends on compliance value: operations with real audit/insurance requirements typically justify the cost; operations without don't.

cons_detail.title: Integrations need a paid plan
cons_detail.explanation: Free-plan users can't connect Mitti to other systems; integrations start on Premium.

tools.implementation_notes: Setup time depends on how many inspection workflows you build. Mitti's pricing table lists onboarding services and training as not included on Free and as a contact-sales item on Premium and Enterprise. Start from the public template library, adapt the templates to your own workflows, set photo standards, and roll the mobile app out to field staff. If you are replacing paper, the work is mostly habit: make inspections a required step, or uptake stays slow. If you are moving from another inspection tool, expect to rebuild your templates.

tool_faqs.q: Is Mitti the same as SafetyCulture and iAuditor?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. SafetyCulture rebranded as Mitti on 11 August 2026, and safetyculture.com now redirects to mitti.com; the product had earlier been renamed from iAuditor to SafetyCulture in 2022. Same product and company, new name. Older documentation and YouTube tutorials may still use the SafetyCulture or iAuditor branding.

tool_faqs.q: Do I need SafetyCulture if I have a general FSM platform?
tool_faqs.a: Depends on your compliance requirements. If your operations face OSHA inspections, insurance audit requirements, or customer compliance documentation needs (commercial property service, healthcare facility maintenance, government contracting), Mitti's structured inspections are built for that documentation: Mitti says each inspection keeps a complete record, including date and time stamps, GPS location and user attribution. If your operations don't face these requirements, general FSM with built-in photo documentation is usually sufficient.

tool_faqs.q: Is SafetyCulture's free tier actually usable for a real business?
tool_faqs.a: Yes for operations up to 10 users with core inspection needs. Mitti says the Free plan has no time limit; it covers up to 10 seats with 5 active inspection templates at a time (unlimited inspections), basic analytics, training, tasks and issue reporting. Premium ($24/seat/month billed annually, $29 monthly) removes the seat and template caps and adds advanced analytics, extended data history, integrations and SSO. Integrations need Premium or Enterprise.

tool_faqs.q: How does SafetyCulture compare to GoCanvas?
tool_faqs.a: Both are mobile-forms platforms with overlapping use cases. Mitti (SafetyCulture) is inspection and safety focused, with a large public template library and a free plan for up to 10 seats. GoCanvas is a general mobile-forms tool with broader uses beyond inspections. If you specifically need inspection and compliance workflows, Mitti's depth fits better; for generic mobile forms, compare GoCanvas's current plans.

tool_faqs.q: Does SafetyCulture work alongside ServiceTitan or Jobber?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Mitti works alongside a general FSM platform as an inspection layer: the FSM handles customers, scheduling and billing, and Mitti handles inspections and compliance records. Results can move between them through Zapier or Workato, or by export.

tools.name: UpKeep
tools.tagline: Mobile-first CMMS for maintenance teams that look after their own equipment and facilities

pricing.pricing_note: Per user per month: Essential $24, Premium $55; Professional and Enterprise are quote-only. Billing term is not stated on the page. View-only users, requesters and third-party vendors do not need paid licenses. Free trial with no credit card on Essential and Premium; the page advertises '7 Days Risk Free'. Optional implementation: Training Only $500, Quickstart $1,500, Advanced $5,000, custom enterprise by quote. Verified against upkeep.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: In-house maintenance teams in manufacturing, facilities, property management, hospitality, food and beverage and similar operations that maintain their own assets (not contractors billing customers)
tools.weaknesses: Built for in-house maintenance, not contractor billing; per-user pricing; offline mobile mode and full analytics need the quote-only Professional plan
tools.long_description:
UpKeep is a CMMS (computerized maintenance management system) for teams that maintain their own equipment and facilities. UpKeep says it was founded in 2015 by CEO Ryan Chan, a former process-development engineer at a membrane manufacturing plant, and it is based in Los Angeles (UpKeep Technologies, Inc.). UpKeep says more than 4,000 companies and 40,000 users rely on it, across manufacturing, facility management, data centers, energy and utilities, food and beverage, healthcare, fleet, property management, education, hospitality and more.

The core CMMS covers work orders, preventive maintenance, asset management, parts and inventory, purchase orders, work requests, meter readings, checklists, QR codes for asset identification, and analytics and reporting, with iOS and Android apps. UpKeep has added Nova AI (automated work order generation and asset intelligence), UpKeep Learn (training built from your procedures), safety and EHS tools, Edge IoT sensors and fleet maintenance.

Pricing is per user per month: Essential $24 (unlimited work orders and locations, Nova AI) and Premium $55 (adds PM scheduling, custom checklists, parts and inventory with costing, time and labor tracking and 30-day analytics history). Professional (adds mobile offline mode, an external request portal, full analytics history, asset lifecycle tracking and signature capture) and Enterprise (multi-site, workflow automation, PO management, API and custom integrations, SSO) are quote-only. View-only users, requesters and outside vendors do not need paid licenses. Essential and Premium have a free trial with no credit card, the pricing page advertises '7 Days Risk Free', and paid implementation packages run from $500 (training only) to $5,000.

Named integrations include SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, QuickBooks and Zapier; UpKeep says it connects to more than 1,000 systems through native integrations, Zapier and its public REST API.

The trade-off: UpKeep is for internal maintenance, not customer-facing field service. HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors who quote, dispatch and invoice customers need an FSM platform such as Jobber, Housecall Pro or ServiceTitan instead. Within CMMS, compare UpKeep with MaintainX and Limble at your team size, and note that offline mobile mode, full analytics history and the request portal sit on the quote-only Professional plan.

pros_detail.title: Published entry prices
pros_detail.explanation: Essential ($24) and Premium ($55) per user per month are listed on the pricing page, with a free trial that needs no credit card.

pros_detail.title: Free licenses for requesters and viewers
pros_detail.explanation: View-only users, requesters and outside vendors do not need paid licenses, so only active technicians and managers count toward the bill.

pros_detail.title: Mobile apps with QR codes
pros_detail.explanation: iOS and Android apps let technicians handle work orders on the floor, and QR codes on equipment identify assets.

pros_detail.title: Broad CMMS coverage
pros_detail.explanation: Work orders, preventive maintenance, asset management, parts and inventory, purchase orders, meter readings and reporting in one system.

pros_detail.title: ERP integrations
pros_detail.explanation: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics and QuickBooks are named, plus Zapier and a REST API.

pros_detail.title: More than a CMMS
pros_detail.explanation: Safety and EHS tools, IoT sensors, fleet maintenance and Nova AI extend the platform.

cons_detail.title: Internal maintenance only, not customer-facing FSM
cons_detail.explanation: UpKeep is not designed to quote and bill customers. Contractors need an FSM platform such as Jobber, Housecall Pro or ServiceTitan; read the CMMS vs FSM glossary entry before deciding.

cons_detail.title: Key features sit on higher plans
cons_detail.explanation: PM scheduling starts at Premium, and mobile offline mode, the external request portal and full analytics history need the quote-only Professional plan.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Each technician or manager needs a paid license, so cost grows with the team.

cons_detail.title: Paid implementation packages
cons_detail.explanation: Training-only help costs $500, the Quickstart implementation plan $1,500 and expanded training $5,000.

cons_detail.title: Short risk-free period
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page advertises 7 days risk free, which may not cover a full monthly preventive-maintenance cycle.

tools.implementation_notes: Start a free trial on Essential or Premium (no credit card) and pick the plan by the features you need: PM scheduling needs Premium, and offline mode and the request portal need Professional. Build your location hierarchy, import your asset list (with make, model and meter readings where relevant) and print QR codes for key equipment. Load parts and inventory, set up preventive maintenance schedules and checklists, and add requesters and view-only users, who do not need paid licenses. Connect your ERP or accounting system (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics or QuickBooks) or use Zapier or the API. UpKeep sells implementation help from $500 for training to $5,000 for expanded training if you want guided setup.

tool_faqs.q: How does UpKeep compare to MaintainX and Limble?
tool_faqs.a: All three are mobile-first CMMS tools for in-house maintenance teams. UpKeep publishes Essential ($24) and Premium ($55) per-user prices, with Professional and Enterprise quote-only. Compare each vendor's current pricing page and feature list at your team size, and trial the ones that fit.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between UpKeep's plans?
tool_faqs.a: Essential ($24 per user per month) covers unlimited work orders and locations plus Nova AI. Premium ($55) adds PM scheduling, custom checklists, parts and inventory with costing, and time and labor tracking. Professional adds mobile offline mode, an external request portal, full analytics history and asset lifecycle tracking. Enterprise adds multi-site support, workflow automation, PO management, API and custom integrations, and SSO. Professional and Enterprise are quote-only.

tool_faqs.q: Does UpKeep integrate with SAP or Oracle?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. UpKeep's integrations page names SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, QuickBooks and Zapier, and it offers a public REST API. API and custom integrations are listed as an Enterprise plan feature.

tool_faqs.q: Is UpKeep right for HVAC or plumbing contractors?
tool_faqs.a: Usually not. UpKeep manages maintenance of equipment your organization owns. Contractors who quote, dispatch and invoice customers need field service management software instead.

tool_faqs.q: Does UpKeep have a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Essential and Premium have a free trial with no credit card required, and the pricing page advertises 7 days risk free.

tool_faqs.q: Does UpKeep work offline?
tool_faqs.a: Mobile offline mode is listed as a Professional plan feature, so confirm it is in your quote if your techs work in basements, plant rooms or remote sites.

tools.name: FieldEdge Flat Rate (formerly Coolfront)
tools.tagline: Flat-rate price book and mobile work orders for HVAC, plumbing, and electrical service

pricing.pricing_note: No price is published for new buyers: FieldEdge sells Flat Rate through a demo or a "Request Info" form and its plans page promotes it under "Popular Features" next to add-ons such as MarketingEdge and Proposal Pro, and FieldEdge's own plans are quoted. The standalone Flat Rate Mobile app is billed per work order, not per user: its live login page announces $4.89 per work order effective April 1 (absent from the archived copy of 2026-01-20, present from 2026-04-20, so April 1, 2026). The last published price was $2.09 per work order (coolfront.com, 2021 to 2023), and Coolfront's pricing pages said that fee is added into each database repair price. Verified against fieldedge.com/coolfront, fieldedge.com/pricing, fieldedge.com/flat-rate-pricing-software and secure.coolfront.com/login 2026-09-26.

tools.best_for: HVAC, plumbing, and electrical service shops on FieldEdge, or existing Coolfront users, that want a managed flat-rate price book instead of maintaining their own
tools.weaknesses: Now a FieldEdge product: new buyers are sent to a demo with no published price; the standalone app's per-work-order fee is now more than double its last published price; no published integration with any FSM other than FieldEdge
tools.long_description:
FieldEdge Flat Rate, formerly Coolfront, is a flat-rate price book and mobile work-order tool for service technicians. Coolfront launched in 1999 as a printed flat-rate pricing guide and was acquired in February 2019 by Clearent Software Holdings, the parent of FieldEdge. It is now sold as FieldEdge Flat Rate, and FieldEdge operates in Xplor's Field Services division.

The core is a managed repair database that FieldEdge maintains and updates, so the office is not re-keying price changes. FieldEdge's pages put it at 25,000 to over 30,000 repairs across HVAC, plumbing, and electrical work, with its Coolfront page adding appliance repairs. A technician picks the repair, the price is calculated, and the customer sees the options up front; you can still set your own prices and create custom repairs. FieldEdge says everything Coolfront offered, including its mobile app, is now part of FieldEdge Flat Rate, which works within FieldEdge and syncs with QuickBooks.

No price is published for new buyers. FieldEdge sells Flat Rate through a demo or a "Request Info" form and its plans page promotes it under "Popular Features" next to add-ons such as MarketingEdge and Proposal Pro, and FieldEdge's own plans are quoted; FieldEdge says it does not offer a free trial of FieldEdge. The standalone Flat Rate Mobile app is billed per work order rather than per user: its login page announces $4.89 per work order from April 1, 2026. The last published price was $2.09 (coolfront.com, 2021 to 2023), and FieldEdge calls the app zero-cost because Coolfront's pricing pages said the fee is added into each database repair price, so the customer's payment covers it.

The trade-off is that this is now a FieldEdge product. It covers pricing and work orders, and FieldEdge's answer for scheduling, dispatch, and the rest of the job is its own FSM. Neither FieldEdge's pages nor Coolfront's last own homepage (July 2023) list an integration with another FSM such as ServiceTitan, Jobber, or Housecall Pro; that homepage listed Google Calendar, PartCart, Dropbox, eTouch, and QuickBooks. Shops on another FSM should start with that platform's own price book; FieldEdge customers should ask whether the managed Flat Rate database is part of their quote.

pros_detail.title: Managed, regularly updated price book
pros_detail.explanation: FieldEdge maintains the repair and pricing database and updates it, so the office is not hand-maintaining prices. You can still adjust any price and add custom repairs.

pros_detail.title: Options presented up front
pros_detail.explanation: Techs pick a repair and show the customer pricing and equipment options on the spot. FieldEdge pitches this as less customer pushback and more consistent pricing across techs.

pros_detail.title: Office, trucks, and QuickBooks stay in sync
pros_detail.explanation: FieldEdge says pricing and work-order changes sync instantly across the office, the fleet, and QuickBooks, with cloud work orders visible to the office in real time.

pros_detail.title: No per-user fee on the standalone app
pros_detail.explanation: The standalone app charges per work order rather than per seat, and Coolfront's pricing pages said the fee is added into each database repair price so the customer's payment covers it.

pros_detail.title: Part of FieldEdge
pros_detail.explanation: Clearent Software Holdings, FieldEdge's parent, acquired Coolfront in February 2019. FieldEdge says everything available in Coolfront, including the mobile app, is now part of FieldEdge Flat Rate.

pros_detail.title: 25+ years of pricebook curation
pros_detail.explanation: Coolfront launched in 1999 with a printed flat-rate pricing guide and a parts-and-repair database; FieldEdge's pages now put the database at 25,000 to over 30,000 repairs. New competitors with less curation history can't easily match that breadth.

cons_detail.title: Not a full FSM on its own
cons_detail.explanation: Flat Rate covers pricing and work orders. For scheduling, dispatch, and the rest of the job, FieldEdge's answer is its own FSM.

cons_detail.title: Per-work-order fee is now $4.89
cons_detail.explanation: The standalone app's login page announces $4.89 per work order from April 1, 2026, more than double the last published price of $2.09. Coolfront's pricing pages said the fee is added into each database repair price; confirm that still holds at $4.89 and how it applies to custom repairs.

cons_detail.title: No published price for new buyers
cons_detail.explanation: FieldEdge sells Flat Rate through a demo or a "Request Info" form, and its plans page promotes it under "Popular Features" next to add-ons such as MarketingEdge and Proposal Pro, so you cannot compare cost up front. FieldEdge's pages do not say whether new customers can still buy the standalone app.

cons_detail.title: Few published integrations
cons_detail.explanation: FieldEdge's pages mention QuickBooks sync. Coolfront's last own homepage (July 2023) listed Google Calendar, PartCart, Dropbox, eTouch, and QuickBooks. No integration with another FSM, such as ServiceTitan, Jobber, or Housecall Pro, is listed.

cons_detail.title: Trial terms unclear
cons_detail.explanation: FieldEdge says it does not offer a free trial of FieldEdge. Coolfront's legacy pricing page still offers 25 free work orders (50 elsewhere on the same page), but it also shows the old $2.09 price, so ask what applies before you sign.

tools.implementation_notes: New buyers go through a FieldEdge demo or "Request Info" form, and FieldEdge onboards its customers with its own team rather than offering a free trial of FieldEdge. Existing Coolfront users still sign in at secure.coolfront.com (Flat Rate Mobile) and secure.coolfrontbooks.com (Flat Rate Books). The real adoption work is behavioral: techs have to price from the database and present options on every call, and the office has to settle its own pricing adjustments and custom repairs before go-live. On the standalone app, confirm how the per-work-order fee is recovered, especially on custom repairs, since that is what makes the model cost-neutral.

tool_faqs.q: Is Coolfront a replacement for my FSM?
tool_faqs.a: No. FieldEdge Flat Rate handles flat-rate pricing and work orders. FieldEdge sells it alongside its own FSM and its plans page promotes it under "Popular Features" next to add-ons such as MarketingEdge and Proposal Pro. Neither FieldEdge nor Coolfront's archived site lists an integration with another FSM such as ServiceTitan, Jobber, or Housecall Pro, so if you run another FSM, start with that platform's own price book.

tool_faqs.q: How does Coolfront's pricebook update process work?
tool_faqs.a: FieldEdge maintains the repair database and updates repair and equipment pricing within FieldEdge, so you are not re-keying price changes yourself. Its pages put the database at 25,000 to over 30,000 repairs across HVAC, plumbing, and electrical work, plus appliance repairs. You can still adjust any price and create custom repairs for jobs the database does not cover.

tool_faqs.q: Does Coolfront work with my FSM?
tool_faqs.a: Only with FieldEdge, as far as the vendor publishes. FieldEdge Flat Rate works within FieldEdge and syncs with QuickBooks. Coolfront's last own homepage (July 2023) listed Google Calendar, PartCart, Dropbox, eTouch, and QuickBooks integrations; no FieldEdge or Coolfront page lists ServiceTitan, Successware, Jobber, or Housecall Pro.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Coolfront?
tool_faqs.a: FieldEdge. Clearent Software Holdings, FieldEdge's parent, announced the acquisition of Coolfront Technologies on February 7, 2019, and Coolfront has since been renamed FieldEdge Flat Rate; coolfront.com's homepage now redirects to FieldEdge's Coolfront page. FieldEdge operates in the Field Services division of Xplor, the company Clearent and TSG merged to form in 2021.

tool_faqs.q: How much does FieldEdge Flat Rate cost?
tool_faqs.a: There is no published price for new buyers: FieldEdge sells Flat Rate through a demo or a "Request Info" form, and its own plans are quoted. The standalone Flat Rate Mobile app is billed per work order, not per user: its login page announces $4.89 per work order from April 1, 2026, against a last published price of $2.09. Coolfront's pricing pages said the fee is added into each database repair price so the customer's payment covers it; confirm that still holds before you sign.

tools.name: Otuvy (formerly CleanTelligent)
tools.tagline: Inspection, work order and client reporting software for commercial cleaning companies, formerly CleanTelligent

pricing.pricing_note: Billed annually. QM Inspect $150/month with 5 users included, additional users $25/user/month; QM Pro $250/month with 5 users included, additional users $45/user/month, adds work orders, recurring job scheduling, QR code forms and client portal access; QM Enterprise custom quote. A one-time Otuvy Ignite implementation program is required at sign-up, priced by package and user count and not published. Add-ons: Operational Intelligence Core $99/month or Platinum $249/month; Otuvy Frontline $50/month plus $7/user/month. No trial terms are stated. Verified against otuvy.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Commercial cleaning and facility service contractors that need site inspections, work orders and reports they can share with building clients
tools.weaknesses: A one-time Otuvy Ignite implementation fee is required and not published; plans are billed annually; no third-party integrations are listed on the vendor's site; work orders and the client portal need QM Pro; built for commercial contract cleaning rather than residential booking
tools.long_description:
Otuvy, called CleanTelligent Software until August 2023, makes quality management software for commercial cleaning and facility service companies. The company says it began as a commercial cleaning business and started CleanTelligent in 2003. It is based in Provo, Utah, and its CEO is Caden Hutchens. Otuvy says its software has been used by more than 105,000 service professionals, with more than 19 million inspections and work orders recorded across more than 429,000 service locations.

The main product, Otuvy QM, is built around site inspections. Supervisors run inspections from templates on the web or the mobile app, including offline, and the results feed reports you can share with building clients. QM Pro adds work orders (Otuvy says a work order can be created automatically when an inspection flags a deficiency), scheduling for recurring periodic work, QR code forms that let clients, building occupants or staff send feedback, and a client portal where clients see inspection and work order messages. The help center also covers client surveys, text and email notifications, and managing subcontracted service providers.

Pricing is published and billed annually. QM Inspect is $150 a month with 5 users included and $25 per extra user per month. QM Pro is $250 a month with 5 users and $45 per extra user per month. QM Enterprise is quoted. Add-ons include Operational Intelligence dashboards ($99 or $249 a month) and Otuvy Frontline, a separate task app for frontline staff ($50 a month plus $7 per user per month). Every plan also requires a one-time Otuvy Ignite implementation program, covering training and workflow setup, priced by package and user count and not published.

The trade-off: Otuvy is a specialist tool for proving cleaning quality to commercial clients, not a booking and scheduling system for residential cleaners. The required Ignite fee means the first-year cost is higher than the monthly figures suggest, and we found no third-party integrations such as accounting or payroll listed on its site, so ask how data gets in and out before you sign.

pros_detail.title: Built around inspections
pros_detail.explanation: Inspection templates, unlimited inspections and shareable inspection reports are the core of every plan, which suits contractors who have to show building clients that the work was done.

pros_detail.title: Work orders tied to inspections
pros_detail.explanation: On QM Pro, Otuvy says a flagged deficiency can create a work order automatically, so problems found on an inspection get assigned and tracked.

pros_detail.title: Client-facing tools
pros_detail.explanation: QM Pro adds a client portal for inspection and work order messages and QR code forms for feedback from clients, occupants and staff. The help center also covers client surveys.

pros_detail.title: Published pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Plan prices, included users and per-user fees are on the pricing page ($150 or $250 a month with 5 users), which is uncommon for commercial cleaning software.

pros_detail.title: Long track record
pros_detail.explanation: The product has been sold since 2003 and Otuvy reports more than 105,000 users across more than 429,000 service locations.

cons_detail.title: Required, unpublished implementation fee
cons_detail.explanation: Every plan requires the one-time Otuvy Ignite implementation program, priced by package and user count. Get the full first-year cost in writing.

cons_detail.title: Billed annually
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page lists every plan and add-on as billed annually, so plan for a yearly commitment rather than month to month.

cons_detail.title: No integrations listed
cons_detail.explanation: We found no accounting, payroll or other third-party integrations named on Otuvy's site or help center. The help center covers importing clients, locations, contacts and employees.

cons_detail.title: Key client tools need QM Pro
cons_detail.explanation: Work orders, recurring job scheduling, QR code forms and the client portal are QM Pro features; QM Inspect covers inspections and reports only.

tools.implementation_notes: Otuvy requires its paid Ignite implementation program at sign-up, which covers training and workflow setup, so agree the scope and price before you commit. Gather your client list, service locations, contacts and employees in spreadsheets first, since the help center documents imports for each. Build your client and service provider organization charts, then set up inspection templates and rating scales for each type of site you clean. Configure email and text notification templates, and on QM Pro give client contacts portal access and set up QR code forms or surveys. Train supervisors to run inspections and create work orders in the mobile app, then run a few inspections and share the reports with a friendly client before rolling out to every account.

tool_faqs.q: Is CleanTelligent the same as Otuvy?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. CleanTelligent Software renamed itself Otuvy in August 2023. The CleanTelligent product is now called Otuvy QM, and the company also launched Otuvy Frontline, a task app for frontline staff.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Otuvy cost?
tool_faqs.a: QM Inspect is $150 a month with 5 users ($25 per extra user per month) and QM Pro is $250 a month with 5 users ($45 per extra user per month), both billed annually. QM Enterprise is quoted. A one-time Otuvy Ignite implementation fee is required and not published.

tool_faqs.q: Is Otuvy for residential or commercial cleaning?
tool_faqs.a: Otuvy is built for commercial cleaning and facility service contractors: inspections, work orders and reports for building clients. Residential maid services usually need booking-focused software such as ZenMaid or Automaid instead.

tool_faqs.q: Does Otuvy integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: We found no QuickBooks or other third-party integration named on Otuvy's website, pricing page or help center. The help center documents spreadsheet imports for clients, locations, contacts and employees. Ask Otuvy directly if you need an integration.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The Otuvy QM mobile app lets supervisors perform inspections, create work orders, view reports and manage notifications, and the pricing page lists offline inspections. Otuvy Frontline is a separate paid add-on for frontline staff tasks.

tools.name: MaintainX
tools.tagline: Modern mobile-first CMMS and work order management

pricing.pricing_note: Basic plan free forever (unlimited work orders; limited to 2 work orders with attached procedures and 2 active repeating work orders); Essential $20/user/mo billed annually ($25 monthly); Premium $65/user/mo billed annually ($75 monthly); Enterprise custom-quoted. Acquired by Autodesk (closed 2026-08-03); still sold under the MaintainX brand. Verified against getmaintainx.com/pricing 2026-09-10.

tools.best_for: Internal maintenance teams (5-500) wanting modern mobile-first CMMS
tools.weaknesses: Focus on internal maintenance not customer-facing service; not designed as a customer-billing FSM
tools.long_description:
MaintainX is a cloud CMMS (computerized maintenance management system) and work-order platform for internal maintenance teams, founded in 2018 in San Francisco. Autodesk completed its acquisition of MaintainX in August 2026, and it is still sold under the MaintainX brand.

It is built mobile-first: offline-capable apps for techs in basements and on rooftops, QR codes on assets for instant work-order lookup, procedure and checklist templates, and messaging. The Basic plan is free with unlimited non-recurring work orders and a limited number of templates; Essential is $20 per user per month billed annually ($25 monthly), Premium $65 ($75 monthly), and Enterprise is custom-quoted, with a 30-day free trial of paid plans.

Integrations include SAP, Oracle and Microsoft Dynamics ERPs, QuickBooks, Slack, Power BI, Samsara and Zapier.

The trade-off: MaintainX is internal maintenance, not customer-facing field service. HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors visiting customer sites need an FSM platform (ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro), not a CMMS. MaintainX is for the facility maintenance team at the building, not the contractor servicing it.

pros_detail.title: Mobile-first, offline-capable
pros_detail.explanation: The mobile app works offline for techs in basements, rooftops and other low-signal locations, and syncs when they reconnect.

pros_detail.title: Free plan
pros_detail.explanation: The Basic plan is free with no time limit and unlimited non-recurring work orders, a low-risk way to start before moving to a paid plan.

pros_detail.title: QR code asset scanning
pros_detail.explanation: Print QR codes on equipment; techs scan to instantly load work order history, manuals, and parts lists. Critical for operations with hundreds of pieces of equipment across multiple buildings.

pros_detail.title: 30-day free trial
pros_detail.explanation: Paid plans can be trialed for 30 days, long enough for a monthly preventive maintenance cycle to run.

pros_detail.title: ERP and chat integrations
pros_detail.explanation: SAP, Oracle and Microsoft Dynamics ERP integrations, plus Slack, Power BI, Samsara and QuickBooks, so work orders reach the systems and chat tools the team already uses.

cons_detail.title: Internal maintenance only, not customer-facing FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Not designed to bill customers. HVAC, plumbing, electrical contractors need ServiceTitan, Jobber, or Housecall Pro for customer-billing workflows. Confusion between CMMS and FSM is the most common buyer mistake in this space.

cons_detail.title: Free plan has real limits
cons_detail.explanation: Basic limits templates, procedures and recurring work, and lacks the automation and reporting of paid plans; most real operations need at least Essential ($20/user/month billed annually).

cons_detail.title: Enterprise pricing is quoted
cons_detail.explanation: Large operations on Enterprise get a custom quote, so compare it against Limble and UpKeep quotes at the same scale.

cons_detail.title: Newer than legacy CMMS
cons_detail.explanation: 2018 founding versus Maximo's 1990s/2000s history. Feature depth in edge cases (complex parts hierarchies, multi-site enterprise reporting) less mature than legacy enterprise CMMS.

cons_detail.title: Limble is a direct competitor with similar features
cons_detail.explanation: Both are modern cloud CMMS platforms, so evaluate them side by side rather than picking either by default; implementation and pricing differ.

tools.implementation_notes: Deployment usually takes a few weeks. Set up locations and assets (manually or by CSV), create work order templates, print QR codes for key assets, and schedule preventive maintenance. Roll the mobile app out to techs, then add reporting, parts inventory and integrations (ERP, QuickBooks, Slack). Moving from paper or spreadsheets is mostly a fresh start; moving from a legacy CMMS usually means rebuilding the asset library, so plan a period of running both systems.

tool_faqs.q: What's the difference between CMMS and FSM software?
tool_faqs.a: CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) is for INTERNAL maintenance teams, such as the facility manager at a hospital, school, or office building managing their building's equipment. FSM (Field Service Management) is for CONTRACTORS visiting customer sites, such as the HVAC company servicing that hospital. MaintainX is CMMS. ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro are FSM. They're different software for different jobs and the buyers are different people.

tool_faqs.q: How does MaintainX compare to UpKeep and Limble CMMS?
tool_faqs.a: All three are modern cloud CMMS competitors. MaintainX publishes per-user prices (Essential $20, Premium $65 per user per month billed annually) and has a free Basic plan; UpKeep publishes per-user prices (Essential $24); Limble quotes through a price calculator. For a 30-tech team, MaintainX's list prices come to about $600/month (Essential) or $1,950/month (Premium) billed annually and UpKeep's to about $720 (Essential), so get quotes from all three at your usage.

tool_faqs.q: Is MaintainX's free tier actually usable?
tool_faqs.a: Yes for very small operations. The Basic plan has no time limit and includes unlimited non-recurring work orders, unlimited assets and team messaging, but only a limited number of templates, checklists and procedures, and recurring work is limited.
