Growing teams usually move to Essential ($20/user/month billed annually) for automation and reporting.

tool_faqs.q: Does MaintainX integrate with SAP or Oracle?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. MaintainX integrates with SAP (B1, ECC and S/4HANA), Oracle and Microsoft Dynamics ERPs, as well as QuickBooks, Slack, Power BI and Samsara, and connects to other apps through Zapier or its API.

tool_faqs.q: When should I choose MaintainX over a full FSM platform?
tool_faqs.a: Choose CMMS over FSM when: (1) you're an internal maintenance team at a building/facility, not a contractor billing customers; (2) you're tracking work orders for equipment you own, not services rendered to customers; (3) you don't need quote-to-invoice workflows; (4) you're paying technicians, not invoicing customers. If you don't fit those criteria, you probably want FSM (ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro) instead.

tools.name: FieldAware
tools.tagline: Field service management software for equipment service organizations, owned by GPS Insight

pricing.pricing_note: FieldAware does not publish prices or a free trial on fieldaware.com; pricing is by quote after a demo. Verified against fieldaware.com (home, tour and extensions pages) 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Mid-size and larger organizations that install, service and maintain equipment (building services, facilities, industrial and commercial equipment, medtech, oil and gas) and want work orders, asset history and scheduling on mobile
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing or trial; few named integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, CentralBOS) beyond its open API; aimed at equipment service rather than residential trades
tools.long_description:
FieldAware is cloud field service management software. FieldAware says it was founded in 2011, and since December 2021 it has been owned by GPS Insight, a fleet tracking company based in Scottsdale, Arizona. The product is now sold as FieldAware by GPS Insight, with sales contacts for the US, Canada, the UK and Australia/APAC.

FieldAware targets organizations that service equipment: building and construction services, facility and property management, industrial and commercial equipment, health sciences and medtech, and oil and gas. In the office it handles work orders, scheduling and dispatch, route and schedule optimization, asset management, invoicing, reporting and a customer portal. In the field, the mobile app offers mobile forms, a knowledge base, alerts, time tracking and offline work. Asset records support preventive maintenance scheduling and service contract compliance, with service history that stays with the equipment.

FieldAware's website does not list prices or a free trial; you request a demo and a quote.

Named integrations are a NetSuite connector, a QuickBooks connector and a CentralBOS integration. Beyond those, FieldAware offers an open API with published documentation and works with implementation and solution partners.

The trade-off: FieldAware is aimed at equipment-focused service organizations rather than small residential trade shops, and its public integration list is short. If you rely on Xero, Sage or Salesforce, ask how FieldAware would connect through its API or a partner before you commit. Because it is now part of GPS Insight, also ask about the product roadmap and how it works alongside GPS Insight's fleet tracking.

pros_detail.title: Built for equipment service
pros_detail.explanation: Asset records keep service history with the equipment, support preventive maintenance scheduling and help track service contract compliance.

pros_detail.title: Route and schedule optimization
pros_detail.explanation: Scheduling and dispatch include route and schedule optimization for field teams.

pros_detail.title: Capable mobile app
pros_detail.explanation: Technicians get mobile forms, a knowledge base, alerts, time tracking and offline capability.

pros_detail.title: NetSuite and QuickBooks connectors
pros_detail.explanation: FieldAware offers a NetSuite connector for companies running NetSuite and a QuickBooks connector for smaller accounting setups.

pros_detail.title: Open API
pros_detail.explanation: An open API lets you build integrations with other systems, with documentation published online.

pros_detail.title: Backed by GPS Insight
pros_detail.explanation: Owned by GPS Insight since 2021, which also sells fleet tracking, dash cams and ELD compliance tools.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: FieldAware does not list prices, so you need a sales conversation to compare costs.

cons_detail.title: Short integration list
cons_detail.explanation: Only NetSuite, QuickBooks and CentralBOS are named; other systems need the API or a partner.

cons_detail.title: Not aimed at small residential trades
cons_detail.explanation: Its industries are equipment service, facilities, medtech and oil and gas, so a small plumbing or HVAC shop may find simpler tools a better fit.

cons_detail.title: No self-serve trial listed
cons_detail.explanation: The website offers demos and a platform tour, but no free trial is listed.

cons_detail.title: Ownership change
cons_detail.explanation: FieldAware is now a GPS Insight product, so confirm roadmap and support arrangements during evaluation.

tools.implementation_notes: Request a demo and a written quote that covers user counts, integrations and implementation services. Before rollout, gather your customer and site list, the equipment you service (serial numbers, install dates, service history) and any service contract terms, so asset records and preventive maintenance schedules can be loaded. Decide how FieldAware will connect to your accounting system (the NetSuite or QuickBooks connector, or the open API) and test that work orders and invoices flow through. Build mobile forms for your inspections, set up scheduling rules and routes, train dispatchers first, then roll out the mobile app to technicians and check that offline work syncs.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns FieldAware?
tool_faqs.a: GPS Insight, a fleet tracking company based in Scottsdale, Arizona, acquired FieldAware in December 2021. The product is now marketed as FieldAware by GPS Insight.

tool_faqs.q: What does FieldAware cost?
tool_faqs.a: FieldAware does not publish prices. Request a demo and a written quote that includes users, integrations and implementation.

tool_faqs.q: Does FieldAware integrate with NetSuite and QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. FieldAware offers a NetSuite connector and a QuickBooks connector, plus a CentralBOS integration and an open API for other systems.

tool_faqs.q: What kinds of businesses use FieldAware?
tool_faqs.a: FieldAware lists building and construction services, facility and property management, industrial equipment, commercial equipment, health sciences and medtech, and oil and gas.

tool_faqs.q: Does the mobile app work offline?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. FieldAware lists offline capability for its mobile app, alongside mobile forms, knowledge management, alerts and time tracking.

tools.name: Limble CMMS
tools.tagline: Modern mobile-first CMMS for maintenance teams

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote via Limble price calculator; pricing page lists Standard, Premium+, and Enterprise tiers with no published dollar amounts and no free tier.

tools.best_for: Internal maintenance teams (5-200) that want a modern, mobile CMMS with ERP integrations
tools.weaknesses: Built for internal maintenance, not customer-facing service; no published prices or free plan
tools.long_description:
Limble is a cloud CMMS (computerized maintenance management system) for internal maintenance teams, founded in 2015 in Lehi, Utah. In June 2023 it raised a $58 million Series B led by Goldman Sachs Asset Management at a $450 million valuation, and it says thousands of customers use it across manufacturing, facilities and other asset-heavy operations.

It covers work orders, preventive maintenance, asset hierarchies, parts inventory, vendor management, purchase orders, mobile apps and reporting. Limble no longer publishes dollar prices or a free tier: its pricing page lists Standard, Premium+ and Enterprise plans priced through a calculator or sales. Integrations include SAP S/4HANA, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, QuickBooks Online, Slack, calendars and Zapier, plus a REST API.

The trade-off: Limble is for internal maintenance, not customer-facing field service. HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors visiting customer sites need an FSM platform (ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro), not a CMMS. Limble is for the facility maintenance team at the building, not the contractor servicing it.

pros_detail.title: Full CMMS feature set
pros_detail.explanation: Work orders, preventive maintenance, asset hierarchies, parts inventory, vendor management and purchase orders in one mobile-first system.

pros_detail.title: Free trial on paid plans
pros_detail.explanation: A free trial lets a preventive maintenance cycle run before you commit; confirm the current trial length with Limble.

pros_detail.title: ERP integrations
pros_detail.explanation: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle NetSuite and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central integrations, plus QuickBooks Online, suit larger maintenance operations tied to an ERP.

pros_detail.title: Vendor management + purchase orders built in
pros_detail.explanation: Vendor tracking with service history, automated purchase orders for parts replenishment. Important for operations with significant parts spend or third-party vendor management responsibilities.

cons_detail.title: Internal maintenance only, not customer-facing FSM
cons_detail.explanation: Not designed to bill customers. HVAC, plumbing, electrical contractors need ServiceTitan, Jobber, or Housecall Pro for customer-billing workflows. CMMS vs FSM confusion is the most common buyer mistake; read the glossary entry before deciding.

cons_detail.title: No published prices or free plan
cons_detail.explanation: Standard, Premium+ and Enterprise are all priced through a calculator or sales, so get a quote at your team size and compare it with MaintainX's and UpKeep's published per-user prices.

cons_detail.title: Younger than legacy enterprise CMMS
cons_detail.explanation: Founded in 2015, Limble is newer than legacy enterprise CMMS such as Maximo. Check depth in specialized areas (complex multi-site parts hierarchies, regulated-industry compliance reporting) during the trial.

tools.implementation_notes: Deployment usually takes a few weeks, depending on how many assets and locations you have. Set up the location and asset hierarchy (manually or by CSV), build work order templates and preventive maintenance schedules, generate QR codes if you scan assets, then roll the mobile app out to technicians. Add reporting, parts inventory and your ERP or QuickBooks integration once the basics run. Moving from paper or spreadsheets is mostly a fresh start; moving from a legacy CMMS usually means rebuilding the asset library, so plan a period of running both systems.

tool_faqs.q: How does Limble compare to MaintainX and UpKeep?
tool_faqs.a: All three are modern cloud CMMS with similar core features. Limble quotes through a price calculator and publishes no prices; MaintainX Essential is $20 per user per month billed annually and UpKeep Essential $24 per user per month. MaintainX has a free Basic plan; Limble and UpKeep do not. Because Limble does not publish rates, get quotes at your team size and compare them feature by feature.

tool_faqs.q: Does Limble have a free tier?
tool_faqs.a: No longer. Limble's pricing page lists Standard, Premium+ and Enterprise plans with no free tier and no published dollar amounts; pricing comes from its price calculator or sales team.

tool_faqs.q: Does Limble integrate with SAP or Oracle?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Limble integrates with SAP S/4HANA, Oracle NetSuite and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, as well as QuickBooks Online, and offers a REST API and Zapier for other systems.

tool_faqs.q: When should I choose Limble over a full FSM platform?
tool_faqs.a: Choose CMMS over FSM when: (1) you're an internal maintenance team at a building/facility, not a contractor billing customers; (2) you're tracking work orders for equipment you own, not services rendered to customers; (3) you don't need quote-to-invoice workflows; (4) you pay technicians on payroll, you don't invoice customers. If you don't fit those criteria, you probably want FSM (Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan) instead. See the glossary for the full CMMS vs FSM distinction.

tool_faqs.q: What are Limble's plans?
tool_faqs.a: Limble's pricing page lists Standard, Premium+ and Enterprise plans without published dollar amounts; you get a price from its calculator or sales team. Compare the feature lists on the pricing page to see what Premium+ and Enterprise add.

tools.name: Praxedo
tools.tagline: Field service management software for mid-size and large service organizations in Europe and the Americas

pricing.pricing_note: Per user per month in USD: Basic $39, Advanced $69, Optimized $99, Automated $149; Large Enterprises custom-quoted. Minimum 5 users. Listed rates exclude one-time implementation and setup fees. Billing term (monthly or annual) is not stated, and no free trial is listed. Add-ons: Customer Portal, Appointment Portal (priced by appointments managed) and Video-Assistance (priced by number of experts). Verified against praxedo.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Service organizations with 5 to 500+ technicians (telecoms, energy and utilities, HVAC and refrigeration, plumbing, maintenance) that need scheduling, a mobile app and ERP or CRM connectors
tools.weaknesses: 5-user minimum and one-time implementation fees; customer portal, appointment portal and video assistance are add-ons; no free trial listed
tools.long_description:
Praxedo is cloud field service management software from France. Praxedo says it was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Paris, with a US office in Chicago, a Canadian office in Montreal and operations in Spain, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, the UK, Mexico and Chile. It says more than 1,500 customers across 50+ industries use it, with 65,000 daily users and 150,000 jobs processed a day, for organizations with 5 to 500+ technicians.

The core product covers work order management, scheduling and dispatch, technician tracking, a mobile app for Android, iOS and Windows that works offline, digital reports with photos, dashboards and analytics. Higher plans add criteria-based appointment booking, AI-assisted scheduling and automated quality control, and the top published plan adds real-time AI scheduling and premium support. Add-ons include a Customer Portal, an Appointment Portal (priced by the number of appointments) and Video-Assistance (priced by the number of experts). Praxedo says it is ISO 27001 certified.

Pricing is published in US dollars per user per month: Basic $39, Advanced $69, Optimized $99 and Automated $149, with custom plans for large enterprises. Plans need a minimum of 5 users, and the listed rates exclude one-time implementation and setup fees. The pricing page does not say whether prices are billed monthly or annually, and it does not list a free trial.

Praxedo lists connectors for Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365 (including a Business Central connector), Oracle NetSuite, SAP, Sage X3 and QuickBooks, plus REST APIs and web services for custom integrations.

The trade-off: Praxedo is priced and set up for teams, not solo trades. With a 5-user minimum, implementation fees on top and portals sold as add-ons, a small US shop will usually find simpler tools cheaper; a multi-country or ERP-connected service organization is the buyer it is built for.

pros_detail.title: Published per-user pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Four plans from $39 to $149 per user per month are listed on the website, so you can budget before a sales call.

pros_detail.title: AI scheduling options
pros_detail.explanation: Optimized adds AI-assisted scheduling and Automated adds real-time AI scheduling for larger dispatch teams.

pros_detail.title: ERP and CRM connectors
pros_detail.explanation: Connectors cover Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Oracle NetSuite, SAP, Sage X3 and QuickBooks, with REST APIs for anything else.

pros_detail.title: Offline mobile app on several platforms
pros_detail.explanation: Technicians can use Android, iOS or Windows devices and keep working without a connection.

pros_detail.title: International presence
pros_detail.explanation: Praxedo operates in France, Spain, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, the UK, the US, Canada, Mexico and Chile, which helps multi-country service organizations.

pros_detail.title: Established vendor
pros_detail.explanation: Founded in 2005, Praxedo says it serves more than 1,500 customers with 65,000 daily users.

cons_detail.title: 5-user minimum
cons_detail.explanation: Plans require at least 5 users, so the smallest bill is $195 a month on Basic before implementation fees.

cons_detail.title: Implementation fees on top
cons_detail.explanation: Listed rates exclude one-time implementation and setup fees, and those fees are not published.

cons_detail.title: Portals and video assistance cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: The Customer Portal, Appointment Portal and Video-Assistance are add-ons with their own pricing.

cons_detail.title: No free trial listed
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page does not list a free trial; evaluation is through a demo.

cons_detail.title: Built for larger teams
cons_detail.explanation: Praxedo focuses on organizations with 5 to 500+ technicians in sectors like telecoms and utilities, so a small residential trade business may find it more than it needs.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and ask for a written quote that covers your plan, user count (5 minimum), add-ons and the one-time implementation and setup fees. Before rollout, prepare your customer and site data, work order types, technician skills and schedules, and decide which system is the source of truth for customers and invoices (Salesforce, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, SAP, Sage X3 or QuickBooks). Configure the connector or API integration and test that work orders and reports flow both ways. Set up report templates for technicians, train dispatchers on scheduling, then roll out the mobile app and confirm offline sync on the devices your team uses.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Praxedo cost?
tool_faqs.a: Praxedo publishes US prices per user per month: Basic $39, Advanced $69, Optimized $99 and Automated $149, with custom plans for large enterprises. There is a 5-user minimum, and one-time implementation and setup fees are extra.

tool_faqs.q: Is Praxedo suitable for US-based service operations?
tool_faqs.a: Praxedo sells in the US from its Chicago office and publishes US dollar pricing. It suits US service organizations with at least 5 field users that want scheduling, a mobile app and connectors to systems like Salesforce, Dynamics 365, NetSuite or QuickBooks.

tool_faqs.q: Does Praxedo integrate with SAP?
tool_faqs.a: Praxedo lists SAP among its ERP connectors, alongside Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Oracle NetSuite, Sage X3 and QuickBooks. It also offers REST APIs and web services.

tool_faqs.q: Does Praxedo have a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: The pricing page does not list one. Praxedo sells through demos, and implementation is priced separately.

tool_faqs.q: Where is Praxedo based?
tool_faqs.a: Praxedo is headquartered in Paris, France, with a US office in Chicago and a Canadian office in Montreal. It says it was founded in 2005.

tools.name: MeasureSquare
tools.tagline: Flooring takeoff and estimating software for desktop and mobile, with an add-on CRM for contractors

pricing.pricing_note: Per user, per product. Tier prices are month-to-month rates; annual prices are Mobile Retail $540/yr, Mobile Multi-family $870/yr, MeasureSquare 8 Retail $540/yr, Multi-family $1,640/yr, Commercial $1,970/yr, CRM Sales Essential $690/yr (Contractor Pro $990/yr or $99/mo, Contractor Complete $1,490/yr or $149/mo). Stone Commercial $1,290/yr ($129/mo), Stone & Tile Commercial $1,790/yr ($179/mo). Bundles: Mobile Retail + Desktop Multi-Family $1,970/yr ($197/mo), Mobile Retail + Desktop Commercial $2,190/yr ($219/mo). Starting price is $540/yr divided by 12. MeasureSquare 8 and Stone & Tile are Windows only; Mobile is iOS and Android. No contract or setup fee. Optional Onboarding Starter Kit $400; Pasadena class $199 per person per day. 14-day free trial, no card. Verified against measuresquare.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Flooring, tile and stone estimators who need accurate takeoffs, roll layouts and seam diagrams, measured on site with a laser meter or taken off from plans on a Windows PC
tools.weaknesses: Each product is priced separately per user, so a shop that wants mobile measuring, desktop takeoff and the CRM pays for each; the desktop edition is Windows only; it is not a store system (no point of sale or inventory), and its QuickBooks Online link is labeled beta on the integrations page
tools.long_description:
MeasureSquare is takeoff and estimating software for flooring, tile, stone and countertop businesses. Measure Square Corp. was founded in 2001 and is based in Pasadena, California, and says more than 4,500 businesses use its software. Its core job is working out how much material a job needs: estimators draw or import a floor plan, the software lays out cuts on the roll with seam optimization, handles pattern matching and waste, and produces cut sheets, seam diagrams and a quote.

The product line has several parts. MeasureSquare Mobile (iOS and Android) is for measuring and quoting on site and pairs with Bluetooth laser meters from Leica, DeWALT, Moasure, Stabila, Hilti and others. MeasureSquare 8 is the Windows desktop program for plan-based takeoffs in Retail, Multi-family and Commercial editions. Stone & Tile covers cut-to-size stone and tile work, and MeasureSquare CRM is a web app that tracks leads, quotes, purchase orders, work orders, invoices, install schedules and, on the top plan, change orders and job costing. MeasureSquare also advertises AI takeoff tools and a free LiDAR room scanner app.

Pricing is published and per user. Mobile Retail and MeasureSquare 8 Retail are each $540 a year or $54 a month; Mobile Multi-family is $870 a year ($87 monthly); MeasureSquare 8 Multi-family is $1,640 a year ($164 monthly) and Commercial $1,970 a year ($197 monthly). The CRM runs $690 to $1,490 a year per user ($69 to $149 monthly), and bundles pair Mobile Retail with a desktop edition from $1,970 a year. There is no contract or setup fee, and a 14-day free trial needs no credit card.

MeasureSquare connects to flooring business systems rather than replacing them. Its integrations page lists QFloors and RollMaster (through the MeasureSquare Cloud API), Comp-U-Floor, ServiceTitan and others, and the CRM syncs with QuickBooks Online and Xero and takes payments through Stripe.

The trade-off: MeasureSquare is built around measuring and estimating. It does not run a showroom's point of sale or inventory, so dealers usually pair it with a flooring ERP, and a shop that wants mobile, desktop and CRM pays for each product per user.

pros_detail.title: Built for flooring takeoff
pros_detail.explanation: Roll layout with seam optimization, pattern matching, waste control and a tile pattern library handle the calculations that decide how much material a flooring job needs.

pros_detail.title: Measure on site with a laser meter
pros_detail.explanation: The Mobile app for iOS and Android pairs with Bluetooth laser meters from Leica, DeWALT, Moasure, Stabila, Hilti and others, so estimators can draw the room and quote while on site.

pros_detail.title: Published, per-user prices
pros_detail.explanation: Every product has a listed price, from $540 a year ($54 monthly) for Mobile Retail or MeasureSquare 8 Retail, with no contract or setup fee.

pros_detail.title: Connects to flooring business systems
pros_detail.explanation: MeasureSquare lists integrations with QFloors, RollMaster, Comp-U-Floor and ServiceTitan, and its CRM syncs with QuickBooks Online and Xero.

pros_detail.title: Free trial without a card
pros_detail.explanation: A 14-day trial is fully functional and does not ask for a credit card, and free Udemy courses and tutorials cover the basics.

cons_detail.title: Each product is priced separately
cons_detail.explanation: Mobile, MeasureSquare 8, Stone & Tile and the CRM are separate per-user subscriptions. Bundles help, but a shop that wants all of them pays for each seat on each product.

cons_detail.title: Desktop edition is Windows only
cons_detail.explanation: MeasureSquare 8 and Stone & Tile run only on Windows, so Mac-based offices need a Windows machine for plan-based takeoffs.

cons_detail.title: Not a store system
cons_detail.explanation: There is no point of sale or inventory. Dealers still need a flooring ERP or accounting system, which MeasureSquare connects to rather than replaces.

cons_detail.title: Some features sit on higher CRM plans
cons_detail.explanation: Install scheduling starts on Contractor Pro ($990 a year per user) and change orders and job costing need Contractor Complete ($1,490 a year per user).

cons_detail.title: Hands-on training costs extra
cons_detail.explanation: Free courses are available, but the Onboarding Starter Kit is $400 and in-person classes in Pasadena are $199 per person per day.

tools.implementation_notes: Start by choosing products: Mobile for on-site measuring, MeasureSquare 8 (Windows) for plan-based takeoffs in the Retail, Multi-family or Commercial edition, Stone & Tile for stone work, and the CRM if you want lead, order and install tracking. Run the 14-day trial on a real job before buying. Load your product catalog, labor rates and waste settings so estimates match how you price, and pair any Bluetooth laser meters your estimators use with the Mobile app. If you run QFloors, RollMaster, Comp-U-Floor or ServiceTitan, set up the integration so estimates and diagrams flow into that system; CRM users can connect QuickBooks Online or Xero. Use the free Udemy courses first, and buy the $400 Onboarding Starter Kit if you want guided sessions.

tool_faqs.q: How much does MeasureSquare cost?
tool_faqs.a: Prices are per user. Mobile Retail and MeasureSquare 8 Retail are $540 a year or $54 a month each; Mobile Multi-family is $870 a year ($87 monthly); MeasureSquare 8 Multi-family is $1,640 a year ($164 monthly) and Commercial $1,970 a year ($197 monthly). The CRM is $690 to $1,490 a year per user, and bundles start at $1,970 a year. There is no contract or setup fee.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. MeasureSquare offers a fully functional 14-day free trial with no credit card required.

tool_faqs.q: Does MeasureSquare run on a Mac or iPad?
tool_faqs.a: The Mobile app runs on iOS and Android, including iPads. The desktop MeasureSquare 8 and Stone & Tile programs are Windows only. The CRM is web-based.

tool_faqs.q: Does it work with my flooring ERP?
tool_faqs.a: MeasureSquare's integrations page lists QFloors and RollMaster (through the MeasureSquare Cloud API), Comp-U-Floor, C/F Data Systems STRUCTURE (file import), Carman and JobRunner, plus ServiceTitan. Check the exact data that moves for your system before buying.

tool_faqs.q: Does it connect to QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: The MeasureSquare CRM syncs with QuickBooks Online and Xero. The integrations page labels the QuickBooks Online link as beta, so test it during the trial.

tool_faqs.q: Is MeasureSquare a full flooring business system?
tool_faqs.a: No. It handles measuring, takeoff, estimating and, through the CRM, job tracking. It has no point of sale or inventory, so most dealers pair it with a flooring ERP such as QFloors, RollMaster or RFMS.

tools.name: RFMS
tools.tagline: Flooring ERP from Cyncly for dealers, builders and commercial contractors: orders, inventory, scheduling and accounting in one system

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing. Cyncly sells RFMS in Core, Professional and Enterprise packages (per its 2024 package sheet), quoted by package and named users for CRM and mobile apps; hosting included, dedicated hosting on Enterprise. No trial published. Verified against cyncly.com/products/rfms-core and rfms.com package sheet 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Flooring dealers, builder and multi-family contractors, and commercial flooring firms that want one ERP for order entry, inventory, scheduling, accounting and HR
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing, so every evaluation starts with a sales call; key tools such as CRM, mobile apps, batch job costing and business intelligence sit on the higher Professional and Enterprise packages; and Cyncly is moving the product to a new cloud platform, so ask what version you would be buying
tools.long_description:
RFMS is business management (ERP) software for the flooring industry, now sold by Cyncly as RFMS ERP. Cyncly, then called Compusoft + 2020, acquired RFMS in 2022, and it now sits in Cyncly Flooring alongside Broadlume, RollMaster and Pacific Solutions. The RFMS team is based in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, and Cyncly describes it as having more than 35 years of experience serving flooring businesses.

RFMS serves residential dealers and installers, builder and multi-family flooring contractors, commercial flooring firms and flooring manufacturers. Cyncly's 2024 package sheet lists three subscriptions. RFMS Core covers order entry, products, inventory, sales reports, BidPro estimating, Schedule Pro scheduling, accounting and human resources on a hosted server. Professional adds B2B e-commerce, contract pricing, batch job costing, direct deposit, business intelligence reports, a CRM and the RFMS Mobile and Measure Mobile apps for named users. Enterprise adds project management, mobile work orders, enterprise reporting, multi-database access, a dedicated hosted service and a fuller API.

Cyncly does not publish RFMS prices; packages are quoted. Prebuilt integrations include Paperless, HeyPros and Zapier, and leads from Broadlume websites can flow directly into RFMS. Related Cyncly products include JobRunner for bids and projects and Measure Desktop for takeoffs.

The platform is in transition. Cyncly launched RFMS Next in 2023 to deliver a web-based sales, purchasing, inventory, payroll and accounting system, and at its 2025 user conference it announced Project Summit, a cloud-based, AI-supported architecture described as the next step for RFMS Next. Cyncly told users it continues to support the existing solutions.

The trade-off: RFMS covers the whole flooring operation, including accounting and HR, but pricing is quote only, many tools sit on the upper packages, and buyers should confirm which platform version they are signing up for.

pros_detail.title: One system for the whole operation
pros_detail.explanation: Order entry, products, inventory, estimating (BidPro), scheduling (Schedule Pro), accounting and human resources are all in the Core package.

pros_detail.title: Built for several flooring markets
pros_detail.explanation: Cyncly aims RFMS at residential dealers and installers, builder and multi-family contractors, commercial flooring firms and manufacturers.

pros_detail.title: Packages that scale up
pros_detail.explanation: Professional and Enterprise add B2B e-commerce, contract pricing, batch job costing, CRM, mobile apps, project management and business intelligence as a business grows.

pros_detail.title: Part of a larger flooring software group
pros_detail.explanation: Cyncly also owns Broadlume websites, RollMaster and Pacific Solutions' JobRunner, and Broadlume website leads can flow straight into RFMS.

pros_detail.title: Training and success plans
pros_detail.explanation: Cyncly offers an RFMS Academy, Customer Success Plans and virtual services for onboarding and ongoing help.

cons_detail.title: No public pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Cyncly does not publish RFMS prices, so budgeting and comparison shopping start with a sales call and a custom quote.

cons_detail.title: Many tools are on higher packages
cons_detail.explanation: CRM, the mobile apps, batch job costing and BI start at Professional, and mobile work orders and project management need Enterprise.

cons_detail.title: Platform in transition
cons_detail.explanation: Cyncly is moving RFMS toward RFMS Next and Project Summit. Ask which version you would run and what the migration path looks like.

cons_detail.title: A full ERP rollout
cons_detail.explanation: Because RFMS replaces your accounting and HR as well as sales tools, switching involves migrating data and training every role, not just installing an app.

tools.implementation_notes: Contact Cyncly sales for a demo and a written quote that names the package (Core, Professional or Enterprise), the number of named users for CRM and mobile apps, hosting, and any Customer Success Plan. Ask whether you would start on the current RFMS or the newer RFMS Next platform. Before migration, clean up your product catalog, inventory counts, customer list and open orders. Train by role (sales and order entry, warehouse, scheduling, accounting and payroll) using the RFMS Academy. If you use a Broadlume website, set up the lead integration so web leads land in RFMS.

tool_faqs.q: How much does RFMS cost?
tool_faqs.a: Cyncly does not publish RFMS pricing. It sells Core, Professional and Enterprise packages by quote, so ask for a written quote listing the package, named users, hosting and support plan.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns RFMS?
tool_faqs.a: Cyncly. It acquired RFMS in 2022 under its earlier name, Compusoft + 2020, and RFMS is now part of Cyncly Flooring with Broadlume, RollMaster and Pacific Solutions.

tool_faqs.q: What is in RFMS Core?
tool_faqs.a: Cyncly's 2024 package sheet lists order entry, products, inventory, sales reports, BidPro, Schedule Pro, accounting, human resources and a hosted server. CRM and the mobile apps start on the Professional package.

tool_faqs.q: Is RFMS cloud-based?
tool_faqs.a: RFMS packages include a hosted server, and Cyncly is building RFMS Next and Project Summit as a web-based, cloud platform. Ask sales which version a new customer starts on.

tool_faqs.q: Does RFMS integrate with other tools?
tool_faqs.a: Cyncly lists prebuilt integrations such as Paperless, HeyPros and Zapier, and API access that grows with the package. Broadlume websites can send leads directly into RFMS.

tools.name: QFloors
tools.tagline: Cloud business management software for flooring dealers, from sales and inventory to job costing and accounting

pricing.pricing_note: QFloors starts at $89 per user per month, depending on the number of users and features; a one-time setup fee applies and may be waived for annual subscriptions; no maintenance fees. Enterprise (25+ users) price not published. Add-ons from: QTagger $3,000/yr; Installer View, Account View, QOrders and QLeads $1,200/yr each (QLeads free with Roomvo CRM or site); QSched $1,850 per site license; File & Document Manager $650 per site license. QFloors + Roomvo bundles offered, prices not published. No free trial published. Verified against qfloors.com/faq and qfloors.com/add-on-products 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Flooring stores that want one cloud system for sales, inventory, purchasing, job costing and full accounting in place of QuickBooks
tools.weaknesses: Only the $89 per user per month starting price is published, and a setup fee applies; scheduling, installer and customer portals, lead capture and showroom tags are paid add-ons; it is cloud only, with no on-premise option
tools.long_description:
QFloors is business management software for floor covering dealers. It was launched in 1999 by Chad and Trent Ogden, whose family ran carpet stores, and is based in South Jordan, Utah. In January 2025 it was bought by Leap Tools, Inc., which does business as Roomvo, the Toronto-based room visualization company. The Ogden family continues to lead QFloors, and QFloors says more than a thousand businesses use it.

The software covers the store's core operations: leads, customer invoicing, estimating, purchasing, inventory, vendor invoicing, job costing, a checkbook and full accounting, with reporting across all of it. QFloors says over 90% of its customers use it for their complete accounting, so it is sold as a replacement for QuickBooks rather than an add-on to it. It is cloud only, with mobile app options. An Enterprise edition targets operations that need 25 or more users and adds work orders, purchase order management, credit card processing and a third-party API.

QFloors says pricing starts at $89 per user per month, depending on the number of users and features, plus a one-time setup fee that may be waived on annual subscriptions. There are no maintenance fees. Several tools are add-ons with published starting prices: QSched labor scheduling from $1,850 per site license, Installer View, Account View, QLeads and QOrders from $1,200 a year each, QTagger showroom tags from $3,000 a year, and a document manager from $650 per site license. QFloors and Roomvo also sell combined bundles.

QFloors lists integrations with MeasureSquare, Zoho CRM, Swell and Patriot payroll. Support runs Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM Mountain Time, with after-hours emergency support, and is included in the subscription.

The trade-off: QFloors replaces your accounting system as well as your sales tools, so switching is a bigger project than adding an app, and features such as scheduling and installer access cost extra on top of the per-user price.

pros_detail.title: One system for the whole store
pros_detail.explanation: Leads, invoicing, purchasing, inventory, job costing and full accounting live in one cloud system, so there is no separate accounting package to reconcile.

pros_detail.title: Published starting price
pros_detail.explanation: QFloors says it starts at $89 per user per month, with no maintenance fees, and add-ons have listed starting prices.

pros_detail.title: Support included
pros_detail.explanation: Unlimited support is part of the subscription, weekdays 8 AM to 5 PM Mountain Time, with after-hours emergency support.

pros_detail.title: Room to grow
pros_detail.explanation: An Enterprise edition serves operations with 25 or more users and adds work orders, purchase order management, card processing and an API.

pros_detail.title: Works with MeasureSquare and Roomvo
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates from MeasureSquare flow in through its Cloud API, and QLeads is free when connected to a Roomvo site or CRM.

cons_detail.title: Setup fee on top of the subscription
cons_detail.explanation: A one-time setup fee applies unless it is waived on an annual subscription, so the first-year cost is higher than the monthly rate suggests.

cons_detail.title: Key tools are paid add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: Labor scheduling (QSched), installer and customer portals, lead capture and showroom tags each carry their own fee, from $650 to $3,000 or more.

cons_detail.title: Replacing QuickBooks is a real project
cons_detail.explanation: QFloors is built to be your accounting system. Moving books, vendors and inventory out of QuickBooks takes planning and training.

cons_detail.title: Cloud only
cons_detail.explanation: There is no on-premise option, so the store needs a reliable internet connection to use it.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo or discovery call and ask for a written quote covering users, the setup fee and each add-on you need (QSched, Installer View, QLeads and so on), and ask whether an annual subscription waives the setup fee. Plan the move off QuickBooks or your old system: QFloors says customer, inventory, vendor, product and employee data can transfer, so clean those lists first. Decide the cut-over date for accounting with your bookkeeper. Connect MeasureSquare if your estimators use it, and set up Patriot if you want payroll linked. Train each role (sales, purchasing, warehouse, accounting) on its own screens before go-live.

tool_faqs.q: How much does QFloors cost?
tool_faqs.a: QFloors says it starts at $89 per user per month, depending on the number of users and features, plus a one-time setup fee that may be waived for annual subscriptions. There are no maintenance fees. Add-ons such as QSched scheduling or Installer View cost extra.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns QFloors?
tool_faqs.a: Leap Tools, Inc., which does business as Roomvo, bought QFloors in January 2025. The Ogden family, who founded QFloors in 1999, continues to lead it.

tool_faqs.q: Does QFloors work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: QFloors is designed to replace QuickBooks, not sync with it. It says over 90% of its customers run their complete accounting in QFloors, and customer, inventory, vendor, product and employee data can be moved over.

tool_faqs.q: Is QFloors cloud-based?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, and only cloud-based. There is no on-premise version, so you need an internet connection to use it.

tool_faqs.q: What integrations does QFloors have?
tool_faqs.a: Its FAQ lists MeasureSquare, Zoho CRM, Swell and Patriot for payroll. QLeads can link leads from your website, and it is free when connected to a Roomvo site or CRM.

tool_faqs.q: What are QFloors support hours?
tool_faqs.a: Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM Mountain Time, with after-hours emergency support. Unlimited support is included in the subscription.

tools.name: RollMaster
tools.tagline: Cloud flooring business software with built-in accounting, now sold by Broadlume, a Cyncly company

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing; Broadlume sells the business management software (RollMaster) by demo and quote. Published payment processing rates through Broadlume Payments: 2.79% swiped, 2.99% non-swiped, 1% ACH. No trial published. Verified against broadlume.com/products/flooring-software 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Flooring retailers and contractors that want estimating, inventory, job costing and full accounting in one cloud system instead of QuickBooks
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing; the product is now marketed under the Broadlume name, so confirm what you are buying and its roadmap under Cyncly; and it replaces your accounting system, which makes switching a larger project
tools.long_description:
RollMaster is business management software for flooring retailers and contractors. Broadlume acquired RollMaster in 2021, and Broadlume itself became part of Cyncly, announced in December 2024. Broadlume now markets the product as its flooring business management software, and the Cyncly Flooring FAQ says existing RollMaster customers will continue to be supported and the product maintained.

The software is cloud-based and ties estimating, inventory, job costing and accounting together. Broadlume's pages describe real-time inventory valuation, wireless warehouse barcoding and cycle counts; job costs that update from the moment a job or purchase order is entered; and integrated accounting with a general ledger, installer payables and sales commissions. Broadlume pitches it as a replacement for QuickBooks. Reports cover financials, sales, job costing, salesperson performance and inventory, and export to spreadsheets. Broadlume says its customers range from retail to multi-family and commercial.

Payments run through Broadlume Payments, which is integrated with the software and publishes its rates: 2.79% for swiped cards, 2.99% for non-swiped cards and 1% for ACH, with payment links and next-business-day deposits. A Retail Lead Management integration connects leads to the business software, and MeasureSquare lists RollMaster as integrated with its takeoff software through the MeasureSquare Cloud API.

Broadlume does not publish prices for the software; it is sold by demo and quote. The trade-off: you get accounting, inventory and job costing in one flooring-specific system, but pricing is opaque, the RollMaster name is being folded into Broadlume and Cyncly, and moving your books off QuickBooks is part of the switch.

pros_detail.title: Accounting built in
pros_detail.explanation: General ledger, installer payables and sales commissions are part of the system, so there is no separate QuickBooks file to reconcile.

pros_detail.title: Inventory with barcoding
pros_detail.explanation: Real-time inventory valuation, wireless warehouse barcoding and cycle counts help keep stock and the books in line.

pros_detail.title: Real-time job costing
pros_detail.explanation: Costs update from the moment a job or purchase order is entered, so margins are visible while the job is open.

pros_detail.title: Published payment rates
pros_detail.explanation: Broadlume Payments lists 2.79% swiped, 2.99% non-swiped and 1% ACH, with payments applied to jobs automatically.

pros_detail.title: Connects to takeoff and lead tools
pros_detail.explanation: MeasureSquare integrates with RollMaster through its Cloud API, and Broadlume's Retail Lead Management connects leads to the software.

cons_detail.title: No public pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Broadlume does not publish software prices, so you need a demo and a quote to budget.

cons_detail.title: Brand in transition
cons_detail.explanation: RollMaster is now sold under the Broadlume name inside Cyncly, which also owns RFMS. Ask how the product fits Cyncly's plans before a long contract.

cons_detail.title: Replacing QuickBooks is a real project
cons_detail.explanation: Because accounting is built in, switching means moving your books, vendors and inventory, not just adding an app.

cons_detail.title: Card rates are above ACH
cons_detail.explanation: The 1% headline rate applies to ACH; card payments are 2.79% swiped and 2.99% non-swiped.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo through Broadlume and ask for a written quote that lists modules, users and any setup or training costs. Confirm you are buying the product existing RollMaster customers use and how Cyncly plans to support it. Plan the accounting cut-over with your bookkeeper, since the software replaces QuickBooks, and clean up your product catalog, inventory counts and vendor list before migration. Set up barcoding in the warehouse, connect Broadlume Payments if you want integrated card and ACH payments, and link MeasureSquare if your estimators use it.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns RollMaster?
tool_faqs.a: Broadlume acquired RollMaster in 2021, and Broadlume became part of Cyncly in a deal announced in December 2024. Cyncly also owns RFMS.

tool_faqs.q: Is RollMaster still sold?
tool_faqs.a: Broadlume now markets it as its flooring business management software. Cyncly's FAQ says existing RollMaster customers will keep being supported and the product maintained.

tool_faqs.q: How much does RollMaster cost?
tool_faqs.a: Broadlume does not publish software pricing; it is quoted after a demo. Broadlume Payments rates are published: 2.79% swiped, 2.99% non-swiped and 1% ACH.

tool_faqs.q: Does RollMaster work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: It is built to replace QuickBooks. Broadlume says the accounting is fully integrated with purchase orders and inventory.

tool_faqs.q: Is it cloud-based?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Broadlume describes it as cloud-based software you can use from any device.

tools.name: Floorzap
tools.tagline: Flooring store management software for quoting, scheduling, inventory, invoicing and payments

pricing.pricing_note: 'Starting at $399 / per month + one time setup fee'; setup fee amount and included user count not published. Includes training for all staff, ongoing support, multiple locations and user roles, unlimited contractors, QuickBooks and MeasureSquare integrations. Integrated accounting and AI call answering listed as coming soon. No free trial published. Verified against floorzap.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Independent flooring retailers that want quoting, scheduling, inventory, invoicing, payments and customer texting in one cloud system, with QuickBooks kept for accounting
tools.weaknesses: Starts at $399 a month plus a setup fee whose amount is not published; the pricing page does not say how many users the base price covers or offer a free trial; and built-in accounting is still listed as coming soon, so you keep QuickBooks
tools.long_description:
FloorZap is business management software for flooring retailers and remodelers, based in Lehi, Utah. The company says its founders have backgrounds in flooring and software engineering and that it serves hundreds of independent flooring stores across the country. It is cloud-based and runs on computers and mobile devices.

The system covers the path from lead to paid invoice. It handles customer and lead management, quotes and estimates, scheduling of measures, deliveries and installs, job costing and inventory, and sends quotes and invoices by email or text. Payments can be taken online, in the store or by text-to-pay, with surcharging options to offset card fees, and Wisetack consumer financing is built into the quote screen. A bilingual installer portal gives crews their jobs on their phones. FloorZap also includes two-way texting, email marketing, reputation management, showroom QR codes, website lead capture, manufacturer credit and rebate tracking, and support for multiple locations and user roles.

Pricing starts at $399 a month plus a one-time setup fee, with training for all staff, ongoing support and unlimited contractors included. The pricing page lists integrations with QuickBooks, MeasureSquare and B2B product catalogs, and FloorZap's payments page describes a full QuickBooks sync. Integrated accounting and AI call answering are listed as coming soon.

The trade-off: FloorZap bundles most store operations for one monthly price, but it relies on QuickBooks for accounting today, and the setup fee and the number of users included are only available from sales.

pros_detail.title: Lead to paid invoice in one system
pros_detail.explanation: CRM, quotes, scheduling, job costing, inventory, invoicing and payments are connected, so a job moves from quote to install to payment without re-entry.

pros_detail.title: Payments and financing built in
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can pay online, in the store or by text-to-pay, surcharging can offset card fees, and Wisetack financing starts from the quote screen.

pros_detail.title: Training and support included
pros_detail.explanation: The pricing page includes training for all your staff, ongoing support, software updates and unlimited contractors.

pros_detail.title: Installer portal
pros_detail.explanation: A bilingual installer portal shows crews their schedules and job details on their phones.

pros_detail.title: Works with QuickBooks and MeasureSquare
pros_detail.explanation: FloorZap syncs with QuickBooks for accounting and lists a MeasureSquare integration for takeoffs.

cons_detail.title: Setup fee not published
cons_detail.explanation: A one-time setup fee is added to the $399 monthly starting price, and the amount comes from sales.

cons_detail.title: User count unclear
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page says 'starting at' but does not state how many users the base price covers, so get the quote for your team size in writing.

cons_detail.title: No published free trial
cons_detail.explanation: FloorZap offers demos rather than a self-serve trial, so you evaluate it with a salesperson.

cons_detail.title: Accounting still in QuickBooks
cons_detail.explanation: Integrated accounting is listed as coming soon, so today you keep QuickBooks alongside FloorZap.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and ask for a written quote with the monthly price for your number of users and locations and the exact setup fee. Before onboarding, export your customer list and product catalog, since FloorZap offers customer and product imports. Connect QuickBooks so invoices and payments sync, set up payments and decide whether to use surcharging, and enroll in Wisetack if you want to offer financing. Invite installers to the installer portal, link your website lead forms, and connect MeasureSquare if your estimators use it. Use the included staff training to get sales, scheduling and installers on the system.

tool_faqs.q: How much does FloorZap cost?
tool_faqs.a: FloorZap's pricing page says it starts at $399 a month plus a one-time setup fee. The setup fee amount and the number of users included are not published, so ask for a written quote.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: FloorZap does not publish a free trial. It offers demos through its website and by phone.

tool_faqs.q: Does FloorZap work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The pricing page lists a QuickBooks integration and the payments page describes a full QuickBooks sync. FloorZap lists its own integrated accounting as coming soon.

tool_faqs.q: Can customers finance a flooring job through FloorZap?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Wisetack financing is built in: you send a prequalification link from the quote, and Wisetack charges the dealer 3.9% on completed loans.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns FloorZap?
tool_faqs.a: FloorZap does not name a parent company on its site, and it is not one of the Cyncly Flooring brands (RFMS, Broadlume, RollMaster). It is based in Lehi, Utah.

tools.name: Broadlume
tools.tagline: Flooring websites, marketing and business management software from one vendor, part of Cyncly

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing for websites, marketing or the business management software; all quoted after a demo. Published Broadlume Payments rates: 2.79% swiped, 2.99% non-swiped, 1% ACH. Broadlume is a Cyncly company (announced December 2024). No trial published. Verified against broadlume.com/products and broadlume.com/products/flooring-software/payment-processing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Flooring retailers that want their website, online advertising, reviews, lead handling and showroom visualization from one vendor, with the option of Broadlume's business management software for back-office work
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing for websites, marketing or software, so scope and cost come from a sales quote; the product line is broad and still being folded into Cyncly Flooring; and card processing costs 2.79% to 2.99%, with the 1% headline rate applying to ACH only
tools.long_description:
Broadlume sells websites, marketing and business software to the flooring industry. It started in 2015 as Adhawk, an advertising technology company founded in New York by Todd Saunders and Dan Pratt, moved into flooring by buying FloorForce in 2018, and took the Broadlume name in 2020. It then acquired Freetail, Retail Lead Management and the RollMaster business management software. Cyncly, which also owns RFMS, announced its acquisition of Broadlume in December 2024, and the brands now operate as Cyncly Flooring. Broadlume is based in Harrison, New York, and says it serves thousands of flooring retailers and works with more than 300 manufacturers.

The customer-facing products are the core. Broadlume builds flooring websites with product catalogs and a flooring visualizer, and adds digital advertising, SEO, ratings and reviews, web chat and texting, call tracking and recording, and lead management. Its Retail Selling System adds in-store visualization and e-commerce sample ordering for showrooms.

The back-office product is Broadlume's flooring business management software, the former RollMaster. It is cloud-based and combines estimating, inventory, job costing, reporting and built-in accounting, and Broadlume pitches it as a replacement for QuickBooks. Broadlume Payments is integrated with it and publishes its rates: 2.79% for swiped cards, 2.99% for non-swiped cards and 1% for ACH. Broadlume websites can also send leads directly into RFMS for dealers who run that ERP.

Broadlume does not publish prices; everything is sold by demo and quote. In its Cyncly FAQ it said it had no current plans to change pricing for existing customers.

The trade-off: one vendor can cover your website, marketing and back office, but the scope is wide and unpriced, so pin down exactly which products you are buying, and expect changes as Cyncly combines its flooring brands.

pros_detail.title: Website and marketing in one place
pros_detail.explanation: Flooring websites with product catalogs and a visualizer come with digital advertising, SEO, reviews, web chat, texting and call tracking from the same vendor.

pros_detail.title: Showroom tools
pros_detail.explanation: The Retail Selling System adds in-store visualization and e-commerce sample ordering to connect the website and the showroom.

pros_detail.title: Back office available too
pros_detail.explanation: Broadlume's business management software (the former RollMaster) covers estimating, inventory, job costing, reporting and accounting in the cloud.

pros_detail.title: Published payment rates
pros_detail.explanation: Broadlume Payments lists 2.79% swiped, 2.99% non-swiped and 1% ACH, with payment links and next-business-day deposits.

pros_detail.title: Works with RFMS
pros_detail.explanation: Dealers on RFMS can keep their ERP and have Broadlume website leads flow straight into it.

cons_detail.title: No public pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Websites, marketing services and software are all quoted, so you need a sales conversation to compare costs.

cons_detail.title: Broad product line
cons_detail.explanation: With websites, ads, SEO, reviews, visualization, sample ordering, software and payments on offer, it is easy to buy more or less than you need. Get the list of included products in writing.

cons_detail.title: Brands being combined
cons_detail.explanation: Broadlume is now part of Cyncly Flooring with RFMS and other brands. Ask how your products will be supported as Cyncly integrates them.

cons_detail.title: The 1% rate is for ACH
cons_detail.explanation: Card payments cost 2.79% swiped and 2.99% non-swiped; only ACH bank payments are 1%.

tools.implementation_notes: Decide which pieces you need before the demo: a website and marketing, showroom visualization and sample ordering, the business management software, payments, or a combination. Ask for a written quote that lists each product, any setup fees and the contract term. If you are moving an existing website, plan the content and redirects so search traffic carries over. If you run RFMS, ask for the website-to-RFMS lead integration; if you adopt Broadlume's business management software, plan the accounting move off QuickBooks with your bookkeeper and set up Broadlume Payments if you want integrated card and ACH processing.

tool_faqs.q: What is Broadlume?
tool_faqs.a: Broadlume sells websites, digital marketing, reviews, lead management, showroom visualization and business management software to flooring retailers. It started in 2015 as Adhawk and is now part of Cyncly.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Broadlume?
tool_faqs.a: Cyncly, which announced the acquisition in December 2024. Cyncly also owns RFMS, and the brands now operate as Cyncly Flooring.

tool_faqs.q: Does Broadlume own RollMaster, QFloors or MeasureSquare?
tool_faqs.a: Broadlume acquired RollMaster in 2021 and now sells it as its business management software. QFloors is owned by Roomvo's parent, Leap Tools, and MeasureSquare is an independent company.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Broadlume cost?
tool_faqs.a: Broadlume does not publish prices; websites, marketing and software are quoted. Payment processing rates are published: 2.79% swiped, 2.99% non-swiped and 1% ACH.

tool_faqs.q: Does Broadlume work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Broadlume's business management software has accounting built in and is pitched as a replacement for QuickBooks rather than an add-on to it.

tool_faqs.q: Can I use a Broadlume website with RFMS?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Broadlume offers a website integration that sends leads captured on your site directly into RFMS.

tools.name: ServiceCore
tools.tagline: Job, route, inventory and billing software for portable toilet, septic and roll-off dumpster businesses

pricing.pricing_note: No prices are published; the pricing page asks you to schedule a demo. ServiceCore's FAQ says it charges per truck (no charge for office staff seats), billed monthly on an annual contract, with customer and job management, routing, inventory and billing included. Its comparison articles add an implementation fee and state there is no free trial. Verified against servicecore.com/pricing, servicecore.com/servicecore-software-faqs and servicecore.com/llms.txt 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Portable restroom, septic (including grease trap) and roll-off dumpster operators with several trucks who want scheduling, routing, unit tracking and billing in one system that syncs with QuickBooks Online
tools.weaknesses: No published prices; sold per truck on an annual contract with an implementation fee and no free trial. New accounting connections are QuickBooks Online (US) only, and the product is built for sanitation and waste work, not general trades.
tools.long_description:
ServiceCore is business software for portable restroom rental, septic pumping (including grease trap, or FOG, work) and roll-off dumpster companies. It covers customer and job management, scheduling and dispatch, route optimization, inventory tracking of placed units on a map, and automated billing, with a driver app for iOS and Android phones and tablets. ServiceCore says its billing automation can cut invoicing time to about 5 minutes a day.

The company was formed in April 2017, when 1bg acquired Clear Computing and created ServiceCore, and it is based in Colorado. Private equity firm Mainsail Partners invested $54 million in February 2022. In May 2023 ServiceCore bought Docket, a Dayton, Ohio, maker of dumpster rental and junk removal software, and Docket is still sold under its own brand as a ServiceCore company. Mainsail says ServiceCore customers have completed more than 3.5 million jobs in the software and track more than 550,000 sanitation, dumpster and other units.

In the field, drivers see their stops in order, get turn-by-turn directions, capture photos and signatures, scan barcodes and record the GPS location of each unit they place, and the app works offline. Customers get a self-service portal to view invoices, pay by card or ACH and request service. Online payments run through ServiceCore Pay, powered by Fiserv, and ServiceCore's help center puts ACH at 1% per payment. Accounting syncs with QuickBooks Online (US accounts): customers, services, tax codes and similar records sync both ways, and invoices, payments, credit memos and refunds flow from ServiceCore to QuickBooks. ServiceCore no longer sets up new QuickBooks Desktop connections and supports existing Desktop links as legacy only.

ServiceCore does not publish prices. Its FAQ says it charges per truck, with no charge for office staff seats, billed monthly on an annual contract, and that customer and job management, routing, inventory and billing are all included. Its comparison articles add an implementation fee and say there is no free trial; you evaluate it through a guided demo. An implementation specialist leads a 6-step onboarding that ServiceCore says typically takes 6 to 12 weeks, depending on company size. The trade-off: you commit to a year and an onboarding project before the software is running, and a one- or two-truck operator should check the per-truck math against lighter tools.

pros_detail.title: Built for sanitation and waste work
pros_detail.explanation: Jobs, routes and billing are organized around units placed at customer sites and serviced on repeat cycles, for portable toilets, septic and roll-off work, rather than one-off service visits.

pros_detail.title: Unit tracking on a map
pros_detail.explanation: Drivers record the GPS location of each unit they place with one tap in the app, and the office sees inventory on a map, which helps find and bill every toilet, tank or container.

pros_detail.title: No charge for office seats
pros_detail.explanation: ServiceCore prices per truck and says it does not charge for office staff seats, so adding a dispatcher or billing clerk does not raise the subscription.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online sync
pros_detail.explanation: Customers, services, tax codes and related records sync both ways with QuickBooks Online, and invoices, payments, credit memos and refunds post to QuickBooks automatically.

pros_detail.title: Card and ACH payments with a customer portal
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can view invoices, pay by card or ACH and request service in a self-service portal. Payments run through ServiceCore Pay, powered by Fiserv.

pros_detail.title: Guided onboarding
pros_detail.explanation: An implementation specialist and a customer success engineer handle setup and the QuickBooks data import, and ServiceCore says it hires former operators to train staff on site or remotely.

cons_detail.title: No published price
cons_detail.explanation: You need a demo and a quote to learn the cost, which makes side-by-side comparison with other tools slow.

cons_detail.title: Annual contract, setup fee, no trial
cons_detail.explanation: ServiceCore bills monthly but on an annual contract, charges an implementation fee and does not offer a free trial.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Desktop is legacy only
cons_detail.explanation: New customers cannot connect QuickBooks Desktop; ServiceCore supports Desktop only for existing links and recommends QuickBooks Online. The Online sync requires a US QuickBooks account.

cons_detail.title: Longer rollout
cons_detail.explanation: ServiceCore says its onboarding typically takes 6 to 12 weeks, so plan the switch ahead of your busy season.

cons_detail.title: Narrow by design
cons_detail.explanation: It is built for portable sanitation, septic and dumpster companies, so contractors in other trades are not the target customer.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and bring your truck count, unit counts (toilets, tanks, containers), recurring service patterns and billing cycles so the quote matches your operation, and get the per-truck price, implementation fee and contract term in writing. After signing, an implementation specialist runs a 6-step onboarding that starts with a data review call and an import of customers, sites, services and tax rates from QuickBooks Online, then sets up routes, recurring jobs, billing and payments. If you still use QuickBooks Desktop, plan a move to QuickBooks Online first, since new Desktop connections are not offered. Install the driver app on iOS or Android devices and train drivers before go-live. If roll-off is most of your business, ask whether ServiceCore or its sister product Docket is the better fit.

tool_faqs.q: What does ServiceCore cost?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceCore does not publish prices. It charges per truck on the road with no charge for office staff seats, billed monthly on an annual contract, and its comparison articles mention an implementation fee. You get a quote after a demo.

tool_faqs.q: Does ServiceCore offer a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: No. ServiceCore says it does not offer a free trial; you evaluate it through a guided demo.

tool_faqs.q: Does ServiceCore work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, with QuickBooks Online (US accounts). Customers, services, tax codes and similar records sync both ways, and invoices, payments, credit memos and refunds flow into QuickBooks. New QuickBooks Desktop connections are not offered; existing Desktop links get legacy support only.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns ServiceCore, and how does it relate to Docket?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceCore is based in Colorado and backed by private equity firm Mainsail Partners, which invested $54 million in February 2022. ServiceCore bought Docket, a dumpster rental and junk removal software maker, in May 2023. Docket is still sold as its own product and describes itself as a ServiceCore company.

tool_faqs.q: What businesses is ServiceCore for?
tool_faqs.a: Portable restroom rental, septic pumping and grease trap (FOG) service, and roll-off dumpster companies. ServiceCore says it works best for operators with multiple trucks.

tool_faqs.q: How long does setup take?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceCore says its 6-step onboarding typically takes 6 to 12 weeks, depending on company size. An implementation specialist leads it, and former operators train your staff on site or remotely.

tools.name: Docket
tools.tagline: Dumpster rental and junk removal software with dispatch, online ordering, billing and a driver app

pricing.pricing_note: Plan prices are not published; the pricing page asks you to schedule a demo to see pricing. It does publish payment rates: card payments at 3.0% + 30 cents on Grow and 2.8% + 30 cents on Pro and Pro Plus, ACH at 1% per transaction on all plans. Grow includes 500 text messages a month and a basic online shopping cart; Pro and Pro Plus include 1,000 messages and a premium cart; Pro Plus adds IronRouteAI route creation. No free trial is advertised. Verified against yourdocket.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Roll-off dumpster rental and junk removal companies that want dispatch, container tracking, billing, payments, online ordering and a rental website in one system
tools.weaknesses: No published plan prices (quote after a demo); card processing rates depend on the plan; the AI route creation tool is only in the top plan; built for dumpster and junk hauling, not septic or portable toilet work
tools.long_description:
Docket is software for roll-off dumpster rental and junk removal businesses. It covers customer management, drag-and-drop scheduling and dispatch with live driver tracking, a driver app that works online and offline, container tracking, billing and payments, a customer portal, broker tools and reporting. Docket also builds custom dumpster rental websites with a shopping cart connected to the software, so customers can order online.

Docket was founded in 2019 in Dayton, Ohio, by Brian Ingle and Dan Klimkowski. ServiceCore, the Colorado-based portable toilet, septic and roll-off software company, bought it in May 2023. Docket's site now describes it as a ServiceCore company with a Denver, Colorado, address, and it keeps its own brand, website, sales line and support line.

Dispatchers can schedule drop-offs and pickups plus exchanges, relocations, dump and returns, and live loads. Docket's GPS dumpster tracking records where each container sits, using PIN or QR code scans in the driver app. Docket says it sends more than 30 customizable email and text notifications, and customers can pay online, at the job site or through the customer portal. The pricing page lists integrations with QuickBooks Online, Mailchimp, Samsara, Verizon Connect and Dumpsters.com on every plan.

Docket sells three plans, Grow, Pro and Pro Plus, and does not publish their prices; you see pricing after a demo. The plans differ in card processing rates (3.0% plus 30 cents on Grow, 2.8% plus 30 cents on Pro and Pro Plus; ACH is 1% on all), included text messages (500 a month on Grow, 1,000 on Pro and Pro Plus) and the online shopping cart (basic on Grow, premium on the others). Pro Plus adds IronRouteAI, Docket's AI route creation tool. The trade-off: you cannot compare total cost without a sales call, and the built-in payment rates are part of what you really pay each month.

pros_detail.title: Built for dumpster and junk hauling
pros_detail.explanation: Scheduling handles drop-offs, pickups, exchanges, relocations, dump and returns, and live loads, the jobs a roll-off company runs every day.

pros_detail.title: Rental website and online ordering
pros_detail.explanation: Docket builds custom dumpster rental websites with a shopping cart tied to the software, and local SEO is listed on every plan.

pros_detail.title: Container tracking
pros_detail.explanation: Drivers scan a PIN or QR code in the app to record where each dumpster sits, so the office can see container locations.

pros_detail.title: Hauler-focused integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan lists QuickBooks Online, Samsara, Verizon Connect, Mailchimp and Dumpsters.com integrations.

pros_detail.title: Customer messaging and payments
pros_detail.explanation: Docket says it sends more than 30 customizable email and text notifications, and customers can pay online, at the job site or in the customer portal.

cons_detail.title: No published plan prices
cons_detail.explanation: Docket lists three plans but shows prices only after a demo, so budgeting and comparison need a sales conversation.

cons_detail.title: Processing rates vary by plan
cons_detail.explanation: Card payments cost 3.0% plus 30 cents on Grow and 2.8% plus 30 cents on Pro and Pro Plus, so check the fee difference against the plan price difference.

cons_detail.title: AI routing only on the top plan
cons_detail.explanation: IronRouteAI route creation is included only in Pro Plus.

cons_detail.title: Overlap with ServiceCore
cons_detail.explanation: The same parent company also sells ServiceCore to roll-off operators, so ask which product fits your mix of work.

cons_detail.title: Narrow focus
cons_detail.explanation: Docket is built for dumpster rental and junk removal. Portable toilet and septic companies are served by ServiceCore or other tools.

tools.implementation_notes: Schedule a demo and bring your container counts by size, truck count, service area and current website setup, then get plan pricing, any setup costs and contract terms in writing. Decide early whether to take card and ACH payments through Docket, since the card rate depends on the plan. Setup covers importing customers and containers, setting dumpster sizes and prices for online ordering, connecting QuickBooks Online, and linking Samsara or Verizon Connect if your trucks use them. Install the driver app and train drivers on PIN or QR code scanning so container locations stay accurate. If you also run portable toilets or septic, ask whether ServiceCore is the better fit.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Docket cost?
tool_faqs.a: Docket does not publish plan prices; you see pricing after a demo. The pricing page does publish payment rates: card payments at 3.0% plus 30 cents on Grow and 2.8% plus 30 cents on Pro and Pro Plus, and ACH at 1% on all plans.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Docket?
tool_faqs.a: ServiceCore bought Docket in May 2023. Docket was founded in 2019 in Dayton, Ohio, by Brian Ingle and Dan Klimkowski, and its site now calls it a ServiceCore company with a Denver, Colorado, address.

tool_faqs.q: Can my customers order dumpsters online?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Docket builds custom dumpster rental websites with a shopping cart connected to the software. Grow includes a basic cart; Pro and Pro Plus include a premium cart.

tool_faqs.q: What does Docket integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Its pricing page lists QuickBooks Online, Mailchimp, Samsara, Verizon Connect and Dumpsters.com on all three plans.

tool_faqs.q: Does Docket do route optimization?
tool_faqs.a: All plans include drag-and-drop scheduling and dispatch with live driver tracking. The Pro Plus plan adds IronRouteAI, Docket's AI route creation tool.

tool_faqs.q: Docket or ServiceCore?
tool_faqs.a: Both are sold by the same company. Docket is built for dumpster rental and junk removal; ServiceCore covers portable toilets, septic and roll-off. Ask during the demo which one fits your mix of work.

tools.name: Starlight Software
