pricing.pricing_note: No prices are published. The site's calls to action are demo requests (web form or phone), and no free trial or free version is advertised. Verified against starlightsoftwaresolutions.com (home, feature-advantages and business-lines pages) 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Waste and recycling companies running several lines of business (roll-off, commercial and residential collection, portable toilets, recycling facilities) that want live dispatch, billing, detailed reporting and a branded ordering app for their customers
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing or free trial; integrations other than QuickBooks are not documented on the site; route optimization is not advertised (the site describes live dispatch maps and route reports)
tools.long_description:
Starlight Software Solutions makes waste and recycling management software for haulers and facility operators. Its site lists six business lines: roll-off, commercial collections, residential collections, portable toilets, facility management and municipal reporting. The core is live, map-based dispatch with driver, truck and container visibility, order and subscription management, automated billing with custom pricing, and a reporting engine that breaks out profitability by customer, route, job site, service type, container size, material and disposal site.

Two apps sit on top of that. The driver app handles messages with dispatch and photo uploads, with date, time and location stamps. The Contractor App, for Android and Apple devices, is a customer-facing app you brand as your own: roll-off customers use it to place and change orders, check job status, review and pay invoices, and run material reports. For recycling facilities, Starlight lists unattended or driver-assisted weight capture, multi-scale and multi-facility reporting, and a spotter tablet for documenting loads. Portable toilet operators can bill per service, per toilet or per gallon pumped and put accounts on seasonal hold.

Starlight is based in Denver, Colorado. Its about page says founder and CEO Bill Bradley built the product after buying a 35-truck hauling company in Colorado and finding no modern software for it. The site names no outside owner or parent company. Its pages mention integration with QuickBooks and other accounting systems, including QuickBooks Online, but no integrations list is published.

Starlight does not publish prices, and every call to action on its site is a demo request; no free trial or free version is advertised. The trade-off: you cannot compare cost without a sales process, and because the site gives little detail on integrations, telematics or route optimization, confirm the workflows you depend on during the demo.

pros_detail.title: Several waste lines in one system
pros_detail.explanation: Roll-off, commercial and residential collection, portable toilets and recycling facilities run on one platform, which suits companies with mixed service lines.

pros_detail.title: Branded customer app
pros_detail.explanation: The Contractor App, sold under your brand, lets customers place and change orders, check job status, pay invoices and run material reports from a phone.

pros_detail.title: Live dispatch map
pros_detail.explanation: Dispatchers see drivers, trucks, containers and orders on a live map and can match trucks to last-minute orders.

pros_detail.title: Detailed profitability reporting
pros_detail.explanation: Reports break out profitability by customer, route, job site, service type, container size, material and disposal site, with drag-and-drop custom reports.

pros_detail.title: Recycling facility tools
pros_detail.explanation: Facility management covers weight capture, multi-scale and multi-facility reporting, and a spotter tablet for documenting inbound loads.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Prices come only through a demo and quote, which makes budgeting and comparison slower.

cons_detail.title: No free trial advertised
cons_detail.explanation: The site offers demos only, so you cannot test it with your own data before buying.

cons_detail.title: Integrations not documented
cons_detail.explanation: The site mentions QuickBooks and other accounting systems but publishes no list of accounting, payment or telematics integrations.

cons_detail.title: No route optimization advertised
cons_detail.explanation: Routing features on the site are live dispatch maps and route reports; automatic route optimization is not described.

cons_detail.title: Little public detail on terms
cons_detail.explanation: Support hours, onboarding steps and contract terms are not published, so get them in writing during the sales process.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo through the website or by phone and bring a list of your business lines, truck and container counts, disposal sites and current accounting system. Get pricing, contract terms, onboarding steps and support hours in writing, since none are published. Confirm how the QuickBooks (or other accounting) integration works, which payment processor handles card payments, and whether your GPS or telematics provider connects. If you plan to offer the branded Contractor App to customers, ask how it is set up and published under your name. Then migrate customers, containers, pricing and recurring services, and train drivers on the driver app before go-live.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Starlight Software cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starlight does not publish prices. Its site offers demos by web form or phone, and pricing comes as a quote after the demo.

tool_faqs.q: Does Starlight offer a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: No free trial or free version is advertised; every call to action on the site is a demo request.

tool_faqs.q: What is the Starlight Contractor App?
tool_faqs.a: A customer-facing app for Android and Apple devices, branded as your company's app. Your customers use it to place and change orders, check job status, review and pay invoices, and run material reports.

tool_faqs.q: Does Starlight integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Its residential collections page lists integration of QuickBooks and other accounting systems, and its portable toilet page lists QuickBooks Online. Ask during the demo how the sync works.

tool_faqs.q: What kinds of waste businesses does Starlight serve?
tool_faqs.a: Roll-off, commercial collections, residential collections, portable toilets, recycling facilities (facility management) and municipal reporting.

tools.name: Routeware
tools.tagline: Waste and recycling collection software for private haulers and municipalities: routing, dispatch, in-cab tools, billing and resident engagement

pricing.pricing_note: No prices are published. Routeware's pricing page says every deployment is custom quoted and that pricing depends on fleet size, services and operational needs; you submit a form and then book a call with sales. No free trial is advertised. Verified against routeware.com/get-pricing-for-routeware 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Private waste haulers and city or county solid waste departments that need route optimization, dispatch, in-cab driver tools, billing and customer or resident self-service across a collection fleet
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (custom quote based on fleet size, services and needs); the product line spans several brands (Elements, SmartCity, ReCollect and older products), so scope the quote carefully; built for collection fleets and public agencies, not small rental-only or junk removal businesses
tools.long_description:
Routeware makes software for waste and recycling collection. Its flagship products are Routeware Elements for private haulers, Routeware SmartCity for governments and Routeware ReCollect for resident communication, alongside older products (RCC, EnCore, EasyRoute) and specialty tools (Recyclist, Compliance Publishing). Across these it covers route optimization, dispatch, in-cab driver tools, fleet and equipment reporting, billing and payments, customer service, self-service portals, compliance, and specialty lines such as medical waste and site services. Its customers include private haulers, cities, universities and specialty fleets.

Routeware says it was founded 25 years ago, and a Waste Dive interview republished on its site dates it to 2000. It moved its headquarters from Portland, Oregon, to Austin, Texas, on December 1, 2025, and has offices and customers in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada. The same interview says Routeware is backed by California-based investor K1 and bought Rubicon's SmartCity municipal routing business in 2024. Jeremy Collins became CEO in January 2026. Routeware says it has more than 1,500 customers, 18,000 trucks using its technology and 88 million residents covered.

Routeware Elements combines cloud dispatch with a single view of trucks, orders and status, in-cab tools tied to the back office, automated invoicing and auto-pay with online payment through customer portals, and a CRM view of each account. Routeware describes Elements as hardware-light, with an open API and bring-your-own-device support, and says Elements deployments are completed in under 90 days. Elements names integrations with Samsara, Geotab, Worldpay and MyTruckScales, and Routeware's partner page adds Esri mapping, WasteVision AI contamination cameras and Open311 service requests.

Routeware does not publish prices. Its pricing page says every deployment is custom quoted based on fleet size, services and operational needs, and it leads to a form and a call with sales. The trade-off: Routeware is built for collection fleets and public agencies, with a sales-led buying process to match, and no accounting system is named among its integrations. A small roll-off, junk removal or portable toilet company is usually closer in size to tools like ServiceCore, Docket or Trash Flow.

pros_detail.title: Built for haulers and municipalities
pros_detail.explanation: Elements serves private haulers and SmartCity serves governments, so the same vendor covers both sides of waste collection.

pros_detail.title: Routing, dispatch and in-cab together
pros_detail.explanation: Route optimization, cloud dispatch and in-cab driver tools share one back office, so drivers and dispatchers work from the same orders.

pros_detail.title: Resident and customer self-service
pros_detail.explanation: ReCollect, customer portals and Open311 service requests let residents and customers look up service and report issues without calling.

pros_detail.title: Telematics and payment partners
pros_detail.explanation: Named integrations include Samsara and Geotab telematics, Worldpay payments, Esri mapping and MyTruckScales scale tickets.

pros_detail.title: Specialty lines covered
pros_detail.explanation: Medical waste, site services and compliance reporting sit alongside residential and commercial collection.

pros_detail.title: Large installed base
pros_detail.explanation: Routeware says more than 1,500 customers and 18,000 trucks use its technology.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Every deployment is custom quoted, so you need a sales call and a scoped proposal to learn the cost.

cons_detail.title: Several product brands
cons_detail.explanation: Elements, SmartCity, ReCollect, EasyRoute and other products came together over the years, so confirm which product and modules your quote covers.

cons_detail.title: Sized for fleets
cons_detail.explanation: The sales-led process and fleet-wide scope are a poor match for a one- or two-truck operator.

cons_detail.title: No named accounting integration
cons_detail.explanation: Routeware's partner and product pages list telematics, payment and mapping partners but no accounting system, so ask how billing data reaches your books.

cons_detail.title: Recent leadership and HQ changes
cons_detail.explanation: A new CEO started in January 2026 and headquarters moved in December 2025, so ask about the product roadmap and your support contacts.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with the pricing request form; Routeware's sales team scopes the quote by fleet size, services and operational needs. Before the call, list your lines of business (residential, commercial, roll-off, medical waste, site services), truck count, telematics provider (Samsara and Geotab are named partners), payment processor, GIS data and accounting system. Confirm which product (Elements, SmartCity or ReCollect) and which modules the quote covers, and how billing data moves into your accounting system. Routeware says Elements deployments are completed in under 90 days; get the rollout plan, data migration steps and driver training schedule in writing.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Routeware cost?
tool_faqs.a: Routeware does not publish prices. Its pricing page says each deployment is custom quoted based on fleet size, services and operational needs.

tool_faqs.q: Who is Routeware for?
tool_faqs.a: Private waste haulers and municipal solid waste departments, plus universities and specialty fleets. Routeware's CEO told Waste Dive the customer base is split roughly evenly between private haulers and municipalities.

tool_faqs.q: What are Routeware Elements, SmartCity and ReCollect?
tool_faqs.a: Elements is the platform for private haulers (dispatch, routing, in-cab, billing, CRM). SmartCity is for governments and came from Routeware's 2024 purchase of Rubicon's SmartCity business. ReCollect handles resident communication and self-service.

tool_faqs.q: Where is Routeware based, and who owns it?
tool_faqs.a: Routeware moved its headquarters from Portland, Oregon, to Austin, Texas, in December 2025. A Waste Dive interview republished on its site says it is backed by California-based investor K1. Jeremy Collins became CEO in January 2026.

tool_faqs.q: What does Routeware integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Its pages name Samsara and Geotab telematics, Worldpay payments, Esri mapping, MyTruckScales, WasteVision AI cameras and Open311. Routeware also describes an open API. No accounting system is listed, so ask how billing data is exported.

tool_faqs.q: Is Routeware a fit for a small junk removal or roll-off company?
tool_faqs.a: Usually not. Routeware is built and sold for collection fleets and public agencies. Smaller rental and hauling businesses often look at ServiceCore, Docket, Trash Flow or a general field service tool.

pricing.pricing_note: Trash Flow is sold as a one-time license built from modules, and the site does not publish a standalone core price. Published one-time prices: Base + Billing + Advanced Billing with Container Tracking $3,600, or $4,150 with Routing; Container Tracking module $550; TipTicket landfill package with Trash Flow Plus and one scale house $3,950 (extra scale house $800, electronic scale interface $400). Monthly add-ons: AVS Mapping $25 for one license ($12.50 per network for 2-8 licenses, $6.25 for 9 or more), Route Optimization $60 for the first user ($30 for users 2-8, $15 from the 9th; requires AVS), TeleRoute $35 per truck (requires AVS), Cloud Database $40 for one license. Verified against trashflow.com (container-tracking, landfill-management, cloud, avs-mapping, route-optimization, teleroute and tech-support pages) 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential, commercial and roll-off trash haulers, plus landfills and transfer stations, that want Windows software they buy in modules and can test with a free 90-day license
tools.weaknesses: Installed Windows software rather than a browser app; mapping, route optimization, the TeleRoute truck app and the cloud database are separate monthly add-ons; no standalone core license price is published; ongoing support costs a percentage of your system total
tools.long_description:
Trash Flow is billing and route management software for trash haulers, made by Ivy Computer, Inc. of Waterbury Center, Vermont. It is installed software that runs on Windows 10 (version 21H2 or newer) and Windows 11, with an optional cloud database for companies with more than one office. It is built from modules: billing (Standard and Advanced Billing), routing, dispatch and work orders, container tracking, AVS mapping and address verification, route optimization, the TeleRoute in-truck app, landfill and transfer station management (TipTicket) with a scale interface, and an Accounting Link that exports payments and charges for import into your accounting software.

Billing handles multiple billing cycles (annual, monthly, quarterly and others), discounts and promotions, variable rate charges, printed statements and invoices, and a record of changes to customer accounts. TrashBilling.com, included with Standard and Advanced Billing, lets your customers pay by Visa, Mastercard, Discover or American Express and set up auto-pay; Trash Flow says it charges per transaction with no monthly minimum or contract. Container tracking covers roll-offs, compactors, dumpsters and carts, with rental fees beyond a free-day period and drop, pull, disposal and overweight charges. TeleRoute runs on standard tablets and phones, with hands-free stop completion, photos, live truck tracking on the dispatch map, and offline work that syncs later.

Ivy Computer says it has built software for the hauling industry since 1985, and its about page dates Trash Flow itself to 1989. Technical support runs 24/7 by phone and email. The first 90 days of support after purchase are free; after that, an optional support contract costs 1% of your system total a month or 12% a year, and since May 1, 2025, it includes offsite backup.

Trash Flow publishes many prices but not a standalone core license price. Its container tracking page lists a Base, Billing and Advanced Billing bundle with container tracking for $3,600, or $4,150 with routing added, and the container tracking module alone for $550. The landfill package (TipTicket with Trash Flow Plus and one scale house) is $3,950. Monthly add-ons include AVS mapping ($25 a month for one license), route optimization ($60 a month for the first user, requires AVS), TeleRoute ($35 per truck per month, requires AVS) and the cloud database ($40 a month for one license). You can download a free 90-day license to test it. The trade-off: you pay for a one-time license, monthly add-ons and a support contract, and you run it on your own Windows PCs, rather than paying one monthly subscription for a browser-based system.

pros_detail.title: Buy only the modules you need
pros_detail.explanation: Start with billing and routing and add container tracking, mapping, route optimization, the truck app or landfill tools later.

pros_detail.title: Many prices are published
pros_detail.explanation: Module bundles, add-ons and support costs are listed on the site, so you can estimate cost before calling sales.

pros_detail.title: Free 90-day trial license
pros_detail.explanation: You can download Trash Flow and test it with your own data for 90 days before buying.

pros_detail.title: 24/7 support, first 90 days free
pros_detail.explanation: Phone and email support runs around the clock, and the first 90 days after purchase are included.

pros_detail.title: Landfill and transfer station tools
pros_detail.explanation: TipTicket runs scale house weigh-in and weigh-out, tickets, cash at the scale and transfer station material tracking, with an optional scale interface.

pros_detail.title: Customer payments included
pros_detail.explanation: TrashBilling.com comes with Standard and Advanced Billing and charges per transaction, with no monthly minimum or contract.

cons_detail.title: Windows-only installed software
cons_detail.explanation: Trash Flow runs on Windows 10 or 11 PCs; multi-office access needs a network setup or the paid cloud database.

cons_detail.title: Monthly add-on fees
cons_detail.explanation: AVS mapping, route optimization, TeleRoute and the cloud database are billed monthly on top of the license, and route optimization and TeleRoute both require AVS.

cons_detail.title: Ongoing support costs
cons_detail.explanation: After the free 90 days, support costs 12% of your system total a year (or 1% a month).

cons_detail.title: No named accounting integration
cons_detail.explanation: Accounting Link exports a file of payments and charges to import into your accounting software; no direct sync with a named accounting product is listed.

cons_detail.title: No standalone core price
cons_detail.explanation: The site lists bundles and add-ons but not the price of the base system alone, so get a full written quote.

tools.implementation_notes: Download the free 90-day license and install it on a Windows 10 (21H2 or newer) or Windows 11 PC to test billing and routing with your own data. List the modules you need now (billing, container tracking, routing) and later (AVS mapping, route optimization, TeleRoute, TipTicket), and ask sales for a written quote that covers the license, monthly add-ons and the support contract. If you have more than one office, choose between a local network setup and the cloud database. Set up Accounting Link to export payments and charges to your accounting software, turn on TrashBilling.com for online payments, and use the 90 days of included support to finish setup and training.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Trash Flow cost?
tool_faqs.a: Trash Flow is a one-time modular license. Published bundles include Base, Billing and Advanced Billing with container tracking for $3,600, or $4,150 with routing. Add-ons such as AVS mapping ($25 a month for one license), route optimization ($60 a month for the first user) and TeleRoute ($35 per truck per month) are billed monthly, and support after 90 days costs 12% of your system total a year.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Trash Flow offers a free 90-day license that you download and install.

tool_faqs.q: Does Trash Flow work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Trash Flow does not list a direct QuickBooks integration. Its Accounting Link module creates a file of payments and charges that you import into your accounting software, and the site has a page comparing Trash Flow with QuickBooks for hauler billing.

tool_faqs.q: Is Trash Flow cloud software?
tool_faqs.a: No. It is installed on Windows 10 (21H2 or newer) or Windows 11. An optional cloud database lets several offices share data, starting at $40 a month for one license.

tool_faqs.q: Does Trash Flow have a driver app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. TeleRoute runs on standard tablets and phones for $35 per truck per month and requires Trash Flow's AVS mapping service.

tool_faqs.q: What support is included?
tool_faqs.a: Support is 24/7 by phone and email. The first 90 days after purchase are free; after that, an optional support contract costs 1% of your system total a month or 12% a year and includes software updates and offsite backup.

Inspect Point is software for fire and life-safety inspection, testing and maintenance contractors in the US and Canada. It was founded in 2014 in Troy, New York, by Padraic Doyle, Drew Slocum, Jennifer Doyle and Phil Sirigiano, and is still based there, with Doyle as CEO. The company was bootstrapped until January 2022, when Mainsail Partners made a $28 million growth equity investment. In April 2025 it acquired FireCAD, a design tool for fire alarm and security layout drawings, which runs as its own brand under Inspect Point. Inspect Point says more than 15,000 fire protection professionals use the platform.

Technicians inspect on an iPad or iPhone using built-in question sets that follow NFPA editions in the US (including NFPA 25, 72 and 10) and ULC standards in Canada. The vendor covers sprinkler, fire alarm, extinguisher, chemical suppression, special hazards, backflow, and fire door and damper work. Inspections that have synced to the device can be completed without a connection and sent to the office later. Deficiencies found on site flow into proposals, work orders and invoices without retyping, and a customer portal shows clients their upcoming visits, reports, proposals and invoices.

In the office, Inspect Point handles scheduling and dispatch for recurring inspections and service calls, invoices sent by email or text with automated reminders, and card payments through Inspect Point Payments. Inspect Point AI includes an assistant for bulk actions and data questions. Native integrations include QuickBooks Online and Desktop, Sage 100 Contractor, Simpro, BuildOps and Salesforce, and reports can be submitted to AHJ platforms such as The Compliance Engine, IROL and LivSafe. An open API and Zapier come with the Platinum plan.

Prices are not published. There are three plans: Silver (digital inspections, compliant reports and deficiency management, with email support), Gold (adds proposals from deficiencies and premium email support) and Platinum (adds service work orders and API access, with premium email and phone support). Inspect Point says plans start at three technicians, or one or two technicians running 400 or more inspections a year. The trade-off: the field app is Apple-only, and the features that turn inspection findings into repair revenue sit on the Gold and Platinum plans, so price the plan you actually need.

BuildingReports makes mobile and web inspection reporting software for fire, life-safety and security systems. The company is based in Suwanee, Georgia, was founded in 2000, and marked 25 years in business in April 2025. It serves three groups: service companies that inspect buildings, facility managers and national accounts, and fire safety officials (AHJs) who review compliance. It also has Canada and Latin America operations.

The core product is ScanSeries, a mobile inspection suite for iOS and Android with barcode scanning. It is split into apps by system: FireScan for fire alarms, SprinklerScan, SuppressionScan for kitchen hood systems, SafetyScan for life-safety equipment, SecurityScan for low-voltage security and HVACScan for mechanical work. ScanSeries can be licensed one app at a time, as several apps, or as the full suite. ManagerSeries covers scheduling, dispatch and work tracking, BRForms handles digital forms on mobile and web, and customizable web portals give customers access to their reports. For fire officials there is a web-based compliance reporting hub.

BuildingReports said in April 2025 that its network had passed 13 million inspections and included more than 1,400 service and facility management companies. It integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics and ServiceTrade, and sends reports to compliance platforms including IROL, LIV, Brycer's The Compliance Engine and the FDNY extinguisher filing process. An API supports custom integrations. QuickBooks is listed on its integrations page as coming soon.

Pricing is not published; you request a quote. The trade-off: BuildingReports is built around the inspection report and the compliance record. Its product pages do not describe quoting or invoicing tools, so a contractor that bills from QuickBooks or another system should confirm in a demo how inspection work gets from BuildingReports to an invoice.

Uptick is inspection and service software for fire protection businesses. It started in Australia in 2014, founded by CEO Aidan Lister, and now has offices in Melbourne (Australia and New Zealand), London (UK and Ireland) and Denver (North America). Accel-KKR made a growth investment in Uptick in July 2021, and in August 2023 Uptick acquired FireMate, an Australian fire maintenance software company. Uptick says it has more than 1,200 fire and security customers managing over 2.5 million buildings and 40 million assets.

The product is built around assets. Technicians work from asset lists and digital inspection forms built around local standards, record deficiencies, and send deficiency quotes straight from the field. The iPhone and Android app has an offline mode, so inspections and reports continue without signal. Floorplans help technicians and customers find assets on site.

In the office, Uptick handles recurring inspection scheduling, an AI scheduler, route suggestions for technicians, sales quoting for installs and inspections, billing and invoicing, inventory, timesheets, install projects and reports. A customer portal lets clients see the work done on their buildings. Integrations include QuickBooks, Xero, Sage and MYOB for accounting, The Compliance Engine for report submission, and Joyfill, Honeywell and Locatrix.

Uptick does not publish its rate. Its pricing page describes a per-user monthly fee for each desk and field user, with unlimited free customer and subcontractor licenses, monthly invoicing, no annual upfront payment and the option to cancel at any time. The trade-off: Uptick is a deep, asset-level system, and it says most companies can be up and running within two months depending on team size and data migration, so a small shop with simple inspections may find it more than it needs.

A one-time setup fee covers a dedicated setup coach and onboarding; the amount is not published. No long-term contracts; seasonal pause at $50/mo for up to 4 months per calendar year. Verified against responsibid.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Window-cleaning, pressure-washing, gutter, carpet, maid and similar home service businesses that want instant online quotes, customer self-scheduling and automated follow-up, connected to a CRM such as Jobber or Housecall Pro
tools.weaknesses: A quoting and sales tool rather than a full business system: ResponsiBid says it is not a CRM and works best paired with one for invoicing and job management. Follow-up, CRM connections and self-scheduling start on the $179 Scaling plan, and the one-time setup fee is not published.
tools.long_description:
ResponsiBid is quoting and sales software for home service businesses. Its pricing page names window cleaning, pressure washing, gutter cleaning, maid services, carpet and tile cleaning, pest control and dog waste removal. It is made by Symphosize, LLC, which does business as ResponsiBid and lists an address in Queen Creek, Arizona. Founder Curt Kempton built it while he was running his own window-cleaning business.

The core is a quoting calculator. You set up your services, service tiers, bundles and automatic upsells, then quote in person, over the phone or through an instant quote form on your website, and the quote is presented as a proposal with package pricing. Customers can choose services and book a time themselves, and the CrewCal feature suggests dates based on your calendar and drive time. After the quote, customizable follow-up sequences send emails and text messages, and the SendJim integration adds postcards, letters and voicemail drops. A sales pipeline, customer profiles and custom statuses track where each lead stands.

ResponsiBid says it is not a CRM and is built to work alongside one. Direct connections push leads and scheduled work into Jobber, Housecall Pro, The Customer Factor, ServiceMonster and Markate, and scheduled jobs sync to Google Calendar. Zapier covers other tools. Other integrations include SendJim (mail), NiceJob (review invitations), Quality Driven Software (customer surveys), Twilio and PayPal (collecting a deposit before a customer self-schedules).

The Startup plan is free and covers the quoting calculator, service tiers, bundles, upsells and instant website quoting. Scaling is $179 a month and adds the CRM connections, sales pipeline, email and text follow-up, calendar scheduling, CrewCal and customer self-scheduling. Pro is $229 a month and adds the PayPal, NiceJob and Quality Driven Software integrations, account success coaching and access to the user group. Every plan includes 1 admin user and unlimited sub-users. ResponsiBid charges a one-time setup fee that pays for a dedicated setup coach, but it does not publish the amount. It says there are no long-term contracts, and seasonal businesses can pause for $50 a month for up to 4 months a calendar year.

The trade-off: ResponsiBid covers the front of the sale (quote, follow-up, booking) and leaves invoicing and day-to-day job management to your CRM, so you pay for two systems. It fits businesses with enough quote requests that faster quoting and steady follow-up cover the monthly fee.

pros_detail.title: Quotes in person, by phone or on your website
pros_detail.explanation: The same quoting calculator works face to face, on a call screen during phone calls, and as an instant quote form on your website, so every customer gets consistent prices.

pros_detail.title: Tiers, bundles and upsells built in
pros_detail.explanation: You can offer several service tiers, discount bundles and automatic upsells in the quote, which helps raise the ticket size without extra effort from the salesperson.

pros_detail.title: Automated follow-up on several channels
pros_detail.explanation: Follow-up sequences send emails and texts automatically, and the SendJim integration adds postcards, letters and voicemail drops to the same sequence.

pros_detail.title: Customer self-scheduling
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can pick their services and book a time themselves, and CrewCal suggests dates based on your calendar and drive time.

pros_detail.title: Connects to common home service CRMs
pros_detail.explanation: Leads and scheduled work flow into Jobber, Housecall Pro, The Customer Factor, ServiceMonster or Markate, with Zapier for other tools.

pros_detail.title: Free plan to start
pros_detail.explanation: The Startup plan is free and includes the quoting calculator and instant website quoting, with 1 admin user and unlimited sub-users.

cons_detail.title: Needs a CRM alongside it
cons_detail.explanation: ResponsiBid says it is not a CRM. Invoicing and day-to-day job management happen in a separate system, which means a second subscription.

cons_detail.title: Setup fee not published
cons_detail.explanation: There is a one-time setup fee for a dedicated setup coach, but the pricing page does not show the amount. Ask for it in writing before you sign up.

cons_detail.title: Key features start at $179 a month
cons_detail.explanation: Email and text follow-up, CRM connections, calendar scheduling and customer self-scheduling are on Scaling ($179 a month), not the free plan.

cons_detail.title: Coaching and some integrations on Pro only
cons_detail.explanation: Account success coaching, the user group and the PayPal, NiceJob and Quality Driven Software integrations require Pro at $229 a month.

cons_detail.title: Narrow trade focus
cons_detail.explanation: It is built for cleaning and exterior service menus such as windows, pressure washing and gutters. Trades with custom, project-style estimates may find it a poor fit.

tools.implementation_notes: Pick the CRM that runs your jobs and invoices first, and check that it is on ResponsiBid's integration list (Jobber, Housecall Pro, The Customer Factor, ServiceMonster, Markate) or reachable through Zapier. Setup is run with a dedicated coach paid for by the setup fee, and ResponsiBid says watching its Certification Videos before the setup meetings shortens the process. Enter your services and prices first, then your tiers, bundles and upsells, then build the email and text follow-up sequences (and SendJim mail if you use it). Once the quote flow works, add the instant quote form to your website, connect Google Calendar or your CRM calendar, and turn on customer self-scheduling. If your business is seasonal, ask about the $50-a-month pause option.

tool_faqs.q: How much does ResponsiBid cost?
tool_faqs.a: The Startup plan is free. Scaling is $179 a month and Pro is $229 a month. Every plan includes 1 admin user and unlimited sub-users. There is also a one-time setup fee for a dedicated setup coach; ResponsiBid does not publish the amount. Budget for your CRM subscription too.

tool_faqs.q: Is ResponsiBid a CRM?
tool_faqs.a: No. ResponsiBid says it is a sales tool built to work with your CRM of choice. It handles quoting, follow-up and booking, and passes leads and scheduled work to the CRM where you manage jobs and invoices.

tool_faqs.q: Which CRMs does ResponsiBid connect to?
tool_faqs.a: Its integrations page lists Jobber, Housecall Pro, The Customer Factor, ServiceMonster and Markate, plus Google Calendar sync. Other tools can be reached through Zapier. The CRM connections start on the Scaling plan.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a contract?
tool_faqs.a: ResponsiBid's pricing page says there are no long-term contracts and you can cancel anytime. Seasonal businesses can pause their account for $50 a month for up to 4 months a calendar year.

tool_faqs.q: Who is ResponsiBid for?
tool_faqs.a: Home service businesses that sell from a service menu, such as window cleaning, pressure washing, gutter cleaning, maid service, carpet and tile cleaning, pest control and dog waste removal, and that get enough quote requests for automated follow-up to matter.

tools.name: The Customer Factor
tools.tagline: Flat-price CRM and scheduling software for window cleaners, pressure washers and cleaning services

pricing.pricing_note: One flat plan: $44.95/mo billed monthly, or $449.50/yr (2 months free, about $37.46/mo). Unlimited employees and subusers, unlimited emails and uploads, no contracts, no setup fees. 30-day money-back period rather than a free trial. Automated texts cost $0.0075 per message. The company says members keep their join price while subscribed, and it has announced a move to 3 tiers with limits on the lower two. Verified against thecustomerfactor.com/pricing and /join-now 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Owner-operators and small crews in window cleaning, pressure washing, carpet cleaning and house cleaning who want one flat monthly price for customers, scheduling, invoicing and automated reminders
tools.weaknesses: The vendor has announced a move from one flat plan to three tiers, with limits on the lower two. Automated texts cost extra per message, and the features page describes Google Maps daily directions rather than route optimization. It does not list online booking or a customer portal.
tools.long_description:
The Customer Factor is a CRM built for service businesses such as window cleaners, pressure washers, carpet cleaners and house cleaning companies. The company says Steve Wright, its CEO and President, started it in 2004 while he owned a window-cleaning business and was tired of tracking customers on index cards.

It is built around repeat service. Each customer has a service frequency, a quick summary shows who is due to be contacted, and drip campaigns send a series of automated emails as a customer's next service comes due. You schedule estimates, jobs, appointments and tasks on color-coded calendars, create invoices in five customizable formats, and send confirmation, reminder, thank-you and receipt emails automatically. Automated text confirmations, reminders and thank-you messages cost $0.0075 per message. After a job, it can email customers a review request that sends happy customers to sites such as Google and Facebook.

Card payments run through Square, Stripe or Worldpay, and customers can pay from the invoice email. It syncs with QuickBooks Online (automatically each night) or QuickBooks Desktop, and it links to Google Maps for printable daily directions. iOS and Android apps let crews schedule, take photos and videos, create and email invoices, and clock in and out. Reports cover sales, profit and loss, employee pay and hours, taxes collected, expenses and an income forecast. ResponsiBid, a separate quoting tool, lists The Customer Factor as a direct integration.

Pricing is one flat plan: $44.95 a month, or $449.50 a year (two months free). The pricing page lists unlimited employees, unlimited subusers, unlimited emails, uploads and data, no contracts, no setup fees and a 30-day money-back period. The company says members keep their join price for as long as they stay subscribed. It has also announced a move to three pricing tiers, with limits on the two lower tiers, so check the current offer before you join.

The trade-off: it is a compact tool for small cleaning operations. The features page describes Google Maps directions rather than route optimization, texts cost extra, and online booking and a customer portal are not listed. Businesses that want instant online quotes can add ResponsiBid on top.

pros_detail.title: One flat price with unlimited users
pros_detail.explanation: $44.95 a month or $449.50 a year covers unlimited employees and subusers, so adding crew members does not raise the bill.

pros_detail.title: Built around repeat service
pros_detail.explanation: Service frequencies drive a list of customers who are due, plus drip emails as their next service comes up, which suits window cleaning and other recurring work.

pros_detail.title: Automated emails, texts and review requests
pros_detail.explanation: Confirmations, reminders, thank-you notes and receipts go out automatically by email, texts are available per message, and review requests follow completed jobs.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks Online or Desktop
pros_detail.explanation: It syncs with either version of QuickBooks, with automatic nightly transfers for QuickBooks Online.

pros_detail.title: Mobile apps with a time clock
pros_detail.explanation: iOS and Android apps handle scheduling, photos, videos and invoices in the field, and include clock in and clock out.

pros_detail.title: Low-risk start
pros_detail.explanation: There is no contract and no setup fee, and the company refunds the payment if you cancel within the first 30 days.

cons_detail.title: Announced pricing change
cons_detail.explanation: The vendor says it is moving to three tiers, with limits on the two lower tiers. No date or tier prices are published yet.

cons_detail.title: Texts cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Automated text messages are billed at $0.0075 per message on top of the subscription.

cons_detail.title: Basic routing
cons_detail.explanation: The features page describes printable Google Maps daily directions, not route optimization for multiple crews.

cons_detail.title: No online booking listed
cons_detail.explanation: Online booking and a customer portal are not on the features page. For instant online quotes, businesses pair it with a tool such as ResponsiBid.

tools.implementation_notes: Start by entering or importing your customers with their service frequency, since service due dates drive the quick summary and the drip campaigns. Set up your services, pick an invoice format and turn on the automated confirmation, reminder, thank-you and receipt emails, then add employees or crews. Connect one of the supported card processors (Square, Stripe or Worldpay) and choose QuickBooks Online or Desktop sync if you use QuickBooks. Install the iOS or Android app on crew phones. Use the 30-day money-back window to run real jobs through it; to cancel, call or email support.

tool_faqs.q: How much does The Customer Factor cost?
tool_faqs.a: $44.95 a month, or $449.50 a year (two months free, about $37.46 a month). There are no per-user fees and no setup fees. The company has announced a move to three pricing tiers, with limits on the two lower tiers, so confirm the current offer before joining.

tool_faqs.q: Does it charge per user?
tool_faqs.a: No. The pricing page lists unlimited employees and unlimited subusers on the current plan.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: No free trial is listed. Instead there is a 30-day money-back period: cancel within 30 days of signing up and the payment is refunded. After that, cancelling stops future charges, but the last payment is not refunded.

tool_faqs.q: Does The Customer Factor work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. It syncs with QuickBooks Online, with automatic nightly transfers, or with QuickBooks Desktop through a manual sync.

tool_faqs.q: Does it handle recurring services?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Each customer has a service frequency, the software shows who is due, and drip campaigns email customers as their next service approaches.

tool_faqs.q: The Customer Factor vs ResponsiBid?
tool_faqs.a: They do different jobs. The Customer Factor is a CRM for scheduling, invoicing and customer follow-up. ResponsiBid is a quoting and booking tool that sends leads into a CRM, and The Customer Factor is one of the CRMs it connects to.

tools.name: Solargraf
tools.tagline: Solar design, proposal and permitting software owned by Enphase, sold on annual plans with project and user limits

pricing.pricing_note: Billed annually per company: Starter $2,799 a year (about $233 a month) for 2 users and 240 projects; Small Business $4,799 a year for 4 users and 480 projects; Teams $6,399 a year for 6 users and 720 projects; Enterprise $12,999 a year for unlimited users and 1,500 projects. Tier prices above are monthly equivalents. Extra projects cost $11, $10, $9 and $9 each by plan; extra users cost $1,440, $1,200 and $960 a year on Starter, Small Business and Teams. Public API access is $4,000 a year, included in Enterprise. No monthly plan or free trial is shown. Verified against solargraf.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential solar installers and sales teams, especially Enphase installers, who want design, proposals, financing and permit plan sets in one tool and can commit to an annual plan
tools.weaknesses: Annual billing only, with no monthly plan or published free trial; each plan caps projects and users, with per-project and per-user overage fees; public API access costs $4,000 a year below Enterprise
tools.long_description:
Solargraf is solar design, proposal and permitting software for installers. Enphase Energy owns it: Enphase bought Sofdesk, the Montreal company that built Solargraf, in January 2021 and still develops the product. From one account, a rep can design a system, build a proposal with financing, collect a signature and generate permit plan sets. Solargraf says more than 1,000 customers use it, and its site lists support for 16 languages.

The design side includes AI-assisted layouts, shading tools and battery design, and Solargraf's site says it covers both residential and commercial projects. Enphase says LightReach, EnFin and GoodLeap are fully integrated for third-party ownership (TPO) financing, and that NREL validated Solargraf's production modeling against measured PV system data (September 2025 announcement). It links to Enphase Enlighten, connects to DocuSign for e-signatures and offers a public API. In April 2026 Enerflo announced an integration that syncs Solargraf designs into its platform for US companies that subscribe to both.

Prices are published and billed annually per company. Starter is $2,799 a year for 2 users and 240 projects. Small Business is $4,799 a year for 4 users and 480 projects. Teams is $6,399 a year for 6 users and 720 projects. Enterprise is $12,999 a year for unlimited users and 1,500 projects. Extra projects cost $9 to $11 each and extra users $960 to $1,440 a year, depending on the plan. Public API access is $4,000 a year on the lower plans and included in Enterprise.

Solargraf is not limited to Enphase hardware: its 2025 product recap says it supports more than 30 batteries, including all Enphase batteries. Enphase has also released it in the Netherlands, Germany, Austria and Japan. The trade-off: there is no monthly plan and no published free trial, so the entry cost is $2,799 up front, and busy teams need to watch the project and user limits. Installers who mainly sell other brands may want to compare it with tools such as Aurora Solar or OpenSolar.

pros_detail.title: Design to permit in one tool
pros_detail.explanation: Solargraf's pricing page lists proposals, shading tools, design, permitting, financing and a CRM on every plan, so reps and office staff work from the same project.

pros_detail.title: Owned by Enphase
pros_detail.explanation: Enphase develops Solargraf and links it to Enphase Enlighten, with Enphase-specific design options such as battery oversizing and power control support. That suits installers who sell Enphase microinverters and batteries.

pros_detail.title: Financing inside the proposal
pros_detail.explanation: Enphase says LightReach, EnFin and GoodLeap are fully integrated for TPO financing, so reps can show financing options in the proposal.

pros_detail.title: Published prices
pros_detail.explanation: All four plans and their overage fees are on the pricing page, which makes budgeting easier than with quote-only tools.

pros_detail.title: Independent check on production modeling
pros_detail.explanation: Enphase says NREL validated Solargraf's performance against measured PV system data and found accuracy comparable to NREL's own System Advisor Model.

cons_detail.title: Annual billing only
cons_detail.explanation: Every plan is priced per year, starting at $2,799, and the pricing page shows no monthly option or free trial.

cons_detail.title: Project and user limits
cons_detail.explanation: Each plan includes a set number of projects and users. Extra projects cost $9 to $11 each and extra users $960 to $1,440 a year, depending on the plan.

cons_detail.title: API access costs extra below Enterprise
cons_detail.explanation: The public API is a $4,000 a year add-on on Starter, Small Business and Teams. It is included only in Enterprise.

cons_detail.title: Enphase-specific features
cons_detail.explanation: Several features, such as Enlighten integration and Enphase battery oversizing, only help Enphase installers. Installers who mainly sell other brands should confirm their equipment and workflows are covered.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo, since no self-serve trial is published. Pick a plan by counting both users and projects per year, and price out overage fees before you commit to annual billing. Set up proposal templates, financing partners and branding, then connect DocuSign from the External Integrations page. If you sell Enphase equipment, link Enphase Enlighten. If you need a CRM connection, check whether your CRM (for example Enerflo) already integrates, or budget for the $4,000 a year API add-on, which is included in Enterprise. Run a few past jobs through the design and production tools and compare the results with your current process before rolling it out to every rep.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Solargraf?
tool_faqs.a: Enphase Energy. Enphase closed its purchase of Sofdesk, the Montreal company that built Solargraf, in January 2021 and still develops the product.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Solargraf cost?
tool_faqs.a: Plans are billed annually: Starter $2,799 a year (2 users, 240 projects), Small Business $4,799 (4 users, 480 projects), Teams $6,399 (6 users, 720 projects) and Enterprise $12,999 (unlimited users, 1,500 projects). Extra projects cost $9 to $11 each, extra users $960 to $1,440 a year, and public API access is $4,000 a year unless you are on Enterprise.

tool_faqs.q: Does Solargraf have a free trial or a monthly plan?
tool_faqs.a: The pricing page shows annual plans only and does not mention a free trial. The site offers a demo instead.

tool_faqs.q: Does Solargraf only work with Enphase equipment?
tool_faqs.a: No. Solargraf's 2025 product recap says it supports more than 30 batteries, including all Enphase batteries. It adds Enphase-specific features on top, such as Enlighten integration.

tool_faqs.q: What does Solargraf integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: DocuSign for e-signatures, Enphase Enlighten, TPO financiers (Enphase says LightReach, EnFin and GoodLeap are fully integrated), Enerflo (announced April 2026) and a public API for connecting a CRM.

tool_faqs.q: Can Solargraf create permit plan sets?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Permitting is included on every plan, and Solargraf says it auto-generates permit plan sets that meet local compliance standards. Its site also advertises permit services with expert review and stamps.

tools.name: Scoop
tools.tagline: Configurable operations platform for solar, storage, EV charging and other energy field teams, with unlimited users

pricing.pricing_note: No prices published. Scoop's pricing page asks for company and team details to send tailored pricing, and its FAQ says pricing depends on modules, workflows and installation or service volume. All plans include unlimited users, storage and devices. Verified against scoop.solar/pricing and scoop.solar/faq 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Solar installers, O&M providers and other energy and infrastructure contractors that need to standardize project workflows, field checklists and scheduling across office staff, crews and subcontractors
tools.weaknesses: No published prices; it runs operations, not solar design or sales proposals, so most solar companies pair it with other tools; the no-code setup and integrations take planning up front
tools.long_description:
Scoop is a no-code operations platform for renewable energy and infrastructure teams, made by Scoop Robotix Inc. of Vancouver, British Columbia. Its site says the company was started by two engineers and turned its focus to solar and renewables in 2017-2018. Today it markets Scoop to commercial and residential solar, solar and wind O&M, EV charging, battery storage, modular construction, data centers, home energy services and telecom. Scoop says more than 250,000 project sites use it.

The core is project management with configurable stages, task ownership and automated actions (Scoop calls them Auto Actions) that create tasks, send emails and hand off work when set conditions are met. Field crews use a native mobile app for iOS and Android to complete checklists, capture photos and update jobs, and Scoop says the app works offline and syncs when a connection returns. Other modules cover scheduling and dispatch, LOOXY dashboards and reporting, and IMRP inventory and resource planning.

Integrations run through GLOO, Scoop's integration service, which it says offers more than 500 integration connections. Scoop has integration pages for QuickBooks Online, Zapier, Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, DocuSign, CompanyCam, Aurora Solar, OpenSolar, Solargraf, Enerflo and many more. Its FAQ says onboarding is guided by a dedicated success team that helps with workflow mapping, integrations, data migration and training.

Scoop does not publish prices. Its FAQ says pricing depends on modules, workflows and installation or service volume, and every plan includes unlimited users, so office staff, technicians, partners and subcontractors can all have accounts. The trade-off: you need a sales conversation to learn the cost, and Scoop handles operations rather than design or proposals, so a solar company still needs a separate design and sales tool.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Scoop's FAQ says all plans include unlimited users, so you can give subcontractors and partners access without paying per seat.

pros_detail.title: Workflow automation
pros_detail.explanation: Configurable project stages and Auto Actions create tasks, send emails and hand off work when set conditions are met, which cuts manual follow-up.

pros_detail.title: Field app that works offline
pros_detail.explanation: The native mobile app handles checklists, photos and job updates, and Scoop says data syncs once the device is back online.

pros_detail.title: Wide integration catalog
pros_detail.explanation: GLOO connects Scoop to accounting, CRM, design and e-signature tools, including QuickBooks Online, Salesforce, HubSpot, Aurora Solar and Zapier.

pros_detail.title: Covers more than solar
pros_detail.explanation: Scoop supports solar, battery storage, EV charging, wind O&M and telecom work, which helps contractors that run several energy service lines.

pros_detail.title: Guided onboarding
pros_detail.explanation: Scoop says each customer gets a dedicated success manager who helps with workflow mapping, integrations, data migration and role-based training.

cons_detail.title: No public pricing
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page asks for company and team details before sending pricing, so you cannot compare cost up front.

cons_detail.title: Operations only
cons_detail.explanation: Scoop does not do system design or homeowner proposals. Solar companies typically run it next to a separate design and proposal tool.

cons_detail.title: Setup takes planning
cons_detail.explanation: Because it is no-code and highly configurable, you need to map stages, checklists and automations before it pays off.

cons_detail.title: Integrations are scoped per customer
cons_detail.explanation: Integrations are delivered through GLOO with data mappings set up for your workflows. Confirm which connections are in your quote and exactly what data syncs.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with a demo and a quote, since prices are not published. Before setup, write down your project stages, the photos and checklists each job type needs, and who owns each step. Scoop assigns a success manager to guide workflow mapping, integrations, data migration and role-based training. List the tools you need connected (for example your CRM, QuickBooks Online and your design software) and confirm with Scoop how each one connects through GLOO and what data syncs. Roll out in phases, starting with one workflow, then invite field crews and subcontractors to the mobile app, since users are unlimited.

tool_faqs.q: What is Scoop?
tool_faqs.a: A no-code operations platform for solar and other energy and infrastructure contractors. It covers project workflows, automated task handoffs, field checklists, scheduling and dispatch, reporting and inventory, with a mobile app for field crews. Scoop says more than 250,000 project sites use it.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Scoop cost?
tool_faqs.a: Scoop does not publish prices. Its FAQ says pricing depends on the modules, workflows and installation or service volume you need, and every plan includes unlimited users. You request pricing through a form on its pricing page.

tool_faqs.q: Does Scoop do solar design and proposals?
tool_faqs.a: No. Scoop handles operations after the sale. It integrates with design and proposal tools such as Aurora Solar, OpenSolar, Solargraf and Enerflo instead.

tool_faqs.q: What does Scoop integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Through its GLOO integration service, Scoop lists integrations with QuickBooks Online, Zapier, Salesforce, HubSpot, NetSuite, Pipedrive, DocuSign, Dropbox, Google Drive, CompanyCam, ServiceTitan, JobNimbus and many others. Scoop says GLOO offers more than 500 integration connections.

tool_faqs.q: Does the Scoop mobile app work offline?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, according to Scoop's FAQ: field teams can keep working offline, and data syncs when the connection returns. The app is available for iOS and Android.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Scoop?
tool_faqs.a: Scoop Robotix Inc., based in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its site says the company was started by two engineers and shifted its focus to solar and renewables in 2017-2018.

tools.name: Bodhi
tools.tagline: Customer experience platform for residential solar installers: automated project updates, a branded homeowner app, surveys and referrals

pricing.pricing_note: Free plan: $0, up to 5 new projects a month and 60 in total, no credit card required. Starter and Pro are sold as project packages and the pricing page does not show their prices. Paid packages are invoiced monthly in 12 equal installments based on package and project volume. Pro requires a CRM or project management integration. OneEthos solar installers get Bodhi free as a partner benefit. Verified against bodhi.solar/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential solar installers that want to keep homeowners updated from contract to activation, handle customer messages in one inbox, and collect reviews and referrals
tools.weaknesses: Starter and Pro prices are not published; CRM integration and the AI features require the Pro plan; it is a customer communication layer, not a design, proposal or full project management tool
tools.long_description:
Bodhi is customer experience software for residential solar companies. It gives homeowners a white-labeled app and project tracker, sends automated project updates, and puts text, email and in-app messages into one team inbox. The aim is fewer status calls and escalations in the months between contract and activation, and more reviews and referrals afterward.

OneEthos, a solar financing fintech that works with community banks, credit unions and green banks, announced on March 31, 2026 that it had acquired Bodhi. The product is still sold as Bodhi at bodhi.solar, and its pricing page says OneEthos solar installers get Bodhi free as a partner benefit.

The Free plan covers up to 5 new projects a month (60 in total) and includes the team inbox, the branded customer app and a document repository. Starter adds unlimited customer journeys, automated time-based project updates, e-signatures, and CSAT and NPS surveys with referral requests. Pro adds integration and data syncing with your CRM and cloud document storage, updates triggered by CRM data, AI sentiment analysis and an AI customer support agent. Bodhi lists CRM integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, Microsoft Dynamics, Pipedrive, Monday.com, Quick Base, Sunbase, SolarSuccess and others, plus Google Drive, Dropbox and Amazon S3 for documents.

Starter and Pro are sold as project packages. Bodhi does not show their prices, and it invoices paid packages monthly in 12 equal installments based on the package and project volume. The trade-off: the free plan is enough to test the homeowner app and inbox, but CRM-triggered updates and the AI features sit in Pro, and you need a sales call to price it.

pros_detail.title: Free plan to start
pros_detail.explanation: Bodhi Free costs nothing for up to 5 new projects a month (60 in total) and needs no credit card.

pros_detail.title: Branded homeowner app
pros_detail.explanation: Homeowners get a white-labeled app and project tracker, so they can check progress without calling the office.

pros_detail.title: One inbox for customer messages
pros_detail.explanation: Text, email and in-app messages from homeowners land in one shared team inbox.

pros_detail.title: Works with many solar CRMs
pros_detail.explanation: On Pro, Bodhi syncs with Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, Sunbase, SolarSuccess, Monday.com and other CRMs, so updates can follow the milestones you already track.

pros_detail.title: Surveys and referral requests
pros_detail.explanation: Starter and Pro include CSAT and NPS surveys and referral requests, so feedback and referrals are part of the customer journey.

pros_detail.title: Free for OneEthos installers
pros_detail.explanation: Installers who work with OneEthos get Bodhi at no cost, according to Bodhi's pricing page.

cons_detail.title: Paid prices not published
cons_detail.explanation: Starter and Pro are sold as project packages with no prices shown, so you need a sales conversation to budget.

cons_detail.title: Key features are Pro-only
cons_detail.explanation: CRM integration, CRM-triggered updates and the AI features are in Pro. Free and Starter run as standalone products.

cons_detail.title: Not a design or operations platform
cons_detail.explanation: Bodhi handles homeowner communication. You still need a CRM or project management tool and a design and proposal tool.

cons_detail.title: New owner
cons_detail.explanation: OneEthos bought Bodhi in March 2026. Ask how support, pricing and the product roadmap are handled under the new owner.

cons_detail.title: Installment billing
cons_detail.explanation: Paid packages are invoiced in 12 equal monthly installments based on your package. Ask about the contract term before you sign.

tools.implementation_notes: Start on Bodhi Free to test the homeowner app, project tracker and team inbox on a few new jobs. Decide which project milestones should trigger homeowner updates and write the message templates. If you want updates to fire from your CRM, you need Pro: check that your CRM is on Bodhi's integration list and plan the field mapping with Bodhi's customer success manager. Set up survey and referral requests for completed installs. Record your current call volume, escalations and referral share before launch so you can judge the results. If you work with OneEthos, ask whether your account qualifies for free access.

tool_faqs.q: What does Bodhi do?
tool_faqs.a: Bodhi keeps residential solar customers informed. It gives homeowners a branded app and project tracker, sends automated project updates, collects messages in one team inbox, and runs surveys and referral requests. It is a customer communication layer, not a design or operations tool.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Bodhi cost?
tool_faqs.a: Bodhi Free is $0 for up to 5 new projects a month and 60 in total, with no credit card. Starter and Pro are sold as project packages whose prices are not published, invoiced in 12 equal monthly installments. OneEthos installers get Bodhi free.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Bodhi?
tool_faqs.a: OneEthos, a solar financing fintech, announced its acquisition of Bodhi on March 31, 2026. The product is still sold under the Bodhi name.

tool_faqs.q: Does Bodhi replace my CRM?
tool_faqs.a: No. On the Pro plan Bodhi syncs with your CRM (for example Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, Sunbase or SolarSuccess) and with Google Drive, Dropbox or Amazon S3 for documents. Free and Starter run standalone.

tool_faqs.q: What AI features does Bodhi have?
tool_faqs.a: Pro includes AI sentiment analysis of customer messages and an AI customer support agent, according to Bodhi's pricing page.

tools.name: Pylon
tools.tagline: Pay-per-project solar design and proposal software from Sydney, with 3D shading, battery design and an optional solar CRM

pricing.pricing_note: Pay per project, with no subscription and no monthly minimum. The main (Australian) site lists Standard at $4.00 per project and Pro at $10.00 per project without labeling the currency; the UK site lists £4.00 and £10.00. New users get free credits for five Standard projects with no credit card. A project is one address with up to five designs, and revisits and edits are free. Unlimited team users. Enterprise (SSO, API support, dedicated support) is quoted. Add-ons: Solar CRM from $49 per user per month billed monthly; payment gateway 2.5% per transaction. Verified against getpylon.com/pricing and getpylon.com/uk/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Solar installers in Australia and the UK who want fast residential or commercial designs and proposals without a monthly subscription
tools.weaknesses: Built mainly for the Australian market, with a separate UK site and no US-specific site or pricing; the currency on the main pricing page is not labeled; the CRM is a separate per-user subscription; per-project charges add up at high volume
tools.long_description:
Pylon is solar design and proposal software made by Saru Technologies Pty. Ltd. in Sydney, Australia. Designers place panels on high-resolution imagery or on an uploaded blueprint or drone photo, run 3D shading simulations, and choose hardware from a library that Pylon says holds over 20,000 panels, inverters and batteries. Proposals come out as web pages and PDFs, and Pylon advertises solar proposals in 2 minutes.

Other tools include battery design with savings modeled against real electricity tariffs, automatic single-line diagrams (editable in Pylon since a July 2026 update), voltage rise reports, installer job sheets, customer owner's manuals and e-signatures. The main site is built for Australia, with Australian retailers, incentives and finance partners. A separate UK site covers MCS calculations, and the July 2026 update added MCS roof splitting for UK installers.

Pylon charges per project instead of a subscription. The main site lists Standard at $4.00 per project and Pro at $10.00 per project without labeling the currency, while the UK site shows £4.00 and £10.00. Pro adds custom load profiles, battery storage design and commercial-sized projects. A project is one address with up to five designs, and revisiting or editing a project costs nothing extra. New users get free credits for five Standard projects with no credit card, there is no monthly minimum, and teams can add unlimited users. Enterprise (single sign-on, API support, dedicated support) is quoted. The Solar CRM add-on starts at $49 per user per month, and the payment gateway charges 2.5% per transaction.

Integrations include Xero, ServiceM8, Mailchimp, Nearmap imagery, finance providers Brighte, Smart Ease and Solaris Finance, lead sources SolarQuotes, SolarChoice and Facebook Lead Ads, and Google Workspace and Microsoft 365. Pylon also offers an API with webhooks. The trade-off: pay-per-project pricing is cheap to try, but high-volume teams should compare the per-project total with a flat subscription, and installers outside Australia and the UK should confirm imagery, equipment and incentive support for their market first.

pros_detail.title: No subscription
pros_detail.explanation: You pay per project with no monthly minimum, and new users get free credits for five Standard projects with no credit card.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited team users
pros_detail.explanation: Pylon lets you add unlimited users to your team, so design costs depend on projects, not seats.

pros_detail.title: Fast proposals
pros_detail.explanation: Pylon advertises solar proposals in 2 minutes, delivered as web and PDF proposals with e-signatures.

pros_detail.title: Large equipment library
pros_detail.explanation: Pylon says its library holds over 20,000 panels, inverters and batteries, with filters for phases, type and MPPTs.

pros_detail.title: Battery and commercial work on Pro
pros_detail.explanation: Pro projects add battery storage design, custom load profiles and commercial-sized projects.

pros_detail.title: Install paperwork included
pros_detail.explanation: Single-line diagrams, voltage rise reports, installer job sheets and owner's manuals come out of the same design.

cons_detail.title: Australia first
cons_detail.explanation: The main site, incentives, retailers and finance partners are Australian. There is a UK site but no US version, so installers elsewhere should confirm coverage.

cons_detail.title: Currency not labeled
cons_detail.explanation: The main pricing page shows prices with a plain $ sign and GST notes. Confirm the currency and tax treatment for your country before budgeting.

cons_detail.title: Costs add up at volume
cons_detail.explanation: Per-project pricing is cheap to start, but a busy team should compare its monthly project total with flat-subscription tools.

cons_detail.title: CRM costs extra per user
cons_detail.explanation: The Solar CRM add-on starts at $49 per user per month, billed monthly, on top of project charges.

cons_detail.title: Imagery varies by country
cons_detail.explanation: Pylon says high-resolution imagery is available in select countries. Elsewhere you may need to upload a blueprint or drone photo.

tools.implementation_notes: Use the five free Standard project credits (no credit card) to design a few recent jobs and check imagery quality, shading results and whether your equipment is in the component library. If you sell batteries or do commercial work, upgrade a test project to Pro to try those tools. Set up proposal branding, tariffs and finance options, and connect Xero or ServiceM8 if you use them. Invite your team, since users are unlimited. Decide whether you need the Solar CRM add-on (from $49 per user per month) or keep using your current CRM, and contact Pylon support for API access if you want to connect other systems. Track your monthly project count for a few months to compare per-project costs with subscription tools.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Pylon cost?
tool_faqs.a: Pylon charges per project with no subscription or monthly minimum. The main (Australian) site lists Standard at $4.00 and Pro at $10.00 per project without a currency label; the UK site shows £4.00 and £10.00. New users get five free Standard project credits. Enterprise is quoted, and the Solar CRM add-on starts at $49 per user per month.

tool_faqs.q: Can Pylon design commercial systems?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, on Pro projects. Pylon's pricing page lists commercial-sized projects as a Pro feature, and its HelioScope comparison page quotes $10 per commercial project.

tool_faqs.q: Is Pylon available in the US?
tool_faqs.a: Pylon's main site targets Australia, and it runs a separate UK site. We did not find a US-specific site or US pricing, so US installers should confirm imagery, equipment and incentive support with Pylon before relying on it.

tool_faqs.q: What does Pylon integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Xero, ServiceM8, Mailchimp, Nearmap, finance providers Brighte, Smart Ease and Solaris Finance, lead sources SolarQuotes, SolarChoice and Facebook Lead Ads, and Google Workspace and Microsoft 365. It also has an API with webhooks; Pylon says using the API carries no extra charge.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Pylon?
tool_faqs.a: Saru Technologies Pty. Ltd., based in Sydney, Australia.

tools.name: Network Leads
tools.tagline: Moving leads, CRM, dispatch and email and SMS marketing from one vendor

pricing.pricing_note: Starter is $249 a month (3 office users, 50,000 emails a month). Growth is $399 a month (7 office users, 100,000 emails a month, developer hub and API access, dedicated success manager, priority support). Enterprise is custom-priced. The page offers 10% off for annual billing and has no long-term contracts. Leads are billed per lead ($15-$100), and add-ons include a phone system at $49 per user a month, a custom website at $99 a month plus $600 setup, and SEO at $29 a month. The page advertises a 14-day free trial and a 14-day money-back guarantee on every plan. Verified against network-leads.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Moving companies, van lines and relocation brokers that buy leads and want their CRM, dispatch, payments and email and SMS marketing in the same system
tools.weaknesses: Starter includes only 3 office users and Growth 7; leads, the phone system, websites and SEO are billed on top of the software. Support hours are weekdays 9am-6pm ET. Built only for the moving industry.
tools.long_description:
Network Leads sells moving leads and moving company software. The company says it was founded in 2017, lists its headquarters in Newark, Delaware, and says more than 1,000 moving companies use it. It serves moving companies, van lines and relocation brokers in all 50 states.

The software covers CRM and lead management with automated follow-ups, drag-and-drop scheduling and dispatch, an automation center, payments and invoicing through Stripe, e-signatures and bills of lading, and built-in calls, SMS and email. Marketing tools include email campaigns, SMS marketing, review requests and landing pages, and an AI assistant writes emails and summarizes calls. Storage and document management are included, and crews use a mobile crew panel in the browser with no app to download. Alongside the software, Network Leads sells pay-per-lead moving leads, websites and SEO, and commission-based sales agents.

Software pricing is published. Starter is $249 a month with 3 office users and 50,000 emails a month. Growth is $399 a month with 7 office users, 100,000 emails a month, a developer hub with API access and a dedicated success manager. Enterprise is priced by quote. The pricing page offers 10% off for annual billing, no long-term contracts, and a 14-day free trial backed by a 14-day money-back guarantee. Leads cost from $15 (a local lead shared with 4 movers) to $100 (an interstate live call transfer). The integrations page lists lead sources such as Angi Leads, HomeAdvisor and Thumbtack, plus Google Calendar, Gmail, Zapier, webhooks, Stripe, Authorize.net and NMI, and the software page says it connects with QuickBooks and Twilio.

The trade-off: Starter covers 3 office users and Growth 7, so a larger office needs Growth or an Enterprise quote. Add-ons such as the phone system ($49 per user a month), a custom website ($99 a month plus $600 setup) and leads add to the software fee. Support is listed as Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm Eastern. It is built only for the moving industry.

pros_detail.title: Leads and software from one vendor
pros_detail.explanation: Network Leads sells pay-per-lead moving leads and the CRM that works them, so leads land straight in the pipeline with automated follow-ups.

pros_detail.title: Published pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Starter is $249 a month and Growth $399 a month, with 10% off for annual billing and no long-term contracts.

pros_detail.title: Marketing built in
pros_detail.explanation: Email campaigns (50,000 to 100,000 emails a month by plan), SMS marketing, review requests and landing pages come with the software.

pros_detail.title: Many lead-source integrations
pros_detail.explanation: The integrations page lists more than a dozen lead sources, including Angi Leads, HomeAdvisor, moveBuddha and Thumbtack, plus Zapier and webhooks.

pros_detail.title: Low-risk start
pros_detail.explanation: The pricing page offers a 14-day free trial and a 14-day money-back guarantee, and the software page lists free training and data migration.

cons_detail.title: User caps
cons_detail.explanation: Starter includes 3 office users and Growth 7, so a growing office moves up a plan or to an Enterprise quote.

cons_detail.title: Add-ons add up
cons_detail.explanation: The phone system is $49 per user a month, a custom website $99 a month plus $600 setup, SEO $29 a month, and leads are billed per lead.

cons_detail.title: Weekday support hours
cons_detail.explanation: Support is listed as Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm Eastern, which can leave evening and weekend moves without live help.

cons_detail.title: Browser-based crew panel
cons_detail.explanation: Crews use a mobile crew panel in the browser rather than a native iOS or Android app.

cons_detail.title: Moving-industry only
cons_detail.explanation: Network Leads is built for movers, van lines and brokers and is not a general field service tool.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with the 14-day trial to test the workflow against how you book and run moves. Choose the plan by office headcount and email volume: Starter covers 3 office users and 50,000 emails a month, and Growth covers 7 users and 100,000 emails. Network Leads offers free training and data migration and says setup can be done in 24 hours. Connect your lead sources (such as Angi Leads, HomeAdvisor or Thumbtack) first, then set up automated follow-ups, dispatch, and payments through Stripe, Authorize.net or NMI. Give crews the browser-based crew panel, and build email and SMS campaigns once the pipeline is running.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Network Leads cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starter is $249 a month (3 office users, 50,000 emails a month) and Growth is $399 a month (7 office users, 100,000 emails a month, API access and a dedicated success manager). Enterprise is priced by quote. The pricing page offers 10% off for annual billing and has no long-term contracts.

tool_faqs.q: How much do Network Leads' moving leads cost?
tool_faqs.a: Leads are pay-per-lead with no monthly minimum: a local lead shared with 4 movers is $15 ($20 interstate), shared with 2 movers $28 ($38), exclusive $45 ($85), and a live call transfer $60 ($100). Network Leads has a 7-day credit policy for bad leads.

tool_faqs.q: Who is Network Leads for?
tool_faqs.a: Moving companies, van lines and relocation brokers across the US that want to buy leads and run their CRM, dispatch, payments and marketing in one system.

tool_faqs.q: Does Network Leads integrate with QuickBooks?
