tool_faqs.a: Its software page says it connects with QuickBooks, Stripe, Twilio and Google Calendar via API. The integrations page lists Google Calendar, Gmail, Zapier, webhooks, Stripe, Authorize.net and NMI, plus lead sources and website builders. Ask in a demo how the QuickBooks connection works.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The pricing page advertises a 14-day free trial and a 14-day money-back guarantee on every plan.

tools.name: Moveware
tools.tagline: Moving and storage ERP and CRM with its own built-in accounting package

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing. moveconnect.com (home, product suite, system features, support and implementation pages) shows no prices, so Moveware is priced by quote. Its integrated accounting package needs no additional licence. No free trial is published. Verified against moveconnect.com 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Mid-size and larger moving, relocation, international and storage companies that want one system for sales, surveys, operations, storage billing and accounting
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing. A full ERP rollout (configuration, templates, data import, training) takes more work than a small-business moving CRM. Few named third-party integrations. Head office and development are in Melbourne, Australia, with the Americas served from Toronto.
tools.long_description:
Moveware is ERP and CRM software for the moving and storage industry, sold through its website moveconnect.com. Brothers Dean and Tony Kent set up the company in Melbourne, Australia, in 2001 after buying the rights to an earlier moving package, Removals 2000, and the company says they still own it and work in the business full time. Moveware has offices in Melbourne (head office and development), London, Toronto and Bangkok (support), and says more than 300 companies in 35 countries use it, handling more than 500,000 moves a year.

The core Moveware system covers pre-move sales, CRM, operations planning, manifesting, post-move reviews, storage management with automatic storage billing, and more than 200 built-in reports. It includes its own accounting package, with invoices, online payments, receivables, supplier management, banking, general ledger and budgets, at no extra licence cost. Moveware says it can also connect to external accounting programs, but that 85% of its clients keep all their accounting inside the system. It supports multi-company, multi-branch, multi-country and multi-currency operations.

Around the core sit several apps and portals: MobiSurvey for room-by-room pre-move surveys, MobiCrew for crews to view job instructions, complete packing lists and inventories and collect signatures, MoveClient for customers to track their move and send leads through your website, MovePartner for corporate accounts and agents to track moves and approve quotes, and MoveTransfer for exchanging shipment details electronically with partners and agents. Moveware serves international, domestic, commercial, fine art, military, van line and storage companies, and says support is available 24 hours a day from its regional offices.

The trade-off: Moveware does not publish prices, and its implementation runs through planning, configuration, installation, document and report writing, data import, training and a review, which is more work than signing up for a small-business moving CRM. It suits companies with complex, international or multi-branch operations more than a single-truck local mover.

pros_detail.title: Accounting built in
pros_detail.explanation: Moveware includes its own accounting package (receivables, supplier management, banking, general ledger and budgets) with no extra licence, so jobs and financials live in one system.

pros_detail.title: Built for complex moves
pros_detail.explanation: It handles international export, import and third-country moves as well as fine art, military, commercial, van line and storage work, with multi-company, multi-branch and multi-currency support.

pros_detail.title: Apps for every party
pros_detail.explanation: MobiSurvey for surveyors, MobiCrew for crews, MoveClient for customers and MovePartner for corporate accounts and agents all connect to the same system.

pros_detail.title: Deep reporting
pros_detail.explanation: More than 200 built-in reports plus online dashboards, with output to Excel and PDF.

pros_detail.title: Support around the clock
pros_detail.explanation: Moveware says its support teams cover 24 hours a day from offices in Melbourne, Bangkok, London and Toronto.

pros_detail.title: Stable ownership
pros_detail.explanation: The same two founders have run the company since 2001, according to Moveware.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Moveware shows no prices on its site, so you need a quote for the modules, apps and users you want.

cons_detail.title: Heavier implementation
cons_detail.explanation: Moveware's own rollout process covers planning, configuration, installation, custom templates and reports, data import, training and a review.

cons_detail.title: More than a small mover needs
cons_detail.explanation: Multi-company accounting, international move handling and partner portals are more system than a single-truck local mover is likely to use.

cons_detail.title: Few named integrations
cons_detail.explanation: Moveware offers an integration API and says it can connect to external accounting programs, but its site does not name specific integrations such as QuickBooks.

cons_detail.title: Head office outside the US
cons_detail.explanation: Development and the head office are in Melbourne, and the Americas office is in Toronto. US buyers should ask for references from companies in their region.

tools.implementation_notes: Moveware describes a structured implementation: a project plan with tasks, timelines and a go-live date, then configuration of the database to your processes, software installation, custom quote and invoice templates and reports, import of your customer, vendor and inventory data, role-based staff training, and a final implementation review. Decide early whether you will run accounting inside Moveware or keep an external package, since that changes what you import. Ask about the cloud hosting option and which apps (MobiSurvey, MobiCrew, MoveClient, MovePartner, MoveTransfer) you need, and get all of them itemized in the written quote.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Moveware cost?
tool_faqs.a: Moveware does not publish prices. Its site shows no pricing, so you need a quote for the modules, apps and users you need.

tool_faqs.q: Does Moveware include accounting?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Moveware includes an integrated accounting package with invoices, receivables, supplier management, banking, general ledger and budgets, with no additional licence. It says it can connect to external accounting programs, but that 85% of clients keep all accounting inside Moveware.

tool_faqs.q: Where is Moveware based?
tool_faqs.a: Its head office and development team are in Melbourne, Australia. It also has offices in London and Toronto (which covers the Americas) and a support office in Bangkok.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Moveware?
tool_faqs.a: Brothers Dean and Tony Kent founded Moveware in 2001. According to the company, they still own it and work in the business full time.

tool_faqs.q: Is Moveware right for a small moving company?
tool_faqs.a: It can be configured for small operators, but its depth (multi-company accounting, international moves, partner portals) and formal implementation fit mid-size and larger companies best. A small local mover may be better served by a lighter moving CRM.

tools.name: PSA
tools.tagline: Restoration job management, CRM and built-in construction accounting from Canam Systems

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing or setup fee on canamsys.com; buyers request a demo and a quote. PSA is sold as Proven modules (Jobs, Accounting, CRM, OnSite, Analytics). Verified against canamsys.com 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Property restoration contractors, including franchise groups, that want job management, CRM and full accounting (general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll and work-in-process) in one system tied to Xactimate and XactAnalysis
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing (demo and quote only); a broad system with accounting, payroll and job costing takes real setup and training; switching means replacing more than a job tracker; restoration focused, so not a fit for other trades
tools.long_description:
PSA is restoration software from Canam Systems, a company founded in 1994 that describes itself as independently owned. Its listed office is in Barrie, Ontario, Tolga Tari is President and CEO, and Canam says it serves more than 1,500 restoration contractors, including a number of franchise groups, across North America.

PSA is sold as a set of modules under the Proven name: Proven Jobs (job management), Proven Accounting, Proven CRM, Proven OnSite (customer communication) and Proven Analytics. Proven Jobs covers job intake and dispatch (Canam says in 30 seconds or less), budgets for labor, materials, subcontractors and miscellaneous costs, real-time job cost recognition, work-in-progress automation, electronic timecards, e-signatures, equipment and materials tracking, Gantt-chart production views and calendar reminders. Its mobile app works offline and includes a dry logs module for site readings. Proven Accounting adds a general ledger and banking, payables and receivables, purchase orders, automatic work-in-process and over/under-billing calculations, inventory costing and integrated payroll.

Canam lists integrations with Xactimate and XactAnalysis, CoreLogic Symbility, Encircle, Matterport, DocuSketch, Moisture Mapper and QuickBooks, plus partners for payroll (ADP, Paychex, CheckMark, EasyPay), payments (Gravity Payments), communications (Twilio, Mailchimp, Mailgun), moisture meters (Tramex), floor plans (magicplan), asset tracking (Nero, Invisi-Tag, Camcode) and answering services.

Canam does not publish PSA pricing; buyers request a demo. Training options include customized onboarding, on-site training in your office, online training and the Proven Academy online courses. Support is by phone Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 7 PM Eastern, with an emergency after-hours line.

The trade-off: PSA can replace several tools, including your accounting system if you use Proven Accounting, so switching is a bigger project than adding a job tracker. Get a written quote that lists modules, users and any setup or training charges, since none are published.

pros_detail.title: Accounting built for restoration
pros_detail.explanation: Proven Accounting includes a general ledger, payables and receivables, purchase orders, inventory costing and integrated payroll, so job and financial data live in one system.

pros_detail.title: Real-time job costing and WIP
pros_detail.explanation: Budgets for labor, materials, subcontractors and miscellaneous costs, real-time job cost recognition and automatic work-in-process and over/under-billing calculations show job profitability while work is under way.

pros_detail.title: Insurance software connections
pros_detail.explanation: PSA integrates with Xactimate and XactAnalysis and with CoreLogic Symbility, so estimates from either insurance estimating platform can flow into PSA.

pros_detail.title: Wide partner list
pros_detail.explanation: Integrations cover documentation (Encircle, Matterport, DocuSketch, Moisture Mapper), payroll (ADP, Paychex), communications (Twilio, Mailchimp), moisture meters and asset tracking.

pros_detail.title: Training options
pros_detail.explanation: Canam offers customized onboarding, on-site and online training, the Proven Academy courses and bi-weekly Lunch and Learn sessions.

pros_detail.title: Long track record
pros_detail.explanation: Canam Systems was founded in 1994 and says it serves more than 1,500 restoration contractors across North America, including franchise groups.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: Canam publishes no PSA prices or setup fees, so you need a demo and a written quote to compare costs.

cons_detail.title: A bigger switch
cons_detail.explanation: Because PSA can include accounting and payroll, moving to it can mean replacing your books as well as your job tracker, which takes planning and training.

cons_detail.title: Restoration focus
cons_detail.explanation: PSA is built for property restoration and cleaning contractors and is not a fit for other trades.

cons_detail.title: Weekday support hours
cons_detail.explanation: Standard support runs Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 7 PM Eastern; outside those hours there is an emergency line.

tools.implementation_notes: Request a demo from Canam Systems and ask for a written quote covering the Proven modules you need, your user count and any setup or training fees. Decide early whether Proven Accounting replaces your current books or whether you keep QuickBooks connected. Set up job-cost budgets for labor, materials, subcontractors and miscellaneous costs, then connect Xactimate and XactAnalysis (or Symbility) so estimates and assignments flow in, along with documentation tools you use such as Encircle, Matterport or DocuSketch. Use the customized onboarding and on-site or online training, and point staff to the Proven Academy courses. Roll out the mobile app with the dry logs module to field technicians.

tool_faqs.q: How much does PSA cost?
tool_faqs.a: Canam Systems does not publish PSA pricing or setup fees. Request a demo and a written quote for the modules and number of users you need.

tool_faqs.q: Does PSA integrate with Xactimate and QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Canam lists integrations with Xactimate and XactAnalysis, CoreLogic Symbility and QuickBooks, along with Encircle, Matterport, DocuSketch and Moisture Mapper.

tool_faqs.q: Does PSA include accounting?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Proven Accounting includes a general ledger and banking, payables and receivables, purchase orders, automatic work-in-process calculations, inventory costing and integrated payroll.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes PSA?
tool_faqs.a: Canam Systems, founded in 1994 and independently owned, with an office in Barrie, Ontario. Tolga Tari is President and CEO.

tool_faqs.q: What training and support does Canam offer?
tool_faqs.a: Customized onboarding, on-site training, online training and the Proven Academy courses. Phone support runs Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 7 PM Eastern, with an emergency after-hours line.

tools.name: KnowHow
tools.tagline: AI knowledge, SOP and training platform for restoration companies and trade franchise networks

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing. KnowHow's site has no pricing page in its navigation and directs buyers to book a demo for a quote. Its partners page says Restoration Industry Association members get exclusive pricing. Verified against tryknowhow.com (home page, roi.html, resources/partners.html) 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Restoration companies and multi-location trade franchisors that want to turn their procedures into mobile, multilingual training and on-the-job answers for field crews
tools.weaknesses: A training, SOP and knowledge tool, not job management or estimating software, so it runs alongside your operations platform; no public pricing; no software integrations are listed
tools.long_description:
KnowHow is a knowledge and training platform for trade service companies. It is run by Manifest Labs Inc., which does business as KnowHow from Calgary, Alberta, Canada, and its CEO is Leighton Healey. KnowHow describes itself as an AI-powered platform that helps restoration companies raise workforce productivity by putting procedures and best practices in a mobile-first app, and its customers also include franchisors and painting and cleaning companies. KnowHow says more than 10,000 frontline employees use it.

The product has three parts. Define turns how your best people work into a written standard: record a process on desktop, with a Chrome extension or on a phone and KnowHow's AI turns it into a structured step-by-step guide, or type the name of a process and the AI drafts most of the guide for you to edit. Train gives each role a structured training path with auto-generated multiple-choice and true/false quizzes, spaced repetition, badges and a real-time view of who is progressing and who needs coaching. Execute lets crews ask questions in plain language and get answers drawn from your company's own content rather than the public internet. Howie, KnowHow's AI assistant, can also answer from uploaded manuals and documents, a feature KnowHow calls Magic Docs.

Content is translated automatically into more than 14 languages and runs on iPhone (iOS 13 and later), Android (5 and later) and major web browsers, and step-by-step instructions can be downloaded for offline use. KnowHow also offers reporting and documentation features aimed at compliance. For franchisors, Network Mode sends the brand playbook to every location while leaving room for local additions. KnowHow is an affinity partner of the Restoration Industry Association, with special pricing for RIA members.

Customers named on its site include FRSTeam, PuroClean, ATI Restoration, EverLine, Thomasville Restoration, Paul Davis Restoration of the Mountain West, Alpine Cleaning and Restoration Specialists and Restoration 1, which rolled KnowHow out to its franchisees. KnowHow announced partnerships with PuroClean in January 2026 and Rainbow Restoration in February 2026, and its customers page states that FP Property Restoration achieved a 20x ROI in 2023. Pricing is not published; KnowHow sells through demos.

The trade-off: KnowHow handles people and process, not jobs, estimates or invoices, so it sits alongside restoration job management software such as DASH, Albi or PSA rather than replacing it. Its site lists no integrations with those systems, pricing requires a sales call, and the payoff depends on someone keeping procedures current and crews actually using the app.

pros_detail.title: Turns know-how into written standards
pros_detail.explanation: Record a process on video or type its name, and KnowHow's AI drafts a structured step-by-step guide you can edit, so owners do not start every SOP from a blank page.

pros_detail.title: Structured training with checks
pros_detail.explanation: Role-based training paths come with auto-generated quizzes, spaced repetition, badges and a live view of who needs coaching.

pros_detail.title: Answers from your own content
pros_detail.explanation: Crews ask questions in plain language and get answers from your procedures and uploaded manuals through the Howie AI assistant, not from the public internet.

pros_detail.title: Multilingual and mobile
pros_detail.explanation: Procedures are translated automatically into more than 14 languages and work on iOS, Android and the web, with offline downloads for job sites without signal.

pros_detail.title: Built for franchise networks
pros_detail.explanation: Network Mode pushes one brand playbook to every location. Restoration 1, PuroClean, Rainbow Restoration and FRSTeam are among the franchise brands KnowHow names.

cons_detail.title: Not job management
cons_detail.explanation: KnowHow does not schedule jobs, write estimates or invoice. You still need a job management platform such as DASH, Albi or PSA alongside it.

cons_detail.title: No public pricing
cons_detail.explanation: There is no pricing page; you need a demo and a quote to learn the cost for your team.

cons_detail.title: No listed integrations
cons_detail.explanation: KnowHow's site does not list integrations with job management, HR or accounting software, so content and users are managed inside KnowHow.

cons_detail.title: Content needs an owner
cons_detail.explanation: AI drafts and translations speed things up, but someone has to review procedures and keep them current for the answers to stay right.

cons_detail.title: Restoration-focused library
cons_detail.explanation: Most named customers and partners are restoration and franchise brands. Companies in other trades should check how well it fits their work in the demo.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo to get a quote for your team size, and mention RIA membership if you have it. Start with the procedures new hires need first: record your best techs doing them or let the AI draft them from a title, then edit each guide to match how your company works. Upload existing manuals so Howie can answer from them. Build a training path for each role with its quizzes, then roll the app out to crews on iOS, Android or the web in their preferred language. Name one person to keep procedures current. Franchisors can use Network Mode to send the brand playbook to each location.

tool_faqs.q: What is KnowHow?
tool_faqs.a: KnowHow is a knowledge and training platform for trade service companies, mainly restoration businesses and franchise networks. It turns company procedures into step-by-step guides, trains staff with role-based paths and quizzes, and answers field questions from your own content through an AI assistant called Howie.

tool_faqs.q: How much does KnowHow cost?
tool_faqs.a: KnowHow does not publish pricing. You book a demo to get a quote. Its partners page says Restoration Industry Association members get exclusive pricing.

tool_faqs.q: Does KnowHow replace my restoration job management software?
tool_faqs.a: No. KnowHow covers training, procedures and on-the-job answers. It runs alongside job management software such as DASH, Albi or PSA, and its site lists no integrations with them.

tool_faqs.q: What languages and devices does KnowHow support?
tool_faqs.a: Procedures are translated automatically into more than 14 languages. The app runs on iPhone (iOS 13 and later), Android (5 and later) and major web browsers, and step-by-step instructions can be downloaded for offline use.

tool_faqs.q: Who uses KnowHow?
tool_faqs.a: KnowHow says more than 10,000 frontline employees use it. Named customers include FRSTeam, PuroClean, ATI Restoration, EverLine, Thomasville Restoration and Restoration 1, and its site states that FP Property Restoration achieved a 20x ROI in 2023.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes KnowHow?
tool_faqs.a: KnowHow is run by Manifest Labs Inc., based in Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Leighton Healey is the CEO.

tools.name: Pool Brain
tools.tagline: Pool service software for medium and large pool companies, built around custom alerts, chemical dosing and technician accountability

pricing.pricing_note: The pricing page lists $65 a month per active field technician, with unlimited office users, all features and free setup. The office-user base charge is shown only by the page's interactive calculator; Pool Brain's own comparison pages price 3 technicians at $245 a month, which implies a $50 monthly base (so one tech is about $115 a month). No annual plan is listed. 30-day free trial. Verified against poolbrain.com/pricing and poolcompanysoftware.poolbrain.com comparison pages 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Medium and large pool service companies, including multi-branch and franchise operators, that want alerts, guided workflows and technician scorecards to keep service consistent as they add routes
tools.weaknesses: Priced per active field technician on top of a base charge, so cost rises with every tech hired; the base charge is shown only in an interactive calculator; built for pool service only
tools.long_description:
Pool Brain is pool service software from Pool Brain LLC, headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. Its founder and CEO, Adam Beech, previously owned a Phoenix pool company that the vendor says ran more than 35 trucks, and Pool Brain describes itself as a platform for medium to large pool service businesses. It names Keith Zars, Shasta Pools, Riverbend Sandler, Poolie, National Pool Partners and America's Swimming Pool Company (ASP) among its customers; ASP selected it for its franchise locations in December 2024.

The core idea is to catch problems before they turn into complaints. Custom alerts flag issues such as chemical levels, flow, leaks, time on site and costs, while guided workflows and job templates walk techs through each stop. The technician app for iOS and Android calculates chemical doses, handles multiple bodies of water per property, tracks filter and salt cell cleans and equipment, and works without cell signal. Owners get one-click route optimization with drag-and-drop editing, graphs and charts, route profit, technician scorecards and technician pay tools. A January 2026 update added AI-based auto-dosing for chlorine tabs as a beta.

Quotes become jobs and jobs become invoices, with automatic or manual billing, card and ACH autopay with an automatic retry when a card is declined, proof-of-service emails and a self-serve customer portal. Integrations include a two-way QuickBooks Online sync, WaterGuru remote monitoring, LaMotte Spin Touch readings, the Orenda calculator for LSI-based dosing and Heritage Pool Supply for product costs and ordering. Pool Brain also offers API access, and in May 2026 it announced a planned integration with Pentair.

Pricing is $65 per active field technician a month, with unlimited office users, every feature and free setup included. The base charge for office users appears only in the pricing page's calculator; Pool Brain's own comparison pages price a company with 3 technicians at $245 a month, which works out to a $50 monthly base plus $65 per tech. A 30-day free trial is offered.

The trade-off: cost follows field headcount, so every tech you add costs another $65 a month regardless of how many pools they service. The alerts and workflows only pay off once they are set up to match your standards, which takes owner time up front. Pool Brain is built for pool service and is not a general field service tool.

pros_detail.title: Custom alerts and guided workflows
pros_detail.explanation: Alerts on chemicals, flow, leaks, time and costs, plus guided workflows and job templates, help owners spot missed steps and problem pools before a customer calls.

pros_detail.title: Chemistry tools
pros_detail.explanation: The app calculates doses, tracks chemical use and cost, handles pools and spas on the same property, and connects to the Orenda calculator, LaMotte Spin Touch and WaterGuru.

pros_detail.title: Works without signal
pros_detail.explanation: Pool Brain says its tech app does not need a cell signal to operate, so techs can finish stops in dead zones and sync later.

pros_detail.title: Owner visibility
pros_detail.explanation: Graphs and charts, route profit, technician scorecards and issue reports show which routes and techs need attention.

pros_detail.title: Two-way QuickBooks Online sync
pros_detail.explanation: Customers, invoices, payments, refunds and products sync both ways between Pool Brain and QuickBooks Online.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited office users and free setup
pros_detail.explanation: The pricing page includes unlimited office users, all features and free setup, with a 30-day free trial.

cons_detail.title: Cost scales with field techs
cons_detail.explanation: Each active field technician adds $65 a month on top of the base charge, so a growing crew raises the bill even if the pool count per tech stays low.

cons_detail.title: Base charge not printed
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page shows the office-user charge only inside its calculator. Pool Brain's comparison pages imply a $50 base; confirm the total for your team before you sign up.

cons_detail.title: Setup takes owner time
cons_detail.explanation: The alerts, workflows and job templates reflect your own service standards, so they need to be configured before they deliver value.

cons_detail.title: Aimed at larger companies
cons_detail.explanation: Pool Brain positions itself for medium to large pool service businesses. A one-truck owner-operator may not use much of the accountability tooling.

cons_detail.title: Pool service only
cons_detail.explanation: Pool Brain is built for pool service and does not cover other trades.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 30-day free trial and use the free setup included in the price. Import customers and properties, adding each body of water, then build routes and run the optimizer. Configure custom alerts, guided workflows and job templates to match your service standards, since that is where Pool Brain's accountability features come from. Connect QuickBooks Online and turn on card or ACH autopay for recurring customers. If you use LaMotte Spin Touch, WaterGuru or Heritage Pool Supply, connect them so readings and product costs flow in. Have techs install the iOS or Android app and ride along on a few stops before moving whole routes over.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Pool Brain cost?
tool_faqs.a: Pool Brain's pricing page lists $65 per active field technician a month, with unlimited office users, all features and free setup. The office-user base charge appears only in the page's calculator; Pool Brain's comparison pages price 3 technicians at $245 a month, which implies a $50 base. A 30-day free trial is offered.

tool_faqs.q: Does Pool Brain charge for office staff?
tool_faqs.a: Office users are unlimited. You pay a base charge for the office side and $65 a month for each active field technician.

tool_faqs.q: Does Pool Brain work offline?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Pool Brain says its iOS and Android tech app does not need a cell signal to operate, and data syncs when the phone reconnects.

tool_faqs.q: What does Pool Brain integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: QuickBooks Online (two-way sync), WaterGuru, LaMotte Spin Touch, the Orenda calculator and Heritage Pool Supply, plus API access. A Pentair integration was announced as planned in May 2026.

tool_faqs.q: Who is Pool Brain built for?
tool_faqs.a: Pool Brain describes itself as a platform for medium to large pool service businesses. Named customers include National Pool Partners, America's Swimming Pool Company, Keith Zars, Shasta Pools, Riverbend Sandler and Poolie.

tool_faqs.q: How is Pool Brain priced compared with Skimmer?
tool_faqs.a: Pool Brain charges per active field technician ($65 a month each) plus a base charge. Skimmer charges per serviced location ($1 or $2 a month per location, depending on plan) with unlimited users. Which is cheaper depends on how many pools each of your techs services.

tools.name: Pool Founder
tools.tagline: Pool service software priced by technician count, not by pool, with every feature on every plan

pricing.pricing_note: Flat monthly price per company, set by technician count: Solo $49 (1 tech), Team $99 (up to 3), Growth $179 (up to 6), Pro $249 (up to 10), Enterprise custom (unlimited techs). Every feature is on every plan, pools are unlimited and there are no per-pool fees. Month-to-month billing, cancel anytime; the vendor says existing customers keep their sign-up price. 30-day free trial, no credit card. Verified against poolfounder.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Pool service companies with 1 to 10 technicians (Enterprise above that) that want pool-specific routing, chemistry logging and billing at a flat price that does not rise with pool count
tools.weaknesses: A young company, launched in 2025 by a small team; the price jumps at each technician cap; built for pool service only, and the vendor says it is not meant for pool builders, retail stores or multi-region enterprises
tools.long_description:
Pool Founder is pool service software launched in 2025 and based in Kennesaw, Georgia. It was started by Corey Adams, who has more than 15 years of pool route experience starting at DC Pool Services in Kennesaw, and his co-founder Zach, a software developer who was first Corey's pool customer. Pool Founder says it is built for pool service businesses with 1 to 50 technicians, not for other trades, pool builders or retail stores.

The product covers route building and traffic-aware route optimization, recurring and one-time job scheduling, work orders, service reports and quotes. Techs use an iOS and Android app that works offline, logs FC, pH, TA, CYA and salt readings, calculates dose amounts and keeps each pool's chemistry history. Completed work turns into invoices with autopay on saved cards, and payments run through Stripe and ACH with a QuickBooks sync. Owners also get GPS tracking on completed stops, a live technician map, route profitability, team and payroll tracking (clock-in, drive time, time on site, mileage and overtime), a customer texting inbox, reminders and a customer portal. An AI assistant called George answers questions about the business and makes changes such as moving jobs, and AI-assisted import turns spreadsheets into customer records.

Pricing is flat per company, set by the number of technicians: Solo is $49 a month for 1 tech, Team $99 for up to 3, Growth $179 for up to 6, Pro $249 for up to 10, and Enterprise is custom priced for larger teams. Every plan has every feature and unlimited pools, billing is month to month, and there is a 30-day free trial with no credit card. Pool Founder says existing customers keep the price they signed up at, and it offers free data import and route setup.

The trade-off: Pool Founder is new. Its homepage counts about 8,300 completed visits and 33,000 chemistry readings on the platform so far, far fewer than older tools such as Skimmer (launched 2017) or Pool Brain. The price steps up at each technician cap, so adding a fourth tech moves you from $99 to $179 a month. Check that the QuickBooks sync and payment setup fit your books during the trial.

pros_detail.title: Priced by technicians, not pools
pros_detail.explanation: Plans run from $49 a month for 1 tech to $249 for up to 10, with unlimited pools, so a dense route does not raise the bill.

pros_detail.title: Every feature on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Pool Founder does not gate features by tier; plans differ only by the number of technicians.

pros_detail.title: Pool-specific chemistry logging
pros_detail.explanation: Techs log FC, pH, TA, CYA and salt, the app calculates doses, and each pool keeps its chemistry history.

pros_detail.title: Offline app with GPS and payroll
pros_detail.explanation: The iOS and Android app works offline, records GPS on completed stops, and tracks clock-in, drive time, mileage and overtime for payroll.

pros_detail.title: Low-risk start
pros_detail.explanation: A 30-day free trial with no credit card, month-to-month billing and free data import and route setup make it easy to test on real routes.

cons_detail.title: New and small
cons_detail.explanation: Pool Founder launched in 2025 and describes itself as a small team, so it has a short track record compared with older pool software.

cons_detail.title: Steps at each technician cap
cons_detail.explanation: Going from 3 to 4 techs moves you from Team ($99) to Growth ($179), and from 6 to 7 techs moves you to Pro ($249).

cons_detail.title: Short integration list
cons_detail.explanation: The confirmed integrations are QuickBooks and Stripe payments. Check the QuickBooks setup against your accounting during the trial.

cons_detail.title: Pool service only
cons_detail.explanation: The vendor says it is not built for other trades, pool builders, retail stores or multi-region enterprises.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 30-day free trial (no credit card) and ask for the free data import and route setup, or use the AI import to turn your customer spreadsheet into records. Build routes, run the optimizer and set up recurring service for each pool. Connect Stripe for card and ACH payments, turn on autopay for recurring customers, and connect QuickBooks. Have techs install the iOS or Android app and log readings and doses on a few stops before moving whole routes over. Before the trial ends, check which technician tier your crew needs, since the price is set by tech count.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Pool Founder cost?
tool_faqs.a: Solo is $49 a month for 1 technician, Team $99 for up to 3, Growth $179 for up to 6, Pro $249 for up to 10, and Enterprise is custom. Every plan includes every feature and unlimited pools, and billing is month to month.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, 30 days with no credit card required.

tool_faqs.q: Does Pool Founder charge per pool?
tool_faqs.a: No. Pricing is set by the number of technicians, and all plans include unlimited pools.

tool_faqs.q: Who is behind Pool Founder?
tool_faqs.a: Pool Founder launched in 2025 in Kennesaw, Georgia. It was founded by Corey Adams, a pool technician with more than 15 years on the route, and co-founder and CEO Zach, a software developer.

tool_faqs.q: What does Pool Founder integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: Pool Founder names QuickBooks and Stripe (cards and ACH) as the systems it keeps in sync.

tool_faqs.q: Does the app work offline?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The iOS and Android tech app works offline and syncs later.

tools.name: Paythepoolman
tools.tagline: Pool service software with routing, billing and a branded customer app

pricing.pricing_note: One plan: $50 a month base plus $15 a month per technician (one tech is $65 a month). No free plan. Billed monthly, no contract, cancel anytime. Add-ons: Pool Junction branded customer app $25 a month per company; integrated payroll $12 per employee a month plus a one-time sign-up fee; pay-per-credit text packages (overdue reminders are free); optional $1.50 convenience fee per card transaction, paid by the customer. 30-day free trial. Verified against paythepoolman.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Owner-operators and small pool service companies that want routing, recurring billing, bids and a customer app at a low monthly price that adds only $15 per extra technician
tools.weaknesses: No free plan; the branded customer app, payroll and text credits cost extra; support is weekday business hours only; built for pool service only
tools.long_description:
Paythepoolman is pool service management software founded by Jeff Posth, who ran pool routes for 13 years before launching it. The company is based in Riverside, California, and describes itself as independent and private with more than 10 years in business. It says customers have sent more than $1.3 billion in bids, invoiced more than $1 billion and processed more than $422 million in payments through the platform.

For route work, it supports weekly and bi-weekly routes with one-click optimization, a live progress dashboard, GPS tracking, repair scheduling and filter and salt cell tracking. Techs use the Plus app on iOS or Android, where they can import water test results from a LaMotte SpinTouch, attach before-and-after video to service logs and clock in for payroll. The Orenda integration calculates the Langelier Saturation Index and suggests doses. Other tools include an equipment log, shopping list, fleet management, task hub, project management, leads, mass communication and bulk rate increases.

On the money side, Run Billing generates every invoice on the billing cycle and adds the extras techs logged, then sends them by email, print or both, with an optional invoice mailing service. Customers can pay with cards on file, autopay, ACH, Apple Pay or Google Pay, and you can pass card costs to them with a convenience fee. Late fees, statements and a QuickBooks sync are built in, and a bank feed turns into an expense ledger with receipts captured in the field. Contactless bidding shows the profit on each line. Pool Junction, the customer-facing app, shows each customer their balance, invoices, bids, service photos and messages under your company's brand.

Pricing is one plan: $50 a month plus $15 a month per technician, month to month with no contract, and a 30-day free trial. Add-ons are Pool Junction ($25 a month for the whole company), integrated payroll ($12 per employee a month plus a one-time sign-up fee) and pay-per-credit text packages. Support is free on weekdays from 8am to 4pm Eastern.

The trade-off: there is no free plan, and the branded app, payroll and texting are paid extras, so price the add-ons you need. Support is limited to weekday business hours, and the software is built only for pool service.

pros_detail.title: Low cost per added tech
pros_detail.explanation: The price is a $50 monthly base plus $15 per technician, so a one-tech shop pays $65 a month and each new hire adds $15.

pros_detail.title: Branded customer app
pros_detail.explanation: Pool Junction ($25 a month per company) gives customers their balance, invoices, bids, service photos and messages under your brand.

pros_detail.title: Billing tools for recurring service
pros_detail.explanation: Run Billing creates every invoice on the cycle, with autopay, ACH, Apple Pay and Google Pay, optional card convenience fees, late fees, statements and QuickBooks sync.

pros_detail.title: Water testing integrations
pros_detail.explanation: Techs import LaMotte SpinTouch results straight into the Plus app, and the Orenda integration calculates LSI and dosing.

pros_detail.title: Beyond routes
pros_detail.explanation: Contactless bidding with per-line profit, payroll, bank feeds, fleet management and an equipment log cover much of the back office.

pros_detail.title: Easy switch from Skimmer
pros_detail.explanation: A Skimmer customer importer brings your customer list over, and the team walks you through it.

cons_detail.title: No free plan
cons_detail.explanation: After the 30-day trial every account pays the $50 base plus $15 per technician.

cons_detail.title: Paid add-ons
cons_detail.explanation: The branded customer app ($25 a month), payroll ($12 per employee a month plus a sign-up fee) and text credits are billed separately.

cons_detail.title: Weekday support hours
cons_detail.explanation: Free support runs Monday to Friday, 8am to 4pm Eastern, which is early afternoon for West Coast companies.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks version not stated
cons_detail.explanation: The site says QuickBooks sync is built in but does not say whether it covers QuickBooks Online, Desktop or both. Ask before you rely on it.

cons_detail.title: Pool service only
cons_detail.explanation: Paythepoolman is built for pool service and does not cover other trades.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 30-day free trial. If you are coming from Skimmer, use the customer importer and ask the Paythepoolman team to walk you through it; otherwise import your customer list and build weekly or bi-weekly routes, then run the one-click optimizer. Set up your billing cycle, autopay and any card convenience fee, and connect QuickBooks and your bank feed. Decide whether you need the Pool Junction customer app, payroll or text credits, since each is billed separately. Have techs install the Plus app on iOS or Android and, if you use a LaMotte SpinTouch or Orenda, connect them so readings and doses flow into service logs.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Paythepoolman cost?
tool_faqs.a: $50 a month plus $15 a month per technician, billed monthly with no contract. A one-tech company pays $65 a month. Pool Junction ($25 a month), payroll ($12 per employee a month plus a sign-up fee) and text credits are extra.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free plan or trial?
tool_faqs.a: There is no free plan. New accounts get a 30-day free trial and can cancel anytime.

tool_faqs.q: What is Pool Junction?
tool_faqs.a: Pool Junction is the customer-facing app. It shows each customer their balance, invoices, bids, service photos and messages, branded to your company, for $25 a month for the whole company.

tool_faqs.q: How does Paythepoolman's pricing compare with Skimmer and Pool Brain?
tool_faqs.a: Paythepoolman charges $50 plus $15 per technician. Pool Brain lists $65 per active field technician plus a base charge, and Skimmer charges $1 or $2 per serviced location a month with unlimited users. Run your own tech and pool counts through each.

tool_faqs.q: Does Paythepoolman work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: The site says QuickBooks sync is built in, alongside late fees and statements. It does not say which QuickBooks version, so confirm yours is supported.

tool_faqs.q: When is support available?
tool_faqs.a: Free support runs Monday to Friday, 8am to 4pm Eastern.

tools.name: STACK
tools.tagline: Cloud takeoff and estimating software for contractors and subcontractors, with a free plan

pricing.pricing_note: Takeoff & Estimate: Free $0 (1 active project per month, up to 300 plan pages, 50 measurements per project, 7 days of Pro features at sign-up, no credit card); Premium $249 and Pro $299 per user per month billed annually; Build Your Own is custom. Paid plans are 12-month terms: pay upfront annually (STACK says this saves 20%) or spread payments monthly. Add-ons: Aerial Image Takeoff (Premium required) and ERP connectors (Pro required). The separate Build & Operate field product starts at $49 per user per month billed annually, and the Full STACK Platform bundle is listed from $298 per user per month. Verified against stackct.com/takeoff-and-estimate-pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Contractors and subcontractors who bid from plans every week and want takeoff, labor and material estimating and proposals in one browser-based tool
tools.weaknesses: Paid plans are 12-month commitments at $249 or more per user per month billed annually, and labor and material estimating, proposals and ERP connectors need the $299 Pro plan; the Free plan allows only one active project a month
tools.long_description:
STACK is cloud-based takeoff and estimating software for contractors and subcontractors. Estimators upload plan sets, measure quantities, build labor and material estimates from items and assemblies, and produce proposals in a web browser. STACK says the software is 100% cloud-based, so there is nothing to install. The same company sells Build & Operate, a field product for plan viewing, markup, issues, punch lists and daily reports, and bundles the two as the Full STACK Platform.

STACK Construction Technologies is based in Cincinnati, Ohio, with a Canadian office in Longueuil, Quebec. Its founder, Phil Ogilby, started out as a residential and commercial roofing contractor in 1984. Growth investor Level Equity has backed the company since 2018, and in 2022 STACK bought Bid Retriever (bid management for subcontractors) and K-Ops (office-to-field project documentation).

Takeoff & Estimate has three published plans. Free costs $0 and allows 1 active project per month, up to 300 plan pages and 50 measurements per project, with 7 days of Pro features when you sign up. Premium is $249 per user per month billed annually and adds unlimited projects and measurements, a prebuilt item and assembly library, plan overlay, symbol search, AI Takeoffs and STACK IQ. Pro is $299 per user per month billed annually and adds worksheet-style labor and material estimating, a regional BNi cost library, STACK for Excel and native proposal generation. All paid subscriptions run 12 months; STACK says paying upfront annually saves 20% compared with spreading payments monthly.

STACK IQ connects STACK to AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude so users can set up projects and create or edit takeoffs by describing what they need; STACK says it is included on all subscription levels at no extra charge. STACK Assist answers questions about a plan set with sheet references. STACK lists integrations with QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, Acumatica, Procore and Autodesk, plus plan rooms such as Dodge Data and BidCentral. ERP connectors are an add-on that requires Pro.

The trade-off: beyond one active project a month, STACK is a yearly commitment of $249 or more per estimator per month, and the estimating and proposal tools most bidders want sit in Pro at $299. A shop that bids a few jobs a month can test the Free plan first, but a busy estimating team should budget for Pro seats for every estimator who builds bids.

pros_detail.title: Takeoff, estimate and proposal in one place
pros_detail.explanation: On the Pro plan, estimators measure plans, build labor and material estimates from items and assemblies, and generate proposals without moving data between programs.

pros_detail.title: Free plan to start
pros_detail.explanation: The $0 Free plan covers 1 active project per month with up to 300 plan pages and 50 measurements per project, and includes 7 days of Pro features when you sign up.

pros_detail.title: Browser-based
pros_detail.explanation: STACK says it is 100% cloud-based, so estimators can open the same projects from any computer without installing software.

pros_detail.title: AI tools included
pros_detail.explanation: Premium and Pro include AI Takeoffs and STACK IQ, which lets users direct takeoff and project setup through ChatGPT or Claude. STACK says STACK IQ carries no extra charge.

pros_detail.title: Accounting and ERP connections
pros_detail.explanation: STACK lists integrations with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite and Acumatica, plus Procore for project management.

cons_detail.title: Annual commitment
cons_detail.explanation: All paid Takeoff & Estimate subscriptions are 12-month terms. You can spread payments monthly, but STACK says paying upfront saves 20%.

cons_detail.title: Estimating needs Pro
cons_detail.explanation: Worksheet-style labor and material estimating, the BNi cost library and native proposals are Pro features at $299 per user per month billed annually. Premium at $249 is mainly takeoff.

cons_detail.title: Per-user pricing adds up
cons_detail.explanation: Each estimator who builds takeoffs or estimates needs a paid seat, so a team of five on Pro is about $1,495 a month billed annually.

cons_detail.title: Add-ons cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Aerial Image Takeoff (Premium required) and ERP connectors (Pro required) are listed as add-ons on top of the plan price.

cons_detail.title: Free plan is small
cons_detail.explanation: One active project per month and 50 measurements per project is enough to test the software, not to run a bidding operation.

tools.implementation_notes: Start on the Free plan and use the 7 days of Pro features to run one real bid from plan upload to proposal. Decide which estimators need paid seats and whether they need Pro for labor and material estimating and proposals or only Premium for takeoff. Load your own items and assemblies, or adapt the prebuilt library, and set your labor rates and material prices before bidding live work. If you use QuickBooks, Sage Intacct, NetSuite or Acumatica, confirm whether your connection needs the ERP connector add-on (Pro required). Connect Procore or your plan rooms if you pull drawings from them.

tool_faqs.q: How much does STACK cost?
tool_faqs.a: Takeoff & Estimate has a Free plan at $0 (1 active project per month, up to 300 plan pages, 50 measurements per project), Premium at $249 per user per month billed annually and Pro at $299 per user per month billed annually, plus a custom Build Your Own option. Paid plans are 12-month terms; paying upfront annually saves 20% versus monthly payments. Aerial Image Takeoff and ERP connectors are add-ons.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free version of STACK?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. The Free plan costs $0 with no credit card and includes 7 days of Pro features, then continues with 1 active project per month, up to 300 plan pages and 50 measurements per project.

tool_faqs.q: What is the difference between Premium and Pro?
tool_faqs.a: Premium covers unlimited takeoff with a prebuilt item and assembly library, overlay, symbol search, AI Takeoffs and STACK IQ. Pro adds worksheet-style labor and material estimating, a regional BNi cost library, STACK for Excel, native proposal generation and access to the ERP connector add-on.

tool_faqs.q: Does STACK have AI features?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Premium and Pro include AI Takeoffs and STACK IQ, which connects STACK to AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude so you can set up projects and create or edit takeoffs by describing what you need. STACK Assist answers questions about a plan set with sheet references.

tool_faqs.q: What does STACK integrate with?
tool_faqs.a: STACK lists integrations with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Sage Intacct, Oracle NetSuite, Acumatica, Procore, Autodesk, Dodge Data, BidCentral and others. ERP connectors are an add-on that requires the Pro plan.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns STACK?
tool_faqs.a: STACK Construction Technologies, based in Cincinnati, Ohio. It was started by former roofing contractor Phil Ogilby, and growth investor Level Equity has backed it since 2018.

tools.name: PlanSwift
tools.tagline: Point-and-click takeoff and estimating software from ConstructConnect, sold by quote

pricing.pricing_note: No public PlanSwift price: ConstructConnect says pricing varies by number of seats and business needs, and offers a free trial (length not stated). Trade-specific plug-ins are sold separately. ConstructConnect's pricing page lists PlanSwift without a price; the prices shown there ($1,200 and $2,200 per seat per year) belong to the separate ConstructConnect Takeoff product. Verified against constructconnect.com/products/planswift and constructconnect.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Contractors and subcontractors who want fast point-and-click quantity takeoffs and assemblies that turn measurements into material and labor estimates
tools.weaknesses: No published price (quoted by seat count and business needs), trade-specific plug-ins are sold separately, and it is a takeoff and estimating tool, not project management or accounting
tools.long_description:
PlanSwift is digital takeoff and estimating software sold by ConstructConnect. Estimators load plans (PDF, DWG, JPG, TIFF and other formats), then measure areas, lengths and volumes with a few clicks, count symbols such as doors, windows and fixtures, and compare plan versions with overlays. Assemblies that include material and labor costing turn those quantities into an estimate, and results can be exported to Excel.

ConstructConnect lists PlanSwift for general contractors and a wide range of trades, including concrete, drywall, electrical, excavation, flooring, framing, HVAC, landscape, painting and plumbing. You can build your own formulas and assemblies, and ConstructConnect says it has several trade-specific plug-ins available for purchase. Markup and annotation tools and team sharing of takeoffs and estimates are also included, and the FAQ says PlanSwift integrates with Excel, QuickBooks and other estimating software.

PlanSwift was founded in 2007 and was based in Bountiful, Utah, when ConstructConnect bought its assets in April 2018. ConstructConnect, headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, was itself acquired by Roper Technologies in 2016. ConstructConnect also sells other takeoff products, including On-Screen Takeoff and ConstructConnect Takeoff.

ConstructConnect does not publish a PlanSwift price. It says pricing varies with the number of seats and your business needs, and it offers a free trial. By comparison, the separate ConstructConnect Takeoff product has published prices of $1,200 and $2,200 per seat per year.

The trade-off: you need a sales quote to know the cost, and trade plug-ins add to it. PlanSwift covers takeoff and estimating only, so scheduling, job management and accounting stay in other software (with QuickBooks as a named integration).

pros_detail.title: Fast point-and-click takeoff
pros_detail.explanation: Measure areas, lengths and volumes with a few clicks and count repeated symbols such as doors, windows and fixtures.

pros_detail.title: Assemblies with material and labor
pros_detail.explanation: Assemblies and custom formulas turn measured quantities into material and labor costs, so repeat items do not have to be priced by hand on every job.

pros_detail.title: Plan version overlays
pros_detail.explanation: Overlay comparisons show changes between plan revisions, which helps catch scope changes before you re-bid.

pros_detail.title: Many trades covered
pros_detail.explanation: ConstructConnect lists general contractors plus concrete, drywall, electrical, excavation, flooring, framing, HVAC, landscape, painting and plumbing, with trade plug-ins available.

pros_detail.title: Excel and QuickBooks
pros_detail.explanation: Takeoff data exports to Excel, and ConstructConnect says PlanSwift integrates with QuickBooks and other estimating software.

cons_detail.title: No published price
cons_detail.explanation: ConstructConnect quotes PlanSwift by seat count and business needs, so you cannot compare cost without talking to sales.

cons_detail.title: Plug-ins cost extra
cons_detail.explanation: Trade-specific plug-ins are sold separately. Without them you build your own assemblies and formulas.

cons_detail.title: Takeoff and estimating only
cons_detail.explanation: PlanSwift does not cover scheduling, job management, invoicing or accounting, so it runs alongside other software.

cons_detail.title: Overlapping products from one vendor
cons_detail.explanation: ConstructConnect also sells On-Screen Takeoff and ConstructConnect Takeoff, so ask sales which product fits your trade and team before you buy.

tools.implementation_notes: Request a quote for your number of seats and ask which trade plug-ins, if any, fit your work, since they are sold separately. Use the free trial to run a real plan set through takeoff, assemblies and Excel export. Before bidding live work, set up your assemblies and formulas with your own material prices and labor rates. If you use QuickBooks, confirm with ConstructConnect how data moves between the two. Ask sales to compare PlanSwift with ConstructConnect Takeoff, which has published per-seat pricing.

tool_faqs.q: How much does PlanSwift cost?
tool_faqs.a: ConstructConnect does not publish a PlanSwift price. It says pricing varies by the number of seats and business needs, and it offers a free trial. Trade-specific plug-ins are sold separately.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns PlanSwift?
tool_faqs.a: ConstructConnect, which bought PlanSwift's assets in April 2018. ConstructConnect is headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, and was acquired by Roper Technologies in 2016.

tool_faqs.q: What is PlanSwift good at?
tool_faqs.a: Point-and-click quantity takeoff: measuring areas, lengths and volumes, counting symbols, comparing plan versions, and turning quantities into material and labor costs with assemblies.

tool_faqs.q: What file types and software does PlanSwift work with?
tool_faqs.a: ConstructConnect says PlanSwift supports PDF, DWG, JPG, TIFF and other common plan formats, exports to Excel, and integrates with QuickBooks and other estimating software.

tool_faqs.q: How is PlanSwift different from STACK?
tool_faqs.a: Both do takeoff and estimating. STACK publishes its prices (including a $0 Free plan) and says it is 100% cloud-based. PlanSwift is sold by quote from ConstructConnect, with trade plug-ins sold separately.

tools.name: Clear Estimates
tools.tagline: Remodeling estimating software with a localized U.S. cost database and prebuilt project templates

pricing.pricing_note: Per company. Standard $59 a month billed annually ($79 monthly), one login. Pro $99 a month billed annually ($119 monthly), additional users $9 a month each. Franchise from $199 a month billed annually ($249 monthly), priced by customization scope. No contract, no setup fee, 30-day free trial. Verified against clearestimates.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: U.S. residential remodelers, handymen and small contractors who want itemized estimates priced with local labor and material rates instead of building their own price list
tools.weaknesses: Estimating only, with no scheduling or project management; cost data covers U.S. areas only and does not use metric units; not built for commercial or restoration work; Standard includes one login, and extra users, AI plan uploads, Buildertrend and Zapier need Pro
tools.long_description:
Clear Estimates is web-based estimating software for residential remodelers and contractors. It pairs a line-item cost database with prebuilt project templates: you pick a template (a bathroom remodel, a deck, a roof), enter the dimensions, and it produces an itemized estimate priced with local labor and material rates. The company says its costs are localized to more than 400 areas in the U.S. and that labor and material rates are updated quarterly. Its pricing page lists a database of more than 13,000 line items and more than 400 preloaded templates, and you can add your own items to the library.

Clear Estimates says it began as in-house software for a Minneapolis remodeling company and launched as a product in 2005. In 2020 it acquired RemodelMAX, its cost-data partner, to bring the database in-house. The company lists its office in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and says it is trusted by more than 50,000 contractors.

Estimates become proposals you can email to the customer, who can review and sign them electronically from any device without creating an account. Proposals carry your logo and boilerplate text, with settings for fonts, colors and which line items and subtotals show. You can also create payable invoices (card or ACH through Clearent by Xplor), export to PDF, Word or Excel, and send project totals to QuickBooks Online or QuickBooks Desktop (Windows). Pro adds an AI Scope Assistant that drafts an estimate from uploaded plans or job-site photos, a Buildertrend integration, CRM sync through Zapier, and property data from ATTOM.

Standard is $59 a month billed annually ($79 monthly) and includes one login. Pro is $99 a month billed annually ($119 monthly), with additional users at $9 a month each. Franchise starts at $199 a month billed annually ($249 monthly) and is priced by the custom branding and development you need. There is no contract or setup fee, and a 30-day free trial.

The trade-off: Clear Estimates is an estimating tool, not a job-management system. The company says it does not handle scheduling or project management, sketching or 3D, commercial construction out of the box, or pricing outside the U.S. Contractors who need those pair it with another tool, and any business that needs more than one login has to be on Pro.

pros_detail.title: Local cost data built in
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates are priced from a database the company localizes to more than 400 U.S. areas, with labor and material rates updated quarterly, so you do not have to build and maintain your own price book from scratch.

pros_detail.title: Prebuilt project templates
pros_detail.explanation: Templates cover common residential jobs such as kitchens, bathrooms, additions, garages, roofs and painting. You pick one, enter the dimensions and adjust the line items.

pros_detail.title: Proposals with e-signature
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can review and sign proposals from any device without an account, and you can make invoices payable by card or ACH through Clearent by Xplor.

pros_detail.title: QuickBooks on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Project totals and customer data can be sent to QuickBooks Online or QuickBooks Desktop (Windows) on all plans, which cuts double entry for the office.

pros_detail.title: Low entry price, no contract
pros_detail.explanation: Standard is $59 a month billed annually ($79 monthly), with no contract, no setup fee and a 30-day free trial.

pros_detail.title: Runs in any browser
pros_detail.explanation: It is cloud software that works on Windows, Mac, tablets and phones through a browser, so you can build an estimate at the customer's home.

cons_detail.title: No scheduling or project management
cons_detail.explanation: Clear Estimates says scheduling and project management are outside its scope. On Pro you can send estimates to Buildertrend; on Standard you need a separate tool.

cons_detail.title: U.S. residential focus
cons_detail.explanation: Cost data covers U.S. areas only and does not use metric units. The company says commercial construction and water, fire or mold restoration are not supported out of the box.

cons_detail.title: Key extras are Pro-only
cons_detail.explanation: Additional users ($9 a month each), the AI Scope Assistant, the Buildertrend and Zapier integrations and ATTOM property data all require Pro.

cons_detail.title: QuickBooks Desktop link is Windows-only
cons_detail.explanation: The QuickBooks Desktop integration is formatted for Windows, so Mac users on QuickBooks Desktop cannot use it.

cons_detail.title: No sketching or 3D
cons_detail.explanation: There are no drawing or 3D modeling tools, so plan measuring or design visuals need another product.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 30-day free trial and book the free walkthrough with a customer success rep that the company offers (it also runs weekly webinars). Under Tools > Options, enter your company data and logo, then set report settings and the boilerplate text that opens and closes your proposals. Review the labor and material rates in the templates you use most against your own costs, and add custom items to the library where needed. Connect QuickBooks Online or QuickBooks Desktop (Windows) under Integrations, and set up a Clearent by Xplor account if you want payable invoices. If more than one person needs a login, or you want the Buildertrend or Zapier integrations, choose Pro.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Clear Estimates cost?
tool_faqs.a: Standard is $59 a month billed annually or $79 monthly. Pro is $99 a month billed annually or $119 monthly, with extra users at $9 a month each. Franchise starts at $199 a month billed annually or $249 monthly, depending on customization. There is a 30-day free trial, no contract and no setup fee.

tool_faqs.q: Where does the cost data come from?
tool_faqs.a: Clear Estimates maintains its own database; it acquired its former cost-data partner, RemodelMAX, in 2020. It says prices are localized to more than 400 U.S. areas and that labor and material rates are updated quarterly.

tool_faqs.q: Does it do scheduling or project management?
tool_faqs.a: No. The company says it focuses on estimating. Pro users can send an estimate to Buildertrend for scheduling and project management.

tool_faqs.q: Does it work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. All plans can send project totals and customer data to QuickBooks Online or QuickBooks Desktop. The Desktop integration works on Windows only.

tool_faqs.q: Can I use it outside the U.S.?
tool_faqs.a: The company says it does not support pricing outside the U.S. or metric measurements, so it is built for U.S. contractors.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: It runs in a web browser rather than a separate app, and the company says it works on any device with an internet connection, including iPads, iPhones and Android phones.

tools.name: Bluebeam Revu
tools.tagline: PDF markup, measurement takeoff and plan collaboration software for construction teams

pricing.pricing_note: Per user per year, billed annually: Basics $260 (about $22 a month), Core $330, Complete $440, Max $590 at an introductory price that Bluebeam says buyers keep through their 2027 renewal (later renewals at a list price to be announced). No monthly billing option is shown. Every plan includes Revu for Windows plus web and mobile access. Free trial: 14 days of Max, no credit card. Verified against bluebeam.com/pricing, bluebeam.com/bluebeam-max and bluebeam.com/trials 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Contractors, estimators and project teams who work from PDF plan sets and need markup, measurement takeoffs and shared plan reviews between office and field
tools.weaknesses: Annual per-user subscription only, key takeoff tools are split across tiers (Basics measures only length and area), and it has no built-in cost database or scheduling, dispatch and invoicing tools
tools.long_description:
Bluebeam Revu is PDF software for architecture, engineering and construction teams. Contractors use it to mark up plan sets, compare drawing versions, manage documents and run shared plan reviews in Studio Sessions and Projects. For estimators, Revu measures directly off the plans: length, polylength, perimeter, area, volume, depth, radius, wall area, angle and count, with Dynamic Fill for complex regions and Quantity Link to push measurement totals into Excel.

Bluebeam has been in business since 2002 and has been part of the Nemetschek Group since 2014. It is headquartered in Pasadena, California, with offices in Dallas, Brisbane, Copenhagen, London, Munich and Stockholm. Bluebeam says more than 4 million people in over 160 countries use its software.

All plans are billed annually per user and include Revu for Windows desktop plus Bluebeam on the web and on iOS and Android. Basics ($260 a year) covers PDF creation, editing, markup and length and area measurement. Core ($330) adds perimeter, volume, angle and count measurement, drawing overlay and CAD plug-ins. Complete ($440) adds Dynamic Fill, Excel Quantity Link, advanced reporting and batch tools. Max ($590 at an introductory price) adds AI drawing reviews and comparisons, AI access through MCP and connected Studio Sessions with Revit. Bluebeam offers a 14-day free trial of Max with no credit card.

Bluebeam lists integrations with Procore, SharePoint, ProjectWise, Newforma and Autodesk Forma, and one-click PDF creation from AutoCAD, Revit, SolidWorks and Navisworks.

The trade-off: Revu measures quantities but does not price them, so estimators pair it with Excel or a separate estimating tool. The takeoff tools most estimators want (perimeter, volume and count) start at Core, and Excel Quantity Link needs Complete. There is no monthly plan, and Max buyers keep the $590 price only through their 2027 renewal.

pros_detail.title: Markup and plan review
pros_detail.explanation: Mark up PDFs, compare drawing versions with overlays and run shared reviews in Studio Sessions and Projects across office and field.

pros_detail.title: Measurement takeoffs
pros_detail.explanation: From Core up, measure length, area, perimeter, volume, angle and count directly on the plans; Complete adds Dynamic Fill and Excel Quantity Link.

pros_detail.title: Desktop, web and mobile
pros_detail.explanation: Every plan includes Revu for Windows desktop plus Bluebeam on the web and on iOS and Android.

pros_detail.title: Construction software connections
pros_detail.explanation: Bluebeam lists integrations with Procore, SharePoint, ProjectWise, Newforma and Autodesk Forma, plus one-click PDF creation from AutoCAD and Revit.

pros_detail.title: Free trial without a card
pros_detail.explanation: The 14-day trial gives full access to the Max plan and does not ask for a credit card.

cons_detail.title: Annual billing only
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing page shows only per-user prices billed annually ($260 to $590 a year), with no monthly plan.

cons_detail.title: Takeoff tools split by tier
cons_detail.explanation: Basics measures only length and area. Perimeter, volume and count need Core, and Excel Quantity Link and Dynamic Fill need Complete.

cons_detail.title: No cost database
cons_detail.explanation: Revu measures quantities but does not price materials and labor, so estimates are finished in Excel or a separate estimating program.

cons_detail.title: Max price is introductory
cons_detail.explanation: Bluebeam says Max buyers keep the $590 price through their 2027 renewal; later renewals move to a list price not yet announced.

cons_detail.title: Not an operations system
cons_detail.explanation: It does not handle scheduling, dispatch, invoicing or accounting, so trade businesses still need separate software for those jobs.

tools.implementation_notes: Start the 14-day Max trial and test markup, measurement and Studio Sessions on a real plan set. Then choose a tier per person: Basics for people who only view and mark up, Core for estimators who need perimeter, volume and count, and Complete if you want Excel Quantity Link. Set up your markup tool sets and measurement scales before live bids, and connect Procore, SharePoint or ProjectWise if your drawings live there. Plan where pricing will happen (an Excel template or an estimating tool), since Revu measures but does not price.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Bluebeam Revu cost?
tool_faqs.a: Per user, billed annually: Basics $260, Core $330, Complete $440 and Max $590 (introductory). Bluebeam says Max buyers keep that price through their 2027 renewal. The pricing page shows no monthly option.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Bluebeam offers 14 days of the Max plan, including Revu for Windows and Bluebeam on web and mobile, with no credit card required.

tool_faqs.q: Which Bluebeam plan do I need for takeoffs?
tool_faqs.a: Basics measures length and area only. Core adds perimeter, volume, angle and count, which most estimators need. Complete adds Dynamic Fill and Quantity Link to Excel for linking measurement totals to bid spreadsheets.

tool_faqs.q: Is Bluebeam an estimating tool?
tool_faqs.a: It does measurement takeoffs off the plans but has no material and labor cost database. Contractors price the quantities in Excel (Quantity Link on Complete and Max) or in a separate estimating program.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns Bluebeam?
tool_faqs.a: Bluebeam, founded in 2002 and based in Pasadena, California, has been part of the Nemetschek Group since 2014.

tool_faqs.q: What is Bluebeam Max?
tool_faqs.a: The top plan, at an introductory $590 per user per year. It adds AI drawing reviews and comparisons, AI access through MCP, AI multi-view stitching and connected Studio Sessions with Revit to everything in Complete.

tools.name: UDA ConstructionOnline
tools.tagline: Construction management software for builders and contractors, from estimating and scheduling to job costing and client portals

pricing.pricing_note: Basics is priced per user: UDA's October 2025 announcement lists $199 a month or $1,999 a year (about $167 a month) for the first user, plus $30 a month or $300 a year per additional user; the Basics page sells 1-15 users through a calculator. Full plans (residential, commercial, specialty and multifamily, at Pro, Team and Business levels) are quoted based on construction volume and tools, and include unlimited users plus unlimited client and subcontractor access. Enterprise starts at $36,840 billed annually (about $3,070 a month). 10-day free trial. Verified against us.constructiononline.com pricing pages and news.constructiononline.com 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Residential builders, general contractors, remodelers and specialty contractors who want estimating, scheduling, financials, documents and client portals in one system, with unlimited users on the full plans
tools.weaknesses: Full plans are quote-only; Redline Takeoff is limited to Team, Business and Enterprise; it is built for project-based construction, not service-call dispatch; the entry Basics plan is priced per user
tools.long_description:
UDA ConstructionOnline is cloud construction management software from UDA Technologies, a company based in Auburn, Alabama. UDA says it first released software in 1999, and that its founder, Michael Stevens, came from the multifamily, commercial and custom residential construction markets. UDA says more than 950,000 construction professionals use its platforms. It sells ConstructionOnline to residential and production builders, general contractors, multifamily builders and specialty contractors such as electrical, HVAC, plumbing and roofing firms.

The platform covers estimating and proposals with costbooks, change orders, purchase orders, bills, invoicing and job costing; Gantt scheduling with baseline tracking; daily logs, punch lists, RFIs, submittals and time tracking; a plan room with markup; file and photo storage; and client and subcontractor portals. Redline Takeoff, UDA's on-screen takeoff tool, measures areas, counts and volumes on plans and sends the quantities into estimates. The help center says it comes with Team, Business and Enterprise subscriptions (one, three and ten licenses), not with Pro. There is a mobile app.

QuickBooks Online connects through a two-way sync: estimates, change orders and invoices go to QuickBooks, and actuals, committed costs and invoiced amounts come back for job costing. QuickBooks Desktop and PlanSwift connect through Socket, a Windows app from UDA installed on the same computer as QuickBooks. UDA also lists integrations with Docusign, Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook 365, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box and HubSpot, plus an API for custom connections.

Pricing has two tracks. ConstructionOnline Basics is priced per user: a UDA announcement from October 2025 lists $199 a month or $1,999 a year for the first user, plus $30 a month or $300 a year for each additional user, and the pricing page sells Basics for 1 to 15 users. The full residential, commercial, specialty and multifamily plans are quoted based on your construction volume and the tools you need, and include unlimited users and unlimited client and subcontractor access. Enterprise starts at $36,840 a year. UDA offers a 10-day free trial and says the full plans include free onboarding and training and U.S.-based support.

The trade-off: outside Basics and Enterprise you need a sales quote to learn the price, and takeoff requires Team or higher. ConstructionOnline is built around project-based construction work (estimates, schedules, budgets, documents) rather than dispatching technicians to service calls, so service trades that run on a dispatch board may be better served by field service software.

pros_detail.title: Broad project toolset
pros_detail.explanation: Estimating, scheduling, change orders, purchase orders, invoicing, job costing, daily logs, RFIs, submittals, plan markup and client portals sit in one system, so a builder does not have to stitch separate tools together.

pros_detail.title: Unlimited users on full plans
pros_detail.explanation: The residential, commercial, specialty and multifamily plans include unlimited users plus unlimited client and subcontractor portal access, so adding field and office staff does not add seat fees.

pros_detail.title: Two-way QuickBooks Online sync
pros_detail.explanation: Estimates, change orders and invoices go to QuickBooks Online, and actuals, committed costs and invoiced amounts come back into ConstructionOnline for job costing. QuickBooks Desktop connects through UDA's Socket app.

pros_detail.title: Built-in takeoff
pros_detail.explanation: Redline Takeoff measures floor and wall areas, fixture counts and concrete volumes on plans and sends the quantities into estimates, on Team, Business and Enterprise plans.

pros_detail.title: Per-user entry plan
pros_detail.explanation: Basics lets a small team start with estimating, selections, change orders, invoicing, Gantt scheduling, daily logs, client portals and 100 GB of storage without buying a full plan.

pros_detail.title: Onboarding included
pros_detail.explanation: UDA says its full plans include free onboarding and training and U.S.-based customer support.

cons_detail.title: Full-plan prices are not published
cons_detail.explanation: Residential, commercial, specialty and multifamily plans are quoted after you share details about your business, so you cannot compare costs without talking to sales. Enterprise starts at $36,840 a year.

cons_detail.title: Takeoff is not on every plan
cons_detail.explanation: Redline Takeoff comes only with Team, Business and Enterprise, with a set number of licenses (one, three or ten); Pro subscriptions do not include it.

cons_detail.title: Basics is priced per user
