cons_detail.explanation: Unlike the full plans, Basics charges for each user (UDA's October 2025 announcement lists $30 a month per added user), and the online calculator goes up to 15 users.

cons_detail.title: Not a service dispatch tool
cons_detail.explanation: It is built for project-based construction, not for dispatching technicians to service calls or planning routes.

cons_detail.title: A lot to set up
cons_detail.explanation: Estimating, scheduling, financial and portal tools each need setup (costbooks, schedule templates, QuickBooks mapping, permissions), so plan time for onboarding.

tools.implementation_notes: Start with the 10-day free trial and decide between Basics (priced per user) and a quoted full plan based on team size and whether you need Redline Takeoff (Team and up). Set up costbooks and estimate templates first, then schedule templates, user permissions and client and subcontractor portal access. Connect QuickBooks Online through the built-in two-way integration, or install UDA's Socket app on the Windows computer that runs QuickBooks Desktop. On a full plan, use the free onboarding and training UDA lists, and ask a product specialist to assign any takeoff licenses, which the help center says are assigned manually at a company admin's request.

tool_faqs.q: How much does UDA ConstructionOnline cost?
tool_faqs.a: Basics is priced per user: UDA's October 2025 announcement lists $199 a month or $1,999 a year for the first user, plus $30 a month or $300 a year per additional user. The full residential, commercial, specialty and multifamily plans are quoted to your business. Enterprise starts at $36,840 a year. There is a 10-day free trial.

tool_faqs.q: Does it include unlimited users?
tool_faqs.a: The full plans include unlimited users and unlimited client and subcontractor access. Basics is the exception: it is priced per user and sold for up to 15 users online.

tool_faqs.q: Does ConstructionOnline integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. QuickBooks Online has a two-way sync that sends estimates, change orders and invoices to QuickBooks and brings actuals and committed costs back. QuickBooks Desktop connects through UDA's Socket app on Windows.

tool_faqs.q: Does it include takeoff?
tool_faqs.a: Redline Takeoff is included with Team (one license), Business (three) and Enterprise (ten) subscriptions. Pro subscriptions do not include it, and extra licenses can be purchased.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes ConstructionOnline?
tool_faqs.a: UDA Technologies, based in Auburn, Alabama. UDA says it first released software in 1999 and that more than 950,000 construction professionals use its platforms.

tool_faqs.q: Is ConstructionOnline a field service (FSM) tool?
tool_faqs.a: Not primarily. It is built for project-based construction (estimating, scheduling, job costing, documents) rather than dispatching technicians to service calls.

tools.name: McCormick Estimating
tools.tagline: Electrical, plumbing and mechanical estimating software with built-in takeoff, from Foundation Software

pricing.pricing_note: No public pricing: mccormicksys.com shows no prices and directs buyers to request a demo. McCormick offers a cloud-based version, an on-premises option and hosted setups; subscription or license terms are not published. Verified against mccormicksys.com (home, software and industry pages) 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Electrical, plumbing and mechanical contractors who want trade-specific estimating with built-in takeoff, preloaded items and labor units, and supplier price updates
tools.weaknesses: No published pricing, it covers estimating rather than field operations, and it is built for electrical, plumbing and mechanical work rather than general trades
tools.long_description:
McCormick is estimating software for electrical, plumbing and mechanical contractors. It combines built-in takeoff (Design Estimating Pro) with preloaded databases of items, assemblies and labor units, so an estimator can measure a plan set and price the job in one system. McCormick says its electrical database has over 55,000 items and 25,000 prebuilt assemblies, and its mechanical product covers boiler systems, fire suppression, fire sprinklers and closed-circuit systems.

McCormick Systems was created in 1979 and is based in Chandler, Arizona. Foundation Software, a construction software company, acquired it in 2021, and the McCormick site describes the product as built and supported by the same team behind Foundation Software.

Labor units come preloaded, and McCormick says you can use NECA, PHCC or MCAA labor standards and adjust them. Material prices can be updated from major pricing services or directly from supply houses. Other features named on the site include auto-count takeoff, the patented Auto Home Run for electrical, reusable estimate templates, change order tracking, estimates vs. actual reports, and proposals and bid documents.

McCormick describes its software as cloud-based so several estimators can work on the same estimate, and it also offers an on-premises option and hosted setups. It does not publish prices; you request a demo and a quote. McCormick says its in-house support team has an average response time of under 10 minutes.

The trade-off: you cannot compare cost without a sales call, and McCormick covers estimating, not scheduling, dispatch or invoicing, so it runs alongside your field and accounting software. It is built around electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, so contractors in other trades will get little from its databases.

pros_detail.title: Trade-specific databases
pros_detail.explanation: Preloaded items, assemblies and labor units for electrical, plumbing and mechanical work; McCormick says the electrical database alone has over 55,000 items and 25,000 assemblies.

pros_detail.title: Built-in takeoff
pros_detail.explanation: Design Estimating Pro and auto-count let estimators measure and count from digital plans inside the same program that prices the job.

pros_detail.title: Current material prices
pros_detail.explanation: Prices can be updated from major pricing services or directly from your supply house, so estimates reflect current costs.

pros_detail.title: Labor standards
pros_detail.explanation: Labor units come preloaded, with NECA, PHCC and MCAA standards available and adjustable for your crews.

pros_detail.title: Cloud or on-premises
pros_detail.explanation: McCormick is cloud-based for shared access, and it also offers an on-premises option and hosted setups.

pros_detail.title: Backed by Foundation Software
pros_detail.explanation: Foundation Software has owned McCormick since 2021, and the same team builds and supports it.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing
cons_detail.explanation: McCormick does not list prices on its site, so you need a demo and quote to learn the cost.

cons_detail.title: Estimating only
cons_detail.explanation: It produces estimates, change orders and bid documents, not scheduling, dispatch or invoicing, so it runs alongside other software.

cons_detail.title: Narrow trade focus
cons_detail.explanation: The databases are built for electrical, plumbing and mechanical work. Contractors in other trades should look at a general takeoff tool.

cons_detail.title: Setup to match your shop
cons_detail.explanation: Getting accurate bids means adjusting labor units, assemblies and supplier pricing to how your shop actually works, which takes time before the first live bid.

tools.implementation_notes: Request a demo and a quote, and decide between the cloud version, the on-premises option or a hosted setup. Before bidding live work, set your labor units (NECA, PHCC or MCAA if you use them), connect your supply house or pricing service for material prices, and build templates for the job types you bid most. Train estimators on takeoff with Design Estimating Pro and auto-count. Ask McCormick which accounting systems it connects with, since the site does not name them.

tool_faqs.q: How much does McCormick Estimating cost?
tool_faqs.a: McCormick does not publish prices. You request a demo and a quote from its sales team.

tool_faqs.q: Who owns McCormick Systems?
tool_faqs.a: Foundation Software, which acquired McCormick in 2021. McCormick was created in 1979 and is based in Chandler, Arizona.

tool_faqs.q: Which trades is McCormick for?
tool_faqs.a: Electrical, plumbing and mechanical contractors, with pages also for transmission and distribution and automated building systems. Its databases and labor units are built for those trades.

tool_faqs.q: Is McCormick cloud-based?
tool_faqs.a: McCormick describes its software as cloud-based, and it also offers an on-premises option for contractors who want local control, plus hosted setups.

tool_faqs.q: Does McCormick include takeoff?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. Design Estimating Pro provides built-in digital takeoff, with auto-count and, for electrical, the patented Auto Home Run feature.

tool_faqs.q: How is McCormick different from STACK or PlanSwift?
tool_faqs.a: STACK and PlanSwift are general takeoff and estimating tools used across many trades. McCormick is built only for electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, with preloaded trade items, assemblies and labor units.

tools.name: FastEST
tools.tagline: Estimating software for plumbing, mechanical piping, HVAC ductwork and insulation (FastPIPE, FastDUCT, FastWRAP)

pricing.pricing_note: Per application, for a stand-alone install on a single PC or tablet. Lease: $250/mo first application, $105/mo each additional (FastPIPE + FastDUCT combo $355/mo), maintenance included, license owned after 36 payments. Purchase: $4,995 first application, $2,495 each additional; optional maintenance $1,250/yr after the first year. 60-day money-back guarantee. Shared-session (network) licensing is quoted.

tools.best_for: Commercial plumbing, mechanical, HVAC sheet metal and insulation contractors who want trade-specific estimating on Windows and prefer to lease or buy a license rather than subscribe
tools.weaknesses: Each application is priced separately ($250 a month lease or $4,995 purchase for the first one), published prices cover one PC or tablet, and it is Windows estimating software with no accounting integrations named
tools.long_description:
FastEST is estimating software for mechanical trades, sold as three applications on a shared platform: FastPIPE for plumbing, HVAC piping and industrial process piping; FastDUCT for commercial HVAC sheet metal and industrial ductwork; and FastWRAP for mechanical insulation. Estimators take off quantities on screen from PDF plans and image files, and the software calculates quantities such as linear feet, weight, surface area, material costs and labor hours. Results export to Excel, CSV and XML for the final bid summary.

FastEST, Inc. was incorporated in 1994 and is headquartered in Wichita, Kansas. It says it has thousands of users, from single-estimator startups to large multi-office firms. The catalogs include duct, fittings, piping and insulation products, with material pricing you can set per job from your supplier quotes. FastPIPE can use MCAA or PHCC labor estimates, and FastDUCT works together with FastPIPE on combined jobs. The software runs on Windows, including tablets and touch-screen PCs.

Each application is priced for a stand-alone install on one PC or tablet. You can lease at $250 a month for the first application and $105 a month for each additional one (FastPIPE and FastDUCT together are $355 a month); maintenance is included and the license is yours after 36 payments. Or you can buy at $4,995 for the first application and $2,495 for each additional one, with the first year of maintenance included and optional maintenance of $1,250 a year after that. Purchases include installation assistance, online training and support, and material pricing updates, with a 60-day money-back guarantee. Shared network licensing is quoted separately.

The trade-off: FastEST is a real upfront or monthly cost per application, and a contractor who bids piping, ductwork and insulation needs more than one. It covers estimating only, runs on Windows, and names no accounting or field-service integrations, so data moves to other systems through Excel, CSV or XML exports.

pros_detail.title: Built for mechanical trades
pros_detail.explanation: FastPIPE, FastDUCT and FastWRAP each cover one scope (piping, ductwork, insulation) with catalogs and labor data for that work.

pros_detail.title: Lease or buy
pros_detail.explanation: Lease from $250 a month for the first application and own it after 36 payments, or buy it for $4,995. Both options include maintenance for the covered period.

pros_detail.title: Training and updates included
pros_detail.explanation: Purchases include installation assistance, online training and support, and material pricing updates.

pros_detail.title: 60-day money-back guarantee
pros_detail.explanation: FastEST offers a 60-day money-back guarantee on both lease and purchase.

pros_detail.title: Industry labor data
pros_detail.explanation: FastPIPE can use MCAA or PHCC labor estimates, and FastDUCT labor rates can be adjusted for job or site conditions.

cons_detail.title: Priced per application
cons_detail.explanation: Each application costs $250 a month or $4,995 for the first one, plus $105 a month or $2,495 for each additional, so covering piping, ductwork and insulation adds up.

cons_detail.title: One PC per license
cons_detail.explanation: Published prices cover a stand-alone install on one PC or tablet. Several estimators sharing a network license need a quote.

cons_detail.title: Windows only
cons_detail.explanation: FastEST describes its software as running on Windows PCs and tablets; no web or Mac version is mentioned.

cons_detail.title: Estimating only
cons_detail.explanation: It produces takeoffs and bid summaries, not scheduling, dispatch or invoicing, and no accounting integration is named.

tools.implementation_notes: Decide which applications you need (FastPIPE for piping, FastDUCT for ductwork, FastWRAP for insulation) and whether to lease or buy; the lease includes maintenance and the license is owned after 36 payments. If more than one estimator needs access, ask for network licensing pricing. Use the included installation assistance and online training to set up your material prices from supplier quotes and adjust labor rates for your crews. Test a real bid inside the 60-day money-back window, and set up an Excel template for the bid summary if you move numbers into other systems.

tool_faqs.q: How much does FastEST cost?
tool_faqs.a: Per application, for one PC or tablet. Lease: $250 a month for the first application and $105 a month for each additional one, with maintenance included and the license owned after 36 payments. Purchase: $4,995 for the first application and $2,495 for each additional one, with the first year of maintenance included and $1,250 a year after that. Network licensing is quoted separately.

tool_faqs.q: What are FastPIPE, FastDUCT and FastWRAP?
tool_faqs.a: The three FastEST applications: FastPIPE for plumbing, HVAC piping and industrial process piping; FastDUCT for commercial HVAC sheet metal and ductwork; FastWRAP for mechanical insulation. They share one platform, and FastDUCT works together with FastPIPE.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a money-back guarantee?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. FastEST offers a 60-day money-back guarantee on both purchases and leases.

tool_faqs.q: Does FastEST run in the cloud?
tool_faqs.a: FastEST describes its software as running on Windows, including tablets and touch-screen PCs, installed on a single PC or on a network. No web or Mac version is mentioned.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes FastEST?
tool_faqs.a: FastEST, Inc., incorporated in 1994 and headquartered in Wichita, Kansas. It says it has thousands of users across the country.

tool_faqs.q: FastEST or McCormick for mechanical estimating?
tool_faqs.a: Both are trade-specific estimating tools. FastEST publishes lease and purchase prices per application and covers piping, ductwork and insulation on Windows. McCormick covers electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, is cloud-based with an on-premises option, and is sold by quote.

tools.name: CoreJobTrack
tools.tagline: Flat-priced field service software from Barrett Software, with work orders, dispatch, customer sign-off and equipment reading history

pricing.pricing_note: Flat per-company pricing with user caps: Starter $39/mo (up to 5 users; basic ticketing and tasks, mobile app, offline mode, 5 GB storage), Professional $79/mo (up to 25 users; adds dispatch, customer portal, reports, signatures and attachments, 25 GB), Enterprise $149/mo (unlimited users; adds audit logs, API access, custom integrations and workflows, unlimited storage). Nightly backups add-on $9.99/mo. Monthly or annual billing; annual is advertised as saving 15% (annual amounts not listed). A launch special offered Enterprise features at $39/mo with no stated end date. No free trial: payment is due when you subscribe. Verified against corejobtrack.com/pricing.html and /faq.html 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Small and mid-sized field service businesses (the vendor names HVAC, plumbing, electrical and contracting) that want work orders, dispatch, customer sign-off and per-equipment reading history at a flat monthly price instead of per-user fees.
tools.weaknesses: New product (the corejobtrack.com domain was registered in February 2026) with no named accounting or payment integrations and no free trial. At standard prices, dispatch, the customer portal and signatures start at the $79 Professional plan, and we found no public App Store listing for the mobile app.
tools.long_description:
CoreJobTrack is field service software from Barrett Software, founded by Steve Barrett in Grand Blanc, Michigan. It is aimed at small and mid-sized blue-collar service businesses with field techs and an office dispatch team; its FAQ names HVAC, plumbing, electrical and contracting. The workflow runs from dispatch to signed completion: the office assigns work, dates and priorities, techs document the job with notes, photos, video and files, and the customer signs on the tech's device or remotely through a browser link.

Its most distinctive feature is equipment history. Each equipment reading is tied to the equipment, the visit, the technician and a timestamp, and CoreJobTrack summarizes count changes over a period as production rates and count-over-time charts. Other listed features include an operations dashboard, personal dashboards, technician statistics and leaderboards, customer and contact records linked to locations and equipment, audit history, and a customer portal where clients see ticket status. The features page also lists quotes and proposals, while the docs list that guide as coming soon.

Pricing is per company with user caps rather than per user: Starter is $39 a month for up to 5 users, Professional $79 for up to 25 users and Enterprise $149 for unlimited users, with an optional $9.99 a month nightly backups add-on. Annual billing is advertised as saving 15%. Starter covers basic ticketing and tasks; dispatch, the customer portal, reports and signatures start at Professional; audit logs, API access and custom workflows are Enterprise features. When we checked, a launch special offered Enterprise features at $39 a month with no stated end date. There is no free trial: the FAQ says payment is due when you subscribe.

CoreJobTrack says its mobile app runs on iOS and Android and keeps working offline, syncing when signal returns. We did not find it in a public App Store search, so ask how techs install it. The trade-off: this is a new product (the corejobtrack.com domain was registered in February 2026) with no named accounting or payment integrations, so invoicing and bookkeeping stay in a separate tool, and you pay before you can try it.

pros_detail.title: Flat per-company pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Plans are priced per company with user caps ($39 for up to 5 users, $79 for up to 25, $149 for unlimited), so adding a tech inside a tier does not raise the bill.

pros_detail.title: Equipment readings and production history
pros_detail.explanation: Readings are tied to the equipment, visit, technician and time, with production-rate summaries and count-over-time charts, which suits shops that service machines with meters or counters.

pros_detail.title: Sign-off on site or by link
pros_detail.explanation: Customers can sign on the tech's device after readiness checks, or review the service details and sign remotely in a browser.

pros_detail.title: Offline field work
pros_detail.explanation: The vendor says techs can keep working in dead zones and queued changes sync once signal returns.

pros_detail.title: Published prices
pros_detail.explanation: All three plans and the backups add-on are listed on the pricing page, with no quote gating.

cons_detail.title: New product with little track record
cons_detail.explanation: The corejobtrack.com domain was registered in February 2026 and the vendor publishes no customer count.

cons_detail.title: No named integrations
cons_detail.explanation: The site names no accounting or payment integrations. Enterprise lists API access and custom integrations, but plan to invoice and keep books in a separate tool.

cons_detail.title: No free trial
cons_detail.explanation: The FAQ says payment is due when you subscribe, and there is no no-cost evaluation period.

cons_detail.title: Core features sit in higher tiers
cons_detail.explanation: At standard prices Starter covers basic ticketing and tasks; dispatch, the customer portal, reports and signatures need Professional, and audit logs and API access need Enterprise.

cons_detail.title: Mobile app not in public store search
cons_detail.explanation: CoreJobTrack says it has iOS and Android apps, but we did not find a public App Store listing, so confirm how the app is distributed.

tools.implementation_notes: Setup is self-serve: pick a plan with monthly or annual billing, complete checkout, then create your workspace. Add office staff, techs and customers, and record the equipment you service so readings build a history from the first visit. Decide whether you need the $9.99 a month nightly backups add-on. Since no accounting integrations are named, set up a routine for moving completed work into your invoicing or accounting tool, and ask the vendor how techs install the iOS or Android app. The docs cover the mobile app, web dashboard, admin setup and an API reference, and the vendor invites you to contact it for help with team rollout.

tool_faqs.q: How much does CoreJobTrack cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starter is $39 a month for up to 5 users, Professional $79 a month for up to 25 users and Enterprise $149 a month for unlimited users. Nightly backups are an optional $9.99 a month, and annual billing is advertised as saving 15%. When we checked on 2026-09-29, a launch special offered Enterprise features at $39 a month with no stated end date.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: No. The FAQ says payment is due when you subscribe and CoreJobTrack does not include a no-cost evaluation period.

tool_faqs.q: Does CoreJobTrack integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: No accounting integrations are named on the site. The Enterprise plan lists API access and custom integrations, so ask the vendor if you need a connection to your books.

tool_faqs.q: Who is CoreJobTrack for?
tool_faqs.a: The vendor says it is built for small and mid-sized blue-collar service businesses with field techs and office dispatch, naming HVAC, plumbing, electrical and contracting. Its equipment reading history is most useful to shops that service machines.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a mobile app?
tool_faqs.a: CoreJobTrack says its app runs on iOS and Android with an offline mode. We did not find a public App Store listing, so ask how techs install it.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes CoreJobTrack?
tool_faqs.a: Barrett Software of Grand Blanc, Michigan, founded by Steve Barrett.

tools.name: Roll-Off Amigo
tools.tagline: Phone-first roll-off dispatch, bin tracking and invoicing, with a free plan for owner-operators

pricing.pricing_note: Free Forever is $0/month with unlimited jobs, dispatch board, bin tracking, invoicing and English/Spanish interface; the owner runs the board and drivers have no app login. Pro is $99/month, billed monthly, with unlimited drivers, individual driver app logins, real-time GPS, push notifications, photo proof of delivery, tap-to-navigate and field completion; 30-day free trial, cancel anytime, no contract. No annual plan shown. Invoice payments run through Stripe. Verified against rolloffamigo.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Owner-operators and roll-off companies with 1 to 20 trucks (the vendor's stated range) that run dispatch off a whiteboard and group texts and want a phone-first app at no cost or one flat price, including crews with Spanish-speaking drivers.
tools.weaknesses: New product (iOS version 1.0 released March 10, 2026) with no QuickBooks integration yet (the vendor lists it as coming soon) and no automated route optimization. Driver app logins, GPS and photo proof need the paid Pro plan, and it is not built for front-load or residential routes, portable toilets or compactors.
tools.long_description:
Roll-Off Amigo is operations software for roll-off dumpster companies from Dyrt Labs, Inc. of Vernon, California. It runs on the web, iPhone and Android. The product is new: the rolloffamigo.com domain was registered in February 2026 and version 1.0 of the iOS app was released on March 10, 2026. The vendor targets operations with 1 to 20 trucks and says it is not built for front-load or residential trash routes, portable toilets, compactors or enterprise ERP integration.

The Free Forever plan costs $0 with unlimited jobs, a drag-to-reschedule dispatch board for drops, pickups, swaps and relocations, bin tracking with alerts for bins overdue for pickup, invoicing with card payments through Stripe, and an English and Spanish interface. On the free plan the owner runs the board and still calls or texts drivers. The app also includes customer records with job history, expense and mileage logging, and revenue reports by day, week or month. Per the App Store release notes, jobs can carry a haul fee, included tons, an overage rate and rental days, with customer rates filled in from billing profiles.

Pro is $99 a month, billed monthly, with unlimited drivers and a 30-day free trial. It adds individual driver app logins, real-time GPS tracking, push notifications for new jobs, photo proof of delivery, tap-to-navigate and jobs that complete from the field. Every company also gets a hosted online ordering page that can be embedded on its website with one line of code, and a Roll-Off Amigo Shopify app syncs store orders into dispatch and billing.

The trade-off: the product is months old, and the vendor lists its own gaps: no QuickBooks integration yet (it says coming soon) and no AI-powered route optimization. For now, accounting means moving Stripe payments and invoices into your own books, and any crew beyond a single owner-driver needs Pro to put drivers on the app.

pros_detail.title: A free plan, not a trial
pros_detail.explanation: Free Forever includes unlimited jobs, the dispatch board, bin tracking, invoicing and the bilingual interface with no time limit and no contract.

pros_detail.title: One flat price for any crew size
pros_detail.explanation: Pro is $99 a month with unlimited drivers, so adding trucks does not add seat fees, and it comes with a 30-day free trial and cancel-anytime terms.

pros_detail.title: English and Spanish throughout
pros_detail.explanation: The vendor says the entire app works in both English and Spanish.

pros_detail.title: Online ordering without a developer
pros_detail.explanation: A hosted ordering page, a one-line embed and a Shopify app bring customer orders straight onto the dispatch board.

pros_detail.title: Bin tracking with overdue alerts
pros_detail.explanation: See every bin on a map, whether it is in the yard or on site, and get alerts for bins overdue for pickup.

cons_detail.title: Very new product
cons_detail.explanation: The domain dates to February 2026 and the iOS app to March 2026, so there is little track record to judge.

cons_detail.title: No QuickBooks sync yet
cons_detail.explanation: The vendor lists QuickBooks integration as coming soon; today invoices and payments run through Stripe.

cons_detail.title: No automated routing
cons_detail.explanation: The vendor says it has no AI-powered route optimization yet, and its own blog points fleets that need automated routing for 20-plus trucks to Docket.

cons_detail.title: Driver features are Pro-only
cons_detail.explanation: On the free plan drivers have no app login, so the owner still calls or texts them; GPS, push notifications and photo proof need Pro.

cons_detail.title: Roll-off only
cons_detail.explanation: It is not built for front-load or residential routes, portable toilets or compactors.

tools.implementation_notes: Signup is self-serve, and the vendor says setup takes about five minutes with a guided wizard. Add customers and job sites, enter your bins, and set default rates in Settings so they fill in on new jobs. Connect Stripe to take card payments. If you have drivers, start the 30-day Pro trial so each driver can log in to the iOS or Android app. Share your hosted ordering link or paste the embed code on your website, and install the Shopify app if you sell there. Plan to move invoices into your accounting tool by hand, since QuickBooks integration is listed as coming soon.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Roll-Off Amigo cost?
tool_faqs.a: Free Forever is $0 a month with unlimited jobs, the dispatch board, bin tracking, invoicing and an English and Spanish interface. Pro is $99 a month, billed monthly, with unlimited drivers, driver app logins, real-time GPS, push notifications and photo proof, plus a 30-day free trial and no contract. Card payments run through Stripe. Verified 2026-09-29.

tool_faqs.q: Does Roll-Off Amigo integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Not yet. The vendor lists QuickBooks integration as coming soon. Invoices and payments run through Stripe, and a Shopify app syncs store orders into dispatch and billing.

tool_faqs.q: Is there a driver app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, on iOS and Android, but individual driver logins, GPS tracking, push notifications and photo proof are Pro features. On the free plan the owner assigns jobs on the board and calls or texts drivers.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Roll-Off Amigo?
tool_faqs.a: Dyrt Labs, Inc. of Vernon, California. Version 1.0 of the iOS app was released on March 10, 2026, so the product has a short track record.

tool_faqs.q: What does Roll-Off Amigo not cover?
tool_faqs.a: The vendor says it is not built for front-load or residential trash routes, portable toilets, compactors or enterprise ERP integration such as SAP, Oracle or NetSuite.

tools.name: Bin Boss
tools.tagline: Dumpster rental software built by a working hauler, with online booking, automatic overage charges and QuickBooks Online sync

pricing.pricing_note: One plan, Bin Boss Complete, at $99/month, month-to-month, no contract, cancel anytime. Includes unlimited admins, office users and drivers, online booking widget, dispatch board, driver app, invoicing and payments, CRM, inventory tracking, QuickBooks Online integration, reporting and data exports, and client portal. No free trial, only a free demo with no credit card. Optional websites: template $40/month plus $99 setup, or custom $399 one-time plus $40/month hosting. Card payments run through Stripe (about 2.9% + $0.30) plus a 0.75% platform fee retained by Bin Boss per the Terms of Service updated 2026-03-30; fees are non-refundable unless stated otherwise in writing. Verified against mybinboss.com/pricing and /bin-boss-terms-of-service 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Small roll-off dumpster companies that want 24/7 online booking with deposits, automatic weight-overage charges, QuickBooks Online sync and one flat monthly price with unlimited users and drivers.
tools.weaknesses: Young product with no free trial (demo only), a 0.75% platform fee on card payments on top of Stripe's rate that appears in the Terms of Service rather than on the pricing page, and fees that are non-refundable unless stated otherwise in writing. QuickBooks Desktop is not supported.
tools.long_description:
Bin Boss is dumpster rental software from Bin Boss Software LLC of Miamisburg, Ohio. The vendor says founder Todd Atkinson, who founded Pack Mule Dumpsters, built it to manage his own fleet of more than 80 dumpsters. The mybinboss.com domain was registered in June 2024, and Apple lists the first release of the iOS app (published under STNS Solutions LLC) as July 30, 2025.

One plan, Bin Boss Complete, costs $99 a month, month-to-month with no contract, and the pricing page lists unlimited admins, office users and drivers. It includes an online booking widget that verifies addresses, prices by service area and mileage, blocks booked inventory, collects e-signed rental agreements and takes full payment, a deposit or pay-on-delivery through Stripe. The widget embeds on WordPress, Wix or Squarespace sites or works as a standalone link. Bookings land on a drag-and-drop dispatch board with a live driver map and per-driver routes that the system sequences automatically, and customers can get SMS or email notifications.

The iPhone and Android driver app shows jobs with placement notes and gate codes, opens Google Maps or Apple Maps for navigation, uploads photos, and handles the dump workflow: drivers pick the site, enter the weight ticket and photograph the dump receipt. Bin Boss then compares the weight to the dumpster's allowance and creates a pending overage charge for review before invoicing. The app also has timesheet clock-in and clock-out. The office side adds inventory by storage lot, invoicing, a client portal, CRM with contractor grouping, discount codes, reporting and data exports, and QuickBooks Online sync of invoices, payments and customers.

The trade-off: the Terms of Service (updated March 30, 2026) add a 0.75% platform fee retained by Bin Boss on top of Stripe's roughly 2.9% + $0.30, and fees are non-refundable unless stated otherwise in writing. There is no self-serve trial, only a free demo, and the QuickBooks integration covers QuickBooks Online, not Desktop. Bin Boss also sells websites as an add-on: a template site at $40 a month plus a $99 setup fee, or a custom site at $399 one-time plus $40 a month.

pros_detail.explanation: The vendor says its founder built Bin Boss to run his own fleet of more than 80 dumpsters at Pack Mule Dumpsters.

pros_detail.title: Booking that collects money

pros_detail.title: Automatic overage charges

pros_detail.title: Flat price with unlimited users

pros_detail.title: Dump workflow in the driver app

cons_detail.title: Platform fee on card payments
cons_detail.explanation: The Terms of Service disclose a 0.75% platform fee retained by Bin Boss on top of Stripe's roughly 2.9% + $0.30. The pricing page does not list it.

cons_detail.title: No trial and non-refundable fees

tools.implementation_notes: Start with the free demo. The vendor includes onboarding support and says most customers are up and running in 4-5 days. Connect Stripe for payments and QuickBooks Online for accounting, set your service areas, pricing, weight allowances and rental agreement, then embed the booking widget on your WordPress, Wix or Squarespace site or share the standalone booking link. tool_faqs.q: How much does Bin Boss cost?

Card payments cost Stripe's roughly 2.9% + $0.30 plus a 0.75% Bin Boss platform fee under the Terms of Service. Optional websites are $40 a month plus a $99 setup fee (template) or $399 one-time plus $40 a month (custom). Verified 2026-09-29.

tool_faqs.q: Does Bin Boss integrate with QuickBooks?

tool_faqs.q: Is there a free trial?

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Bin Boss?

tool_faqs.q: Does Bin Boss handle weight overages?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. When a driver enters the actual weight, Bin Boss compares it to the dumpster's weight allowance and creates a pending overage charge that the office reviews before invoicing.

tools.name: iCANS
tools.tagline: Dumpster rental software from a Florida hauler, with unlimited drivers and built-in card and ACH processing

pricing.pricing_note: Flat per-business pricing billed month-to-month; unlimited drivers and orders; no setup fees and no cancellation fees. Base ($99/mo) includes dispatch, driver app, invoicing, QuickBooks Online sync, Tiger Payment card processing, customer portal, website integration, inventory, employee scheduling and custom email notifications. Plus ($159/mo) adds custom text notifications (up to 1,000 messages/month), deeper analytics dashboards and the AI Review Filter. 7-day free trial of Base with no credit card; onboarding included. Card and ACH processing through Tiger Payment Solutions is billed per transaction at unpublished rates. Verified against icans.ai/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Owner-operator and small roll-off dumpster companies that want one flat monthly price with unlimited drivers, a simple driver app, built-in card and ACH processing and two-way QuickBooks Online sync, and that are comfortable starting from a self-serve free trial.
tools.weaknesses: Card and ACH processing rates through Tiger Payment Solutions are not published, text notifications are Plus-only and capped at 1,000 a month, and the customer and volume figures are the vendor's own. The terms rule out refunds for partial billing periods.
tools.long_description:
iCANS is dumpster rental software from iCANS, Inc. of Longwood, Florida. Founder Ricardo Rivera started Junk It Plus Dumpsters in South Florida with a single truck and hired developers to build software for his own operation; the vendor says he still runs that business, now more than 600 dumpsters, while leading iCANS. iCANS says more than 400 dumpster rental companies use it.

The office side is a command center with dispatch: AI-built routes optimized per territory and asset type, drag-and-drop reassignment and live driver locations with ETAs. The iOS and Android driver app shows the day's route, captures photos at each stop, records load states (empty, full, dumped, returned) and customer signatures, and lets drivers flag urgent issues with a photo and timestamp that alerts dispatch. Invoices are generated from completed tasks, card and ACH payments are built in through Tiger Payment Solutions (with Deluxe named as an alternative processor), and a two-way QuickBooks Online sync covers clients, invoices, payments and refunds. A branded customer portal lets commercial accounts book around the clock, pay invoices and overages, track active rentals and request swaps or rescheduled pickups.

Pricing is flat per business, month-to-month: Base is $99 a month and Plus is $159 a month, both with unlimited drivers and orders, no setup fees and no cancellation fees. Base includes dispatch, the driver app, invoicing, QuickBooks Online sync, card processing, the customer portal, website integration, inventory, employee scheduling and custom email notifications. Plus adds custom text notifications (up to 1,000 messages a month), deeper analytics dashboards (asset utilization, profit and loss, landfill cost tracking) and an AI Review Filter for collecting reviews. A 7-day free trial of Base needs no credit card, and onboarding with a dedicated specialist is included.

The trade-off: card and ACH fees are billed per transaction at rates iCANS describes only as industry-competitive, so get the rate in writing before comparing total cost. The customer counts and payment volumes are the vendor's own figures, and the terms of service say refunds are not provided for partial billing periods or unused features.

pros_detail.title: Flat, transparent subscription
pros_detail.explanation: $99 or $159 a month per business with unlimited drivers and orders, month-to-month, with no setup or cancellation fees.

pros_detail.title: Self-serve trial
pros_detail.explanation: A 7-day free trial with every Base feature and no credit card; the vendor says you can be live in under 30 minutes.

pros_detail.title: Two-way QuickBooks Online sync
pros_detail.explanation: Clients, invoices, payments and refunds sync both ways, which cuts double entry.

pros_detail.title: Driver app with proof of service
pros_detail.explanation: Photos at each stop, one-tap load states, on-screen signatures and urgent-issue flags feed dispatch in real time.

pros_detail.title: Customer portal on every plan
pros_detail.explanation: Commercial accounts can book, pay invoices and overages, track rentals and request swaps without calling the office.

cons_detail.title: Processing rates not published
cons_detail.explanation: Card and ACH fees through Tiger Payment Solutions are billed per transaction at rates described only as industry-competitive; ask for the actual rate.

cons_detail.title: Text messages need an upgrade
cons_detail.explanation: Custom text notifications are only on Plus and capped at 1,000 messages a month; Base has custom email notifications.

cons_detail.title: Vendor-reported figures
cons_detail.explanation: The 400-plus customer count, payment volume and other usage figures come from iCANS's own site.

cons_detail.title: No partial-period refunds
cons_detail.explanation: The terms of service say refunds are not provided for partial billing periods or unused features, and the subscription renews each cycle until you cancel by email.

tools.implementation_notes: Sign up for the 7-day trial at app.icans.ai with no credit card. Onboarding is included on every plan: the vendor says a dedicated specialist walks you through setup, imports your existing clients and inventory, configures QuickBooks sync and trains your team. Set up card and ACH processing through Tiger Payment Solutions and get the rates in writing. Have drivers install the iCANS driver app from the App Store or Google Play. Choose Plus if you need text notifications or the deeper analytics; plan changes take effect on the next billing cycle.

tool_faqs.q: How much does iCANS cost?
tool_faqs.a: Base is $99 a month and Plus is $159 a month, billed month-to-month per business with unlimited drivers and orders, no setup fees and no cancellation fees. Card and ACH processing through Tiger Payment Solutions is charged per transaction at rates that are not published. Verified 2026-09-29.

tool_faqs.q: Does iCANS offer a free trial?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. A 7-day free trial with full access to every Base feature and no credit card. If you do not subscribe at the end, the account pauses and nothing is charged.

tool_faqs.q: Does iCANS integrate with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Yes. iCANS advertises two-way QuickBooks Online sync for clients, invoices, payments and refunds, and onboarding includes configuring it.

tool_faqs.q: Is there an iCANS driver app?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, on iOS and Android, included in every plan with unlimited drivers. It covers the day's route, photos, load states, customer signatures, live GPS and urgent-issue reports.

tool_faqs.q: What is the difference between Base and Plus?
tool_faqs.a: Plus adds custom text notifications (up to 1,000 a month), deeper analytics dashboards (asset utilization, profit and loss, landfill cost tracking) and the AI Review Filter. Everything else is the same, and you can switch plans at any time, effective the next billing cycle.

tools.long_description:
Dumpster Rental Systems (DRS) is software for roll-off dumpster rental companies. Event Rental Systems (ERS), which makes software for event rental businesses, describes DRS as its partner software for roll-off dumpster rentals and links to it from its site. The dumpsterrentalsystems.com domain was registered in October 2019, and the DRS Driver App has been on the App Store since May 2020.

The iOS driver app is made for DRS customers. Drivers clock in and out, see their assigned orders for the day, take payments, add photos, and view and sign contracts. Version 5.0.0, released in June 2026, added support for the DynaFlex II Go card reader and one-tap opening of delivery addresses in a maps app.

Ownership is worth asking about. The ERS Master Services Agreement (updated June 2, 2026) names Fullsteam Software Holdings LLC, doing business as Event Rental Systems and a subsidiary of Fullsteam Operations LLC, as the contracting company. That agreement requires ERS clients to enroll in its integrated payment platform within 60 days and reserves the right to charge fees to clients who process payments elsewhere. We could not confirm whether DRS falls under the same ownership or terms.

The pricing section on this page reflects DRS's pricing page as last verified on 2026-08-21. The DRS website blocked our checks in the September 2026 review, so plans, prices, features and integrations could not be rechecked. The trade-off: expect to confirm current plans, payment processing rates and contract terms directly with DRS before you commit.

tools.name: Lavo CRM
tools.tagline: CRM, instant quoting and scheduling software built only for pressure washing and exterior cleaning companies

pricing.pricing_note: Per-company monthly plans: Starter $47/month with 2 users; Core $97/month with 5+ users and Complete $157/month with 7+ users, both labeled 'Launch Special' against regular prices of $127 and $177. No per-user fee is listed. Instant quoting, route density and QuickBooks Online sync start on Core. Yearly billing is advertised as 'Save 15%+' with no annual prices shown. 14-day free trial on every plan; no contract. Card processing rates are not published. Verified against lavocrm.com/pricing 2026-09-29.

tools.best_for: Owner-operators and small crews in pressure washing, soft washing and other exterior cleaning who want address-based instant quotes and zone-based scheduling in one trade-specific tool
tools.weaknesses: Young, small vendor with little independent track record; instant quoting and route density start on Core, not Starter; Core and Complete prices are labeled launch specials; route density groups work by zone and day rather than sequencing stops; annual prices and processing rates are not published
tools.long_description:
Lavo CRM is customer management, quoting and scheduling software built only for pressure washing and exterior cleaning businesses: house washing, soft washing, window cleaning, concrete and similar work. It is made by Fiat Software LLC of Centerburg, Ohio. Founder Aaron May also founded Snappy's Power Washing in Ohio, and Lavo began as software for his own washing business. Mike Carmody, who owns Mike's Pressure Washing and Fresh Rinse Media, handles marketing.

The headline feature is instant quoting: a customer types a property address and gets a price in seconds, based on property data and satellite imagery rather than a hand measurement. Lavo's privacy policy lists RentCast for property data and Mapbox and Google for maps. The second feature is route density: you map service zones, and online booking steers new jobs toward the days and zones where you are already working. Lavo says more than 16,000 quotes have been automated and more than $15 million quoted through the software.

Around those sit the everyday tools: scheduling, a customer portal, online booking, job photos with before-and-after alignment, e-signatures, invoicing with installment billing, card and ACH payments, automated review requests, email and SMS follow-ups, and marketing broadcasts. Integrations include Stripe, Square, QuickBooks Online, Google Calendar and Zapier, plus webhooks and LavoLink, a connector that lets AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude read and work in the CRM.

Pricing is per company. Starter is $47 a month with 2 users. Core is $97 a month with 5 or more users and Complete is $157 a month with 7 or more users; both are marked as launch specials against regular prices of $127 and $177. Instant quoting, route density, SMS follow-ups, QuickBooks Online sync and a branded webpage start on Core, and Complete adds business divisions, webhooks, an AI analyst, sales proposals and a Christmas lighting design tool. Every plan has a 14-day free trial with no contract, and yearly billing is advertised at 15% or more off without published annual prices.

The trade-off: Lavo is a young product from a small team, so there is little independent track record to check. The two features that set it apart are not in the $47 Starter plan, and the Core and Complete prices are promotional. Route density groups jobs by zone and day; it does not plan the order of stops within a day.

pros_detail.title: Built only for exterior cleaning
pros_detail.explanation: Lavo's services, pricing logic and workflows are set up for house washing, soft washing, windows and concrete, so there are no other trades to strip out.

pros_detail.title: Made by working washers
pros_detail.explanation: Founder Aaron May started Snappy's Power Washing and built Lavo for his own business; marketing lead Mike Carmody runs Mike's Pressure Washing.

pros_detail.title: Instant quotes from an address
pros_detail.explanation: On Core and Complete, a customer enters an address and gets a bookable price in seconds from property data and satellite imagery, with no site visit needed for a starting price.

pros_detail.title: Zone-based scheduling
pros_detail.explanation: Route density lets you map service zones and steers online bookings toward days you are already in that area, which helps cut drive time between jobs.

pros_detail.title: Users included in the price
pros_detail.explanation: Plans include 2, 5+ or 7+ users for a flat monthly price, and the pricing page lists no separate per-user fee.

cons_detail.title: Key features start on Core
cons_detail.explanation: Instant quoting, route density, SMS follow-ups and QuickBooks Online sync are not in the $47 Starter plan; you need Core at $97 a month (launch price) or higher.

cons_detail.title: Launch pricing on upper tiers
cons_detail.explanation: Core and Complete are shown as launch specials against regular prices of $127 and $177. Ask whether your rate is locked before you commit.

cons_detail.title: Young vendor
cons_detail.explanation: Lavo is a small, recent company. Its usage figures (quotes automated, dollars quoted) come from the vendor, and there is little independent history to check.

cons_detail.title: Zone grouping, not stop routing
cons_detail.explanation: Route density groups work by service zone and day. It does not sequence the order of stops within a day the way a dedicated routing tool does.

cons_detail.title: Some terms unpublished
cons_detail.explanation: Annual prices, card processing rates and how extra users beyond the included count are billed are not listed on the pricing page.

tools.implementation_notes: Lavo is self-serve with a 14-day free trial on every plan. If instant quoting is the reason you are looking, start on Core, because Starter does not include it. Set up your services and per-surface pricing first, since instant quotes are only as good as those rules. Run the address quote against ten properties you have already quoted by hand and compare the numbers, paying attention to irregular lots, heavy tree cover and multi-story homes. Then map your service zones and assign service days to match how you already work. Connect Stripe or Square for payments and QuickBooks Online if you use it, and load your customer list. Before the trial ends, ask the vendor about annual pricing, processing rates, extra users and whether launch pricing is locked in.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Lavo CRM cost?
tool_faqs.a: Starter is $47 a month with 2 users. Core is $97 a month with 5+ users and Complete is $157 a month with 7+ users; both are launch specials against regular prices of $127 and $177. Every plan has a 14-day free trial and no contract. Yearly billing is advertised at 15% or more off, but annual prices are not published.

tool_faqs.q: Which plan includes instant quoting?
tool_faqs.a: Core and Complete. The Starter plan includes online booking, the customer portal, invoicing and payments, but instant quoting, route density and QuickBooks Online sync start on Core.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Lavo CRM?
tool_faqs.a: Fiat Software LLC of Centerburg, Ohio. Founder Aaron May also founded Snappy's Power Washing, and Lavo started as the software for that business. Mike Carmody, owner of Mike's Pressure Washing and Fresh Rinse Media, handles marketing.

tool_faqs.q: How does the instant address quoting work?
tool_faqs.a: A customer enters a property address and Lavo returns a price in seconds using property data and satellite imagery with your pricing rules. The privacy policy lists RentCast for property data. Test it against jobs you have already quoted by hand before relying on it.

tool_faqs.q: Does Lavo CRM optimize my routes?
tool_faqs.a: Not stop by stop. Route density lets you map service zones and steers online bookings toward days you are already working in an area. It groups work geographically but does not set the order of stops within a day.

tools.name: Calday
tools.tagline: Online booking page, calendar and Stripe deposits for solo service operators

pricing.pricing_note: Free tier is genuinely usable but capped at 1 service, 100 clients and 1 integration. Pro $12/month unlocks unlimited services and clients, payment collection, add-ons and custom booking questions. Yearly billing is 20% off. A 7-day Pro trial is advertised as requiring no credit card. Verified from calday.com/pricing 2026-09-04 and corroborated by the Capterra listing.

tools.best_for: Solo operators who want a public booking page and upfront deposits, not a job-management system
tools.weaknesses: No quoting, estimating, invoicing, job or work-order management, dispatch, route planning, job photos or technician seats. It is an appointment-booking product, so anything past the booking has to live in another tool.
tools.long_description:
Calday is an online booking and scheduling product for very small service businesses, operated by DUDECODE LLC, a Florida company filed in July 2022. It gives an operator a public booking page, a calendar with working hours, breaks, buffers and lead times, a client contact list, automated reminders and confirmations, and Stripe payment collection so a deposit can be taken at the time of booking. There are two plans and both prices are published: a free tier capped at one service, 100 clients and one calendar integration, and Pro at $12 per month for unlimited services and clients plus payment collection, add-on services and custom booking questions. Annual billing is 20% cheaper.

It is important to be precise about what Calday is, because the vendor markets it as service business management software and the product is narrower than that phrase implies. The complete plan comparison table on their own pricing page contains no quoting, no estimating, no invoicing, no job or work-order management, no dispatch, no route planning, no job photos, no timesheets and no technician seats. Their own iOS app, published in January 2026, is titled Calday: Booking & Scheduling. As recently as November 2025 the homepage was titled Free Appointment Scheduling Software and led with tutors, photographers and accountants rather than trades. The trade-specific landing pages are real and the vendor genuinely courts handyman, cleaning, pressure-washing and appliance-repair operators, but the underlying product is a booking tool.

That framing is not a criticism so much as a buying instruction. A solo operator who wants customers to self-book and pay a deposit, and who already handles quotes and invoices somewhere else, is buying exactly the right thing at $12 a month. An operator who needs to quote a job, schedule a crew to it, capture photos on site and bill it afterwards is not, and should be reading Jobber or Housecall Pro instead. Calday's own FAQ concedes as much: it positions itself below ServiceTitan and FieldEdge, and names Calendly, Acuity and Square Appointments as the products people switch from.
tools.implementation_notes:
Setup is genuinely fast and the vendor's claim of a booking page live in about five minutes is plausible given what the product does: you create a service, set working hours, connect a calendar and publish the page. There is no data migration to speak of because there is no job history, invoice ledger or customer job record to bring across, which is the flip side of the product being booking-first. Connect Stripe if you want to take deposits, since payment collection is a Pro feature and is not in the free tier.

Two things to handle deliberately during signup. The consent checkbox on the email registration form links to calday.com/terms and calday.com/privacy, and both return HTTP 404 as of 2026-09-04; the real documents are at /terms-and-conditions and /privacy-policy, so read those before you tick the box. And treat the pricing page's price-lock promise as marketing rather than contract, because the Terms contain no grandfathering language and reserve the right to change prices at any time.

Plan for a second tool from day one. Decide before you start where quotes, invoices and job records will live, because Calday will not hold them, and retrofitting that after you have customers booking through the page is more disruptive than choosing it up front.

pros_detail.title: Both prices are published, with no quote-only path
pros_detail.explanation: Free at $0 per month and Pro at $12 per month are on the pricing page with a full feature comparison table, and the $12 figure is corroborated on Calday's Capterra listing. That puts it at the transparent end of a category where many vendors publish no price at all.

pros_detail.title: The company is independently verifiable and the founder is named
pros_detail.explanation: Calday is operated by DUDECODE LLC, a Florida limited liability company filed 2022-07-01 (document L22000297466, status ACTIVE). The same person named as founder on the About page appears as the authorised person on the state register and as the seller of record on the Apple App Store. Most vendors this small cannot be confirmed at all.

pros_detail.title: A buyer can actually buy it without talking to anyone
pros_detail.explanation: Every call to action routes to a self-serve registration form rather than a demo request, and both cancellation and account deletion are self-serve inside the app. In a category where a large share of vendors gate every button behind a sales call, this matters more than it should.

pros_detail.title: The free tier is usable rather than decorative
pros_detail.explanation: The $0 plan includes the booking page itself, calendar events, breaks, working hours, buffers, reminders and confirmation emails, capped at one service, 100 clients and one calendar integration. A solo operator can run a real booking page on it without paying.

cons_detail.title: The rating shown on Calday's site is self-declared
cons_detail.explanation: Calday's homepage and pricing page carry their own structured data with an aggregate rating based on 11 ratings, and the page names no source for it. We do not reproduce review scores, so check Calday's current reviews on G2 and Capterra yourself before relying on that rating. Checked 2026-09-04.

cons_detail.title: The public customer figure is framed as active usage and the vendor's own number does not support it
cons_detail.explanation: The site states 2,500+ service businesses already saving hours every week, and 2,500+ service businesses across 25 industries. The founder told WrenchStack on 2026-09-02 that the base is 2,000+ registered accounts with approximately 200 to 300 monthly active users. The public figure exceeds his own registration count and is roughly eight to twelve times his own active count, and none of the pages carrying it describe it as cumulative sign-ups. Verified 2026-09-04.

cons_detail.title: The Terms and Privacy links on the signup consent checkbox are dead
cons_detail.explanation: Creating an account requires ticking a box agreeing to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy, but those two links point at calday.com/terms and calday.com/privacy, which both return HTTP 404. The real documents exist at /terms-and-conditions and /privacy-policy. Users are therefore agreeing to documents the form itself cannot open. Verified 2026-09-04.

cons_detail.title: The price-lock promise on the pricing page is not in the contract
cons_detail.explanation: The pricing FAQ says there will be no surprise hikes and that existing customers keep their current rate as long as their subscription stays active. The Terms contain no grandfathering language at all and reserve the opposite, stating that Calday reserves the right to change prices and revise the resources usage policy at any moment, inside an entire-agreement clause that supersedes prior representations. Verified 2026-09-04.

cons_detail.title: This is booking and scheduling, not field-service management
cons_detail.explanation: The complete plan comparison table has no quoting, estimating, invoicing, job or work-order management, dispatch, route planning, job photos, timesheets or technician seats. Calday's own iOS app is titled Calday: Booking & Scheduling. If you need to quote a job, bill it and track the work, Calday handles the appointment and something else has to handle the rest.

cons_detail.title: Short operating history and almost no independent review base
cons_detail.explanation: calday.com served no live product before 2024-12-11 and the product ran at calday.app from 2023-05-18. The iOS app shipped 2026-01-22 and carries one rating. As recently as 2025-11-14 the homepage was titled Free Appointment Scheduling Software and led with tutors, photographers and accountants, so the service-business positioning is under a year old. There is no track record yet on reliability, pricing stability or support.

tool_faqs.q: Is Calday field service management software?
tool_faqs.a: No. It is an appointment-booking and scheduling product. The full plan comparison on Calday's own pricing page has no quoting, estimating, invoicing, job or work-order management, dispatch, route planning, job photos or technician seats, and their own iOS app is titled Calday: Booking & Scheduling. It gives you a public booking page, a calendar, reminders, a client list and Stripe deposits. If you need to quote, schedule a crew, capture site photos and invoice, you need a field-service platform such as Jobber or Housecall Pro, and Calday's own FAQ positions it below those.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Calday cost?
tool_faqs.a: There are two published plans. Free at $0 per month covers the booking page, calendar, working hours, breaks, buffers, reminders and confirmation emails, capped at one service, 100 clients and one calendar integration. Pro is $12 per month and adds unlimited services and clients, Stripe payment collection, add-on services, custom booking questions and priority support. Annual billing is 20% cheaper. A 7-day Pro trial is advertised as requiring no credit card. Verified 2026-09-04.

tool_faqs.q: Is the rating on Calday's website real?
tool_faqs.a: We could not confirm it. The rating is published in Calday's own page markup as a self-declared aggregate from 11 ratings, with no attribution to G2 or any other review site. Read Calday's reviews on the review sites directly before relying on it.

tool_faqs.q: Who is behind Calday?
tool_faqs.a: DUDECODE LLC, a Florida limited liability company filed on 2022-07-01, document number L22000297466, status ACTIVE. The founder, Pavlo Grinevich, is named publicly on the company's About page, appears as the authorised person on the Florida state register, and DUDECODE LLC is the seller of record on the Apple App Store listing. That level of confirmation is unusual for a vendor this small.

tool_faqs.q: What should I watch for when signing up to Calday?
tool_faqs.a: Two things as of 2026-09-04. The consent checkbox on the registration form links to calday.com/terms and calday.com/privacy, and both return a 404; read the real documents at /terms-and-conditions and /privacy-policy before agreeing. And the pricing page promises existing customers keep their rate if prices change, but the Terms contain no grandfathering language and reserve the right to change prices at any moment under an entire-agreement clause, so treat that promise as marketing rather than contract.

tools.name: Solea
tools.tagline: Pest control software with a built-in AI voice agent, quoted as one system

pricing.pricing_note: Custom quote. Solea publishes no rate card ('no two pest control offices run the same way') and quotes the whole system, including the AI voice agent, with no modules to add on, 'based on the size of your operation'. The quote form asks for technicians running routes, yearly revenue band and current system. In an email to us on October 1, 2026, Solea said the quote is driven by revenue (the vendor's statement; no page we read states a rate, though its ROI calculator models an estimated price as a share of revenue 'for the ROI view only'). Not published and not answered by the vendor: whether AI voice calls or minutes are capped or billed by use (the terms allow overage charges at the price set in each order), any setup or migration fee, and the minimum contract length. No free trial is stated on the pricing page or in the terms. Verified against solea.ai/pricing, solea.ai/compare/pestpac, solea.ai/roi-calculator and solea.ai/terms-and-conditions 2026-10-03.

tools.best_for: Pest control companies with five or more technicians that want the phones, scheduling, routing, billing and collections in one pest-specific system and are comfortable buying by quote
tools.weaknesses: No published price, and AI voice usage, setup fees and the minimum term are not disclosed; no accounting integration (CSV and Excel export only); the published terms auto-renew, give no refunds and contain no data-export right when you leave.
tools.long_description:
Solea is field service software made for pest control companies, with an AI voice agent built in. Its homepage says it is 'made for pest control, not generic home services', and its about page gives a San Francisco address and names co-founders Christopher Brodowski (CEO) and Paul Muller. Solea's terms name Solea Inc.; Solea told us on October 1, 2026 that this is a trading name of Humanss AI Inc., a Delaware corporation, which the App Store lists as the seller of Solea's iPhone app. Solea says it has raised $10 million in total (vendor-reported).

The voice agent answers 24/7 in the office's name, in English, Spanish or both, books onto the live schedule, and transfers callers or emails the office a summary and transcript. Each night, auto-scheduling places due and unassigned work into routes optimized on the drive time between stops, and dispatchers can lock visits and set a freeze window. The system also covers customer records, a shared inbox for texts and email, proposals customers sign online, invoicing, billing through Stripe, overdue reminders, CSV and Excel reports, a customer portal and multiple branches in one account.

For pest work, technicians scan stations by barcode and log activity and bait use. Solea fills in product details from an EPA registration number and totals usage by product and active ingredient, grouped by state, though it says ready-to-file state pesticide-use report formats are not confirmed. It manages Sentricon sites and books fumigation on a separate capacity schedule with daily slot limits. Solea says it handles WDO reports through document templates built from your state's own form; no specific WDO form is named on the pages we read.

Solea's site names customers that moved from FieldRoutes, PestPac and ServSuite. Three of them, Horizon Pest Control and Bug Boys Services in New Jersey and Compass Pest Management in Georgia and South Carolina, link their own customer logins to Solea. Its two detailed case studies are Hawaii companies. Solea told us more than 50 pest control companies are live on it (vendor-reported; no page we read gives a count).

The trade-off: pricing is by quote only, there is no accounting integration, and the published terms auto-renew, give no refunds and let Solea end the agreement on 30 days' notice. The company is young. Solea's own buying guide suggests GorillaDesk for companies with fewer than five technicians; larger pest companies buying by quote can demo Solea alongside PestPac and FieldRoutes.

pros_detail.title: AI voice agent in the same quote
pros_detail.explanation: The agent answers 24/7 in your office's name, in English, Spanish or both, and books onto the live schedule. Solea says its quote covers the whole system, including the AI voice agent, with no modules to add on. Whether calls or minutes are capped or billed by use is not stated.

pros_detail.title: Overnight scheduling around drive time
pros_detail.explanation: Each night, auto-scheduling places due and unassigned work into routes optimized on the drive time between every pair of stops. Dispatchers can lock a visit's time or technician, set a freeze window and preview changes as a dry run.

pros_detail.title: Pest-specific field and chemical records
pros_detail.explanation: Technicians scan stations by barcode, log activity and bait use, and work from a schedule that stays readable offline. Enter an EPA registration number and Solea fills in the product details, and usage totals by product and active ingredient can be grouped and filtered by state. Solea says ready-to-file state pesticide-use report formats are not confirmed.

pros_detail.title: Billing and collections in one place
pros_detail.explanation: Card, ACH, autopay and payment links run through Stripe, with billing on a schedule, per completed service or once at renewal. Overdue notices go out by email or text with a payment link, and customers are warned before their saved cards expire.

pros_detail.title: Customers you can check
pros_detail.explanation: Horizon Pest Control, Compass Pest Management and Bug Boys Services, which Solea names as companies that moved from FieldRoutes or PestPac, link their own customer logins to Solea.

pros_detail.title: Written limits on data use
pros_detail.explanation: The terms say the customer owns its data and the AI output, though Solea owns de-identified data it derives from them. The privacy policy says Solea does not use personal information in customer data, including call recordings and transcripts, to train general-purpose or foundation AI models, and does not sell customer data for monetary consideration. Those limits are narrow: the same policy lets Solea use aggregated or de-identified data to improve the service.

cons_detail.title: No published price, and key costs undisclosed
cons_detail.explanation: Solea quotes one system and told us the quote is driven by revenue. Neither the pages we read nor its reply to us says whether AI voice calls or minutes are capped or billed by use, whether there is a setup or migration fee, or how long the minimum term is. The terms allow overage charges at the price set in each order.

cons_detail.title: No accounting integration
cons_detail.explanation: Asked whether it integrates with your accounting system, Solea's integrations page answers 'Not today'. Invoices, sales tax and worklogs export to CSV and reports download as CSV or Excel, so your bookkeeping runs on file exports. Public API access and webhooks are not confirmed either.

cons_detail.title: Auto-renewal, no refunds and a 30-day vendor exit
cons_detail.explanation: Each subscription period renews automatically unless either side gives written notice at least 30 days before it ends, and the terms say Solea is not obligated to refund fees paid. Solea may end the agreement on 30 days' written notice; the customer has no right to end it mid-term for convenience, only for an uncured material breach or after an infringement claim if Solea's replacement is not acceptable. Solea may change prices from the next service period, and may amend the terms on notice, from the next period unless the notice says otherwise; a customer that does not agree must stop using the service. Each party's liability is capped at the fees paid in the period when the damage occurred, but the cap does not cover indemnity or the customer's payment obligations. The terms contain no uptime or support commitment.

cons_detail.title: You carry call-recording and AI consent
cons_detail.explanation: The terms make the customer responsible for all notices and consents for call recording, monitoring and the use of AI agents, and require the customer to defend and indemnify Solea against third-party claims arising from its use of the service, its data, a breach of those consent duties or a violation of law. Check your state's rules before turning on the voice agent.

cons_detail.title: No data export promised when you leave
cons_detail.explanation: Solea's integrations page says a complete export of accounts and history when you leave is not confirmed, and the published terms contain no clause on returning or deleting your data at termination. The privacy policy defers retention to the customer agreement. Get export and deletion terms written into your order.

cons_detail.title: Young company; reviews unverified
cons_detail.explanation: Solea's about page says it was founded in 2025, though a November 2024 article already described it as a new voice AI start-up. Its two detailed case studies are Hawaii companies, and the Able Pest Management comparison covers one month on Solea (August 2026). We have not verified an independent review base: treat it as unverified, not absent, and check the review sites linked on this page.

cons_detail.title: Android app hard to find
cons_detail.explanation: Solea says its field app runs on iPhone and Android phones, and the iPhone app is on the App Store. The Android app, Solea from Solea Inc. (com.solea.technician, updated August 18, 2026, 10+ downloads), is on Google Play, but it did not appear in our Play searches and Solea's site had no Google Play link on October 3, 2026. Its store description calls it a companion that connects to FieldRoutes and ServiceTitan and is built for pest control, HVAC, plumbing and electrical businesses, which differs from Solea's own site. Test it on your technicians' phones before go-live.

tools.implementation_notes: Book a demo and ask for a written quote that states how AI voice calls or minutes are counted and whether overages apply, any setup or migration fee, the length of the subscription period, and whether a pilot is available. Ask for the order to name Humanss AI Inc., the legal entity Solea says stands behind the Solea Inc. trading name, and to include an uptime and support commitment and a written commitment to export and then delete your data if you leave, since the published terms have none of these. Put the non-renewal deadline, 30 days before each period ends, on your calendar. Before moving over, export customers, recurring service plans, service history, device and station records, chemical records and open balances from your current system, and ask Solea what its team handles during the move. Its pricing page describes a 1-week migration; its Able Pest Management case study (vendor-reported) says the data move took 3 days, with go-live on July 27, 2026 after signing in late May. Bring your WDO report, any completion certificate and your state's WDO form to the walkthrough, as Solea's WDO page suggests, and ask to see your state's pesticide-use report. Plan your accounting routine around CSV exports, check your state's call-recording and AI disclosure rules before switching on the voice agent, and test the field app on your technicians' Android phones before go-live.

tool_faqs.q: Who makes Solea?
tool_faqs.a: Solea's terms and privacy policy name Solea Inc., at a San Francisco address. Solea told us in October 2026 that Solea Inc. is a trading name of Humanss AI Inc., a Delaware corporation, and that customer contracts are signed under the Solea Inc. name. Humanss AI Inc. sells Solea's iPhone app, and OpenCorporates lists it as a Delaware corporation with an active California registration whose mailing address matches the one in Solea's terms. Solea's about page says the company was founded in 2025 and names co-founders Christopher Brodowski (CEO) and Paul Muller.

tool_faqs.q: How much does Solea cost?
tool_faqs.a: Solea does not publish prices. It quotes one system, including the AI voice agent, based on the size of your operation, and its quote form asks for your technician count, yearly revenue band and current system. Solea told us the quote is driven by revenue. AI voice usage limits, any setup or migration fee and the minimum term are not published, so ask for them in writing.

tool_faqs.q: Does Solea work with QuickBooks?
tool_faqs.a: Not directly. Asked whether it integrates with your accounting system, Solea's integrations page answers 'Not today': invoices, sales tax and worklogs export to CSV, and reports download as CSV or Excel. QuickBooks is not named on that page. Its listed connections are Stripe, Sentricon, Scorpion, SmarterLaunch, Applause, TalkDesk and Voice for Pest, plus Apple Maps and Google Maps.

tool_faqs.q: Does the Solea app work on Android?
tool_faqs.a: Yes, per Solea and Google Play. The Android app is Solea from Solea Inc. (com.solea.technician), last updated August 18, 2026. It did not appear in our Google Play searches on October 3, 2026 and Solea's site had no Google Play link, so ask Solea for the link. Its store description describes a technician companion that connects to FieldRoutes and ServiceTitan, which differs from Solea's own site, so test it on your technicians' phones before you roll it out.

tool_faqs.q: What does Solea replace?
tool_faqs.a: Solea pitches itself as a replacement for FieldRoutes, PestPac and ServSuite, and its site names customers that moved from each. It covers customer records, scheduling and routing, the technician app, invoicing, recurring billing, card and ACH payments, collections, reporting, a customer portal and the phones, through the AI voice agent. It does not replace your accounting software, because it has no accounting integration.

tool_faqs.q: Does Solea handle termite, WDO and fumigation work?
tool_faqs.a: It manages Sentricon sites and records device and bait-station inspections by barcode scan. Solea says it handles WDO reports through document templates, switched on per office: you upload your state's form, map its fields to Solea data, add a drawing area for the diagram and collect signatures. No specific WDO form is named on the pages we read, and Solea's WDO page asks buyers to bring their exact report and any completion certificate to the product walkthrough. Fumigation is booked on a separate capacity schedule with daily slot limits; no tarp, crew or clearance tools are named on the pages we read.

tool_faqs.q: Is Solea built for small pest control companies?
tool_faqs.a: Solea says it is built for operators from 5 technicians up to multi-branch companies, and its own buying guide suggests GorillaDesk for companies with fewer than 5 technicians.
